REGISTER: cycle
NUMBER: 0xc00
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: For base ISAs with XLEN ≥ 64, the RDCYCLE pseudoinstruction reads the full 64-bit value of the cycle CSR.
RULE 2: The cycle counter can be read using the canonical csrrs rd, cycle, x0 instruction as well as the read-only CSRRC, CSRRSI, and CSRRCI forms.
RULE 3: The RDCYCLE pseudoinstruction reads the low XLEN bits of the cycle CSR.
RULE 4: The presented code sequence ensures that a consistent 64-bit cycle counter value is read even if the lower half overflows between the reads.
RULE 5: The cycle CSR is located at address 0xC00 and is designated as unprivileged read-only (URO).
RULE 6: The cycleh CSR is located at address 0xC80 and is designated as unprivileged read-only (URO).
RULE 7: The cycle CSR provides a cycle counter that is accessed by the RDCYCLE instruction.
RULE 8: When the RDCYCLE instruction reads CSR 0xC00, the value returned equals the current cycle counter.
RULE 9: The mcycle register is located at address 0xB00 and provides the Machine cycle counter.
RULE 10: The mcycle CSR counts the number of clock cycles executed by the processor core on which the hart is running.
RULE 11: A write to the mcycle CSR stores the specified value into the register.
RULE 12: A write to the mcycle CSR takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 13: If the mcycle CSR is shared between harts on the same core, writes to the mcycle CSR are visible to all those harts.
RULE 14: The cycle counter continues to increment regardless of any reads or writes to the mcounteren register.
RULE 15: When the CY bit in mcounteren is clear, attempts to read the cycle CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 16: When the CY bit in mcounteren is set, access to the cycle CSR is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 17: The cycle CSR is a read-only shadow of the mcycle register.
RULE 18: If a hart that supports U‑mode writes any value to the CY field of the mcounteren CSR, then the write does not raise an illegal‑instruction exception and a subsequent read of mcounteren.CY returns either the value written or zero.
RULE 19: In harts that support U-mode, when the CY field of mcounteren is read-only zero, reads of the cycle CSR from a less-privileged mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 20: When the CY bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mcycle CSR increments on each cycle.
RULE 21: When the CY bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mcycle CSR does not increment on any cycle.
RULE 22: When the mcycle CSR is shared between harts on the same core, the mcountinhibit.CY field is also shared, and writes to mcountinhibit.CY are visible to those harts, thereby controlling whether the shared mcycle CSR increments on each cycle.
RULE 23: By default the cycle counter is not filtered by privilege mode.
RULE 24: The privilege-mode filtering applied to the cycle counter is the same as that applied to the instret counter.
RULE 25: Bit 62 of mcyclecfg, named MINH, when set inhibits counting of cycle events while the processor is executing in machine mode.
RULE 26: Bit 61 of mcyclecfg, named SINH, when set inhibits counting of cycle events while the processor is executing in supervisor or hypervisor mode.
RULE 27: Bit 60 of mcyclecfg, named UINH, when set inhibits counting of cycle events while the processor is executing in user mode.
RULE 28: If all INH bits (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mcyclecfg are zero, counting of cycle events is enabled in all privilege modes.
RULE 29: For any INH bit in positions 61 through 58 of mcyclecfg, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, that bit is read-only zero.
RULE 30: The cycle counter will increment for each CPU cycle while the CPU is executing in a non-inhibited privilege mode.
RULE 31: When mcounteren[0] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1, the cycle register may be read or written via the indirect CSRs while siselect = 0x40.
RULE 32: If mcounteren[0] = 0, any access to the cycle register, cycleh, cyclecfg, or cyclecfgh via the indirect CSRs raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 33: The SCTRCLR instruction must set the cycle counter field of the CTR register to zero and must also set the CCV field to zero.
RULE 34: If the difference between successive reads of the elapsed cycle counter (CtrCycleCounter) does not equal the difference between successive reads of the mcycle CSR, then the counters are not incrementing at the same rate.
RULE 35: Only cycles while CTR is active are counted, where active implies that the current privilege mode is enabled for recording and CTR is not frozen.
RULE 36: Unimplemented CCE bits, which are part of the cycle count exponent, are read-only 0.
RULE 37: If a CSR write to the cycle counter using the standard counter‑modification mechanism does not change the cycle CSR’s readback value (or raises an illegal‑instruction exception), then the implementation violates the rule.
RULE 38: If the CY bit in scounteren is clear, a read of the cycle register while executing in U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 39: If the CY bit in scounteren is set, access to the cycle register from U-mode is permitted.
RULE 40: If the CY bit in scounteren is read-only zero, a U-mode read of the cycle register causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 41: The writability of the CY bit in scounteren is not affected by the setting of the CY bit in mcounteren.
RULE 42: A U-mode read of the cycle register causes an illegal-instruction exception unless both the CY bit in scounteren and the CY bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 43: If both the CY bit in scounteren and the CY bit in mcounteren are set, a U-mode read of the cycle register is permitted.
RULE 44: When the 64-bit cycle counter wraps, the mcause or scause register is set to exception code 13 (counter-overflow interrupt).
RULE 45: When XLEN>32, any attempt to access a high-half cycle CSR (e.g., cycleh) raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 46: In M-mode, accessing cycle register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc00; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 47: In S-mode, accessing cycle register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc00; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 48: In U-mode, accessing cycle register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc00; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 49: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the cycle register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc00, a0; csrr a1, 0xc00; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: fcsr
NUMBER: 0x003
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 32
FIELDS: 7..5=FRM, 4..4=NV, 3..3=DZ, 2..2=OF, 1..1=UF, 0..0=NX
EXTENSIONS: D, F, Q, Zdinx, Zfinx, Zhinx
RULE 1: The fcsr register is not visible to other harts.
RULE 2: Bits 4, 3, 2, 1, and 0 of the fcsr register are aliases of the corresponding bits in the fflags CSR and are tracked as independent units.
RULE 3: If the fcsr CSR is written with a value V, then a subsequent read of the frm CSR returns V[7:5] and a subsequent read of fcsr returns V; if the frm CSR is written with a value R, then a subsequent read of fcsr returns a value whose bits 7:5 equal R[2:0] (other bits unchanged).
RULE 4: Bits 7, 6, and 5 of the fcsr register are aliases of the frm CSR and are tracked as independent units.
RULE 5: Bits 31-8 of fcsr are reserved for other standard extensions, and if those extensions are not present implementations shall ignore writes to these bits and shall return zero for these bits when fcsr is read.
RULE 6: The FSCSR instruction swaps the value in fcsr by copying the original fcsr value into integer register rd and then writing a new value taken from integer register rs1 into fcsr.
RULE 7: The FRRM instruction reads the rounding-mode field frm (bits 7-5 of fcsr) and copies it into the least-significant three bits of integer register rd, setting all other bits of rd to zero.
RULE 8: The FSRM instruction swaps the rounding-mode field frm by copying the original bits 7-5 of fcsr into integer register rd and then writing the three least-significant bits of integer register rs1 into bits 7-5 of fcsr.
RULE 9: The FRFLAGS instruction reads the accrued-exception-flags field fflags (bits 4-0 of fcsr) and copies it into integer register rd, zero-extending the value to the full width of rd.
RULE 10: The FSFLAGS instruction swaps the accrued-exception-flags field by copying the original bits 4-0 of fcsr into integer register rd and then writing the five least-significant bits of integer register rs1 into bits 4-0 of fcsr.
RULE 11: Floating-point operations use either a static rounding mode encoded in the instruction or the dynamic rounding mode held in frm, and an instruction encoding of rm=111 selects the dynamic rounding mode held in frm.
RULE 12: The accrued exception flags in fcsr indicate which exception conditions have arisen on any floating-point arithmetic instruction since the flags were last reset by software.
RULE 13: The base RISC-V ISA does not provide a mechanism to generate a trap on the setting of any floating-point exception flag in fcsr.
RULE 14: Bits 7-5 of fcsr encode the rounding mode with the following meanings: 000 = round to nearest, ties to even (RNE); 001 = round towards zero (RTZ); 010 = round down towards –∞ (RDN); 011 = round up towards +∞ (RUP); 100 = round to nearest, ties to max magnitude (RMM); 101 and 110 are reserved for future use; 111 is reserved in the register and is used in an instruction's rm field to select the dynamic rounding mode.
RULE 15: Bits 4-0 of fcsr encode the accrued exception flags with the following bit assignments: bit 4 = Invalid Operation (NV); bit 3 = Divide by Zero (DZ); bit 2 = Overflow (OF); bit 1 = Underflow (UF); bit 0 = Inexact (NX).
RULE 16: The fcsr has URW privilege, meaning it is readable and writable in unprivileged mode.
RULE 17: The fflags component of the fcsr is URW (unprivileged read/write).
RULE 18: The frm component of the fcsr is URW (unprivileged read/write).
RULE 19: If an instruction (explicitly or implicitly) writes the fcsr while the FS field is Initial or Clean and the write does not modify any fcsr bits, then after the instruction the FS field may either remain unchanged or transition to Dirty (implementation-defined).
RULE 20: Changing the FS field has no effect on the contents of the fcsr.
RULE 21: Setting FS=Off does not destroy the contents of the fcsr.
RULE 22: Setting FS=Initial does not clear the contents of the fcsr.
RULE 23: When misa.F=1, the FCSR bit of mstateen0, hstateen0, and sstateen0 is read-only zero, pertaining to the fcsr register.
RULE 24: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 25: In S-mode, accessing fcsr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 26: In U-mode, accessing fcsr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 27: In M-mode, setting fcsr.FRM (bit 5) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x20) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x20; csrs 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x20].
RULE 28: In M-mode, setting fcsr.NV (bit 4) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x10) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10; csrs 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x10].
RULE 29: In M-mode, setting fcsr.DZ (bit 3) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8; csrs 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8].
RULE 30: In M-mode, setting fcsr.OF (bit 2) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4; csrs 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4].
RULE 31: In M-mode, setting fcsr.UF (bit 1) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2].
RULE 32: In M-mode, setting fcsr.NX (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 33: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the fcsr register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x003, a0; csrr a1, 0x003; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 34: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register while D extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: D; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 35: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register while F extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: F; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register while Q extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Q; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 37: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register while Zdinx extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zdinx; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 38: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register while Zfinx extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zfinx; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 39: In M-mode, accessing fcsr register while Zhinx extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zhinx; csrr a0, 0x003; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: fflags
NUMBER: 0x001
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 32
FIELDS: 4..4=NV, 3..3=DZ, 2..2=OF, 1..1=UF, 0..0=NX
EXTENSIONS: D, F, Q, V
RULE 1: An access to the fcsr CSR also affects the fflags CSR.
RULE 2: The Accrued Exception Flags field named fflags occupies bits 4-0 of the floating-point control and status register (fcsr).
RULE 3: The FRFLAGS instruction reads the current value of fflags and copies it into integer register rd, placing the flag bits in rd bits 4-0 and clearing all other bits of rd to zero.
RULE 4: The FSFLAGS instruction returns the original value of fflags in integer register rd.
RULE 5: The FSFLAGS instruction writes a new value to fflags using the three least-significant bits of integer register rs1 as the source value.
RULE 6: The FSFLAGS instruction updates fflags with the low five bits of rs1, replacing the previous flag contents.
RULE 7: Whenever a floating-point arithmetic instruction encounters an exception condition, the corresponding bit(s) in fflags become set.
RULE 8: Once set, the bits in fflags remain set until software resets the field.
RULE 9: Each of the five bits in fflags (bits 4-0) corresponds to one of the exception mnemonics NV, DZ, OF, UF, and NX, representing Invalid Operation, Divide by Zero, Overflow, Underflow, and Inexact respectively.
RULE 10: Setting a flag bit in fflags never generates a trap in the base RISC-V ISA.
RULE 11: An inactive floating-point element does not set the FP exception flags in the fflags register.
RULE 12: The fflags CSR is accessible with unprivileged read/write (URW) privilege.
RULE 13: The fcsr CSR, which incorporates the fflags field, is accessible with unprivileged read/write (URW) privilege.
RULE 14: Changing the setting of the FS field has no effect on the contents of the fflags CSR.
RULE 15: Setting FS=Off does not destroy the contents of the fflags CSR.
RULE 16: Setting FS=Initial does not clear the contents of the fflags CSR.
RULE 17: In M-mode, accessing fflags register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 18: In S-mode, accessing fflags register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 19: In U-mode, accessing fflags register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 20: In M-mode, setting fflags.NV (bit 4) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x10) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10; csrs 0x001, a0; csrr a1, 0x001; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x10].
RULE 21: In M-mode, setting fflags.DZ (bit 3) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8; csrs 0x001, a0; csrr a1, 0x001; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8].
RULE 22: In M-mode, setting fflags.OF (bit 2) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4; csrs 0x001, a0; csrr a1, 0x001; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4].
RULE 23: In M-mode, setting fflags.UF (bit 1) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x001, a0; csrr a1, 0x001; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2].
RULE 24: In M-mode, setting fflags.NX (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x001, a0; csrr a1, 0x001; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 25: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the fflags register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x001, a0; csrr a1, 0x001; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 26: In M-mode, accessing fflags register while D extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: D; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing fflags register while F extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: F; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing fflags register while Q extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Q; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing fflags register while V extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: V; csrr a0, 0x001; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: frm
NUMBER: 0x002
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 32
FIELDS: 2..0=ROUNDINGMODE
EXTENSIONS: F, V, Zvfbfmin, Zvfbfwma
RULE 1: The frm register is listed as an alias of the fcsr CSR.
RULE 2: The fcsr CSR lists frm as one of its aliases.
RULE 3: Bits 7-5 of the fcsr CSR are an alias of the frm register.
RULE 4: Modifying bits 7-5 of the fcsr CSR changes the value of the frm register.
RULE 5: The FRRM instruction reads the frm field and copies its value into the least-significant three bits of integer register rd while zeroing all other bits of rd.
RULE 6: The FSRM instruction first copies the original frm value into integer register rd and then writes a new value taken from the three least-significant bits of integer register rs1 into the frm field.
RULE 7: When the rm field of a floating-point instruction is binary 111, the instruction selects the dynamic rounding mode held in frm.
RULE 8: When frm holds the binary value 000, it specifies the rounding mode RNE – Round to Nearest, ties to Even.
RULE 9: When frm holds the binary value 001, it specifies the rounding mode RTZ – Round towards Zero.
RULE 10: When frm holds the binary value 010, it specifies the rounding mode RDN – Round Down (towards –∞).
RULE 11: When frm holds the binary value 011, it specifies the rounding mode RUP – Round Up (towards +∞).
RULE 12: When frm holds the binary value 100, it specifies the rounding mode RMM – Round to Nearest, ties to Max Magnitude.
RULE 13: If the frm field of fcsr is set to binary 111 and a floating‑point instruction supplies a non‑zero rm field, then the instruction uses the rm field as the rounding mode (observable by the operation’s result matching that rounding mode).
RULE 14: If the frm field of a floating‑point instruction is 101, 110, or 111, then the instruction raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause set to the illegal‑instruction code).
RULE 15: When the rm field of a scalar floating-point instruction is encoded as DYN (binary 111), the instruction uses the rounding mode specified in the frm CSR.
RULE 16: The sum is rounded according to the frm register.
RULE 17: The vector floating-point/integer conversion instructions vfcvt.xu.f.v, vfcvt.x.f.v, vfcvt.rtz.xu.f.v, vfcvt.rtz.x.f.v, vfcvt.f.xu.v, and vfcvt.f.x.v use the dynamic rounding mode specified in the frm register.
RULE 18: The rtz variants vfcvt.rtz.xu.f.v and vfcvt.rtz.x.f.v do not use the rounding mode in the frm register and instead round towards zero.
RULE 19: The frm register has privilege level URW (User-Read/Write).
RULE 20: In M-mode, accessing frm register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 21: In S-mode, accessing frm register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 22: In U-mode, accessing frm register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 23: In M-mode, setting frm.ROUNDINGMODE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x002, a0; csrr a1, 0x002; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 24: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the frm register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x002, a0; csrr a1, 0x002; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing frm register while F extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: F; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 26: In M-mode, accessing frm register while V extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: V; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing frm register while Zvfbfmin extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zvfbfmin; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing frm register while Zvfbfwma extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zvfbfwma; csrr a0, 0x002; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hcounteren
NUMBER: 0x606
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: 32
FIELDS: 31..31=HPM31, 30..30=HPM30, 29..29=HPM29, 28..28=HPM28, 27..27=HPM27, 26..26=HPM26, 25..25=HPM25, 24..24=HPM24, 23..23=HPM23, 22..22=HPM22, 21..21=HPM21, 20..20=HPM20, 19..19=HPM19, 18..18=HPM18, 17..17=HPM17, 16..16=HPM16, 15..15=HPM15, 14..14=HPM14, 13..13=HPM13, 12..12=HPM12, 11..11=HPM11, 10..10=HPM10, 9..9=HPM9, 8..8=HPM8, 7..7=HPM7, 6..6=HPM6, 5..5=HPM5, 4..4=HPM4, 3..3=HPM3, 2..2=IR, 1..1=TM, 0..0=CY

REGISTER: henvcfg
NUMBER: 0x60a
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=STCE, 62..62=PBMTE, 61..61=ADUE, 7..7=CBZE, 6..6=CBCFE, 5..4=CBIE, 3..3=SSE, 0..0=FIOM
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: Writes to henvcfg.CBIE, henvcfg.CBCFE, or henvcfg.CBZE do not affect the corresponding fields of menvcfg or senvcfg, and reads of those fields in other xenvcfg registers are independent of henvcfg.
RULE 2: If a U‑mode or S‑mode instruction tries to read from or write to the henvcfg CSR, then the processor raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = 2).
RULE 3: The hypervisor CSR henvcfg contains a FIOM bit that is equivalent to the FIOM bit in menvcfg.
RULE 4: henvcfg.PBMTE is read-only zero if the implementation has the hypervisor extension and menvcfg.PBMTE is zero.
RULE 5: henvcfg.ADUE is read-only zero if the implementation has the hypervisor extension and menvcfg.ADUE is zero.
RULE 6: If the Sstc extension is implemented and menvcfg.STCE is zero, henvcfg.STCE is read-only zero.
RULE 7: If menvcfg.SSE is zero, henvcfg.SSE is read-only zero.
RULE 8: The ENVCFG bit in mstateen0 controls access to the henvcfg, henvcfgh, and senvcfg CSRs.
RULE 9: If the hypervisor extension is implemented, the henvcfg .ADUE field is writable.
RULE 10: The henvcfg CSR includes an STCE bit when the Sstc extension is implemented.
RULE 11: If the Svpbmt extension is not implemented, the PBMTE field in henvcfg is read-only zero.
RULE 12: If the Svadu extension is not implemented, the ADUE field in henvcfg is read-only zero.
RULE 13: When CBO.ZERO is executed and the instruction is not HS-qualified, an illegal-instruction exception is raised regardless of the CBZE setting in henvcfg.
RULE 14: When V=1 and CBO.CLEAN or CBO.FLUSH is executed and the instruction is not HS-qualified, an illegal-instruction exception is raised regardless of the CBCFE setting in henvcfg.
RULE 15: When V=1 and CBO.CLEAN or CBO.FLUSH is executed, the instruction is HS-qualified, and CBCFE=1 in henvcfg, the instructions are enabled for execution.
RULE 16: When V=1 and CBO.INVAL is executed and the instruction is not HS-qualified, an illegal-instruction exception is raised regardless of the CBIE setting in henvcfg.
RULE 17: When V=1 and CBO.INVAL is HS-qualified and CBIE=01b or CBIE=11b in henvcfg, the instruction is enabled for execution.
RULE 18: If the Ssnpm extension is not implemented, the PMM field in henvcfg is read-only zero.
RULE 19: When PMM in henvcfg takes the legal WARL value 00, pointer masking is disabled (PMLEN=0).
RULE 20: When PMM in henvcfg takes the legal WARL value 10, pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN=XLEN-57 (PMLEN=7 on RV64).
RULE 21: When PMM in henvcfg takes the legal WARL value 11, pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN=XLEN-48 (PMLEN=16 on RV64).
RULE 22: When the SSE bit in henvcfg is 0 and V=1, 16-bit Zicfiss instructions revert to their behavior defined by Zcmop.
RULE 23: In M-mode, accessing henvcfg register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x60a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 24: In S-mode, accessing henvcfg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x60a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 25: In U-mode, accessing henvcfg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x60a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 26: In M-mode, setting henvcfg.STCE (bit 63) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x60a, a0; csrr a1, 0x60a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 27: In M-mode, setting henvcfg.PBMTE (bit 62) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4000000000000000; csrs 0x60a, a0; csrr a1, 0x60a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 28: In M-mode, setting henvcfg.CBZE (bit 7) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x80) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x80; csrs 0x60a, a0; csrr a1, 0x60a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x80].

REGISTER: hideleg
NUMBER: 0x603
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..16=WPRI, 15..14=WPRI, 13..13=LCOFI, 12..12=S-EXTERNAL, 11..11=WPRI, 10..10=VSEIP, 9..9=S-TIMER, 8..7=WPRI, 6..6=VSTIP, 5..5=S-SOFTWARE, 4..3=WPRI, 2..2=VSSIP, 1..0=WPRI
EXTENSIONS: H, Shlcofideleg

RULE 2: The hideleg CSR is an HSXLEN-bit read/write register.

REGISTER: hie
NUMBER: 0x604
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 63..16=UNKNOWN, 15..14=WPRI, 13..13=SGEIE, 12..11=WPRI, 10..10=VSEIE, 9..8=WPRI, 7..7=WPRI, 6..6=VSTIE, 5..3=WPRI, 2..2=VSSIE, 1..0=WPRI
EXTENSIONS: H, Shlcofideleg, Sstc
RULE 1: The hie CSR has the HRW attribute, indicating that it is both readable and writable.
RULE 2: If a bit in hie is not writable while its corresponding interrupt can become pending in hip, then writing a 1 to that hie bit leaves the hie register unchanged (the bit remains 0 on read‑back).
RULE 3: Bits of hie that are not writable shall be read-only zero.
RULE 4: For each writable bit in sie, the corresponding bit in hie shall be read-only zero.
RULE 5: Nonzero bits in sie and hie are always mutually exclusive.
RULE 6: If the interrupt‑enable bit for a given interrupt in the hie CSR is cleared, then setting the corresponding pending bit in the hip CSR will not make both hip and hie bits 1, so the combined (hip & hie) condition remains false and the interrupt does not become eligible to trigger (no interrupt exception is taken).
RULE 7: An interrupt will trap to HS-mode when its bit is set in both hip and hie and all other trap conditions are satisfied.
RULE 8: The writability of hideleg bit 13 does not directly affect hie.
RULE 9: For any bit position i where the Machine Interrupt Delegation register (mideleg) bit i is zero, the corresponding bit i in the hie register must be a read-only zero.
RULE 10: The SGEIE bit in the mie register is an alias for a corresponding bit in the hie register.
RULE 11: The SSSIE bit in the mie register is an alias for a corresponding bit in the hie register.
RULE 12: In M-mode, accessing hie register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x604; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hip
NUMBER: 0x644
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: UNKNOWN..UNKNOWN=UNDEFINED, 15..15=WPRI, 14..14=LCOFIP, 13..13=SGEIP, 12..12=WPRI, 11..11=VSEIP, 10..10=WPRI, 9..9=WPRI, 8..8=WPRI, 7..7=VSTIP, 6..6=WPRI, 5..5=WPRI, 4..4=WPRI, 3..3=VSSIP, 2..2=WPRI, 1..1=WPRI, 0..0=WPRI

RULE 1: hip has an access type of HRW.
RULE 2: If the Sstc extension is implemented, the STCE bit in menvcfg is zero, and the H extension is implemented, then hip.VSTIP reverts to the behavior defined for a system without the Sstc extension.
RULE 3: For each writable bit in sie, the corresponding bit shall be read-only zero in hip.
RULE 4: Nonzero bits in sip and hip are always mutually exclusive.
RULE 5: An interrupt i will trap to HS-mode whenever (a) either the current operating mode is HS-mode and the SIE bit in sstatus is set, or the current operating mode has less privilege than HS-mode, (b) bit i is set in both hip and hie (or in both sip and sie), and (c) bit i is not set in hideleg.
RULE 6: If bit i in hip is writable, a pending interrupt i can be cleared by writing 0 to this bit.
RULE 7: If an interrupt i can become pending and bit i of the hip CSR is read‑only, then after the interrupt becomes pending, writing a 0 to bit i of the hvip CSR must cause bit i of hip to read back as 0; if clearing hvip does not clear the pending bit, the implementation must provide some other architectural mechanism that, when exercised, results in bit i of hip reading back as 0.
RULE 8: hip.VSSIP is a writable alias of the same bit in hvip.
RULE 9: For each bit position where the corresponding bit in mideleg is zero, the same bit in hip MUST be read-only zero.
RULE 10: The SGEIP bit in the mip CSR is an alias of the SGEIP bit in the hip CSR.

REGISTER: hpmcounter3
NUMBER: 0xc03
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: hpmcounter3 is an unprivileged 64-bit hardware performance counter defined by the Zihpm extension, which adds up to 29 additional counters named hpmcounter3-hpmcounter31.
RULE 2: The hpmcounter3 CSR resides at address 0xC03 and is accessed with URO privilege.
RULE 3: The hpmcounter3 register is readable and writable in machine mode (MRW privilege).
RULE 4: If any field other than the one defined in the siselect = 0x43 entry is mapped to hpmcounter3, then a read of the hpmcounter3 CSR returns a value that does not correspond to that field (the CSR readback value differs from the field’s value).
RULE 5: If a CSR number other than the defined hpmcounter3 address is used in an indirect CSR instruction, then the instruction raises an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 6: Software can write an explicit value to mhpmcounter3.
RULE 7: The event-selector CSR mhpmevent3, which is a 64-bit WARL register, determines which events cause mhpmcounter3 to increment.
RULE 8: If an event‑code field (e.g., in a mhpmevent CSR) contains the value 0, the hardware treats it as “no event” and the associated performance counter does not increment for any activity (its value remains unchanged).
RULE 9: If mhpmevent3 is programmed to 0, mhpmcounter3 will not increment for any event.
RULE 10: If the HPM3 bit in the mcounteren register is clear and the processor is executing in S-mode or U-mode, any attempt to read the hpmcounter3 register causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: If the HPM3 bit in the mcounteren register is set, reads of the hpmcounter3 register are permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 12: The hpmcounter3 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter3 register, and its reads return the current value of mhpmcounter3.
RULE 13: Writing to the hpmcounter3 CSR is not permitted because it is read-only.
RULE 14: The value of mhpmcounter3, and therefore the value observed through hpmcounter3, continues to increment regardless of the HPM3 bit setting in the mcounteren register.
RULE 15: A read of the hpmcounter3 register does not affect the underlying mhpmcounter3 counter.
RULE 16: An attempted write to the hpmcounter3 register does not affect the underlying mhpmcounter3 counter.
RULE 17: The counter-inhibit register mcountinhibit does not affect the accessibility of hpmcounter3.
RULE 18: When the HPM3 bit in mcountinhibit is clear, hpmcounter3 increments as usual.
RULE 19: When the HPM3 bit in mcountinhibit is set, hpmcounter3 does not increment.
RULE 20: If the HPM3 bit in the scounteren CSR is clear, a U-mode read of hpmcounter3 MUST raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 21: If the HPM3 bit in the scounteren CSR is set, accesses to hpmcounter3 are permitted, subject to the additional requirement on the mcounteren CSR.
RULE 22: U-mode access to hpmcounter3 is allowed only when both the HPM3 bit in scounteren and the HPM3 bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 23: The scounteren CSR MUST be implemented, and any of its bits that are read-only zero cause reads to the associated counter, including hpmcounter3, to raise an illegal-instruction exception when executing in U-mode.
RULE 24: The MINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events in M-mode for hpmcounter3.
RULE 25: The SINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events in S/HS-mode for hpmcounter3.
RULE 26: The UINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events in U-mode for hpmcounter3.
RULE 27: When all INH bits (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent3 are zero, hpmcounter3 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 28: The OF bit in mhpmevent3 is set when hpmcounter3 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 29: Overflow of hpmcounter3 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 30: After hpmcounter3 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set, resulting in no loss of information.
RULE 31: If hpmcounter3 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 32: If the OF bit for hpmcounter3 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 33: The OF bit for hpmcounter3 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable.
RULE 34: If a write to mhpmcounter3 or mhpmevent3 would cause the counter to exceed its maximum value, then the hpmcounter3 overflow condition is not raised; overflow is observable only after a hardware increment that wraps the counter from its maximum to zero.
RULE 35: A count overflow interrupt request generated by hpmcounter3 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 36: The mip and sip LCOFIP bits are the interrupt-pending bits for the overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter3.
RULE 37: The mie and sie LCOFIE bits are the interrupt-enable bits for the overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter3.
RULE 38: When the OF bit for hpmcounter3 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 39: The mideleg register controls whether the overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter3 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 40: If the OF bit in the hpmcounter3 CSR is not cleared before writing the initial counter value, then overflow interrupt generation is disabled and no overflow interrupt is raised when the counter wraps.
RULE 41: After hpmcounter3 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 42: In M-mode, hpmcounter3 is always readable.
RULE 43: In S-mode (or HS-mode), hpmcounter3 is readable when mcounteren bit 3 is set, and otherwise reads as zero.
RULE 44: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter3 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc03; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 45: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc03; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 46: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc03; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 47: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter3 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc03, a0; csrr a1, 0xc03; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 48: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter3 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xc03; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 49: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter3 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc03; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 50: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter3 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc03; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter4
NUMBER: 0xc04
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: If software attempts to write CSR 0xC04 (hpmcounter4), then an illegal‑instruction exception is raised (mcause = 2) and the CSR retains its prior value; reading CSR 0xC04 in U‑mode returns the current counter value.
RULE 2: Software may write any value to mhpmcounter4, and the written value becomes the new contents of the register.
RULE 3: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter4 takes effect only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 4: The hpmcounter4 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter4 register.
RULE 5: When the HPM4 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the hpmcounter4 register while executing in S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: If the HPM4 bit in the mcountinhibit CSR is clear, hpmcounter4 increments as usual.
RULE 7: If the HPM4 bit in the mcountinhibit CSR is set, hpmcounter4 does not increment.
RULE 8: If the HPM 4 bit in scounteren is clear, any attempt by U-mode to read hpmcounter4 MUST cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: If the HPM 4 bit in scounteren is set, U-mode is permitted to access hpmcounter4.
RULE 10: U-mode MAY access hpmcounter4 only if both scounteren.HPM 4 and mcounteren.HPM 4 are set.
RULE 11: In the mhpmevent4 register, bit 63 (the OF field) is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when hpmcounter4 overflows.
RULE 12: In the mhpmevent4 register, bit 62 (the MINH field) inhibits counting of events in M-mode for hpmcounter4 when set.
RULE 13: In the mhpmevent4 register, bit 61 (the SINH field) inhibits counting of events in S/HS-mode for hpmcounter4 when set.
RULE 14: In the mhpmevent4 register, bit 60 (the UINH field) inhibits counting of events in U-mode for hpmcounter4 when set.
RULE 15: If a privilege mode corresponding to an INH bit in mhpmevent4 is not implemented, the INH bit reads as zero and is read-only for hpmcounter4.
RULE 16: When any INH bit (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent4 is set, hpmcounter4 does not count events while the processor is executing in the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 17: If all INH bits in mhpmevent4 are zero, hpmcounter4 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 18: Overflow of hpmcounter4 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 19: If hpmcounter4 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 20: If the OF bit of hpmcounter4 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated, and the OF bit also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for hpmcounter4.
RULE 21: Overflow of hpmcounter4 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter4 or mhpmevent4 registers, only from hardware increments.
RULE 22: The count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by hpmcounter4 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers, with the LCOFIP and LCOFIE bits serving as the pending and enable bits respectively.
RULE 23: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter4 sets its associated OF bit.
RULE 24: When the OF bit of hpmcounter4 is set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers, though not necessarily immediately.
RULE 25: The mideleg register controls whether the count-overflow-interrupt generated by hpmcounter4 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 26: Once hpmcounter4 has overflowed, it and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 27: Read access to hpmcounter4 in S-mode is granted only when the corresponding bit for counter 4 in the mcounteren CSR is set.
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter4 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc04; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc04; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 30: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc04; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 31: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter4 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc04, a0; csrr a1, 0xc04; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter4 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc04; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter5
NUMBER: 0xc05
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: H, Smcntrpmf, Smcsrind, Smstateen, Sscofpmf, Sscsrind, Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: Event 0 is defined to mean "no event," and if mhpmevent5 is programmed with 0, hpmcounter5 will not count any events.
RULE 2: After a hart reset, hpmcounter5 contains an arbitrary value and may be written with a given value, with any CSR write taking effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 3: mhpmevent5h exists only when the Sscofpmf extension is present, and it supplies the high-half of the 64-bit event selector for hpmcounter5.
RULE 4: When the HPM5 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, a read of the hpmcounter5 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 5: When the HPM5 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter5 CSR is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 6: The hpmcounter5 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter5 register.
RULE 7: The settings in the mcounteren register control only the accessibility of the hpmcounter5 CSR; reading or writing the hpmcounter5 CSR does not affect the underlying mhpmcounter5 counter, which continues to increment even when the hpmcounter5 CSR is not accessible.
RULE 8: The increment behavior of mhpmcounter5 is controlled by the HPM5 bit in the mcountinhibit register.
RULE 9: When the HPM5 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, mhpmcounter5 increments as usual.
RULE 10: When the HPM5 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, mhpmcounter5 does not increment.
RULE 11: The settings of the mcountinhibit register do not affect the accessibility of mhpmcounter5.
RULE 12: When the HPM5 bit in the scounteren register is clear, attempts to read the hpmcounter5 register while executing in U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: When the HPM5 bit in the scounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter5 register is permitted, subject to the condition on mcounteren described below.
RULE 14: U-mode may only access the hpmcounter5 register if both the HPM5 bit in the scounteren register and the HPM5 bit in the mcounteren register are set.
RULE 15: If the HPM5 bit in the scounteren register is read-only zero, reads of the hpmcounter5 register in U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 16: If the MINH bit in mhpmevent5 is set, counting of events in hpmcounter5 is inhibited while the processor is in M-mode.
RULE 17: If the SINH bit in mhpmevent5 is set, counting of events in hpmcounter5 is inhibited while the processor is in S/HS-mode.
RULE 18: If the UINH bit in mhpmevent5 is set, counting of events in hpmcounter5 is inhibited while the processor is in U-mode.
RULE 19: When all five INH bits in mhpmevent5 are zero, hpmcounter5 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 20: For any privilege mode that is not implemented, the corresponding INH bit in mhpmevent5 reads as zero, so it does not inhibit counting for hpmcounter5.
RULE 21: If a write or automatic increment causes hpmcounter5 to exceed the maximum value representable by its implemented bits, then the CSR readback value wraps modulo 2^N (where N is the number of implemented bits), i.e., the counter exhibits unsigned overflow.
RULE 22: If hpmcounter5 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 23: If hpmcounter5 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 24: hpmcounter5 can overflow only as a result of hardware increments; writes to mhpmcounter5 or mhpmevent5 never cause overflow.
RULE 25: The count-overflow interrupt request generated by hpmcounter5 is mapped to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 26: The LCOFIP bit in mip/sip is the interrupt-pending flag for the count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter5, and the LCOFIE bit in mie/sie is the corresponding interrupt-enable flag.
RULE 27: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by hpmcounter5 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent5.
RULE 28: When the OF bit for hpmcounter5 is set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in mip/sip, though not necessarily immediately.
RULE 29: The mideleg register determines whether the count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter5 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 30: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter5 is performed by clearing the OF bit together with initializing hpmcounter5 to a starting value.
RULE 31: After hpmcounter5 has overflowed, both hpmcounter5 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter5 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc05; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 33: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter5 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc05; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

RULE 35: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter5 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc05, a0; csrr a1, 0xc05; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: hpmcounter6
NUMBER: 0xc06
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: If a lower‑privileged mode reads hpmcounter6 while the corresponding enable bit in the appropriate privileged CSR (hcounteren for HS mode, scounteren for S mode, or mcounteren for U mode) is clear, then the read returns zero.

RULE 3: The event selector CSR mhpmevent6 is a 64-bit WARL register that controls which event causes mhpmcounter6 to increment.
RULE 4: The accessibility of hpmcounter6 is not affected by the settings in the mcountinhibit register.
RULE 5: The HPM 6 bit in mcountinhibit determines whether hpmcounter6 increments.
RULE 6: When the HPM 6 bit in mcountinhibit is clear (0), hpmcounter6 increments as usual.
RULE 7: When the HPM 6 bit in mcountinhibit is set (1), hpmcounter6 does not increment.
RULE 8: When the HPM6 bit in scounteren is clear, any attempt to read hpmcounter6 while executing in U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.

RULE 26: Read access to hpmcounter6 is governed by the same mcounteren CSR (or the combination of mcounteren and hcounteren CSRs) that governs access to the hpmcounter CSRs for the corresponding privilege mode.
RULE 27: In S-mode (or HS-mode), a read of hpmcounter6 is permitted only when mcounteren bit 6 is set; otherwise the read is not permitted.
