RULE 1: The architectural privilege of hpmcounter8 is URO (User-mode Read-Only).
RULE 2: mhpmevent8 controls which event causes mhpmcounter8 to increment.
RULE 3: Event 0, which may be programmed into mhpmevent8, is defined to mean no event for mhpmcounter8.
RULE 4: A CSR write to mhpmcounter8 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 5: If the HPM8 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the hpmcounter8 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: If the HPM8 bit in the mcounteren register is set, reads of the hpmcounter8 CSR are permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 7: If the HPM8 field of the mcounteren register is read-only zero, any read of the hpmcounter8 CSR in a less-privileged mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 8: The hpmcounter8 register's increment behavior is controlled by the HPM 8 bit in the mcountinhibit register, while its accessibility is not affected.
RULE 9: When the HPM 8 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the hpmcounter8 register increments as usual.
RULE 10: When the HPM 8 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the hpmcounter8 register does not increment.
RULE 11: If the HPM8 bit in scounteren is clear, a read of the hpmcounter8 register while executing in U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: If the HPM8 bit in scounteren is set, a read of the hpmcounter8 register while executing in U-mode is permitted (subject to other conditions).
RULE 13: Because scounteren must be implemented, the HPM8 bit may be read-only zero, and in that case a read of the hpmcounter8 register in U-mode will cause an exception.
RULE 14: A U-mode read of the hpmcounter8 register is allowed only when both the HPM8 bit in scounteren and the HPM8 bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 15: The OF bit in mhpmevent8 is set when hpmcounter8 overflows.
RULE 16: hpmcounter8 values are unsigned, and overflow is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 17: If hpmcounter8 overflows while the associated OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 18: If the OF bit associated with hpmcounter8 is one, no interrupt request is generated.
RULE 19: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter8 sets the associated OF bit.
RULE 20: If the OF bit of hpmcounter8 is set, then at some later point (not necessarily immediately) the LCOFIP bit in the mip (in M‑mode) or sip (in S‑mode) register must become 1.
RULE 21: The mip/sip LCOFIP and mie/sie LCOFIE bits are, respectively, the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits for the count overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter8.
RULE 22: The mideleg register controls delegation of the count overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter8 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 23: If the OF bit in the hpmcounter8 control CSR is cleared, then when hpmcounter8 wraps it raises an overflow interrupt (mcause is set to the overflow‑interrupt exception code); if the OF bit is not cleared, the wrap does not generate an interrupt.
RULE 24: Once hpmcounter8 has overflowed, hpmcounter8 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 25: All-zeroes for the INH bits in mhpmevent8 result in counting of events for hpmcounter8 in all privilege modes.
RULE 26: In S-mode, reads of hpmcounter8 return the counter value when mcounteren bit 8 is set, otherwise the read returns zero.
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter8 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc08; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 28: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter8 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc08; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 29: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter8 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc08; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 30: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter8 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc08, a0; csrr a1, 0xc08; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter8 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc08; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter8 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc08; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter9
NUMBER: 0xc09
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Smcsrind, Sscsrind, Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: hpmcounter9 has privilege URO.
RULE 2: hpmcounter9 is readable at the unprivileged level.
RULE 3: hpmcounter9 is not writable.
RULE 4: If mhpmcounter9 is read after a hart reset without a prior write, then the readback value is arbitrary (implementation‑dependent); if a value is written to mhpmcounter9, then a subsequent read returns that written value and no exception is raised.
RULE 5: A write to mhpmcounter9 takes effect only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 6: A legal implementation may implement mhpmcounter9 as a read-only zero register.
RULE 7: When the HPM9 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the hpmcounter9 register while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 8: When the HPM9 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter9 register is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 9: The hpmcounter9 CSR is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter9.
RULE 10: The settings in the mcounteren register only control accessibility of hpmcounter9 and do not affect the underlying counter value, which continues to increment even when not accessible.
RULE 11: The mhpmcounter9 register increments when the HPM9 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear.
RULE 12: The mhpmcounter9 register does not increment when the HPM9 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set.
RULE 13: The accessibility of the mhpmcounter9 register is independent of the setting of the mcountinhibit register.
RULE 14: If the HPM9 bit in the scounteren register is clear, any attempt to read the hpmcounter9 register while executing in U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: If the HPM9 bit in the scounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter9 register is permitted.
RULE 16: U-mode may only access the hpmcounter9 register when both the HPM9 bit in the scounteren register and the HPM9 bit in the mcounteren register are set.
RULE 17: If the HPM9 bit in the scounteren register is read-only zero, reads of the hpmcounter9 register in U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 18: The OF bit in mhpmevent9 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for hpmcounter9.
RULE 19: If hpmcounter9 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 20: If hpmcounter9 overflows while its OF bit is one, no interrupt request is generated.
RULE 21: If a write to or increment of hpmcounter9 produces a value larger than the maximum representable by the implemented counter bits, then the CSR readback contains the result modulo 2^(implemented‑bit‑width), i.e., the counter wraps on unsigned overflow.
RULE 22: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter9 sets the associated OF bit.
RULE 23: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter9 eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers, though not necessarily immediately.
RULE 24: The mideleg register controls whether the overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter9 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 25: For each privilege mode x INH bit in mhpmevent9, setting the INH bit inhibits counting of events for hpmcounter9 while executing in privilege mode x.
RULE 26: If all five x INH bits in mhpmevent9 are zero, hpmcounter9 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 27: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter9 is done by clearing its OF bit together with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 28: After hpmcounter9 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 29: The readability of the overflow flag for hpmcounter9 follows the same mcounteren (and, where applicable, hcounteren) access controls that govern read access to the hpmcounter9 register itself.
RULE 30: If a read of the overflow flag for hpmcounter9 in M‑mode raises an illegal‑instruction (or any other) exception, then the overflow flag is not always readable, violating the rule.
RULE 31: In S-mode (or HS-mode), the overflow flag for hpmcounter9 is readable only when mcounteren bit 9 is set, and reads as zero otherwise.
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter9 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc09; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 33: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter9 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc09; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 34: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter9 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc09; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 35: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter9 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc09, a0; csrr a1, 0xc09; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter9 register while Smcsrind extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcsrind; csrr a0, 0xc09; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 37: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter9 register while Sscsrind extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscsrind; csrr a0, 0xc09; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 38: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter9 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc09; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 39: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter9 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc09; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter10
NUMBER: 0xc0a
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: hpmcounter10 is a URO (unprivileged read-only) CSR.
RULE 2: The mhpmcounter10 CSR appears in the Machine Counter/Timers table, has machine read/write (MRW) privilege, and provides a machine performance-monitoring counter.
RULE 3: The mhpmevent10 CSR appears in the Machine Counter Setup table, has machine read/write (MRW) privilege, and selects the event counted by mhpmcounter10.
RULE 4: If no software write to hpmcounter10 has occurred since the hart reset, then reading the hpmcounter10 CSR returns an implementation‑defined (arbitrary) value.
RULE 5: Any write to the hpmcounter10 CSR takes effect only after the executing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 6: The 64-bit WARL event selector CSR mhpmevent10 determines which events cause hpmcounter10 to increment.
RULE 7: If the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, then any read or write of the mhpmevent10h CSR raises an illegal‑instruction exception; if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, then writing mhpmevent10h selects the high‑half of hpmcounter10, and a subsequent read of hpmcounter10 reflects that high‑half selection.
RULE 8: hpmcounter10 is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter10.
RULE 9: If the HPM10 bit in mcounteren is clear, a read of hpmcounter10 while executing in S-mode or U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: If the HPM10 bit in mcounteren is set, access to hpmcounter10 is permitted in the next implemented lower-privilege mode (S-mode if the implementation provides S-mode, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 11: If the HPM10 bit in scounteren is clear while executing in U-mode, an attempt to read hpmcounter10 causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: If the HPM10 bit in scounteren is set while executing in U-mode, access to hpmcounter10 is permitted and no illegal-instruction exception occurs.
RULE 13: If the HPM10 bit in scounteren is a read-only zero, reads of hpmcounter10 in U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: U-mode may access hpmcounter10 only when both the HPM10 bit in scounteren and the HPM10 bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 15: The writability of the HPM10 bit in scounteren, which determines hpmcounter10 access, is not affected by the setting of the HPM10 bit in mcounteren.
RULE 16: In the mhpmevent register that corresponds to hpmcounter10, bit 63 named OF is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when the counter overflows.
RULE 17: In the mhpmevent register for hpmcounter10, bit 62 named MINH inhibits counting of events in M-mode when set.
RULE 18: In the mhpmevent register for hpmcounter10, bit 61 named SINH inhibits counting of events in S/HS-mode when set.
RULE 19: For each x INH bit in the mhpmevent register for hpmcounter10, if the associated privilege mode x is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 20: For hpmcounter10, each x INH bit, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in privilege mode x.
RULE 21: For hpmcounter10, when all five INH bits are zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 22: The OF bit for hpmcounter10 is set when the corresponding counter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 23: If hpmcounter10 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated; if the OF bit is one, no interrupt request is generated.
RULE 24: The count-overflow-interrupt request generated by hpmcounter10 is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 25: The mip and sip LCOFIP bits are the interrupt-pending bits for the count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter10, and the mie and sie LCOFIE bits are the interrupt-enable bits for that interrupt.
RULE 26: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter10 sets the associated OF bit.
RULE 27: When the OF bit for hpmcounter10 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 28: The mideleg register controls the delegation of the count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter10 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 29: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter10 is done by clearing the OF bit in conjunction with initializing the counter to a starting value, because there are not separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits.
RULE 30: Once hpmcounter10 has overflowed, it and its OF bit MUST be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 31: The read visibility of the overflow flag of hpmcounter10 follows the same mcounteren (or mcounteren and hcounteren) access rules that apply to the hpmcounter10 CSR itself.
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter10 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc0a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 33: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter10 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc0a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 34: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter10 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc0a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 35: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter10 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc0a, a0; csrr a1, 0xc0a; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter10 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xc0a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 37: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter10 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc0a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 38: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter10 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc0a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter11
NUMBER: 0xc0b
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: hpmcounter11 has privilege URO (unprivileged read-only).
RULE 2: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter11 contains an arbitrary value and may be written with any given value.
RULE 3: A write to the mhpmcounter11 CSR takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 4: The mhpmevent11 CSR selects the event that causes mhpmcounter11 to increment.
RULE 5: Writing the value 0 to mhpmevent11 defines "no event" for mhpmcounter11.
RULE 6: If the HPM 11 bit in mcounteren is clear, attempts to read hpmcounter11 while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 7: If the HPM 11 bit in mcounteren is set, access to hpmcounter11 is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 8: hpmcounter11 is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter11.
RULE 9: The setting of the mcountinhibit CSR does not affect the accessibility of hpmcounter11.
RULE 10: If the HPM 11 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, hpmcounter11 increments as usual.
RULE 11: If the HPM 11 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, hpmcounter11 does not increment.
RULE 12: If the HPM 11 bit in the scounteren register is clear, a read of the hpmcounter11 register while executing in U-mode MUST cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: If the HPM 11 bit in the scounteren register is implemented as a read-only zero, a read of the hpmcounter11 register in U-mode MUST cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: The OF bit in mhpmevent11 is set when hpmcounter11 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 15: If the unsigned value of hpmcounter11 exceeds the maximum representable by its implemented counter width and wraps, then a read of hpmcounter11 returns the wrapped value (i.e., the value modulo 2^implemented‑width).
RULE 16: If hpmcounter11 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request for hpmcounter11 is generated.
RULE 17: If hpmcounter11 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request for hpmcounter11 is generated.
RULE 18: When the OF bit associated with hpmcounter11 is one, count-overflow-interrupt requests for hpmcounter11 are disabled.
RULE 19: Writes to mhpmcounter11 or mhpmevent11 never cause overflow of hpmcounter11; overflow arises only from hardware increments of hpmcounter11.
RULE 20: When a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated for hpmcounter11, the OF bit in mhpmevent11 is set.
RULE 21: When the OF bit for hpmcounter11 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 22: When an INH bit in mhpmevent11 for hpmcounter11 is set for the current privilege mode, hpmcounter11 does not count events while executing in that mode.
RULE 23: If all INH bits in mhpmevent11 for hpmcounter11 are zero, hpmcounter11 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 24: Once hpmcounter11 has overflowed and its OF bit is set, software must write a new value to hpmcounter11 and clear the OF bit before another overflow interrupt for hpmcounter11 can be generated.
RULE 25: In S-mode or HS-mode, a read of hpmcounter11 is permitted only when the mcounteren bit 11 is set to 1; if mcounteren[11] is 0, the read is not permitted and the value returned is unspecified.
RULE 26: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter11 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc0b; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 27: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter11 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc0b; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 28: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter11 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc0b; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 29: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter11 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc0b, a0; csrr a1, 0xc0b; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter11 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc0b; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter11 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc0b; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter12
NUMBER: 0xc0c
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: hpmcounter12 is an unprivileged CSR that has privilege level URO, meaning it is read-only.
RULE 2: The mhpmcounter12 CSR has Machine Read/Write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 3: The event selector register mhpmevent12 determines which events cause mhpmcounter12 to increment.
RULE 4: A CSR write to mhpmcounter12 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 5: When the HPM12 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the hpmcounter12 register while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: When the HPM12 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter12 register is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 7: The hpmcounter12 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter12 register.
RULE 8: If the HPM12 bit in scounteren is clear, a read of hpmcounter12 while executing in U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: If the HPM12 bit in scounteren is set, accesses to hpmcounter12 while executing in U-mode are permitted.
RULE 10: U-mode may only access hpmcounter12 when both the HPM12 bit in scounteren and the HPM12 bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 11: If the HPM12 bit in scounteren is read-only zero, a read of hpmcounter12 while executing in U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: The OF bit in mhpmevent12 is set when the corresponding hpmcounter12 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 13: Overflow for hpmcounter12 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 14: If a write to mhpmcounter12 or mhpmevent12 attempts to set the counter beyond its maximum, then the overflow condition is not raised—the register holds the written value and any overflow flag remains clear; overflow can only be observed after a hardware increment that wraps the counter.
RULE 15: If hpmcounter12 overflows while its associated OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 16: If the OF bit associated with hpmcounter12 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 17: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter12 sets its associated OF bit.
RULE 18: When the OF bit associated with hpmcounter12 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 19: The count-overflow-interrupt request generated by hpmcounter12 is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 20: The LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers is the interrupt-pending bit for a count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter12.
RULE 21: The mideleg register controls delegation of the count-overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter12 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 22: When all x INH bits in mhpmevent12 for hpmcounter12 are zero, hpmcounter12 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 23: Read access to hpmcounter12 is controlled by mcounteren bit 12.
RULE 24: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter12 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc0c; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 25: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter12 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc0c; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 26: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter12 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc0c; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 27: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter12 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc0c, a0; csrr a1, 0xc0c; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter12 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xc0c; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter12 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc0c; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter12 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc0c; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hpmcounter13
NUMBER: 0xc0d
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: If the implementation does not implement the Zihpm extension, then executing any CSR access (e.g., csrrs x0, hpmcounter13, x0) to the hpmcounter13 register raises an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 2: If the implementation includes hpmcounter13, then a CSR read of hpmcounter13 returns a 64‑bit value (on RV64) or a zero‑extended 64‑bit value (on RV32); writes to the CSR have no effect.
RULE 3: If a lower‑privileged mode (U‑mode or S‑mode) executes an instruction that reads or writes hpmcounter13, then an illegal‑instruction exception is raised and mcause is set to the illegal‑instruction cause.
RULE 4: The hpmcounter13 CSR has MRW (machine-mode read/write) privilege.
RULE 5: The mcounteren CSR controls whether hpmcounter13 is readable in lower privilege modes.
RULE 6: The mcountinhibit CSR can inhibit counting for hpmcounter13.
RULE 7: The counter mhpmcounter13 is incremented according to the value programmed in the corresponding event-selector CSR mhpmevent13.
RULE 8: The event-selector CSR mhpmevent13 is a 64-bit WARL register that controls which event causes mhpmcounter13 to increment.
RULE 9: Event value 0 in mhpmevent13 is defined to mean "no event".
RULE 10: Software can write a given value to mhpmcounter13.
RULE 11: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter13 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 12: The hpmcounter13 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter13 register.
RULE 13: If the HPM13 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read hpmcounter13 while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: If the HPM13 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to hpmcounter13 is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 15: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the underlying hpmcounter13 counter, which continues to increment even when not accessible.
RULE 16: In harts with U-mode, the mcounteren register must be implemented and its field for hpmcounter13 is WARL and may be read-only zero, indicating that reads to hpmcounter13 will cause an illegal-instruction exception when executing in a less-privileged mode.
RULE 17: When the HPM13 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter13 register increments as usual.
RULE 18: When the HPM13 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter13 register does not increment.
RULE 19: If the HPM13 bit in the scounteren register is clear, a read of the hpmcounter13 register while executing in U-mode MUST cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 20: If the HPM13 bit in the scounteren register is set, access to the hpmcounter13 register is permitted.
RULE 21: U-mode MAY only access the hpmcounter13 register when the HPM13 bit in both the scounteren register and the mcounteren register are set.
RULE 22: Any bit in scounteren, including the HPM13 bit that controls the hpmcounter13 register, MAY be read-only zero, and a zero value causes reads of the hpmcounter13 register in U-mode to raise an illegal-instruction exception, making that bit a WARL field.
RULE 23: The OF bit in the mhpmevent13 register is set when hpmcounter13 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 24: If hpmcounter13 overflows while its associated OF bit is one, no interrupt request is generated.
RULE 25: The mip and sip LCOFIP bits at position 13 are the interrupt-pending bits for the overflow interrupt of hpmcounter13, and the mie and sie LCOFIE bits at position 13 are the interrupt-enable bits for that interrupt.
RULE 26: Count overflow for hpmcounter13 never results from writes to the mhpmcounter13 or mhpmevent13 registers, only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 27: If any INH bit (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent13 for hpmcounter13 is set, counting of events in the corresponding privilege mode is inhibited for hpmcounter13.
RULE 28: If all INH bits in mhpmevent13 for hpmcounter13 are zero, counting of events in all privilege modes is performed for hpmcounter13.
RULE 29: When the OF bit for hpmcounter13 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit at position 13 in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 30: The mideleg register controls the delegation of the overflow interrupt generated by hpmcounter13 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 31: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for hpmcounter13 is done by clearing its OF bit in conjunction with initializing hpmcounter13 to a starting value.
RULE 32: After hpmcounter13 has overflowed, both hpmcounter13 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 33: In M-mode, hpmcounter13 is always readable.
RULE 34: In S-mode and HS-mode, hpmcounter13 reads as zero when mcounteren bit 13 is clear and reads its actual value when mcounteren bit 13 is set.
RULE 35: The HPM13 bit in the hcounteren register is a WARL field that determines the behavior of reads to the hpmcounter13 register.
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter13 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc0d; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 37: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter13 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc0d; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 38: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter13 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc0d; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 39: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter13 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc0d, a0; csrr a1, 0xc0d; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: hpmcounter18
NUMBER: 0xc12
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zicsr, Zihpm
RULE 1: hpmcounter18 has privilege level URO (unprivileged read-only).
RULE 2: The privilege of hpmcounter18 is Machine-mode Read/Write (MRW).
RULE 3: hpmcounter18 is a machine-mode CSR that can be read and written by software executing in M-mode.
RULE 4: mhpmcounter18 is a WARL (Write-Any-Legal-Value) register.
RULE 5: If a hart is reset, then a read of mhpmcounter18 returns an implementation‑defined value (the CSR readback is not guaranteed to be zero).
RULE 6: The register mhpmcounter18 may be written with any given value.
RULE 7: Any write to the mhpmcounter18 CSR takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 8: The event selector CSR mhpmevent18, a 64-bit WARL register, controls which event causes mhpmcounter18 to increment.
RULE 9: If an implementation makes mhpmevent18 read‑only zero, then any write to mhpmevent18 leaves the CSR value at 0, reads of mhpmevent18 return 0, and the associated mhpmcounter18 never increments (its value remains zero).
RULE 10: The high-half CSR mhpmevent18h is provided only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, while the existence of mhpmcounter18h is not conditioned on this extension.
RULE 11: If the HPM 18 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, any attempt to read the hpmcounter18 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: The hpmcounter18 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter18 CSR.
RULE 13: If the HPM 18 field of the mcounteren register is a WARL field that is read-only zero, reads of the hpmcounter18 CSR from S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: The accessibility of hpmcounter18 is not affected by the setting of the mcountinhibit register.
RULE 15: When the HPM 18 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, hpmcounter18 increments as usual.
RULE 16: When the HPM 18 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, hpmcounter18 does not increment.
RULE 17: If the HPM18 bit in the scounteren CSR is clear, a read of hpmcounter18 while executing in U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 18: If the HPM18 bit in the scounteren CSR is set, accesses to hpmcounter18 are permitted.
RULE 19: U-mode may access hpmcounter18 only when both the HPM18 bit in scounteren CSR and the HPM18 bit in mcounteren CSR are set.
RULE 20: If the HPM18 bit in scounteren CSR is read-only zero, a read of hpmcounter18 in U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 21: If a privilege mode associated with an x INH bit in mhpmevent18 for hpmcounter18 is not implemented, that x INH bit reads as zero and is read-only.
RULE 22: When any x INH bit in mhpmevent18 for hpmcounter18 is set, event counting for hpmcounter18 is inhibited while the processor is in privilege mode x.
RULE 23: When all x INH bits in mhpmevent18 for hpmcounter18 are zero, hpmcounter18 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 24: The OF bit in mhpmevent18 for hpmcounter18 is set automatically when hpmcounter18 overflows and remains set until software writes to clear it.
RULE 25: Overflow of hpmcounter18 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 26: If hpmcounter18 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 27: If the OF bit for hpmcounter18 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 28: Writes to mhpmcounter18 or mhpmevent18 cannot cause overflow of hpmcounter18; overflow occurs only from hardware increments.
RULE 29: A count overflow interrupt request generated by hpmcounter18 corresponds to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 30: The LCOFIP bits in mip/sip and the LCOFIE bits in mie/sie serve as the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits, respectively, for the overflow interrupt of hpmcounter18.
RULE 31: When a count overflow interrupt request is generated by hpmcounter18, its OF bit is set.
RULE 32: When the OF bit for hpmcounter18 is set, it eventually causes the LCOFIP bit in mip/sip to be set.
RULE 33: The mideleg register determines whether the overflow interrupt of hpmcounter18 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 34: In M-mode, the overflow flag for hpmcounter18 is always readable.
RULE 35: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter18 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc12; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 36: In S-mode, accessing hpmcounter18 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc12; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 37: In U-mode, accessing hpmcounter18 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc12; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 38: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the hpmcounter18 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc12, a0; csrr a1, 0xc12; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 39: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter18 register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc12; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 40: In M-mode, accessing hpmcounter18 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xc12; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: hstatus
NUMBER: 0x600
MODE: HS-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 33..32=VSXL, 24..24=HUKTE, 22..22=VTSR, 21..21=VTW, 20..20=VTVM, 17..12=VGEIN, 9..9=HU, 8..8=SPVP, 7..7=SPV, 6..6=GVA, 5..5=VSBE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The hstatus register has HRW privilege, allowing it to be read and written in hypervisor mode.
RULE 2: When hstatus.VTVM = 1, SFENCE.W.INVAL and SFENCE.INVAL.IR instructions need not be trapped.
RULE 3: The hstatus CSR is provided to HS-mode.
RULE 4: When HSXLEN = 64 the VSXL field in hstatus is a WARL field encoded identically to the MXL field of misa.
RULE 5: The VGEIN field in hstatus is a WLRL field that must be able to hold values from zero up to the maximum guest external interrupt number (GEILEN), inclusive.
RULE 6: When the HU bit in hstatus is 1, HLV, HLVX, and HSV can be executed in U-mode the same as in HS-mode.
RULE 7: When the HU bit in hstatus is 0, all hypervisor instructions cause an illegal-instruction exception in U-mode.
RULE 8: When the Ssnpm extension is not implemented, the HUPMM field in hstatus is read-only zero.
RULE 9: The SPV bit in hstatus is written by the implementation whenever a trap is taken into HS-mode.
RULE 10: If V = 0 before a trap, the SPVP bit in hstatus is left unchanged on trap entry.
RULE 11: The GVA field in hstatus is written by the implementation whenever a trap is taken into HS-mode.
RULE 12: For any other trap into HS-mode, the GVA field in hstatus is set to 0.
RULE 13: For breakpoint and memory-access traps that write a nonzero value to stval, the GVA field in hstatus is redundant with the SPV bit (both are set the same) except when the explicit memory access of an HLV, HLVX, or HSV instruction causes a fault; in that case SPV = 0 but GVA = 1.
RULE 14: If software attempts to write to hip.VSEIP, the write is ignored (the bit is read‑only) and reading hip.VSEIP returns the logical OR of its three source bits, including the hgeip bit selected by hstatus.VGEIN (i.e., hip.VSEIP is 1 if any source is 1, otherwise 0).
RULE 15: The value of hstatus.VGEIN determines which bit of the hgeip register is included in the logical-OR that defines the read-only hip.VSEIP bit.
RULE 16: Hypervisor virtual-machine load and store instructions are valid only when the current privilege mode is M-mode or HS-mode, or when the current privilege mode is U-mode and the hstatus.HU field equals 1.
RULE 17: When executing a hypervisor virtual-machine load or store instruction from U-mode while the hstatus.HU field is 0, an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 18: Executing an HFENCE.VVMA instruction must not trap because of the hstatus.VTVM field.
RULE 19: The effect of the MPRV bit does not apply to the virtual-machine load/store instructions HLV, HLVX, and HSV, which instead use the hstatus.SPVP field to determine the nominal privilege mode.
RULE 20: For the virtual-machine load/store instructions HLV, HLVX, and HSV, explicit loads and stores always use the nominal privilege mode specified by the hstatus.SPVP field, overriding any effect of MPRV.
RULE 21: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the virtualization mode V field in hstatus is set to 0.
RULE 22: When a trap is taken into HS-mode and the previous privilege mode was U-mode, the SPV field in hstatus is set to 0.
RULE 23: When a trap is taken into HS-mode and the previous privilege mode was HS-mode, the SPV field in hstatus is set to 0.
RULE 24: If the virtualization mode V field in hstatus was 0 before a trap into HS-mode, the SPVP field in hstatus is left unchanged.
RULE 25: When SRET is executed in M-mode or HS-mode (V = 0), the new privilege mode is determined based on the values of hstatus.SPV and sstatus.SPP.
RULE 26: After the privilege-mode determination performed by SRET, the instruction sets hstatus.SPV to 0.

NUMBER: 0x645

FIELDS: 63..16=WPRI, 15..14=WPRI, 13..13=LCOFI, 12..10=WPRI, 9..9=VSEIP, 8..6=WPRI, 5..5=VSTIP, 4..2=WPRI, 1..1=VSSIP, 0..0=WPRI
EXTENSIONS: H, Smaia, Smcdeleg, Ssaia, Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, Sstc
RULE 1: The hvip register has HRW access, meaning it is both readable and writable.
RULE 2: If an implementation supports Smcdeleg or Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, Smaia or Ssaia, and the H extension, then the LCOFI bit (bit 13) in hvip is implemented and writable.
RULE 3: The standard portion of hvip, bits 15:0, contains the VSEIP, VSTIP, and VSSIP bits, and these bits are writable.
RULE 4: The VSEIP bit of hvip is one of the inputs to the logical-OR that defines the read-only VSEIP field in hip.
RULE 5: The VSTIP bit of hvip is one of the inputs to the logical-OR that defines the read-only VSTIP field in hip.
RULE 6: The VSSIP bit in hip is an alias of the VSSIP bit in hvip, so writes to hvip.VSSIP are reflected in hip.VSSIP.

REGISTER: instret
NUMBER: 0xc02
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Smcdeleg, Smcntrpmf, Smcsrind, Smstateen, Ssccfg, Sscsrind, Zicntr, Zicsr
RULE 1: If an instruction retires, then the value read from the instret CSR after the instruction is greater than the value read before it.
RULE 2: When a CSR access instruction reads instret, it obtains the value that existed prior to the execution of that instruction.
RULE 3: When a CSR access instruction writes instret, the explicit write is performed instead of any side-effect update to instret.
RULE 4: The INSTRET CSR is a 64-bit read-only register that counts the number of instructions retired by this hart from an arbitrary start point in the past.
RULE 5: For base ISAs with XLEN ≥ 64, the RDINSTRET pseudoinstruction reads the full 64 bits of the INSTRET counter.
RULE 6: The CSRRC, CSRRSI, and CSRRCI read-only instruction forms are also legal ways to read the INSTRET CSR.
RULE 7: Any read-only CSR instruction may be used to read the INSTRET CSR without modifying it.
RULE 8: Instructions that cause synchronous exceptions, including ECALL and EBREAK, are not considered to retire and therefore do not increment the INSTRET CSR.
RULE 9: The instret CSR is designated with privilege URO (user-read-only).
RULE 10: The instret CSR counts the number of instructions retired and provides the value returned by the RDINSTRET instruction.
RULE 11: The instreth CSR, which supplies the upper 32 bits of instret, is designated with privilege URO.
RULE 12: The machine instructions-retired counter register minstret is located at address 0xB02 and has machine-mode read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 13: The machine instret counter configuration register minstretcfg resides at address 0x322 and is accessible with machine-mode read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 14: If any of the CY, TM, IR, or any HPM n bits in the mcounteren register is clear, a read of the instret CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: When the IR bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the instret CSR is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if it is implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 16: The instret CSR is a read-only shadow of the minstret CSR.
RULE 17: The settings in the mcounteren register control only the accessibility of the instret CSR and do not affect the underlying minstret counter, which continues to increment even when the CSR is not accessible.
RULE 18: In harts that implement U-mode, the IR field of mcounteren is WARL and may be read-only zero, indicating that a read of the instret CSR in a less-privileged mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 19: The settings of the mcountinhibit register control whether the minstret register increments but do not affect the accessibility of the minstret register.
RULE 20: If the IR bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the minstret register increments as usual.
RULE 21: If the IR bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the minstret register does not increment.
RULE 22: If any of the CY, IR, or HPM n bits in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the minstret register increments as usual.
RULE 23: If any of the CY, IR, or HPM n bits in the mcountinhibit register is set, the minstret register does not increment.
RULE 24: By default, the instret counter is not filtered by privilege mode.
RULE 25: If the SINH bit in minstretcfg is set, counting of events in S/HS-mode is inhibited for the instret counters.
RULE 26: If the UINH bit in minstretcfg is set, counting of events in U-mode is inhibited for the instret counters.
RULE 27: When all INH bits (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in minstretcfg are zero, event counting is enabled in all privilege modes for the instret counters.
RULE 28: Counting does not occur for instret while executing in an inhibited privilege mode.
RULE 29: Instructions that retire in a non-inhibited mode increment instret.
RULE 30: Instructions that retire in an inhibited mode do not increment instret.
RULE 31: Instructions that cause synchronous exceptions to a more privileged mode are not considered to retire and therefore do not increment instret.
RULE 32: xRET instructions retire and should increment instret only if the originating privilege mode is not inhibited.
RULE 33: In that scenario the faulting execution of the load will not increment instret because it does not retire.
RULE 34: If an instruction (including xRET) executes while the processor is in inhibited mode, then the `instret` CSR readback value remains unchanged after the instruction.
RULE 35: Only when the load is re-executed and retires will it increment instret.
RULE 36: If the IR bit in scounteren is clear, a read of instret while executing in U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 37: If the IR bit in scounteren is set, a read of instret while executing in U-mode is permitted.
RULE 38: A U-mode read of instret is permitted only when both the IR bit in scounteren and the IR bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 39: If either the IR bit in scounteren or the IR bit in mcounteren is clear, a U-mode read of instret must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 40: In M-mode, accessing instret register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 41: In S-mode, accessing instret register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 42: In U-mode, accessing instret register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 43: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the instret register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc02, a0; csrr a1, 0xc02; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 44: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Smcdeleg extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcdeleg; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 45: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Smcntrpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcntrpmf; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 46: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Smcsrind extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcsrind; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 47: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Smstateen extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smstateen; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 48: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Ssccfg extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssccfg; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 49: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Sscsrind extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscsrind; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 50: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Zicntr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicntr; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 51: In M-mode, accessing instret register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0xc02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: marchid
NUMBER: 0xf12
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=Architecture
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: marchid is a machine-level read-only (MRO) CSR.
RULE 2: marchid is an MXLEN-bit read-only CSR that encodes the base microarchitecture of the hart.
RULE 3: marchid must be readable in any implementation.
RULE 4: Open-source architecture IDs that may be placed in marchid are allocated globally by RISC-V International, are non-zero, and have a zero most-significant-bit.
RULE 5: Commercial architecture IDs that may be placed in marchid are allocated by each commercial vendor independently, must have the most-significant-bit set, and cannot contain zero in the remaining MXLEN-1 bits.
RULE 6: If the most‑significant bit of the value read from the marchid CSR for a commercial implementation is 0, then the commercial architecture ID is not disjoint from open‑source IDs, indicating a collision risk.
RULE 7: In M-mode, accessing marchid register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xf12; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 8: In S-mode, accessing marchid register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xf12; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 9: In U-mode, accessing marchid register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xf12; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 10: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the marchid register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xf12, a0; csrr a1, 0xf12; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: mcause
NUMBER: 0x342
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..63=INT, 62..0=CODE
EXTENSIONS: H, Smdbltrp, Smrnmi, Sscofpmf, Ssdbltrp, Zicfilp
RULE 1: The mcause CSR has machine-mode read/write privilege (MRW).
RULE 2: When a double-trap occurs and either the Smrnmi extension is not implemented or the Smrnmi extension is implemented with mnstatus.NMIE equal to 0, the mcause register is not updated as part of the architectural state.
RULE 3: When a trap is delegated to S-mode, the mcause register is not written.
RULE 4: If an exception occurs and the mcause register contains value N, then bit N of the medeleg CSR determines the handling privilege: a 1 causes the exception to be delegated to the next lower privilege level, while a 0 causes the exception to be handled in machine mode.
RULE 5: If the bit in medeleg that corresponds to the value returned in the mcause register is set, a trap occurring in S-mode or U-mode is delegated to the S-mode trap handler.
RULE 6: The interrupt cause number i reported in the mcause CSR corresponds to bit i in the mip CSR.
RULE 7: The interrupt cause number i reported in the mcause CSR corresponds to bit i in the mie CSR.
RULE 8: mcause is an MXLEN-bit read-write register.
RULE 9: When a trap is taken into M-mode, mcause is written with a code indicating the event that caused the trap.
RULE 10: When a trap is not taken into M-mode, the implementation never writes mcause, although software may write it explicitly.
RULE 11: The Interrupt bit in mcause is set if the trap was caused by an interrupt.
RULE 12: The Exception Code field in mcause contains a code identifying the last exception or interrupt.
RULE 13: Load and load-reserved instructions generate load exceptions whose exception codes (such as 4-7, 13, 15, etc.) are recorded in mcause.
RULE 14: Store, store-conditional, and AMO instructions generate store/AMO exceptions whose exception codes (such as 6, 7, 15, etc.) are recorded in mcause.
RULE 15: If an instruction may raise multiple synchronous exceptions, the decreasing priority order defined in Table 17 determines which exception is taken and reported in mcause.
RULE 16: When virtual address translation determines a specific exception, the exception chosen according to Table 17 priority is the one reported in mcause.
RULE 17: Instruction address-misaligned exceptions are reported in mcause with Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 0 and have lower priority than other instruction-address exceptions.
RULE 18: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 1, the cause is a supervisor software interrupt.
RULE 19: If mcause[Interrupt]=1 and mcause[Exception Code]=2, then the implementation raises an illegal‑instruction exception and mcause is updated to reflect that exception (Interrupt = 0, Exception Code = 2).
RULE 20: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 3, the cause is a machine software interrupt.
RULE 21: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 5, the cause is a supervisor timer interrupt.
RULE 22: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 7, the cause is a machine timer interrupt.
RULE 23: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 9, the cause is a supervisor external interrupt.
RULE 24: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 11, the cause is a machine external interrupt.
RULE 25: When mcause has Interrupt = 1 and Exception Code = 13, the cause is a counter-overflow interrupt.
RULE 26: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 0, the cause is an instruction address misaligned exception.
RULE 27: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 1, the cause is an instruction access fault.
RULE 28: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 2, the cause is an illegal instruction.
RULE 29: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 3, the cause is a breakpoint.
RULE 30: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 4, the cause is a load address misaligned exception.
RULE 31: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 5, the cause is a load access fault.
RULE 32: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 6, the cause is a store/AMO address misaligned exception.
RULE 33: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 7, the cause is a store/AMO access fault.
RULE 34: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 8, the cause is an environment call from U-mode.
RULE 35: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 9, the cause is an environment call from S-mode.
RULE 36: If mcause is read with Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 10, then the reported cause is Reserved (the mcause value reflects those bits, indicating an undefined exception).
RULE 37: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 11, the cause is an environment call from M-mode.
RULE 38: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 12, the cause is an instruction page fault.
RULE 39: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 13, the cause is a load page fault.
RULE 40: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 15, the cause is a store/AMO page fault.
RULE 41: When mcause has Interrupt = 0 and Exception Code = 16, the cause is a double trap.
RULE 42: If the implementation does not distinguish different reset conditions, then after reset the mcause CSR reads a value of 0.
RULE 43: The high Interrupt bit of mcause should be set to indicate that this was an interrupt.
RULE 44: If a UNMI occurs while the hart is executing machine-mode code in a trap handler, the prior value stored in mcause cannot be recovered.
RULE 45: In the double-trap situation described, the hart later sets the mcause register to the fixed exception code 16, which is defined as the double-trap exception code.
RULE 46: In the mcause register the most-significant bit is 1 for interrupt causes and 0 for exception causes.
RULE 47: In the mcause register the remaining bits encode the numeric cause code as defined in the hypervisor-extension trap-cause table.
RULE 48: If the mcause CSR’s interrupt flag is set and its cause‑code field equals 0, then reading mcause returns the interrupt flag = 1 and cause code = 0, which the architecture classifies as a Reserved interrupt.
RULE 49: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 1, mcause reports a Supervisor software interrupt.
RULE 50: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 3, mcause reports a Machine software interrupt.
RULE 51: If mcause’s interrupt bit is set and its cause‑code field equals 4, then the interrupt is reported as a Reserved interrupt (the mcause value indicates a Reserved interrupt).
RULE 52: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 5, mcause reports a Supervisor timer interrupt.
RULE 53: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 7, mcause reports a Machine timer interrupt.
RULE 54: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 9, mcause reports a Supervisor external interrupt.
RULE 55: When mcause indicates an interrupt and the cause code field is 11, mcause reports a Machine external interrupt.
RULE 56: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 0, mcause reports an Instruction address misaligned exception.
RULE 57: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 1, mcause reports an Instruction access fault exception.
RULE 58: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 2, mcause reports an Illegal instruction exception.
RULE 59: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 3, mcause reports a Breakpoint exception.
RULE 60: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 4, mcause reports a Load address misaligned exception.
RULE 61: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 5, mcause reports a Load access fault exception.
RULE 62: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 6, mcause reports a Store/AMO address misaligned exception.
RULE 63: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 7, mcause reports a Store/AMO access fault exception.
RULE 64: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 9, mcause reports an Environment call from HS-mode exception.
RULE 65: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 11, mcause reports an Environment call from M-mode exception.
RULE 66: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 12, mcause reports an Instruction page fault exception.
RULE 67: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 13, mcause reports a Load page fault exception.
RULE 68: If the exception bit in mcause is set and the cause‑code field equals 14, then a Reserved exception is taken and mcause reports the Reserved exception code.
RULE 69: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 15, mcause reports a Store/AMO page fault exception.
RULE 70: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 16, mcause reports a Double trap exception.
RULE 71: If an exception is taken and the cause field in mcause equals 17, then reading mcause in the handler reports a Reserved exception (interrupt bit cleared, cause code 17).
RULE 72: When mcause indicates an exception and the cause code field is 18, mcause reports a Software check exception.
RULE 73: An environment call from HS-mode sets mcause to the exception code 9.
RULE 74: When an instruction can raise multiple synchronous exceptions, the exception with the highest priority according to the defined priority order is the one whose code is written into mcause.
RULE 75: An Instruction address breakpoint (exception code 3) has the highest priority among synchronous exceptions and therefore is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 76: An Instruction access fault with a physical address (exception code 1) has priority over illegal-instruction exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 77: An Instruction address misaligned exception (exception code 0) has priority over environment-call exceptions and is reported in mcause when it occurs.
RULE 78: Optional load/store/AMO address-misaligned exceptions (exception codes 4 or 6) have priority over explicit memory-access page-fault or access-fault exceptions and are reported in mcause when they occur.
RULE 79: Load/store/AMO access-fault exceptions (exception codes 5 or 7) have priority over load/store/AMO address-misaligned exceptions when no higher-priority exception is present and are reported in mcause.
RULE 80: If no higher-priority exception applies, load/store/AMO address-misaligned exceptions (exception codes 4 or 6) are reported in mcause.
RULE 81: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the implementation writes the mcause CSR.
RULE 82: In M-mode, accessing mcause register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x342; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 83: In S-mode, accessing mcause register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x342; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 84: In U-mode, accessing mcause register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x342; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 85: In M-mode, setting mcause.INT (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x342, a0; csrr a1, 0x342; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].
RULE 86: In M-mode, setting mcause.CODE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x342, a0; csrr a1, 0x342; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].

REGISTER: mconfigptr
NUMBER: 0xf15
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDRESS
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The mconfigptr CSR has privilege MRO (machine-read-only).
RULE 2: If software attempts to write any value to the mconfigptr CSR, then an illegal‑instruction exception is raised (mcause = illegal‑instruction) and the CSR value remains unchanged; reading the CSR returns an MXLEN‑bit value that is the physical address of the configuration data structure.
RULE 3: If MXLEN is 8 × n, then the bits mconfigptr[log₂ n-1:0] MUST be zero.
RULE 4: The mconfigptr register MUST be implemented.
RULE 5: In M-mode, accessing mconfigptr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xf15; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

NUMBER: 0x306

WIDTH: 32
FIELDS: 31..31=HPM31, 30..30=HPM30, 29..29=HPM29, 28..28=HPM28, 27..27=HPM27, 26..26=HPM26, 25..25=HPM25, 24..24=HPM24, 23..23=HPM23, 22..22=HPM22, 21..21=HPM21, 20..20=HPM20, 19..19=HPM19, 18..18=HPM18, 17..17=HPM17, 16..16=HPM16, 15..15=HPM15, 14..14=HPM14, 13..13=HPM13, 12..12=HPM12, 11..11=HPM11, 10..10=HPM10, 9..9=HPM9, 8..8=HPM8, 7..7=HPM7, 6..6=HPM6, 5..5=HPM5, 4..4=HPM4, 3..3=HPM3, 2..2=IR, 1..1=TM, 0..0=CY
EXTENSIONS: H, Smcdeleg, Smcntrpmf, Smcsrind, Smstateen, Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, Sscsrind
RULE 1: The mcounteren CSR has machine-mode read-write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the underlying counters, which continue to increment even when not accessible.
RULE 3: If any of the CY, TM, IR, or HPM n bits in the mcounteren register is clear, an attempt to read the corresponding counter register (cycle, time, instret, or hpmcountern) while executing in S-mode or U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 4: If any of the CY, TM, IR, or HPM n bits in the mcounteren register is set, access to the corresponding counter register is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented otherwise U-mode.
RULE 5: In harts that implement U-mode, a zero value in an mcounteren field indicates that reads of the corresponding counter in a less-privileged mode will cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: The mcounteren register permits M-mode to grant the next-lower privilege mode read access to selected hardware counters.
RULE 7: A counter i is delegated when both mcounteren[i] = 1 and menvcfg.CDE = 1.
RULE 8: Setting a bit in mcounteren does not affect whether the corresponding bit in scounteren is writable.
RULE 9: U-mode may only access a counter if the corresponding bits in scounteren and mcounteren are both set.
RULE 10: In M-mode, accessing mcounteren register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x306; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mcountinhibit
NUMBER: 0x320
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 32
FIELDS: 31..31=HPM31, 30..30=HPM30, 29..29=HPM29, 28..28=HPM28, 27..27=HPM27, 26..26=HPM26, 25..25=HPM25, 24..24=HPM24, 23..23=HPM23, 22..22=HPM22, 21..21=HPM21, 20..20=HPM20, 19..19=HPM19, 18..18=HPM18, 17..17=HPM17, 16..16=HPM16, 15..15=HPM15, 14..14=HPM14, 13..13=HPM13, 12..12=HPM12, 11..11=HPM11, 10..10=HPM10, 9..9=HPM9, 8..8=HPM8, 7..7=HPM7, 6..6=HPM6, 5..5=HPM5, 4..4=HPM4, 3..3=HPM3, 2..2=IR, 0..0=CY
EXTENSIONS: Smcdeleg, Ssccfg, Sscofpmf
RULE 1: If software attempts to read or write the mcountinhibit CSR while not in Machine mode, then an illegal‑instruction exception is raised (mcause = 2).
RULE 2: The mcountinhibit CSR has read/write privilege, designated MRW.
RULE 3: Settings in the mcountinhibit register affect only whether the counters increment and do not affect the counters' accessibility.
RULE 4: When a CY, IR, or HPM n bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the corresponding mcycle, minstret, or mhpmcounter n register increments as usual.
RULE 5: When a CY, IR, or HPM n bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the corresponding counter does not increment.
RULE 6: If the mcycle CSR is shared between harts on the same core, the mcountinhibit.CY field is also shared between those harts and writes to mcountinhibit.CY are visible to those harts.
RULE 7: The mcountinhibit mechanism does not inhibit the mtime counter, which may be shared between multiple cores.
RULE 8: For any hardware counter that is delegated to supervisor mode, the corresponding bit in the mcountinhibit register can be read and written via the scountinhibit register.
RULE 9: For any hardware counter that is not delegated to supervisor mode, the corresponding bit in the scountinhibit register reads as zero, indicating that the associated mcountinhibit bit is not accessible through scountinhibit.
RULE 10: If the CDE field of the menvcfg CSR is zero, any attempt to access the scountinhibit register, which aliases mcountinhibit, causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: In M-mode, accessing mcountinhibit register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x320; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 12: In S-mode, accessing mcountinhibit register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x320; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: mcycle
NUMBER: 0xb00
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Smcdeleg, Ssccfg, Sscofpmf
RULE 1: An explicit read of the mcycle CSR returns the mcycle state before the execution of the instruction.
RULE 2: An explicit write to the mcycle CSR suppresses and overrides any implicit writes or modifications to the same CSR by the same instruction.
RULE 3: The mcycle CSR has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 4: The mcycle CSR counts the number of clock cycles executed by the processor core on which the hart is running.
RULE 5: The mcycle register can be written with a given value.
RULE 6: Any write to the mcycle CSR takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 7: The cycle CSR is a read-only shadow of mcycle.
RULE 8: Reading mcycle does not affect its underlying counter value.
RULE 9: Writing mcycle does not affect its underlying counter value.
RULE 10: The mcycle counter continues to increment even when it is not accessible.
RULE 11: If the CY bit in mcounteren is clear, a read of the cycle CSR executed in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception, preventing read access to mcycle in those modes.
RULE 12: In harts that implement U-mode, each field of mcounteren is WARL and may be hardwired to zero, which causes reads of the corresponding counter - including reads of mcycle via the cycle CSR - to raise an illegal-instruction exception when executed in a less-privileged mode.
RULE 13: When the CY bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mcycle register increments as usual.
RULE 14: When the CY bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mcycle register does not increment.
RULE 15: The setting of the mcountinhibit register controls only the incrementing of the mcycle register and does not affect its accessibility.
RULE 16: If the MINH field (bit 62) of mcyclecfg is set, counting of events for mcycle in M-mode is inhibited.
RULE 17: If the SINH field (bit 61) of mcyclecfg is set, counting of events for mcycle in S/HS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 18: If the UINH field (bit 60) of mcyclecfg is set, counting of events for mcycle in U-mode is inhibited.
RULE 19: When all INH bits (bits 62-58) of mcyclecfg are zero, counting of events for mcycle is enabled in all privilege modes.
RULE 20: If a privilege mode referenced by an INH bit (bits 61‑58) of mcyclecfg is not implemented, then any write to that INH bit is ignored, the bit reads back as zero, and mcycle counting proceeds unchanged.
RULE 21: If the mcycle CSR does not increment by one for each elapsed cycle, then after executing a sequence that consumes exactly K cycles, the value read from mcycle will not equal the initial mcycle value plus K.
RULE 22: In M-mode, accessing mcycle register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb00; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 23: In S-mode, accessing mcycle register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb00; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 24: In U-mode, accessing mcycle register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb00; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing mcycle register while Smcdeleg extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcdeleg; csrr a0, 0xb00; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 26: In M-mode, accessing mcycle register while Ssccfg extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssccfg; csrr a0, 0xb00; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing mcycle register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xb00; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: medeleg
NUMBER: 0x302
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 23..23=SGPF, 22..22=VI, 21..21=LGPF, 20..20=IGPF, 15..15=SPF, 13..13=LPF, 12..12=IPF, 11..11=EM, 10..10=EVS, 9..9=ES, 8..8=EU, 7..7=SAF, 6..6=SAM, 5..5=LAF, 4..4=LAM, 3..3=B, 2..2=II, 1..1=IAF, 0..0=IAM
EXTENSIONS: S
RULE 1: The medeleg CSR has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege, meaning it can be read and written in Machine mode.
RULE 2: medeleg is a 64-bit read/write register.
RULE 3: In harts that implement S-mode, medeleg must exist.
RULE 4: Setting a bit in medeleg delegates the corresponding trap, when occurring in S-mode or U-mode, to the S-mode trap handler.
RULE 5: Implementations shall not have any bits of medeleg be read-only one; any synchronous trap that can be delegated must support not being delegated.
RULE 6: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, scause is written with the trap cause.
RULE 7: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, sepc is written with the virtual address of the instruction that took the trap.
RULE 8: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, stval is written with an exception-specific datum.
RULE 9: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the SPP field of mstatus is written with the active privilege mode at the time of the trap.
RULE 10: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the SPIE field of mstatus is written with the value of the SIE field at the time of the trap.
RULE 11: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the SIE field of mstatus is cleared.
RULE 12: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, mcause is not written.
RULE 13: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, mepc is not written.
RULE 14: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, mtval is not written.
RULE 15: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the MPP field of mstatus is not written.
RULE 16: When a trap is delegated to S-mode via medeleg, the MPIE field of mstatus is not written.
RULE 17: medeleg has a bit position allocated for every synchronous exception, with the index of the bit equal to the value returned in the mcause register.
RULE 18: Setting bit 8 in medeleg allows user-mode environment calls to be delegated to a lower-privilege trap handler.
RULE 19: Bits in medeleg that correspond to exceptions that cannot occur in less privileged modes shall be read-only zero.
RULE 20: medeleg[11] is read-only zero.
RULE 21: medeleg[16] is read-only zero.
RULE 22: By default all traps at any privilege level are handled in M-mode, but the medeleg CSR can be used by M-mode to delegate selected traps to HS-mode.
RULE 23: When a trap occurs in HS-mode or U-mode, the trap is taken in M-mode unless medeleg (or mideleg) delegates the trap, in which case the trap is taken in HS-mode.
RULE 24: In M-mode, accessing medeleg register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x302; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 25: In S-mode, accessing medeleg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x302; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 26: In U-mode, accessing medeleg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x302; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 27: In M-mode, setting medeleg.SGPF (bit 23) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x800000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x800000; csrs 0x302, a0; csrr a1, 0x302; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x800000].
