REGISTER: menvcfg
NUMBER: 0x30a
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=STCE, 62..62=PBMTE, 61..61=ADUE, 7..7=CBZE, 6..6=CBCFE, 5..4=CBIE, 3..3=SSE, 0..0=FIOM
EXTENSIONS: Svnapot, Svpbmt
RULE 1: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBIE field of menvcfg equals 00 then an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 2: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBCFE field of menvcfg is false then an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 3: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBCFE field of menvcfg is false, then the instruction raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause set to the illegal‑instruction code).
RULE 4: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBZE field of menvcfg is false then an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 5: If the current privilege mode is not M and the CBZE field of menvcfg is true then the instruction executes.
RULE 6: The CBIE, CBCFE, and CBZE fields in menvcfg do not affect the read or write behavior of the same-named fields in senvcfg or henvcfg.
RULE 7: If an instruction attempts to read or write the menvcfg CSR while the current privilege level is not machine mode, then it raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = 2).
RULE 8: The menvcfg CSR has read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 9: The menvcfgh CSR, which supplies the upper 32 bits of menvcfg, is a machine-level CSR with read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 10: The menvcfg CSR is a 64-bit read/write register.
RULE 11: If Svpbmt is not implemented, the PBMTE bit is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 12: For implementations with the hypervisor extension, henvcfg.PBMTE is read-only zero if menvcfg.PBMTE is zero.
RULE 13: When ADUE=1 in menvcfg, hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled during S-mode address translation, and the implementation behaves as though Svade were not implemented for S-mode address translation.
RULE 14: If Svadu is not implemented, the ADUE bit is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 15: For implementations with the hypervisor extension, henvcfg.ADUE is read-only zero if menvcfg.ADUE is zero.
RULE 16: After changing menvcfg.ADUE, executing an SFENCE.VMA instruction with rs1=x0 and rs2=x0 suffices to synchronize address-translation caches with respect to the altered interpretation of page-table entries' A/D bits.
RULE 17: When ADUE=0 in menvcfg, Svade is implemented, requiring page-fault exceptions to be raised when PTE A/D bits need to be set.
RULE 18: When CDE=0 in menvcfg, the Smcdeleg and Ssccfg extensions appear to be not implemented.
RULE 19: If the Smcdeleg extension is not implemented, the CDE bit is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 20: If the H extension is implemented and STCE in menvcfg is zero, hip.VSTIP also reverts its defined behavior as if the extension were not implemented.
RULE 21: When CBZE=1 in menvcfg, it enables execution of the cache block zero instruction CBO.ZERO in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 22: When CBZE is not set to one in menvcfg, the CBO.ZERO instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 23: When CBCFE=1 in menvcfg, it enables execution of the cache block clean instruction CBO.CLEAN and the cache block flush instruction CBO.FLUSH in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 24: When CBCFE is not set to one in menvcfg, CBO.CLEAN and CBO.FLUSH raise illegal-instruction exceptions in modes less privileged than M.
RULE 25: The CBIE field in menvcfg is a WARL field.
RULE 26: When the Smnpm extension is not implemented, the PMM field is read-only zero in menvcfg.
RULE 27: The PMM field in menvcfg is a WARL field.
RULE 28: The PMM field in menvcfg enables or disables pointer masking for the next-lower privilege mode according to Table 19.
RULE 29: When LPE=1 in menvcfg and S-mode is implemented, the Zicfilp extension is enabled in S-mode.
RULE 30: When LPE=0 in menvcfg, the Zicfilp extension is not enabled in S-mode.
RULE 31: When SSE=1 in menvcfg, the Zicfiss extension is activated in S-mode.
RULE 32: When SSE=0 in menvcfg, 16-bit Zicfiss instructions revert to the behavior defined by Zcmop.
RULE 33: When SSE=0 in menvcfg, the pte.xwr=010b encoding in VS/S-stage page tables becomes reserved.
RULE 34: When SSE=0 in menvcfg, the SSAMOSWAP.W/D instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 35: When SSE=0 in menvcfg, the henvcfg.SSE and senvcfg.SSE fields are read-only zero.
RULE 36: When XLEN=64, the menvcfgh register does not exist, providing no alias for menvcfg.
RULE 37: If menvcfg.CDE = 0, any attempt to access scountinhibit raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 38: When menvcfg.SSE is 1, the SSAMOSWAP.W/D instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception in U-mode.
RULE 39: If the current privilege mode is less than M and the menvcfg.SSE field is 0, an illegal-instruction exception is raised when accessing the ssp CSR.
RULE 40: If the menvcfg.SSE field holds value V, then reading the architectural xSSE setting while in S‑mode or HS‑mode returns V.
RULE 41: In M-mode, the architectural xSSE setting is always 0 regardless of the value of the menvcfg.SSE field.
RULE 42: Updates to the menvcfg.SSE field that affect xSSE take effect immediately and do not require address-translation caches to be synchronized with SFENCE.VMA, HFENCE.GVMA, or HFENCE.VVMA instructions.
RULE 43: In M-mode, accessing menvcfg register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x30a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 44: In S-mode, accessing menvcfg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x30a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 45: In U-mode, accessing menvcfg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x30a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: mepc
NUMBER: 0x341
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=PC
EXTENSIONS: Smdbltrp, Smrnmi
RULE 1: The mepc CSR resides at machine privilege level.
RULE 2: The mepc CSR has machine read/write (MRW) access permissions.
RULE 3: When a trap is delegated to S-mode by setting the corresponding bit in medeleg or mideleg so that the trap occurs in S-mode instead of M-mode, the mepc register is not written.
RULE 4: mepc is an MXLEN-bit read/write register.
RULE 5: The least-significant bit of mepc (mepc[0]) is always zero.
RULE 6: On implementations that support only IALIGN=32, both low bits of mepc (mepc[1] and mepc[0]) are always zero.
RULE 7: If an implementation permits IALIGN to be either 16 or 32, then when IALIGN=32, bit mepc[1] is masked on reads so that it appears to be zero.
RULE 8: The read masking of mepc[1] when IALIGN=32 also applies to the implicit read performed by the MRET instruction.
RULE 9: Although masked on reads when IALIGN=32, bit mepc[1] remains writable.
RULE 10: mepc is a WARL register that MUST be able to hold all valid virtual addresses.
RULE 11: When address translation is not in effect, the set of addresses that mepc must be able to represent includes all physical addresses that can be used as a valid program counter or effective address.
RULE 12: When a trap is taken into M-mode, mepc is written with the virtual address of the instruction that was interrupted or that caused the exception.
RULE 13: In all other circumstances, mepc is never written by the implementation, although software may explicitly write mepc.
RULE 14: For a breakpoint exception raised by C.EBREAK, the virtual address of the faulting instruction is already recorded in mepc.
RULE 15: When an instruction access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on a hart that supports variable-length instructions, mepc points to the beginning of the faulting instruction.
RULE 16: On an illegal-instruction exception, mepc points to the faulting instruction in memory.
RULE 17: When a non-maskable interrupt (UNMI) occurs, the hardware overwrites the current mepc register with the address of the NMI handler executing in machine mode.
RULE 18: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the implementation writes the CSR mepc.
RULE 19: The write to mepc occurs only when a trap is taken into M-mode (i.e., the trap is not delegated to a lower privilege mode).
RULE 20: mepc is written as part of the set of CSRs that are updated on trap entry.
RULE 21: During execution of the MRET instruction, the hardware sets the program counter (pc) to the value contained in the mepc register.
RULE 22: In M-mode, accessing mepc register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x341; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 23: In S-mode, accessing mepc register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x341; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 24: In U-mode, accessing mepc register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x341; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 25: In M-mode, setting mepc.PC (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x341, a0; csrr a1, 0x341; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 26: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the mepc register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x341, a0; csrr a1, 0x341; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing mepc register while Smdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x341; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing mepc register while Smrnmi extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smrnmi; csrr a0, 0x341; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhartid
NUMBER: 0xf14
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ID
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The mhartid CSR is defined to be accessed only at machine privilege level.
RULE 2: The mhartid CSR has machine read-only (MRO) access, meaning it can be read but not written by software.
RULE 3: The mhartid CSR is an MXLEN-bit read-only register that contains the integer ID of the hardware thread executing the code.
RULE 4: The mhartid register MUST be readable in any implementation.
RULE 5: One hart MUST have a hart ID of zero as read from mhartid.
RULE 6: Hart IDs read from mhartid MUST be unique within the execution environment.
RULE 7: In M-mode, accessing mhartid register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xf14; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 8: In S-mode, accessing mhartid register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xf14; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 9: In U-mode, accessing mhartid register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xf14; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 10: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the mhartid register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xf14, a0; csrr a1, 0xf14; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter3
NUMBER: 0xb03
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zihpm
RULE 1: The mhpmcounter3 CSR has machine-level read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: after a hart reset, mhpmcounter3 contains an arbitrary value and can be written with a given value.
RULE 3: a write to mhpmcounter3 takes effect only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 4: the 64-bit WARL register mhpmevent3 controls which event causes mhpmcounter3 to increment.
RULE 5: The HPM 3 bit in the mcounteren register controls the accessibility of the mhpmcounter3 register through its read-only shadow CSR hpmcounter3.
RULE 6: If the HPM 3 bit in mcounteren is clear, any attempt to read the hpmcounter3 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 7: If the HPM 3 bit in mcounteren is set, a read of the hpmcounter3 CSR is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented otherwise U-mode.
RULE 8: The hpmcounter3 CSR is a read-only shadow of mhpmcounter3, and reading hpmcounter3 returns the current value of mhpmcounter3.
RULE 9: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the value of mhpmcounter3.
RULE 10: The mhpmcounter3 counter continues to increment even when it is not accessible.
RULE 11: A zero value in the HPM 3 field of mcounteren indicates that reads to mhpmcounter3 will cause an illegal-instruction exception when executing in a less-privileged mode.
RULE 12: When the HPM3 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter3 register increments.
RULE 13: When the HPM3 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter3 register does not increment.
RULE 14: The settings in the mcountinhibit register do not affect the accessibility of the mhpmcounter3 register.
RULE 15: If mhpmcounter3 is incremented past the maximum value representable by its implemented bits, then reading mhpmcounter3 returns the lower implemented‑bit portion of the result (i.e., the value wraps modulo 2^(implemented bits)).
RULE 16: Overflow of mhpmcounter3 never results from writes to mhpmcounter3 or mhpmevent3, only from hardware increments of mhpmcounter3.
RULE 17: If mhpmcounter3 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 18: If the OF bit of mhpmcounter3 is one when an overflow occurs, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 19: If the OF bit of mhpmcounter3 is cleared and mhpmcounter3 overflows (wraps from its maximum value to zero), then a count‑overflow interrupt is raised; if the OF bit is set, the overflow does not raise an interrupt.
RULE 20: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by mhpmcounter3 sets the OF bit of mhpmcounter3.
RULE 21: When the OF bit of mhpmcounter3 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 22: The LCOFIP bit is cleared by software before servicing the count-overflow interrupt resulting from one or more overflows of mhpmcounter3.
RULE 23: The mip/sip LCOFIP bit and the mie/sie LCOFIE bit serve as the interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits, respectively, for the count-overflow interrupt of mhpmcounter3.
RULE 24: The mideleg register controls delegation of the count-overflow interrupt of mhpmcounter3 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 25: Once mhpmcounter3 has overflowed, mhpmcounter3 and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 26: If the MINH bit in mhpmevent3 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter3 in M-mode is inhibited.
RULE 27: If the SINH bit in mhpmevent3 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter3 in S/HS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 28: If the UINH bit in mhpmevent3 is set, counting of events for mhpmcounter3 in U-mode is inhibited.
RULE 29: When all five x-INH bits in mhpmevent3 are zero, counting of events for mhpmcounter3 occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 30: For any x-INH bit in mhpmevent3, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, that bit is read-only zero for mhpmcounter3.
RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter3 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb03; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 32: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb03; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 33: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb03; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 34: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter3 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xb03; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 35: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter3 register while Zihpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zihpm; csrr a0, 0xb03; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter4
NUMBER: 0xb04
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The privilege level for mhpmcounter4 is MRW (machine-read/write).
RULE 2: A CSR write to mhpmcounter4 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 3: The event selector CSR mhpmevent4 is a 64-bit WARL register that controls which event causes mhpmcounter4 to increment.
RULE 4: When mhpmevent4 is set to 0, no event causes mhpmcounter4 to increment.
RULE 5: When the HPM4 bit in mcounteren is clear, a read of the hpmcounter4 CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: The hpmcounter4 CSR is a read-only shadow of the mhpmcounter4 register.
RULE 7: When the HPM4 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter4 register increments as usual.
RULE 8: When the HPM4 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter4 register does not increment.
RULE 9: The settings in the mcountinhibit register control only whether the mhpmcounter4 register increments and do not affect the accessibility of the mhpmcounter4 register.
RULE 10: The OF bit in mhpmevent4 is set when mhpmcounter4 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 11: When the OF bit for mhpmcounter4 is set, the counter's overflow status is sticky and no further overflow-interrupt request will be generated until software clears the OF bit.
RULE 12: Overflow for mhpmcounter4 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 13: An unsigned wrap-around of the implemented bits of mhpmcounter4 is considered an overflow event.
RULE 14: If mhpmcounter4 overflows while the OF bit in mhpmevent4 is zero, a local count-overflow interrupt is raised.
RULE 15: Setting the OF bit in mhpmevent4 disables count-overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter4.
RULE 16: If a write to mhpmcounter4 or mhpmevent4 would cause mhpmcounter4 to exceed its maximum representable value, then the overflow flag in mhpmevent4 remains clear (no overflow condition is raised).
RULE 17: An overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter4 sets the LCOFIP (bit 13) pending bit in the appropriate mip or sip register.
RULE 18: After mhpmcounter4 overflows and its OF bit is set, the LCOFIP pending bit will eventually be set.
RULE 19: Whether the overflow interrupt from mhpmcounter4 is taken in S-mode or M-mode is determined by the mideleg register.
RULE 20: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter4 is done by clearing its OF bit, typically together with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 21: After mhpmcounter4 overflows, both the counter value and its OF bit must be written to new values before a subsequent overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 22: When the MINH bit in mhpmevent4 is set, mhpmcounter4 does not count events while the processor is in M-mode.
RULE 23: When the SINH bit in mhpmevent4 is set, mhpmcounter4 does not count events while the processor is in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 24: When the UINH bit in mhpmevent4 is set, mhpmcounter4 does not count events while the processor is in U-mode.
RULE 25: For each INH bit in mhpmevent4 that affects mhpmcounter4, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the bit is read-only zero.
RULE 26: mhpmcounter4 counts events in a privilege mode only if the corresponding INH bit in mhpmevent4 for that mode is cleared.
RULE 27: If all five INH bits in mhpmevent4 are zero, mhpmcounter4 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter4 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb04; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb04; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 30: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb04; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter5
NUMBER: 0xb05
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: If mhpmcounter5 is read immediately after a hart reset without a prior write, the readback value is architecturally undefined (any value may appear); writing any value to mhpmcounter5 after reset does not raise an exception and subsequent reads return the written value.
RULE 2: A CSR write to mhpmcounter5 becomes visible only after the executing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 3: When mhpmevent5 is set to 0, mhpmcounter5 does not count any events.
RULE 4: When the HPM 5 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, a read of the mhpmcounter5 register while executing in S-mode or U-mode MUST cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 5: When the HPM 5 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to the mhpmcounter5 register is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 6: Reading the hpmcounter5 CSR reads the current value of the mhpmcounter5 register.
RULE 7: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the mhpmcounter5 counter, which continues to increment even when not accessible.
RULE 8: In harts that implement U-mode, the mcounteren register must be implemented and its fields may be read-only zero, causing a read of the mhpmcounter5 register in a less-privileged mode to cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: If the HPM5 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, mhpmcounter5 increments as usual.
RULE 10: If the HPM5 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, mhpmcounter5 does not increment.
RULE 11: The OF bit in mhpmevent5 is set when mhpmcounter5 overflows.
RULE 12: The OF bit in mhpmevent5 remains set until it is written by software.
RULE 13: Overflow for mhpmcounter5 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 14: If mhpmcounter5 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 15: If the OF bit for mhpmcounter5 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 16: The OF bit for mhpmcounter5 also functions as a count overflow interrupt disable.
RULE 17: The count-overflow-interrupt request generated by mhpmcounter5 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.

RULE 20: If any INH bit in mhpmevent5 is set, counting of events in the corresponding privilege mode is inhibited for mhpmcounter5.
RULE 21: If all INH bits in mhpmevent5 are zero, counting of events in all privilege modes is enabled for mhpmcounter5.
RULE 22: For each INH bit in mhpmevent5, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, that bit is read-only zero for mhpmcounter5.
RULE 23: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter5 is performed by clearing its OF bit together with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 24: After mhpmcounter5 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter5 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb05; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter6
NUMBER: 0xb06
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: Event 0 selected in mhpmevent6 is defined to mean that no event increments mhpmcounter6.

RULE 9: If an operation increments mhpmcounter6 beyond the maximum value representable by its implemented bits, then reading mhpmcounter6 returns the low‑order bits of the result (i.e., the value wraps modulo 2ⁿ, where n is the implemented counter width).
RULE 10: After mhpmcounter6 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit in mhpmevent6 remains set, resulting in no loss of information.

RULE 17: The LCOFIE bits in mie and sie are the interrupt-enable bits for the count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by mhpmcounter6.
RULE 18: When mhpmcounter6 generates a count-overflow-interrupt request, its OF bit in mhpmevent6 is set.
RULE 19: After the OF bit for mhpmcounter6 in mhpmevent6 is set, the corresponding LCOFIP bit in mip or sip will eventually be set.
RULE 20: The LCOFIP bit for mhpmcounter6 is cleared by software before servicing the count overflow interrupt resulting from one or more overflows of mhpmcounter6.
RULE 21: The mideleg register controls whether the count-overflow-interrupt generated by mhpmcounter6 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 22: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter6 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb06; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 23: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter6 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb06; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter7
NUMBER: 0xb07
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: mhpmcounter7 is a machine-read/write (MRW) register.
RULE 2: mhpmcounter7h is a machine-read/write (MRW) register.
RULE 3: If the mhpmcounter7 CSR is read, the architectural readback value is a 64‑bit counter (full XLEN bits on RV64, or low and high 32‑bit halves on RV32).
RULE 4: If a hart reset occurs, then reading mhpmcounter7 returns an unspecified (arbitrary) value.
RULE 5: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter7 may be written with any value.
RULE 6: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter7 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 7: mhpmevent7 is a 64-bit WARL register whose programmed value determines which event causes mhpmcounter7 to increment.
RULE 8: If mhpmevent7 = 0, mhpmcounter7 does not increment for any event.
RULE 9: If the HPM7 bit in mcounteren is clear, a read of hpmcounter7 (the read-only shadow of mhpmcounter7) while executing in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: If the HPM7 bit in mcounteren is set, a read of hpmcounter7 (the read-only shadow of mhpmcounter7) is permitted in the next lower implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).
RULE 11: The settings in mcounteren affect only accessibility and do not affect mhpmcounter7, which continues to increment regardless of the HPM7 bit state.
RULE 12: The increment behavior of mhpmcounter7 is controlled by the HPM7 bit in the mcountinhibit register.
RULE 13: The settings of the mcountinhibit register do not affect the accessibility of mhpmcounter7.
RULE 14: When the HPM7 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, mhpmcounter7 increments as usual.
RULE 15: When the HPM7 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, mhpmcounter7 does not increment.
RULE 16: The OF bit in mhpmevent7 is set when mhpmcounter7 overflows and remains set until software writes to it.
RULE 17: An overflow of mhpmcounter7 occurs when its unsigned value wraps past the most-significant implemented counter bit.
RULE 18: After mhpmcounter7 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while its OF bit stays set.
RULE 19: If mhpmcounter7 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 20: If mhpmcounter7 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 21: Setting the OF bit in mhpmevent7 disables further count-overflow interrupt requests for mhpmcounter7.
RULE 22: mhpmcounter7 can overflow only as a result of hardware increments and never as a result of software writes to mhpmcounter7 or mhpmevent7.
RULE 23: An overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter7 sets the LCOFIP pending bit (bit 13) in mip and sip, and the corresponding LCOFIE enable bits in mie and sie control whether the interrupt is enabled.
RULE 24: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt by mhpmcounter7 sets its OF bit and eventually sets the LCOFIP pending bit in mip and sip.
RULE 25: The mideleg register determines whether the overflow interrupt from mhpmcounter7 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 26: There are no separate overflow status and overflow interrupt enable bits for mhpmcounter7; enabling overflow interrupt generation is performed by clearing the OF bit together with initializing the counter.
RULE 27: After mhpmcounter7 has overflowed, both the counter value and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 28: Setting any INH bit in mhpmevent7 (e.g., MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter7 while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode, and if that privilege mode is not implemented the INH bit reads as zero.
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter7 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb07; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter7 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb07; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 31: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter7 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb07; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmcounter9 is a Machine-level CSR that is readable and writable by machine mode (privilege MRW).

RULE 8: The CSR mhpmcounter9h provides access to bits 63-32 of mhpmcounter9 when the Sscofpmf extension is implemented.

RULE 10: The CSR hpmcounter9 provides a read-only view of mhpmcounter9.
RULE 11: If the HPM9 bit in mcounteren is clear, an attempt to read the shadow CSR hpmcounter9 while executing in S-mode or U-mode must cause an illegal-instruction exception, thereby denying access to mhpmcounter9.

RULE 7: Access to the read-only shadow CSR hpmcounter13 of mhpmcounter13 is permitted only when the HPM13 bit in the mcounteren register is set; if the HPM13 bit is clear, a read of hpmcounter13 from S-mode or U-mode must raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 8: When the HPM13 bit in the mcounteren register is set, a read of hpmcounter13 (the shadow of mhpmcounter13) is permitted in the next implemented lower privilege mode, which is S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode.
RULE 9: The settings in the mcounteren register do not affect the counting operation of mhpmcounter13; mhpmcounter13 continues to increment even when it is not accessible.
RULE 10: If the HPM13 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter13 register increments as usual.
RULE 11: If the HPM13 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter13 register does not increment.
RULE 12: The settings in the mcountinhibit register affect only the incrementing behavior of the mhpmcounter13 register and do not affect its accessibility.
RULE 13: Each x INH bit in mhpmevent13, when set, inhibits counting of events in mhpmcounter13 while executing in privilege mode x.
RULE 14: When all INH bits in mhpmevent13 are zero, mhpmcounter13 counts events in all privilege modes.
RULE 15: The OF bit in mhpmevent13 is set when mhpmcounter13 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 16: If mhpmcounter13 increments past its maximum value for the implemented counter bits (unsigned overflow), then reading mhpmcounter13 returns the result modulo 2^{implemented bits}, i.e., the counter wraps around to the lower bits.
RULE 17: If mhpmcounter13 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 18: If mhpmcounter13 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 19: The OF bit associated with mhpmcounter13 functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for that counter.
RULE 20: Count overflow for mhpmcounter13 never results from writes to mhpmcounter13 or mhpmevent13; it only results from hardware increments of mhpmcounter13.
RULE 21: A count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter13 is signaled as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 22: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by mhpmcounter13 sets the associated OF bit in mhpmevent13.
RULE 23: When the OF bit for mhpmcounter13 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit 13 in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 24: The mideleg register controls delegation of the overflow interrupt of mhpmcounter13 to S-mode versus M-mode.
RULE 25: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmcounter13 is done by clearing its OF bit in conjunction with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 26: Once mhpmcounter13 has overflowed, it and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter13 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb0d; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 28: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter13 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb0d; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 29: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter13 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb0d; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter13 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xb0d; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmcounter14 is a Machine-level Read/Write CSR.

RULE 8: If the HPM14 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, a read of mhpmcounter14 from S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: If the HPM14 bit in the mcounteren register is set, a read of mhpmcounter14 is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).

RULE 16: When a count-overflow interrupt request is generated by mhpmcounter14, its OF bit is set.

RULE 20: After mhpmcounter14 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.

REGISTER: mhpmcounter16
NUMBER: 0xb10
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: After a hart reset, mhpmcounter16 contains an arbitrary value, and it can be written with a specified value.
RULE 2: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter16 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 3: All counters should be implemented, but a legal implementation may implement mhpmcounter16 as a read-only zero register together with its event selector mhpmevent16.
RULE 4: If mhpmevent16 is programmed with the value 0, which denotes "no event," then mhpmcounter16 does not increment for any event.
RULE 5: If the HPM16 bit in the mcounteren register is clear, a read of mhpmcounter16 in S-mode or U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: If the HPM16 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to mhpmcounter16 is permitted in S-mode when S-mode is implemented, otherwise it is permitted in U-mode.
RULE 7: The hpmcounter16 CSR is a read-only shadow of the underlying mhpmcounter16 register.
RULE 8: The value of mhpmcounter16 continues to increment regardless of whether the HPM16 bit in mcounteren is clear or set, and accesses to mcounteren do not affect its count.
RULE 9: When the HPM16 field of mcounteren is a read-only zero WARL value, a read of mhpmcounter16 in a less-privileged mode (S-mode or U-mode) causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 63 named OF, which is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when mhpmcounter16 overflows.
RULE 11: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 62 named MINH, which when set inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter16 while in M-mode.
RULE 12: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 61 named SINH, which when set inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter16 while in S/HS-mode.
RULE 13: The mhpmevent16 register contains bit 60 named UINH, which when set inhibits counting of events for mhpmcounter16 while in U-mode.
RULE 14: All INH bits cleared to zero in mhpmevent16 result in mhpmcounter16 counting events in all modes.
RULE 15: The OF bit in mhpmevent16 is set when mhpmcounter16 overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 16: If mhpmcounter16 is incremented past the maximum value representable by its implemented bits, then reading mhpmcounter16 returns the value modulo 2^(implemented‑bits), i.e., the counter wraps to the low‑order bits indicating an unsigned overflow.
RULE 17: After mhpmcounter16 overflows, the counter wraps around and continues counting while the sticky OF bit remains set.
RULE 18: If mhpmcounter16 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 19: If mhpmcounter16's OF bit is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated for that overflow.
RULE 20: The OF bit in mhpmevent16 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for mhpmcounter16.
RULE 21: Writes to mhpmcounter16 never cause a count overflow; overflow only results from hardware increments of mhpmcounter16.
RULE 22: The mip (or sip) LCOFIP bit is the interrupt-pending bit for the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter16.
RULE 23: The mie (or sie) LCOFIE bit is the interrupt-enable bit for the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter16.
RULE 24: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by mhpmcounter16 sets the associated OF bit in mhpmevent16.
RULE 25: If the OF bit for mhpmcounter16 is set, then the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip register will become 1 (eventually).
RULE 26: Software clears the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers before servicing the count overflow interrupt resulting from mhpmcounter16.
RULE 27: The mideleg register controls whether the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmcounter16 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 28: After mhpmcounter16 has overflowed, software must write a new value to mhpmcounter16 and clear mhpmevent16.OF before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter16 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb10; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In S-mode, accessing mhpmcounter16 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb10; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 31: In U-mode, accessing mhpmcounter16 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb10; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter16 register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0xb10; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmcounter17
NUMBER: 0xb11
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: Zihpm
RULE 1: mhpmcounter17 is a machine-level CSR that provides read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: The event selector CSR mhpmevent17 is a 64-bit WARL register that controls which event causes mhpmcounter17 to increment.
RULE 3: Selecting event 0 in mhpmevent17 causes mhpmcounter17 not to increment.
RULE 4: Any CSR write to mhpmcounter17 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 5: Software can write a given value to mhpmcounter17.

RULE 7: The hpmcounter17 CSR is a read-only shadow that returns the current value of mhpmcounter17.

RULE 9: When the HPM17 bit in the mcounteren register is set, access to mhpmcounter17 is permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode).

RULE 11: If the HPM17 bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the mhpmcounter17 register increments as usual.
RULE 12: If the HPM17 bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the mhpmcounter17 register does not increment.

RULE 14: The OF bit for mhpmcounter17 is set when mhpmcounter17 overflows and remains set until written by software.

RULE 17: If mhpmcounter17 overflows while its OF bit is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.

RULE 26: If the MINH bit (bit 62 of mhpmevent17) is set, counting of events in M-mode for mhpmcounter17 is inhibited.
RULE 27: If the SINH bit (bit 61 of mhpmevent17) is set, counting of events in S/HS-mode for mhpmcounter17 is inhibited.
RULE 28: If the UINH bit (bit 60 of mhpmevent17) is set, counting of events in U-mode for mhpmcounter17 is inhibited.

RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing mhpmcounter17 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb11; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mhpmevent3
NUMBER: 0x323
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The mhpmevent3 register is accessible with machine read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: The LCOFIP bit in the mip register is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from the OF bit of mhpmevent3 being set.
RULE 3: If the OF bit of mhpmevent3 is set, the LCOFIP bit in the mip register becomes set to indicate a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 4: Setting mhpmevent3 to the value 0 selects the defined "no event".
RULE 5: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented and the .OF bit of mhpmevent3 is set, then the sip.LCOFIP bit in the sip CSR may become set, indicating a local‑counter‑overflow interrupt request.
RULE 6: The .OF bit of mhpmevent3 reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request when it is set.
RULE 7: The OF bit in mhpmevent3 is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 8: The MINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in M-mode.
RULE 9: The SINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 10: The UINH bit in mhpmevent3, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in U-mode.
RULE 11: Overflow of the associated hpmcounter is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 12: If the associated hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent3 is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 13: If the OF bit of mhpmevent3 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 14: The OF bit of mhpmevent3 functions as a count overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.

RULE 21: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for the counter associated with mhpmevent3 is done by clearing the OF bit in mhpmevent3 in conjunction with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 22: After the counter associated with mhpmevent3 has overflowed, both the counter and the OF bit in mhpmevent3 must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.

REGISTER: mhpmevent4
NUMBER: 0x324
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zihpm
RULE 1: The mhpmevent4 CSR is accessed with machine-mode read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: If a program writes a value with unsupported bits to the 64‑bit WARL CSR mhpmevent4, then no exception is raised, the value read back from mhpmevent4 is an implementation‑defined legal event selector (unsupported bits are masked or cleared), and mhpmcounter4 increments only when the event selected by that read‑back value occurs.
RULE 3: An event value of 0 in mhpmevent4 is defined to mean "no event".
RULE 4: The OF bit in mhpmevent4 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows.
RULE 5: The OF bit in mhpmevent4 remains set until it is written by software.
RULE 6: When the MINH bit in mhpmevent4 is 1, counting of events is inhibited while the core is in M-mode.
RULE 7: When the SINH bit in mhpmevent4 is 1, counting of events is inhibited while the core is in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 8: When the UINH bit in mhpmevent4 is 1, counting of events is inhibited while the core is in U-mode.
RULE 9: Overflow of the associated hpmcounter is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits, which causes the OF bit in mhpmevent4 to be set.
RULE 10: An hpmcounter overflow generates a count-overflow interrupt request for mhpmevent4 only when the OF bit in mhpmevent4 is zero at the moment of overflow.
RULE 11: When the OF bit in mhpmevent4 is one, further count-overflow interrupt requests for the associated counter are disabled.
RULE 12: A count-overflow interrupt generated by the counter associated with mhpmevent4 raises a standard local interrupt that sets bit 13 in the appropriate interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable CSRs (mip, mie, sip, or sie).
RULE 13: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent4 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent4.
RULE 14: After the OF bit in mhpmevent4 becomes one, the local-count-overflow-interrupt-pending (LCOFIP) bit in mip or sip will be set eventually, but not necessarily immediately.
RULE 15: The delegation of the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent4's counter to S-mode or M-mode is controlled by the mideleg CSR.
RULE 16: After the counter associated with mhpmevent4 has overflowed, the counter and the OF bit MUST be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 17: Writing to the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent4 does not cause a count overflow; overflow occurs only from hardware increments of that counter.

RULE 1: Setting the .OF bit of mhpmevent8 can cause mip.LCOFIP to reflect the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 2: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the .OF bit of mhpmevent8 contributes to the condition that makes the read-write mip.LCOFIP pending bit reflect a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 3: mhpmevent8 controls which event causes mhpmcounter8 to increment.
RULE 4: Event 0 for mhpmevent8 is defined to mean "no event."
RULE 5: A write to the mhpmevent8 CSR takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 6: The mhpmevent8h CSR is provided only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented.
RULE 7: The sip.LCOFIP bit is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from the `.OF` bit in mhpmevent8 being set.
RULE 8: The OF field of mhpmevent8 is the overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 9: The MINH field of mhpmevent8, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in M-mode.
RULE 10: The SINH field of mhpmevent8, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in S/HS-mode.
RULE 11: The UINH field of mhpmevent8, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in U-mode.
RULE 12: Each x INH bit in mhpmevent8, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is in privilege mode x.
RULE 13: When the MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, and VUINH bits in mhpmevent8 are all zero, counting of events occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 14: The OF bit in mhpmevent8 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 15: If an hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent8 is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 16: If the OF bit of mhpmevent8 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 17: When the OF bit of mhpmevent8 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip or sip registers.
RULE 18: The mideleg register determines whether the count-overflow interrupt originating from the OF bit of mhpmevent8 is delegated to S-mode or handled in M-mode.
RULE 19: Enabling overflow-interrupt generation is accomplished by clearing the OF bit of mhpmevent8, typically together with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 20: Once a counter has overflowed, both the counter and the OF bit of mhpmevent8 MUST be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 21: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent8 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x328; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 22: In S-mode, accessing mhpmevent8 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x328; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 23: In U-mode, accessing mhpmevent8 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x328; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 24: In M-mode, setting mhpmevent8.OF (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x328, a0; csrr a1, 0x328; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].

REGISTER: mhpmevent9
NUMBER: 0x329
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the mip.LCOFIP bit is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from any mhpmevent n .OF bit being set, including the .OF bit in mhpmevent9.
RULE 2: Writing the value 0 to mhpmevent9 selects no event for counter 9.
RULE 3: The high-half CSR mhpmevent9h is provided only on implementations that include the Sscofpmf extension.
RULE 4: The OF bit of mhpmevent9 is one of the mhpmevent n .OF bits whose setting can generate a local-counter-overflow interrupt request that is reflected in sip.LCOFIP when the Sscofpmf extension is implemented.
RULE 5: A local-counter-overflow interrupt can trap to S-mode only if the OF bit of mhpmevent9 has been set (producing a pending sip.LCOFIP), the sie.LCOFIE bit is set, and either the current privilege mode is S with the SIE bit in sstatus set or the current privilege mode has less privilege than S-mode.
RULE 6: The OF bit in mhpmevent9 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 7: The MINH bit in mhpmevent9, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in machine mode.
RULE 8: The SINH bit in mhpmevent9, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in supervisor or hypervisor mode.
RULE 9: The UINH bit in mhpmevent9, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in user mode.
RULE 10: Each INH bit in mhpmevent9, when set, inhibits counting of events in its associated privilege mode.
RULE 11: If all INH bits in mhpmevent9 are zero, counting of events is enabled in all privilege modes.
RULE 12: The OF bit in mhpmevent9 is set by hardware when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows and remains set until software writes a zero to it.
RULE 13: The OF bit in mhpmevent9 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 14: Overflow for the purpose of setting the OF bit in mhpmevent9 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 15: If the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent9 overflows while the OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 16: If the OF bit in mhpmevent9 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 17: The count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by overflow of the counter associated with mhpmevent9 is treated as a standard local interrupt corresponding to bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 18: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by the hpmcounter linked to mhpmevent9 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent9.
RULE 19: When the OF bit in mhpmevent9 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.

REGISTER: mhpmevent10
NUMBER: 0x32a
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Zihpm
RULE 1: mhpmevent10 belongs to the Machine Counter Setup group and has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: When the mhpmevent10.OF bit is set and the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the LCOFIP bit in the mip register becomes set.
RULE 3: An event value of 0 programmed in mhpmevent10 is defined to mean "no event".
RULE 4: The CSR mhpmevent10h, which provides the high half of mhpmevent10, is present only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented.
RULE 5: The OF bit in mhpmevent10 is the overflow status and interrupt disable bit that is set when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 6: The MINH bit in mhpmevent10, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in machine mode.
RULE 7: The SINH bit in mhpmevent10, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in supervisor or hypervisor mode.
RULE 8: The UINH bit in mhpmevent10, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in user mode.
RULE 9: When an x INH bit in mhpmevent10 is set, counting of events in the corresponding privilege mode is inhibited.
RULE 10: When all x INH bits in mhpmevent10 are zero, events are counted in all privilege modes.
RULE 11: The OF bit in mhpmevent10 is set when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows and remains set until written by software.
RULE 12: If mhpmcounter10 is incremented while holding the maximum value representable by its implemented bits, then the counter wraps to zero, observable by reading mhpmcounter10 and seeing a value of 0.
RULE 13: If the OF bit in mhpmevent10 is zero when its hpmcounter overflows, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 14: If the OF bit in mhpmevent10 is one when its hpmcounter overflows, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 15: The OF bit in mhpmevent10 also functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 16: Count overflow never results from writes to the mhpmcounter n or mhpmevent n registers, including mhpmevent10; only hardware increments cause overflow.
RULE 17: The LCOFIP bit in the mip/sip registers is the interrupt-pending bit for the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent10.
RULE 18: The LCOFIE bit in the mie/sie registers is the interrupt-enable bit for the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent10.
RULE 19: Generation of a count-overflow interrupt request by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent10 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent10.
RULE 20: When the OF bit in mhpmevent10 becomes set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip/sip registers.
RULE 21: The mideleg register controls whether the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent10 is delegated to supervisor mode or remains in machine mode.
RULE 22: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for the counter associated with mhpmevent10 is done by clearing the OF bit, typically together with initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 23: Once the counter associated with mhpmevent10 has overflowed, both the counter and the OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 24: Read access to the OF bit in mhpmevent10 is controlled by the same mcounteren (and, when applicable, hcounteren) bits that control access to hpmcounter10.
RULE 25: In S-mode or HS-mode, the OF bit in mhpmevent10 is readable only when mcounteren bit 10 is set; otherwise a read returns zero.
RULE 26: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent10 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x32a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 27: In S-mode, accessing mhpmevent10 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x32a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: mhpmevent12
NUMBER: 0x32c
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmevent12 is accessed with Machine Read/Write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting mhpmevent12.OF to 1 can cause mip.LCOFIP to become set (pending).
RULE 3: Writes to mhpmevent12 select the hardware event whose occurrences will cause mhpmcounter12 to increment.
RULE 4: Reads of mhpmevent12 return the currently selected event value.
RULE 5: Writing the value 0 to mhpmevent12 selects "no event", causing mhpmcounter12 not to increment for any event.
RULE 6: A write to mhpmevent12 takes effect after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 7: Setting the .OF bit in mhpmevent12 causes the LCOFIP bit in the sip CSR to reflect the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 8: The OF field of mhpmevent12 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows.
RULE 9: The MINH field of mhpmevent12, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in machine mode.
RULE 10: The SINH field of mhpmevent12, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in supervisor or hypervisor mode.
RULE 11: The UINH field of mhpmevent12, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in user mode.
RULE 12: When any INH bit of mhpmevent12 is set, counting of events in the corresponding privilege mode is inhibited.
RULE 13: When all INH bits of mhpmevent12 are zero, counting of events is enabled in all privilege modes.
RULE 14: A count-overflow-interrupt request is generated for mhpmevent12 when its associated hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent12 is zero.
RULE 15: No count-overflow-interrupt request is generated for mhpmevent12 when its associated hpmcounter overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent12 is one.
RULE 16: The OF bit of mhpmevent12 also functions as a count-overflow-interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter.
RULE 17: The count-overflow-interrupt-request signal for mhpmevent12 is mapped to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie CSRs.
RULE 18: The mip/sip LCOFIP bit and the mie/sie LCOFIE bit are, respectively, the pending and enable bits for the count-overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent12.
RULE 19: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent12 sets the OF bit of mhpmevent12.

REGISTER: mhpmevent13
NUMBER: 0x32d
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64

EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The value in mhpmevent13 controls which event causes the corresponding counter mhpmcounter13 to increment.
RULE 2: Event 0 in mhpmevent13 is defined to mean "no event."
RULE 3: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the .OF bit in mhpmevent13 causes the sip.LCOFIP bit, which is read-write, to become pending.
RULE 4: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the sip.LCOFIP bit reflects the occurrence of a local counter-overflow interrupt request generated by any mhpmevent n .OF bit, including the .OF bit in mhpmevent13.
RULE 5: The mhpmevent13 register bits 63-56 are defined as OF (bit 63), MINH (bit 62), SINH (bit 61), UINH (bit 60), VSINH (bit 59), VUINH (bit 58), and WPRI (bits 57-56, reserved).

RULE 8: The SINH bit in mhpmevent13, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in S/HS-mode.
RULE 9: The UINH bit in mhpmevent13, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in U-mode.

REGISTER: mhpmevent14

MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, setting the mhpmevent14.OF bit causes the mip.LCOFIP read-write bit to reflect the corresponding local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 2: If mhpmevent14 is programmed with an event identifier, then each occurrence of that event causes the mhpmcounter14 CSR to increment (its readback value increases by one); if the event does not match the programmed identifier, mhpmcounter14 does not change.
RULE 3: An event value of 0 written to mhpmevent14 is defined to mean "no event".
RULE 4: Setting the OF bit of mhpmevent14 generates a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 5: The LCOFIP field in the sip register is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request generated by the OF bit of mhpmevent14 being set.
RULE 6: If the MINH bit of mhpmevent14 is set, counting of events in M-mode is inhibited.
RULE 7: If the SINH bit of mhpmevent14 is set, counting of events in S/HS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 8: If the UINH bit of mhpmevent14 is set, counting of events in U-mode is inhibited.
RULE 9: If a program writes a value with either of the two WPRI bits of mhpmevent14 set, then a subsequent read of mhpmevent14 returns zero in those bits (the write is ignored).
RULE 10: For each INH bit of mhpmevent14, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented, that bit is read-only zero.
RULE 11: When any INH bit of mhpmevent14 is set, counting of events is inhibited while the processor is in the corresponding privilege mode, and if all INH bits of mhpmevent14 are zero, counting occurs in all modes.
RULE 12: The OF bit of mhpmevent14 is set when the corresponding hpmcounter overflows.
RULE 13: The OF bit of mhpmevent14 remains set until it is written by software.
RULE 14: Overflow for the counter associated with mhpmevent14 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits.
RULE 15: If the counter associated with mhpmevent14 overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent14 is zero, a count-overflow-interrupt request is generated.
RULE 16: If the OF bit of mhpmevent14 is one, no count-overflow-interrupt request is generated when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 17: If a write to mhpmevent14 is performed, then mhpmcounter14 does not overflow—the counter value does not wrap and its overflow flag remains unchanged.
RULE 18: If a wrap‑around (overflow) of mhpmevent14’s associated counter is observed (the read value changes from its maximum representable value to 0), then the wrap must have been caused by a hardware increment of that counter; a software write to the counter cannot produce such an overflow.
RULE 19: A count-overflow-interrupt request generated by the counter associated with mhpmevent14 is routed to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers as a standard local interrupt.
RULE 20: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by the counter associated with mhpmevent14 sets the OF bit of mhpmevent14.
RULE 21: When the OF bit of mhpmevent14 is set, it eventually, but not necessarily immediately, sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 22: The LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers is cleared by software before servicing the count overflow interrupt caused by mhpmevent14.
RULE 23: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmevent14 is done by clearing the OF bit and initializing the associated counter to a starting value.

RULE 3: The mhpmevent16.OF bit is one of the mhpmevent n . OF bits that can cause the sip.LCOFIP bit to reflect a local-counter-overflow interrupt request.
RULE 4: If the mhpmevent16.OF bit is set, a local-counter-overflow interrupt request occurs.
RULE 5: The OF field of mhpmevent16 is an overflow status and interrupt-disable bit that is set when the associated counter overflows.
RULE 6: The MINH field of mhpmevent16, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in M-mode.
RULE 7: The SINH field of mhpmevent16, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 8: The UINH field of mhpmevent16, when set, inhibits counting of events while the processor is executing in U-mode.
RULE 9: The two WPRI fields of mhpmevent16 are reserved.

RULE 14: If hpmcounter16 overflows while the OF bit of mhpmevent16 is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated; if the OF bit is one, no interrupt request is generated, making the OF bit an interrupt-disable flag.
RULE 15: When hpmcounter16 generates a count-overflow interrupt request, it sets the OF bit of mhpmevent16, which eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers, and software must clear the LCOFIP bit before servicing the interrupt; delegation of this interrupt between S-mode and M-mode is controlled by the mideleg register.
RULE 16: The OF bit of mhpmevent16 serves both as overflow status and overflow-interrupt enable, requiring software to clear the OF bit and reinitialize hpmcounter16 before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 17: In M-mode, the overflow bit of mhpmevent16 is always readable.

REGISTER: mhpmevent17
NUMBER: 0x331
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: Event 0 is defined to mean "no event", and programming mhpmevent17 with the value 0 causes mhpmcounter17 not to increment for any event.
RULE 2: The mhpmevent17h CSR is provided only if the Sscofpmf extension is implemented; otherwise the high-half CSR for mhpmevent17 does not exist.
RULE 3: When the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the mhpmevent17. OF bit contributes to a local-counter-overflow interrupt request that is reflected by the sip.LCOFIP bit.
RULE 4: The MINH field of mhpmevent17, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in machine mode.
RULE 5: The SINH field of mhpmevent17, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in supervisor or hypervisor mode.
RULE 6: The UINH field of mhpmevent17, when set, inhibits counting of events while executing in user mode.
RULE 7: For each INH bit (MINH, SINH, UINH, VSINH, VUINH) in mhpmevent17, if the associated privilege mode is not implemented the bit reads as zero and is read-only.
RULE 8: When any INH bit in mhpmevent17 is set, it inhibits counting of events for its corresponding privilege mode; if all INH bits are zero, counting occurs in all modes.
RULE 9: Overflow for hpmcounter17 is defined as unsigned overflow of the implemented counter bits, which triggers the OF bit in mhpmevent17.
RULE 10: If hpmcounter17 overflows while the OF bit in mhpmevent17 is zero, a count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 11: If the OF bit in mhpmevent17 is one, no count overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 12: The OF bit in mhpmevent17 also functions as a count-overflow-interrupt disable for the associated hpmcounter17.
RULE 13: If a software write to mhpmevent17 is performed, then the associated mhpmcounter17 does not overflow—the counter value does not wrap and no overflow exception is raised.
RULE 14: The count-overflow-interrupt-request generated by hpmcounter17 is presented as a standard local interrupt mapped to bit 13 of the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 15: The LCOFIP bits in mip and sip are the interrupt-pending bits for the count-overflow interrupt, and the LCOFIE bits in mie and sie are the interrupt-enable bits for that interrupt.
RULE 16: Generation of a count-overflow-interrupt request by hpmcounter17 sets the OF bit in mhpmevent17.
RULE 17: When the OF bit in mhpmevent17 becomes set, it eventually causes the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers to be set, though the propagation need not be immediate.
RULE 18: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent17 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x331; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 19: In S-mode, accessing mhpmevent17 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x331; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: mhpmevent18
NUMBER: 0x332
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=OF, 62..62=MINH, 61..61=SINH, 60..60=UINH, 59..59=VSINH, 58..58=VUINH, 57..0=EVENT
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: mhpmevent18 is a 64-bit WARL register that determines which event causes mhpmcounter18 to increment.
RULE 2: When mhpmevent18 contains the value 0, it selects "no event" for mhpmcounter18.
RULE 3: A write to mhpmevent18 takes effect after the instruction that performed the write has otherwise completed.
RULE 4: If the MINH bit in mhpmevent18 is set, counting of events in M-mode is inhibited.
RULE 5: If the SINH bit in mhpmevent18 is set, counting of events in S/HS-mode is inhibited.
RULE 6: If the UINH bit in mhpmevent18 is set, counting of events in U-mode is inhibited.
RULE 7: The two most-significant bits (bits 57 and 56) of mhpmevent18 are reserved (WPRI).
RULE 8: If the associated privilege mode is not implemented, the corresponding INH bit in mhpmevent18 is read-only zero.
RULE 9: When an INH bit in mhpmevent18 is set, counting of events while executing in the corresponding privilege mode is inhibited; if all five INH bits are zero, counting occurs in all privilege modes.
RULE 10: The OF bit in mhpmevent18 is set when the associated hpmcounter overflows and remains set until software writes the bit.
RULE 11: If the mhpmevent18 counter is incremented while holding the maximum value representable in its implemented bit width, then the mhpmcounter18 register wraps to the lower bits of the incremented value (i.e., wraps modulo 2ᴺ), reflecting an unsigned overflow.
RULE 12: After overflow, the counter associated with mhpmevent18 wraps around and continues counting while the OF bit remains set.
RULE 13: If the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent18 overflows while its OF bit is zero, a count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 14: If the OF bit of mhpmevent18 is one, no count-overflow interrupt request is generated.
RULE 15: The OF bit of mhpmevent18 functions as a count-overflow interrupt disable for its associated hpmcounter.
RULE 16: Writes to mhpmevent18 or its associated mhpmcounter never cause a count overflow; overflow occurs only from hardware increments of the counter.
RULE 17: The count-overflow interrupt request generated by mhpmevent18 is mapped to local interrupt bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers, with the LCOFIP bits in mip/sip serving as pending bits and the LCOFIE bits in mie/sie serving as enable bits.
RULE 18: When a count-overflow interrupt request is generated by the hpmcounter associated with mhpmevent18, the OF bit of mhpmevent18 is set.
RULE 19: When the OF bit of mhpmevent18 is set, it eventually sets the LCOFIP bit in the mip and sip registers.
RULE 20: The mideleg register determines whether the overflow interrupt generated by mhpmevent18 is delegated to S-mode or remains in M-mode.
RULE 21: Enabling overflow interrupt generation for mhpmevent18 is achieved by clearing its OF bit while initializing the counter to a starting value.
RULE 22: After the counter associated with mhpmevent18 has overflowed, both the counter and its OF bit must be reinitialized before another overflow interrupt can be generated.
RULE 23: In M-mode, accessing mhpmevent18 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x332; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mideleg
NUMBER: 0x303
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 1..1=SSI, 2..2=VSSI, 3..3=MSI, 5..5=STI, 6..6=VSTI, 7..7=MTI, 9..9=SEI, 10..10=VSEI, 11..11=MEI, 12..12=SGEI, 13..13=LCOFI
EXTENSIONS: H, S, Smaia, Smcdeleg, Ssaia, Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The mideleg register is accessible in machine privilege mode for both read and write operations (MRW).
RULE 2: The mideleg register is an MXLEN-bit read/write register.
RULE 3: In harts that implement S-mode, the mideleg register must exist.
RULE 4: In harts that implement S-mode, setting a bit in mideleg delegates the corresponding trap that occurs in S-mode or U-mode to the S-mode trap handler.
RULE 5: An implementation may support only a subset of delegatable traps, and the supported delegatable bits in mideleg can be discovered by writing one to every bit position of mideleg and then reading back the value to see which bit positions retain a one.
RULE 6: If the supervisor timer interrupt is delegated to S-mode by setting mideleg[5], the supervisor timer interrupt will not be taken while executing in M-mode.
RULE 7: If mideleg[5] is clear, the supervisor timer interrupt can be taken in any mode and will always transfer control to M-mode regardless of the current mode.
RULE 8: The delegation control for the supervisor timer interrupt is located in bit 5 of mideleg.
RULE 9: An interrupt i traps to M-mode only if, when the mideleg register exists, bit i in mideleg is clear.
RULE 10: Setting a bit in the mideleg register delegates the corresponding interrupt to S-mode, making the interrupt visible in the sip register.
RULE 11: Setting a bit in the mideleg register makes the corresponding interrupt maskable via the sie register.
RULE 12: If a bit in the mideleg register is not set, the corresponding bits in sip and sie are read-only zero.
RULE 13: The mideleg register determines whether the count-overflow interrupt is delegated to S-mode or remains handled in M-mode.
RULE 14: The count-overflow interrupt that mideleg delegates is the local count overflow interrupt represented by bit 13 in the mip, mie, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 15: When the hypervisor extension is implemented, bits 10, 6, and 2 of mideleg are each read-only one.
RULE 16: For any bit of mideleg that is zero, the corresponding bits in hideleg, hip, and hie are read-only zeros.
RULE 17: If a trap occurring in HS-mode or U-mode is delegated by mideleg, the trap is taken to HS-mode instead of M-mode.
RULE 18: If a trap occurring in HS-mode or U-mode is not delegated by mideleg (and not delegated by medeleg), the trap is taken to M-mode.
RULE 19: In M-mode, accessing mideleg register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x303; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 20: In S-mode, accessing mideleg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x303; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 21: In U-mode, accessing mideleg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x303; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 22: In M-mode, setting mideleg.SSI (bit 1) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x303, a0; csrr a1, 0x303; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2].

REGISTER: mie
NUMBER: 0x304
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 1..1=SSIE, 2..2=VSSIE, 3..3=MSIE, 5..5=STIE, 6..6=VSTIE, 7..7=MTIE, 9..9=SEIE, 10..10=VSEIE, 11..11=MEIE, 12..12=SGEIE, 13..13=LCOFIE
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf
RULE 1: The mie CSR is a machine-read/write (MRW) register, meaning it can be read and written when the processor is in machine privilege mode.
RULE 2: mie is an MXLEN-bit read/write register that holds interrupt enable bits.
RULE 3: For each interrupt cause number i, bit i in mie corresponds to that cause.
RULE 4: An interrupt i can trap to M-mode only if its corresponding bit i in mie is set.
RULE 5: An explicit write to mie must cause immediate evaluation of interrupt-trap conditions.
RULE 6: Any bit in mie that is not writable must read as zero.
RULE 7: For any interrupt that is not delegated to S-mode via mideleg, the corresponding bit in the supervisor-level view of mie (the sie register) is read-only zero.
RULE 8: The sip and sie registers are subsets of the mip and mie registers.
RULE 9: Reading any implemented field of sie, or writing any writable field of sie, causes a read or write of the corresponding homonymous field of mie.
RULE 10: The count overflow interrupt is treated as a standard local interrupt and is assigned to bit 13 in the mie register.
RULE 11: Bit 13 of the mie register corresponds to the count overflow interrupt, which is also mapped to the same bit position in the mip, sip, and sie registers.
RULE 12: The LCOFIE bit (bit 13) in the mie register is the interrupt-enable bit for the local count overflow interrupt.
RULE 13: The delegation of the local count overflow interrupt between S-mode and M-mode is controlled by the mideleg register, which determines whether the interrupt enabled by the mie register's LCOFIE bit is taken in M-mode or delegated to S-mode.
RULE 14: If a program writes a 1 to bit 1 of the mie CSR, then a subsequent read of mie returns bit 1 cleared (zero).
RULE 15: The SGEIE bit in mie is an alias for the same bit in the hypervisor CSR hie.
RULE 16: The VSTIE bit in mie is an alias for the same bit in the hypervisor CSR hie.
RULE 17: In M-mode, accessing mie register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x304; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 18: In S-mode, accessing mie register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x304; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 19: In U-mode, accessing mie register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x304; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

RULE 1: The mimpid register is a Machine-mode Read-Only (MRO) register.
