REGISTER: minstret
NUMBER: 0xb02
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: H, Smcdeleg, Smcntrpmf, Smcsrind, Smstateen, Ssccfg, Sscsrind
RULE 1: The minstret CSR resides at address 0xB02 and counts the number of instructions retired in machine mode.
RULE 2: The minstret CSR holds the lower 32 bits of the machine instruction-retired counter.
RULE 3: minstret CSR counts the number of instructions the hart has retired.
RULE 4: minstret can be written with a given value.
RULE 5: A write to the minstret CSR takes effect only after the writing instruction has otherwise completed.
RULE 6: The instret CSR is a read-only shadow of the minstret register.
RULE 7: If the IR bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the instret CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception, preventing access to the minstret register.
RULE 8: If the IR bit in the mcounteren register is set, reads of the instret CSR are permitted in the next implemented privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode), allowing access to the minstret register.
RULE 9: Reading or writing the mcounteren register does not affect the underlying counters, and the minstret register continues to increment even when it is not accessible.
RULE 10: When the IR bit in the mcountinhibit register is clear, the minstret register increments as usual.
RULE 11: When the IR bit in the mcountinhibit register is set, the minstret register does not increment.
RULE 12: ECALL and EBREAK should not increment the minstret CSR.
RULE 13: If the SINH bit (bit 61) in the minstretcfg CSR is set to 1, the minstret counter does not increment for instructions executed in S-mode or HS-mode.
RULE 14: If the UINH bit (bit 60) in the minstretcfg CSR is set to 1, the minstret counter does not increment for instructions executed in U-mode.
RULE 15: The overflow (OF) bit at position 63 of the minstretcfg CSR is read-only zero, and no local-counter-overflow interrupt is generated for the minstret counter.
RULE 16: If minstretcfg is configured to inhibit a privilege mode, any instruction that retires while the CPU is executing in that inhibited mode must not increment minstret.
RULE 17: Instructions that cause a synchronous exception to a more-privileged mode are not considered to retire and must not increment minstret.
RULE 18: xRET instructions retire and should increment minstret only when the originating privilege mode is not inhibited by minstretcfg.
RULE 19: A load instruction that faults and therefore does not retire must not increment minstret.
RULE 20: Instructions executed in a privilege mode that is inhibited by minstretcfg must not increment minstret.
RULE 21: An xRET instruction that originates in a privilege mode inhibited by minstretcfg must not increment minstret even if it retires in a non-inhibited mode.
RULE 22: When a previously faulted load is re-executed and successfully retires, it must increment minstret.
RULE 23: If an instruction is emulated by software running in a privilege mode inhibited by minstretcfg, the emulation routine must increment minstret.
RULE 24: In M-mode, accessing minstret register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xb02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 25: In S-mode, accessing minstret register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xb02; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 26: In U-mode, accessing minstret register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xb02; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing minstret register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0xb02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing minstret register while Smcdeleg extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcdeleg; csrr a0, 0xb02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing minstret register while Smcntrpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcntrpmf; csrr a0, 0xb02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing minstret register while Smcsrind extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smcsrind; csrr a0, 0xb02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing minstret register while Smstateen extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smstateen; csrr a0, 0xb02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing minstret register while Ssccfg extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssccfg; csrr a0, 0xb02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 33: In M-mode, accessing minstret register while Sscsrind extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscsrind; csrr a0, 0xb02; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mip
NUMBER: 0x344
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 1..1=SSIP, 2..2=VSSIP, 3..3=MSIP, 5..5=STIP, 6..6=VSTIP, 7..7=MTIP, 9..9=SEIP, 10..10=VSEIP, 11..11=MEIP, 12..12=SGEIP, 13..13=LCOFIP
EXTENSIONS: H, Sscofpmf, Sstc
RULE 1: mip resides in the Machine privilege level.
RULE 2: mip has access type MRW, meaning it is readable and writable in Machine mode.
RULE 3: If the bit positions in mip do not match the corresponding bit positions in mideleg, then a read of the mip and mideleg CSRs will show at least one mismatched bit between them.
RULE 4: The supervisor-timer-interrupt-pending (STIP) field is located at bit 5 of the mip register.
RULE 5: An interrupt i traps to M-mode if bit i is set in both mip and mie (together with the other conditions on mstatus and mideleg).
RULE 6: If a program writes to mip and attempts to change a bit that is defined as read‑only, then after the write the readback of mip shows the original value for that bit (the write is ignored).
RULE 7: When a bit i in mip is writable, a pending interrupt i can be cleared by writing 0 to that bit.
RULE 8: mip.MEIP is read-only and is set and cleared by a platform-specific interrupt controller.
RULE 9: mip.MTIP is read-only and is cleared by writing to the memory-mapped machine-mode timer compare register.
RULE 10: mip.MSIP is read-only.
RULE 11: mip.SEIP is writable and may be written by M-mode software to indicate to S-mode that an external interrupt is pending.
RULE 12: When mip is read with a CSR instruction, the SEIP bit returned equals the logical-OR of the software bit and the external signal, and the external signal is not used to calculate the value written to SEIP.
RULE 13: Only the software-writable SEIP bit participates in the read-modify-write sequence of a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction on mip.
RULE 14: If a csrrs instruction targets the mip CSR, then after execution the SEIP bit in mip must equal the logical‑OR of its previous value and the external‑interrupt‑pending signal, and the software (SW) bit must equal the logical‑OR of its previous value and the rs1 bit; any deviation from these values is observable as an incorrect mip readback.
RULE 15: mip.SSIP is writable and may also be set to 1 by a platform-specific interrupt controller.
RULE 16: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, mip.LCOFIP is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from any mhpmevent n.OF bits being set.
RULE 17: Software-interrupt pending bits are located in the lowest four bits of mip, allowing the use of a single CSR instruction with a five-bit immediate because these bits are often written by software.
RULE 18: If an interrupt is delegated to S-mode by setting a bit in mideleg, the corresponding mip bit becomes visible in the sip register and is maskable using the sie register; otherwise the corresponding bits in sip and sie are read-only zero.
RULE 19: When the Sstc extension is implemented and the STCE field in menvcfg is zero, the STIP bit in mip must behave as defined for a system in which the Sstc extension is not implemented.
RULE 20: The mip register can be interrogated to determine the presence of any interrupt in machine mode.
RULE 21: Reading any implemented field of sip causes a read of the homonymous field of mip.
RULE 22: Writing any writable field of sip causes a write of the homonymous field of mip.
RULE 23: Bit 13 of the mip register is assigned to the new count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 24: The count-overflow interrupt represented by bit 13 in the mip register is treated as a standard local interrupt.
RULE 25: The count-overflow-interrupt-request signal is mapped to bit 13 of the mip register, where that bit represents the pending status of the Local Count Overflow Interrupt.
RULE 26: If the OF bit becomes set, then the LCOFIP bit in the mip CSR will eventually be set to 1 (the update may be delayed).
RULE 27: If the hypervisor extension is implemented, then raising any standard interrupt‑pending bit causes the corresponding bit to be set in mip [15:0] (and no standard interrupt‑pending bit appears in mip bits > 15).
RULE 28: The mip bits SGEIP, VSEIP, VSTIP, and VSSIP are aliases of the corresponding bits in the hypervisor CSR hip.
RULE 29: The alias relationship in the hypervisor CSR hip directly determines the values of the mip bits SGEIP, VSEIP, VSTIP, and VSSIP.
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing mip register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x344; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In S-mode, accessing mip register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x344; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 32: In U-mode, accessing mip register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x344; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 33: In M-mode, setting mip.SSIP (bit 1) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x344, a0; csrr a1, 0x344; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2].
RULE 34: In M-mode, setting mip.VSSIP (bit 2) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4; csrs 0x344, a0; csrr a1, 0x344; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4].
RULE 35: In M-mode, setting mip.MSIP (bit 3) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8; csrs 0x344, a0; csrr a1, 0x344; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 36: In M-mode, setting mip.STIP (bit 5) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x20) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x20; csrs 0x344, a0; csrr a1, 0x344; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x20].
RULE 37: In M-mode, setting mip.MTIP (bit 7) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x80) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x80; csrs 0x344, a0; csrr a1, 0x344; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x80].

REGISTER: misa
NUMBER: 0x301
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..62=MXL, 0..0=A, 1..1=B, 2..2=C, 3..3=D, 5..5=F, 6..6=G, 7..7=H, 8..8=I, 12..12=M, 16..16=Q, 18..18=S, 20..20=U, 21..21=V
EXTENSIONS: A, C, D, F, H, M, V
RULE 1: Implementations providing the misa register and supporting the V extension have the misa.v bit set.
RULE 2: The misa register has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege level.
RULE 3: The misa CSR is a WARL read-write register that reports the ISA supported by the hart.
RULE 4: The misa register must be readable in any implementation.
RULE 5: The MXL field of misa is read-only.
RULE 6: The I bit in the misa Extensions field will be set for the RV32I and RV64I base ISAs.
RULE 7: The Extensions field of misa is a WARL field that can contain writable bits where the implementation allows the supported ISA to be modified.
RULE 8: At reset, the Extensions field of misa shall contain the maximal set of supported extensions, and the I bit shall be selected over the E bit if both are available.
RULE 9: All bits of misa that are reserved for future use must return zero when read.
RULE 10: The X bit in the misa Extensions field will be set if any non-standard extensions are present.
RULE 11: When the B bit in misa is 1, the implementation supports the instructions provided by the Zba, Zbb, and Zbs extensions.
RULE 12: When the M bit in misa is 1, the implementation supports all multiply and division instructions defined by the M extension.
RULE 13: If the S bit in the misa CSR is 0, then any attempt to change to supervisor mode (e.g., by writing S to MPP and executing MRET or by executing a supervisor‑mode privileged instruction) raises an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 14: When the U bit in misa is 1, the implementation supports user mode.
RULE 15: The E bit in misa is read-only.
RULE 16: Unless misa is all read-only zero, the E bit in misa always reads as the complement of the I bit.
RULE 17: If an ISA feature x depends on an ISA feature y, then attempting to enable the x bit in misa while disabling the y bit results in both x and y bits being cleared in misa.
RULE 18: Setting the F bit to 0 and the D bit to 1 in misa results in both the F and D bits being cleared.
RULE 19: Setting the U bit to 0 and the S bit to 1 in misa results in both the U and S bits being cleared.
RULE 20: An attempt to write an unsupported combination of bits in misa causes those bits to be set to some supported combination.
RULE 21: If an instruction that would write misa increases IALIGN and the subsequent instruction's address is not aligned to the new IALIGN, the write to misa is suppressed, leaving misa unchanged.
RULE 22: If a bit in misa[25:0] is 1, then executing an instruction that requires the corresponding feature must not raise an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 23: In the MXL field of misa, the encoding value 1 corresponds to XLEN 32, the encoding value 2 corresponds to XLEN 64, and the encoding value 3 is reserved.
RULE 24: The encoding of the MXL field in the misa register is the same as the encoding used for the SXL and UXL fields in the mstatus register.
RULE 25: When the misa CSR is configured so that IALIGN = 32, bit mepc[1] is masked to 0 on all reads, including the implicit read performed by the MRET instruction.
RULE 26: When the misa CSR is configured so that IALIGN = 32, the bit mepc[1] remains writable despite being masked to 0 on reads.
RULE 27: Upon reset, the misa register is reset to enable the maximal set of supported extensions.
RULE 28: When misa.F = 1, the FCSR bit of the mstateen0 CSR is read-only zero.
RULE 29: When misa.F = 1, the FCSR bit of the hstateen0 and sstateen0 CSRs is read-only zero.
RULE 30: The hypervisor extension is enabled by setting bit 7 in the misa CSR, which corresponds to the letter H.
RULE 31: When HSXLEN = 64, the VSXL field in hstatus is a WARL field whose encoding follows the same encoding rules as the MXL field of the misa register.
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing misa register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x301; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 33: In S-mode, accessing misa register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x301; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 34: In U-mode, accessing misa register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x301; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: miselect
NUMBER: 0x350
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The CSR miselect is accessible at Machine privilege level with MRW access type.
RULE 2: If an illegal (unimplemented) value is written to the miselect CSR, then a subsequent read of miselect returns only a legal value (the written value masked or adjusted to the implemented field), and no exception is raised.
RULE 3: If a required miselect value for any implemented extension has a bit set beyond the most‑significant bit of the miselect CSR, then writing that value to the miselect CSR and reading it back will return a different (truncated) value, indicating that the CSR does not support the needed bits.
RULE 4: In M-mode, accessing miselect register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x350; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 5: In S-mode, accessing miselect register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x350; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 6: In U-mode, accessing miselect register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x350; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: mscratch
NUMBER: 0x340
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=SCRATCH
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The mscratch register has Machine-mode read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: mscratch is an MXLEN-bit read/write register dedicated for use by machine mode.
RULE 3: If a trap is taken into M‑mode, then on entry the mscratch CSR contains the value that was in the designated user register before the trap, and that user register now contains the value that mscratch held before the trap.
RULE 4: In M-mode, accessing mscratch register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x340; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 5: In S-mode, accessing mscratch register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x340; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 6: In U-mode, accessing mscratch register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x340; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: mseccfg
NUMBER: 0x747
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..34=WPRI, 33..32=PMM, 31..11=WPRI, 10..10=MLPE, 9..9=SSEED, 8..8=USEED, 7..3=WPRI, 2..2=RLB, 1..1=MMWP, 0..0=MML
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp, Smmpm, Zicfilp, Zkr
RULE 1: Implementations may implement mseccfg such that the [s,u]seed fields are a read-only constant value 0.
RULE 2: When mseccfg is implemented with the [s,u]seed fields as a read-only constant value 0, those fields read as 0 and are read-only.
RULE 3: If software writes a 1 to the [s,u]seed fields in mseccfg and subsequently reads them back, the read-back value indicates whether access to the seed CSR is enabled in U and S mode.
RULE 4: The mseccfg CSR is readable and writable in Machine mode (MRW privilege).
RULE 5: mseccfg is a 64-bit read/write register that controls security features and exists only if any extension that adds a field to mseccfg is implemented; otherwise it is reserved.
RULE 6: When mseccfg.USED = 0, any access to the seed CSR in U-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 7: When mseccfg.USED = 1, read-write access to the seed CSR from U-mode is allowed and all other types of accesses raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 8: When mseccfg.SSEED = 0, any access to the seed CSR from S-/HS-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 9: When mseccfg.SSEED = 1, read-write access to the seed CSR from S-/HS-mode is allowed and all other types of accesses raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 10: In machine mode, the seed CSR is always available as normal regardless of the values of the fields in mseccfg, and an attempted read without a write raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 11: When mseccfg.USED = 0, any seed CSR access from U-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: When mseccfg.USED = 1, the seed CSR is accessible as normal from U-mode and no exception is raised for read-write accesses.
RULE 13: When mseccfg.SSEED = 0, any seed CSR access from S-/HS-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 14: When mseccfg.SSEED = 1, the seed CSR is accessible as normal from S-/HS-mode and no exception is raised for read-write accesses.
RULE 15: When mseccfg.RLB = 0 and any pmpcfg.L bit is 1 in any rule or entry (including disabled entries), mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and further modifications to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 16: When mseccfg.MMWP is set, the default PMP policy for Machine mode for memory regions without a matching PMP rule changes to denied instead of ignored.
RULE 17: When mseccfg.MML is set, the interpretation of pmpcfg.L changes so that a set pmpcfg.L marks a rule as M-mode-only and an unset pmpcfg.L marks a rule as S/U-mode-only.
RULE 18: When mseccfg.MML is set, the formerly reserved encoding pmpcfg.RW = 01 and the encoding pmpcfg.LRWX = 1111 encode a Shared-Region.
RULE 19: When mseccfg.MML is set, an M-mode-only rule is enforced on Machine mode, denied on Supervisor or User mode, and remains locked so that further modifications to its configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 20: If mseccfg.MML is set and a Supervisor‑ or User‑mode‑only instruction is executed while the processor is in Machine mode, then an illegal‑instruction exception is raised (mcause = 2).
RULE 21: When mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg.L is not set, a Shared-Region rule can be used for sharing data between M-mode and S/U-mode, is not executable, provides read/write access to M-mode, and provides read access to S/U-mode if pmpcfg.X is not set or read/write access if pmpcfg.X is set.
RULE 22: When mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg.L is set, a Shared-Region rule can be used for sharing code between M-mode and S/U-mode, is not writable, provides execute access to both M-mode and S/U-mode, and provides additional read access to M-mode if pmpcfg.X is set.
RULE 23: When mseccfg.MML is set, the encoding pmpcfg.LRWX = 1111 can be used for sharing data between M-mode and S/U-mode where both modes have read-only access, and the rule remains locked unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 24: When mseccfg.MML is set, adding a PMP rule with executable privileges that is either M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region is not possible; such pmpcfg writes are ignored, leaving pmpcfg unchanged, and this restriction can be temporarily lifted by setting mseccfg.RLB.
RULE 25: When mseccfg.MML is set, executing code with Machine mode privileges is only possible from memory regions with a matching M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule with executable privileges; executing code from a region without a matching rule or with a matching S/U-mode-only rule is denied.
RULE 26: If the Smmpm extension is not implemented, the PMM field in mseccfg is read-only zero.
RULE 27: The PMM field in mseccfg is a WARL field whose legal values are 00 meaning pointer masking disabled (PMLEN = 0), 01 reserved, 10 meaning pointer masking enabled with PMLEN = XLEN-57 (7 on RV64), and 11 meaning pointer masking enabled with PMLEN = XLEN-48 (16 on RV64).
RULE 28: When mseccfg.MLPE = 1, the Zicfilp extension is enabled in Machine mode.
RULE 29: If the Zicfilp extension is implemented then the mseccfg.MLPE field MUST be reset to 0.
RULE 30: The MMWP field of the mseccfg register MUST be set to 0 on reset unless the platform mandates a different reset value.
RULE 31: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=0, X=0, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception because the region is inaccessible.
RULE 32: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=0, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region causes an Access Exception because the region is inaccessible.
RULE 33: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=0, X=1, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 34: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=0, X=1, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region is permitted as execute-only.
RULE 35: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=1, X=0, an access in M-mode to the region permits both read and write operations.
RULE 36: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=1, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region permits only read operations.
RULE 37: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=1, X=1, an access in M-mode to the region permits both read and write operations.
RULE 38: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=0, W=1, X=1, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region permits both read and write operations.
RULE 39: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=0, X=0, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 40: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=0, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region is permitted as a read-only region.
RULE 41: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=0, X=1, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 42: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=0, X=1, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region permits both read and execute operations.
RULE 43: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=1, X=0, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 44: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=1, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region permits both read and write operations.
RULE 45: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=1, X=1, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.
RULE 46: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=0, R=1, W=1, X=1, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region permits read, write, and execute operations.
RULE 47: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=0, W=0, X=0, an access in M-mode to the region causes an Access Exception because the region is a locked inaccessible region.
RULE 48: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=0, W=0, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region causes an Access Exception because the region is a locked inaccessible region.

RULE 56: When mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP entry has L=1, R=1, W=0, X=0, an access in S-mode or U-mode to the region causes an Access Exception.

REGISTER: mstateen0
NUMBER: 0x30c
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=SE0, 62..62=ENVCFG, 60..60=CSRIND, 59..59=AIA, 58..58=IMSIC, 57..57=CONTEXT, 56..56=P1P13, 55..55=SRMCFG, 54..54=CTR, 2..2=JVT, 1..1=FCSR, 0..0=C
EXTENSIONS: F, Sdtrig, Smcsrind, Smctr, Smstateen, Ssaia, Sscsrind, Ssctr, Ssqosid, Zcmt, Zdinx, Zfinx
RULE 1: The CSR mstateen0 is a machine-mode read/write register (privilege MRW).
RULE 2: Bits in mstateen0 that are defined to control state that a hart does not implement are read-only zeros for that hart.
RULE 3: All reserved bits in mstateen0 that have not been given a defined meaning are read-only zeros.
RULE 4: For every bit in mstateen0 that is zero, whether read-only zero or set to zero, the same bit appears as read-only zero in the matching hstateen0 and sstateen0 CSRs.
RULE 5: On reset, all writable bits of mstateen0 are initialized by hardware to zero.
RULE 6: Bit 63 of mstateen0 is defined to control access to the matching sstateen0 and hstateen0 CSRs.
RULE 7: A bit in sstateen0 cannot be read-only one unless the same bit is read-only one in mstateen0 and, if it exists, in hstateen0.
RULE 8: A bit in hstateen0 cannot be read-only one unless the same bit is read-only one in mstateen0.
RULE 9: If the C bit in mstateen0 is set and the program executes no custom instructions and does not access any custom state, then execution must not raise an illegal‑instruction exception and all standard instructions must produce the normal architectural results (e.g., destination registers contain the defined values and mcause is unchanged); raising an exception in this situation indicates non‑conforming hardware.
RULE 10: When misa.F = 1, the FCSR bit of mstateen0 is read-only zero.
RULE 11: The SE0 bit in mstateen0 controls access to the hstateen0, hstateen0h, and sstateen0 CSRs.
RULE 12: The ENVCFG bit in mstateen0 controls access to the henvcfg, henvcfgh, and senvcfg CSRs.
RULE 13: After reset, the writable bits of mstateen0 are zero.
RULE 14: The state-enable CSRs, including mstateen0, do not affect the accessibility of any state when execution is in M-mode; they affect accessibility only in privilege modes less privileged than M-mode.
RULE 15: When bit 60 of the CSR mstateen0 is not zero, access to a CSR is not blocked by that bit.
RULE 16: When Smstateen is implemented, the mstateen0.CTR bit controls access to CTR register state from privilege modes less privileged than M-mode.
RULE 17: When mstateen0.CTR = 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access sctrdepth raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 18: When mstateen0.CTR = 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access sctrstatus raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 19: When mstateen0.CTR = 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, execution of the SCTRCLR instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 20: When mstateen0.CTR = 0, hstateen0.CTR is read-only 0.
RULE 21: In M-mode, accessing mstateen0 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x30c; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 22: In S-mode, accessing mstateen0 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x30c; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 23: In U-mode, accessing mstateen0 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x30c; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: mstateen1
NUMBER: 0x30d
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=SE0
EXTENSIONS: Smstateen
RULE 1: If a read accesses CSR address 0x30D, the value returned is the current contents of the mstateen1 register; if a write targets CSR address 0x30D, the mstateen1 register is updated with the written value.
RULE 2: The architectural privilege level for accessing mstateen1 is MRW (machine-read/write).
RULE 3: The mstateen1 CSR controls access to state at all less-privileged privilege levels but does not control access at machine level itself.
RULE 4: If a bit that has a defined purpose in any sstateen CSR is not defined in mstateen1, then any attempt to read or write that bit in mstateen1 raises an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 5: The upper 32 bits of mstateen1 (bits 63-32) control access to state that is inherently inaccessible to user level, and therefore no corresponding enable bits exist in the supervisor-level sstateen CSR.
RULE 6: Bits in mstateen1 that are defined to control state not implemented by a hart, as well as all reserved bits not yet given a defined meaning, are read-only zeros for that hart.
RULE 7: For every bit in mstateen1 that is zero—whether a read-only zero or a writable zero—the same bit appears as a read-only zero in the matching hstateen1 and sstateen1 CSRs.
RULE 8: On reset, all writable bits of mstateen1 are initialized by hardware to zeros.
RULE 9: Bit 63 of mstateen1 is defined to control access to the matching sstateen1 and hstateen1 CSRs.
RULE 10: Bit 63 of mstateen1 may be a read-only zero only if the hypervisor extension is not implemented and the matching sstateen1 CSR is entirely read-only zeros; in that case, machine-level software should emulate attempts to access the affected sstateen1 from S-mode by ignoring writes and returning zero for reads.
RULE 11: After reset, all writable bits of the mstateen1 CSR are initialized to zero.
RULE 12: In M-mode, accessing mstateen1 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x30d; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 13: In S-mode, accessing mstateen1 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x30d; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 14: In U-mode, accessing mstateen1 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x30d; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 15: In M-mode, setting mstateen1.SE0 (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x30d, a0; csrr a1, 0x30d; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].
RULE 16: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the mstateen1 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x30d, a0; csrr a1, 0x30d; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 17: In M-mode, accessing mstateen1 register while Smstateen extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smstateen; csrr a0, 0x30d; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mstateen2
NUMBER: 0x30e
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=SE0
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The CSR at address 0x30E is named mstateen2 and has MRW privilege.
RULE 2: Each bit of mstateen2 controls less-privileged access to the state of the corresponding extension.
RULE 3: mstateen2 controls access to extension state for privilege modes below machine mode, but does not affect access for machine mode itself.
RULE 4: For any bit of mstateen2 that is defined to control state not implemented by a hart, that bit is a read-only zero for that hart.
RULE 5: All reserved bits of mstateen2 are read-only zeros.
RULE 6: For each bit of mstateen2 that is zero, the corresponding bit in hstateen2 and sstateen2 is a read-only zero.
RULE 7: A bit in sstateen2 cannot be read-only one unless the corresponding bit in mstateen2 is read-only one (and, if present, the corresponding bit in hstateen2 is also read-only one).
RULE 8: A bit in hstateen2 cannot be read-only one unless the corresponding bit in mstateen2 is read-only one.
RULE 9: After reset, all writable bits of mstateen2 are hardware-initialized to zero.
RULE 10: Bit 63 of mstateen2 controls access to sstateen2 and hstateen2.
RULE 11: After reset, all writable bits of the machine-level CSR mstateen2 are initialized to zero.
RULE 12: Machine-level software may write 1s to writable bits of mstateen2 to enable less-privileged access to the corresponding state.
RULE 13: When a writable bit of mstateen2 is written with a 1, the matching bit in the corresponding hstateen CSR, if that hstateen CSR exists, must be written with 0.
RULE 14: When a writable bit of mstateen2 is written with a 1 and the same-position bit exists in an sstateen CSR, the matching bit in that sstateen CSR must be written with 0.
RULE 15: When bit 63 of mstateen2 is written with a 1, all bits of the corresponding hstateen CSR must be written with 0.
RULE 16: In M-mode, accessing mstateen2 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x30e; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 17: In S-mode, accessing mstateen2 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x30e; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 18: In U-mode, accessing mstateen2 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x30e; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 19: In M-mode, setting mstateen2.SE0 (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x30e, a0; csrr a1, 0x30e; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].
RULE 20: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the mstateen2 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x30e, a0; csrr a1, 0x30e; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: mstateen3
NUMBER: 0x30f
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..63=SE0
EXTENSIONS: H, Smstateen, Ssstateen
RULE 1: The privilege encoding for mstateen3 is MRW, indicating that the register is machine-read/write accessible.
RULE 2: mstateen3 does not restrict machine-mode accesses and only restricts accesses from lower-privilege modes.
RULE 3: Bit 63 of mstateen3 controls access to the matching sstateen3 and hstateen3 CSRs.
RULE 4: Bit 63 of mstateen3 may be read-only zero only if the hypervisor extension is not implemented and sstateen3 is all read-only zeros.
RULE 5: After reset, every writable bit in mstateen3 is hardware-initialized to zero.
RULE 6: Any bit of mstateen3 that is defined to control state that the hart does not implement is read-only zero.
RULE 7: All reserved bits of mstateen3 that have not been given a defined meaning are read-only zero.
RULE 8: Any bit that is zero in mstateen3, whether read-only zero or writable zero, appears as a read-only zero in the matching sstateen3 and hstateen3 CSRs.
RULE 9: A read-only-one bit in sstateen3 requires the corresponding bit in mstateen3 to be read-only one.
RULE 10: A read-only-one bit in hstateen3 requires the corresponding bit in mstateen3 to be read-only one.
RULE 11: After reset, all writable bits of mstateen3 are initialized to zero.
RULE 12: In M-mode, accessing mstateen3 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x30f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 13: In S-mode, accessing mstateen3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x30f; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 14: In U-mode, accessing mstateen3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x30f; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 15: In M-mode, setting mstateen3.SE0 (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x30f, a0; csrr a1, 0x30f; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].
RULE 16: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the mstateen3 register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x30f, a0; csrr a1, 0x30f; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 17: In M-mode, accessing mstateen3 register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x30f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 18: In M-mode, accessing mstateen3 register while Smstateen extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smstateen; csrr a0, 0x30f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 19: In M-mode, accessing mstateen3 register while Ssstateen extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssstateen; csrr a0, 0x30f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mstatus
NUMBER: 0x300
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..63=SD, 42..42=MDT, 41..41=MPELP, 39..39=MPV, 38..38=GVA, 37..37=MBE, 36..36=SBE, 35..34=SXL, 33..32=UXL, 23..23=SPELP, 22..22=TSR, 21..21=TW, 20..20=TVM, 19..19=MXR, 18..18=SUM, 17..17=MPRV, 16..15=XS, 14..13=FS, 12..11=MPP, 10..9=VS, 8..8=SPP, 7..7=MPIE, 6..6=UBE, 5..5=SPIE, 3..3=MIE, 1..1=SIE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: If mstatus.VS equals Off and an attempt is made to execute any vector instruction or to access any vector CSR, an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 2: If mstatus.VS equals Initial or Clean and an instruction that changes vector state is executed (including accesses to vector CSRs), then mstatus.VS is changed to Dirty.
RULE 3: If mstatus.VS equals Dirty, then mstatus.SD is set to 1.
RULE 4: If mstatus.VS is Dirty, then mstatus.SD is 1.
RULE 5: If mstatus.VS is not Dirty, then the SD bit in mstatus must be 1 only when either mstatus.FS or mstatus.XS is Dirty; otherwise the SD bit must be 0.
RULE 6: If the mstatus.FS field is Off then any attempt to execute a vector floating-point instruction will raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 7: Any vector floating-point instruction that modifies any floating-point extension state must set the mstatus.FS field to Dirty.
RULE 8: The mstatus CSR is defined to be accessed at Machine privilege level.
RULE 9: The mstatus CSR has machine-read/write (MRW) access permissions.
RULE 10: The mstatush CSR is defined to be accessed at Machine privilege level.
RULE 11: The mstatush CSR has machine-read/write (MRW) access permissions.
RULE 12: If a program writes a value to the mstatus CSR, then a subsequent read of mstatus returns that value masked to MXLEN bits and the hart’s current operating state is updated according to the fields in the written value.
RULE 13: If a program writes a value V to mstatush bits 30:4 and then reads mstatus bits 62:36, the read value must be V; otherwise the CSR readback values differ, indicating a violation of the required mapping.
RULE 14: The fields SD, SXL, and UXL are not present in the mstatush register.
RULE 15: The global interrupt-enable bits MIE and SIE reside in the low-order bits of mstatus, permitting atomic set or clear with a single CSR instruction.
RULE 16: In mstatus, interrupt enable for any lower-privilege mode w (w < x) is always globally disabled irrespective of the value of the wIE bit.
RULE 17: If the processor is executing in privilege mode x and the mstatus yIE bit for any higher‑privilege mode y (y > x) is cleared, then an interrupt that would be handled in mode y is still taken, causing a trap to mode y with the appropriate mcause value.
RULE 18: If a program writes to the MPP field of mstatus with a value that has bits outside its two‑bit width, or writes to the SPP field with a value that has bits outside its one‑bit width, then reading back mstatus returns MPP containing only the low two bits of the written value and SPP containing only the low bit of the written value (all higher bits are cleared).
RULE 19: When a trap is taken from privilege mode y into privilege mode x, the mstatus field xPIE is set to the current value of xIE, the mstatus field xIE is cleared to 0, and the mstatus field xPP is written with y.
RULE 20: Executing an xRET instruction (MRET or SRET) sets the mstatus field xIE to the value of xPIE, changes the current privilege mode to the value stored in xPP, sets xPIE in mstatus to 1, writes xPP in mstatus with the least-privileged supported mode (U if U-mode is implemented, otherwise M), and, if the saved privilege mode y is not M, also clears the MPRV bit in mstatus.
RULE 21: The xPP fields in mstatus are WARL fields that may contain only privilege mode x or any implemented privilege mode lower than x, and if privilege mode x is not implemented, the xPP field must be read-only 0.
RULE 22: M-mode software can determine whether a privilege mode is implemented by writing that mode to the MPP field of mstatus and then reading it back.
RULE 23: The MIE bit in mstatus may be set to 1 by an explicit CSR write only if the MDT bit in mstatus is already 0, or, on RV64, if the MDT bit is being set to 0 by the same write.
RULE 24: When executed in M-mode, the SRET instruction sets the MDT bit in mstatus to 0.
RULE 25: In the mstatus register, the SXL and UXL fields are WARL fields that control the XLEN for S-mode and U-mode, respectively, on RV64 harts.
RULE 26: In the mstatus register, the encoding of the SXL and UXL fields is identical to the encoding of the MXL field in the misa register.
RULE 27: If MXLEN is 64 and S-mode is supported, the SXL field in the mstatus register is a WARL field that encodes the current SXLEN value.
RULE 28: If MXLEN is 64 and U-mode is supported, the UXL field in the mstatus register is a WARL field that encodes the current UXLEN value.
RULE 29: When S-mode is implemented, the set of legal values for the UXL field in the mstatus register excludes any encoding that would cause UXLEN to be greater than SXLEN.
RULE 30: If the XLEN value for any privilege mode, as configured by the corresponding fields in the mstatus register, is less than the widest supported XLEN, then all operations must ignore source operand register bits above the configured XLEN and must sign-extend results to fill the entire widest supported XLEN in the destination register.
RULE 31: If the XLEN for a privilege mode, as defined by the mstatus register, is less than the widest supported XLEN, then PC bits above XLEN are ignored and any write to the PC is sign-extended to fill the widest supported XLEN.
RULE 32: The architecture imposes no checks that lower-privilege XLEN settings, as specified by the mstatus fields, are less than or equal to the XLEN setting of the next-higher privilege mode.
RULE 33: When the MPRV bit in mstatus is 0, explicit memory accesses behave as normal, using the translation and protection mechanisms of the current privilege mode.
RULE 34: When the MPRV bit in mstatus is 1, load and store memory addresses are translated and protected, and endianness is applied as though the current privilege mode were set to MPP.
RULE 35: Instruction address-translation and protection are unaffected by the setting of the MPRV bit in mstatus.
RULE 36: An MRET or SRET instruction that changes the privilege mode to a mode less privileged than M also sets the MPRV bit in mstatus to 0.
RULE 37: When the MXR bit in mstatus is 0, only loads from pages marked readable (R=1) will succeed.
RULE 38: When the MXR bit in mstatus is 1, loads from pages marked either readable or executable (R=1 or X=1) will succeed.
RULE 39: When the SUM bit in mstatus is 0, S-mode memory accesses to pages that are accessible by U-mode (U=1) will fault.
RULE 40: SUM in mstatus has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.
RULE 41: SUM in mstatus is ordinarily ignored when not executing in S-mode, but it is in effect when MPRV=1 and MPP=S.
RULE 42: The SUM mechanisms encoded in mstatus have no impact on whether access-fault exceptions are raised due to PMP.
RULE 43: The MBE, SBE, and UBE bits are fields in mstatus and mstatush that control the endianness of memory accesses other than instruction fetches.
RULE 44: Instruction fetches are always little-endian and are not affected by the mstatus MBE, SBE, or UBE bits.
RULE 45: The mstatus.MBE bit controls the endianness of non-instruction-fetch memory accesses made from M-mode when mstatus.MPRV = 0.
RULE 46: When mstatus.MBE = 0, non-instruction-fetch memory accesses from M-mode are little-endian.
RULE 47: When mstatus.MBE = 1, non-instruction-fetch memory accesses from M-mode are big-endian.
RULE 48: The mstatus.SBE bit controls the endianness of explicit load and store memory accesses made from S-mode.
RULE 49: When mstatus.SBE = 0, explicit load and store memory accesses from S-mode are little-endian.
RULE 50: When mstatus.SBE = 1, explicit load and store memory accesses from S-mode are big-endian.
RULE 51: The mstatus.UBE bit controls the endianness of explicit load and store memory accesses made from U-mode.
RULE 52: When mstatus.UBE = 0, explicit load and store memory accesses from U-mode are little-endian.
RULE 53: When mstatus.UBE = 1, explicit load and store memory accesses from U-mode are big-endian.
RULE 54: When the TVM bit in mstatus is 1, attempts to read the satp CSR while executing in S-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 55: When the TVM bit in mstatus is 1, attempts to write the satp CSR while executing in S-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 56: When the TVM bit in mstatus is 1, attempts to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction while executing in S-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 57: When the TVM bit in mstatus is 0, attempts to read or write the satp CSR while executing in S-mode are permitted.
RULE 58: When the TVM bit in mstatus is 0, attempts to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction while executing in S-mode are permitted.
RULE 59: When the TVM bit in mstatus is 0, attempts to execute a SINVAL.VMA instruction while executing in S-mode are permitted.
RULE 60: The TW field in mstatus is a WARL field.
RULE 61: The TSR field in mstatus is a WARL field.
RULE 62: When the TSR bit in mstatus is 1, attempts to execute SRET while executing in S-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 63: When the TSR bit in mstatus is 0, attempts to execute SRET while executing in S-mode are permitted.
RULE 64: The mstatus register contains the FS[1:0] and VS[1:0] fields, which are WARL fields, and the XS[1:0] field, which is a read-only field.
RULE 65: The SD bit in mstatus is a read-only bit that summarizes whether either the FS, VS, or XS fields signal the presence of dirty state that will require saving extended user context to memory.
RULE 66: If the FS, VS, and XS fields in mstatus are all read-only zero, then the SD bit in mstatus is also always zero.
RULE 67: If the F extension is implemented, the FS field in mstatus shall not be read-only zero.
RULE 68: In harts without additional user extensions requiring new state, the XS field in mstatus is read-only zero.
RULE 69: Changing the setting of the FS field in mstatus has no effect on the contents of the floating-point register state.
RULE 70: Setting the FS field in mstatus to Off does not destroy the floating-point state, and setting the FS field to Initial does not clear the floating-point contents.
RULE 71: The FS field in mstatus is set directly by privileged code when resuming a user context, while the XS field in mstatus is set indirectly by writing to the status register of the individual extensions.
RULE 72: Machine mode and Supervisor mode share a single copy of the FS, VS, and XS bits in mstatus.
RULE 73: The SD bit in mstatus is read-only and is set when either the FS, VS, or XS bits in mstatus encode a Dirty state (i.e., SD = (FS==0b11 OR VS==0b11 OR XS==0b11)).
RULE 74: In mstatus, the encoding 0 for FS and VS means Off, 1 means Initial, 2 means Clean, and 3 means Dirty.
RULE 75: If the XS field in mstatus reads 0, then all extension states are off; if it reads 1, then no extensions are dirty and at least one extension is on; if it reads 2, then no extensions are dirty and at least one extension is clean; if it reads 3, then at least one extension is dirty.
RULE 76: When an extension's status field in mstatus is set to Off, any instruction that attempts to read or write the corresponding state causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 77: If the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Off, executing an instruction that reads the corresponding state causes an exception.
RULE 78: If the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Off, executing an instruction that may modify the corresponding state causes an exception.
RULE 79: If the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Initial, executing an instruction that may modify the corresponding state causes the field to transition to Dirty.
RULE 80: If the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Clean, executing an instruction that may modify the corresponding state causes the field to transition to Dirty.
RULE 81: If the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Dirty, executing an instruction that may modify the corresponding state leaves the field in the Dirty state.
RULE 82: If the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Off and an instruction that attempts to unconfigure the corresponding unit is executed, then an illegal‑instruction exception is raised.
RULE 83: If the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Initial, executing an instruction to unconfigure the unit leaves the field in the Initial state.
RULE 84: If the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Clean, executing an instruction to unconfigure the unit transitions the field to the Initial state.
RULE 85: If the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Dirty, executing an instruction to unconfigure the unit transitions the field to the Initial state.
RULE 86: If the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Off, executing an instruction to disable the unit leaves the field in the Off state.
RULE 87: If the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Initial, executing an instruction to disable the unit transitions the field to the Off state.
RULE 88: If the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Clean, executing an instruction to disable the unit transitions the field to the Off state.
RULE 89: If the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Dirty, executing an instruction to disable the unit transitions the field to the Off state.
RULE 90: Executing an instruction to enable a unit when the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Off transitions the field to the Initial state.
RULE 91: Executing an instruction to enable a unit when the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Initial leaves the field in the Initial state.
RULE 92: Executing an instruction to enable a unit when the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Clean transitions the field to the Initial state.
RULE 93: Executing an instruction to enable a unit when the FS, VS, or XS field in mstatus is Dirty transitions the field to the Initial state.
RULE 94: If the xPELP field (SPELP or MPELP) in the mstatus CSR reads 0, then the architectural state indicates NO_LP_EXPECTED; if it reads 1, then the architectural state indicates LP_EXPECTED.
RULE 95: When a trap is delegated to S-mode, the SPP field of mstatus is written with the active privilege mode at the time of the trap.
RULE 96: When a trap is delegated to S-mode, the SPIE field of mstatus is written with the value of the SIE field at the time of the trap.
RULE 97: When a trap is delegated to S-mode, the SIE field of mstatus is cleared.
RULE 98: When a trap is delegated to S-mode, the MPP and MPIE fields of mstatus are not written.
RULE 99: If the current privilege mode is M and the MIE bit in mstatus is set, an interrupt i will trap to M-mode, causing the privilege mode to change to M-mode.
RULE 100: If the current privilege mode has less privilege than M-mode, an interrupt i will trap to M-mode, causing the privilege mode to change to M-mode regardless of the MIE bit in mstatus.
RULE 101: After an explicit write to any CSR on which the interrupt-trap conditions expressly depend, including mstatus, the interrupt-trap conditions must be evaluated immediately.
RULE 102: After execution of an xRET instruction, the interrupt-trap conditions, which depend on mstatus, must be evaluated immediately.
RULE 103: If the TSR bit in the mstatus register is 1, execution of the SRET instruction should raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 104: A hart must resume execution when a locally enabled interrupt becomes pending even if the MIE or SIE bits in mstatus are 0.
RULE 105: Implementations should honor individual interrupt enable bits in mstatus such as MTIE and should avoid resuming the hart if an interrupt is pending but its individual enable bit is not set.
RULE 106: Upon reset, the mstatus fields MIE and MPRV are reset to 0.
RULE 107: If little-endian memory accesses are supported, then upon reset the mstatus or mstatush field MBE is reset to 0.
RULE 108: If the MPRV bit in mstatus is set and the MPP field in mstatus contains the value S or U, then PMP checks are applied to data accesses performed while the processor is in M-mode.
RULE 109: When NMIE is 0, the hart behaves as though the MPRV field of mstatus is cleared, regardless of the actual setting of mstatus.MPRV.
RULE 110: The SPP bit in mstatus indicates the privilege level at which a hart was executing before entering supervisor mode.
RULE 111: When a trap is taken, the SPP bit in mstatus is set to 0 if the trap originated from user mode, otherwise it is set to 1.
RULE 112: When an SRET instruction is executed, the privilege level is set to user mode if the SPP bit in mstatus is 0, otherwise to supervisor mode if the SPP bit in mstatus is 1, and then the SPP bit in mstatus is set to 0.
RULE 113: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, the SPIE bit in mstatus is set to the value of the SIE bit in mstatus, and the SIE bit in mstatus is set to 0.
RULE 114: When an SRET instruction is executed, the SIE bit in mstatus is set to the value of the SPIE bit in mstatus, then the SPIE bit in mstatus is set to 1.
RULE 115: In a straightforward implementation, reading or writing any field in sstatus is equivalent to reading or writing the homonymous field in mstatus.
RULE 116: When the V bit is zero, any access to the SPELP field defined by the Zicfilp extension accesses the homonymous fields of the mstatus register.
RULE 117: The SUM field of the mstatus register is consulted when determining whether a requested memory access is allowed by the pte.u bit.
RULE 118: The MXR field of the mstatus register is consulted when determining whether a requested memory access is allowed by the pte.u bit.
RULE 119: If the decision, which uses the current privilege mode and the SUM and MXR fields of the mstatus register, determines that the access is not allowed, the implementation MUST stop and raise a page-fault exception corresponding to the original access type.
RULE 120: If mstatus.TVM=1, an attempt to execute SINVAL.VMA or HINVAL.GVMA in S-mode or HS-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 121: When mstatus.TVM=1 (or hstatus.VTVM=1), SFENCE.W.INVAL and SFENCE.INVAL.IR instructions do not need to be trapped because they have only ordering effects and no visible side effects.
RULE 122: The MPRV feature in the mstatus register can be used to execute a load or store as though the V bit is 1.
RULE 123: mstatus.TVM does not cause HFENCE.VVMA to trap.
RULE 124: HFENCE.GVMA is valid only in HS-mode when mstatus.TVM = 0.
RULE 125: HFENCE.GVMA is valid in M-mode irrespective of the value of mstatus.TVM.
RULE 126: Executing HFENCE.GVMA in HS-mode when mstatus.TVM = 1 causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 127: MPV is written by the implementation whenever a trap is taken into M-mode.
RULE 128: GVA is written by the implementation whenever a trap is taken into M-mode.
RULE 129: If the TW field of mstatus is set and a WFI instruction executes while the processor is in any privilege mode other than M‑mode, then an illegal‑instruction exception is taken (mcause = illegal‑instruction).
RULE 130: When MPRV = 0 in mstatus, translation and protection behave as normal.
RULE 131: When MPRV = 1 in mstatus, explicit memory accesses are translated and protected, and endianness is applied as though the current virtualization mode were MPV and the current nominal privilege mode were MPP.
RULE 132: If mstatus.MPRV = 1, mstatus.MPV = 0, and mstatus.MPP = 0, then an explicit load, store, or atomic memory instruction is translated using the HS‑mode address‑translation tables (satp) but the access check is performed with U‑level privileges; if the U‑level access check fails, the instruction raises the corresponding load/store page‑fault or access‑fault exception (mcause set to the appropriate fault code).
RULE 133: When MPRV = 1, MPV = 0, and MPP = 1 in mstatus, explicit memory accesses are treated as HS-level accesses with HS-level translation and protection only.
RULE 134: When MPRV = 1 and MPP = 3 in mstatus (MPV value is ignored), explicit memory accesses are treated as M-level accesses with no translation.
RULE 135: MPRV in mstatus does not affect the virtual-machine load/store instructions HLV, HLVX, and HSV.
RULE 136: The explicit loads and stores of the HLV, HLVX, and HSV instructions always act as though V = 1 and the nominal privilege mode were hstatus.SPVP, overriding the effect of MPRV in mstatus.
RULE 137: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the MPV field in mstatus (or mstatush) is set to 0 if the previous privilege mode was U-mode.
RULE 138: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the MPP field in mstatus (or mstatush) is set to 0 if the previous privilege mode was U-mode.
RULE 139: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the MPV field in mstatus (or mstatush) is set to 0 if the previous privilege mode was HS-mode.
RULE 140: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the MPP field in mstatus (or mstatush) is set to 1 if the previous privilege mode was HS-mode.
RULE 141: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the MPV field in mstatus (or mstatush) is set to 0 if the previous privilege mode was M-mode.
RULE 142: When a trap is taken into M-mode, the MPP field in mstatus (or mstatush) is set to 3 if the previous privilege mode was M-mode.
RULE 143: When returning from a trap, the MPV field in mstatus is ignored if the MPP field in mstatus equals 3.
RULE 144: When the MRET instruction is executed, the new privilege mode is determined from the values of the MPP and MPV fields in mstatus or mstatush as specified by the architecture.
RULE 145: When the MRET instruction is executed, the MPV field in mstatus or mstatush is set to 0.
RULE 146: When the MRET instruction is executed, the MPP field in mstatus or mstatush is set to 0.
RULE 147: When the MRET instruction is executed, the MIE field in mstatus or mstatush is written with the current value of the MPIE field.
RULE 148: When the MRET instruction is executed, the MPIE field in mstatus or mstatush is set to 1.
RULE 149: The SPELP bit in mstatus can be accessed through the sstatus CSR.
RULE 150: When a trap is taken into privilege mode x, the x PELP bit in mstatus is set to the current ELP value.
RULE 151: In M-mode, accessing mstatus register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x300; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mtinst
NUMBER: 0x34a
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: H
RULE 1: If a transformed instruction encodes a non‑zero Addr. Offset field but the effective address is aligned, then the instruction raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = 2).
RULE 2: The special pseudoinstruction encoding 0x00002003 (and 0x00002023) corresponds to the instruction lw x0,0(x0).
RULE 3: The special pseudoinstruction encodings 0x00003003 and 0x00003023 also correspond to the 64-bit instructions ld x0,0(x0) and sd x0,0(x0) respectively.

REGISTER: mtval
NUMBER: 0x343
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: H, Smdbltrp, Smrnmi, Zicfilp, Zicfiss
RULE 1: The mtval CSR is machine-read/write (MRW) privileged, meaning it can be read and written when the processor is in machine mode.
RULE 2: When a trap is delegated to S-mode, the mtval register is not written.
RULE 3: If a program writes a value to the mtval CSR that contains bits beyond the current MXLEN, then reading mtval returns only the lower MXLEN bits of the written value (any higher bits are discarded).
RULE 4: When a trap is taken into M-mode, mtval is either set to zero or written with exception-specific information to assist software in handling the trap.
RULE 5: When a trap is not taken into M-mode, mtval is never written by the implementation, though it may be explicitly written by software.
RULE 6: If the hardware platform specifies that no exceptions set mtval to a non-zero value, then mtval is read-only zero.
RULE 7: If mtval is written with a non-zero value when a breakpoint, address-misaligned, access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on an instruction fetch, load, or store, then mtval will contain the faulting virtual address.
RULE 8: On a breakpoint exception raised by an EBREAK or C.EBREAK instruction, mtval is written with either zero or the virtual address of the instruction.
RULE 9: When page-based virtual memory is enabled, mtval is written with the faulting virtual address even for physical-memory access-fault exceptions.
RULE 10: If mtval is written with a non-zero value when a misaligned load or store causes an access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception, then mtval will contain the virtual address of the portion of the access that caused the fault.
RULE 11: If mtval is written with a non-zero value when an instruction access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on a hart with variable-length instructions, then mtval will contain the virtual address of the portion of the instruction that caused the fault, while mepc will point to the beginning of the instruction.
RULE 12: If mtval is written with a non-zero value when an illegal-instruction exception occurs, then mtval will contain the shortest of the actual faulting instruction, the first ILEN bits of the faulting instruction, or the first MXLEN bits of the faulting instruction.
RULE 13: The value loaded into mtval on an illegal-instruction exception is right-justified and all unused upper bits are cleared to zero.
RULE 14: The entire instruction (or at least the first MXLEN bits) must be fetched into mtval before taking the trap.
RULE 15: On a trap caused by a software-check exception, mtval holds the cause for the exception with the defined encodings 0 for no information provided, 2 for Landing Pad Fault, and 3 for Shadow Stack Fault.
RULE 16: If a trap that does not have a defined non‑zero mtval value is taken, then the mtval CSR is written with zero.
RULE 17: If mtval is not read-only zero, it is a WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual addresses and the value zero.
RULE 18: If the feature to return the faulting instruction bits is implemented, mtval must also be able to hold all values less than 2^N, where N is the smaller of MXLEN and ILEN.
RULE 19: The CSR mtval must not be a read-only zero register.
RULE 20: The GVA field of mtval is written by the implementation whenever a trap is taken into M-mode.
RULE 21: On breakpoint, address-misaligned, access-fault, page-fault, or guest-page-fault traps, mtval is written with the guest virtual address that caused the trap.
RULE 22: In M-mode, accessing mtval register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x343; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 23: In S-mode, accessing mtval register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x343; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 24: In U-mode, accessing mtval register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x343; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 25: In M-mode, setting mtval.VALUE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x343, a0; csrr a1, 0x343; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 26: In M-mode, accessing mtval register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x343; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing mtval register while Smdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x343; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: mtvec
NUMBER: 0x305
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..2=BASE, 1..0=MODE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The mtvec register is a Machine-mode CSR that is both readable and writable (MRW).
RULE 2: If a write to the mtvec CSR contains a MODE field that is not a supported mode or a BASE address that is not aligned as required, then a subsequent read of mtvec returns a value with a legal MODE (e.g., 0) and an aligned BASE, and no exception is raised.
RULE 3: The mtvec register must always be implemented.
RULE 4: The value in the BASE field of mtvec must always be aligned on a 4-byte boundary.
RULE 5: When the BASE field of mtvec is used as an address, the lower two bits are filled with zeroes to obtain an XLEN-bit address that is always aligned on a 4-byte boundary.
RULE 6: A mtvec MODE field value of 0 is named Direct and specifies that all traps set the pc to BASE.
RULE 7: When mtvec MODE = Direct, all traps into machine mode cause the pc to be set to the address in the BASE field.
RULE 8: When mtvec MODE = Vectored, all synchronous exceptions into machine mode cause the pc to be set to the address in the BASE field.
RULE 9: For a machine-mode timer interrupt with interrupt cause 2, mtvec causes the pc to be set to BASE + 0x1c (i.e., BASE + 4 × 2 + 4-byte offset for the cause field).
RULE 10: In M-mode, accessing mtvec register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x305; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 11: In S-mode, accessing mtvec register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x305; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 12: In U-mode, accessing mtvec register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x305; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 13: In M-mode, setting mtvec.BASE (bit 2) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4; csrs 0x305, a0; csrr a1, 0x305; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4].

RULE 15: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the mtvec register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x305, a0; csrr a1, 0x305; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
