RULE 6: In M-mode, setting mvip.WPRI (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x309, a0; csrr a1, 0x309; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 7: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the mvip register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x309, a0; csrr a1, 0x309; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 8: In M-mode, accessing mvip register while Smaia extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smaia; csrr a0, 0x309; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 9: In M-mode, accessing mvip register while Ssaia extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssaia; csrr a0, 0x309; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr0
NUMBER: 0x3b0
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr0[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of pmpaddr0[G-1] returns 0.
RULE 2: Executing CSRRC or CSRRS to modify a different bit will cause 0 to be read from pmpaddr0[G-1] and then written back, updating the underlying value to 0.
RULE 3: If an instruction executing at a privilege level lower than machine mode reads or writes pmpaddr0, then the core raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = 2); otherwise, in machine mode the CSR read returns the stored value and a write updates it.
RULE 4: In RV64, pmpaddr0 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 5: pmpaddr0 is a WARL register because not all physical address bits may be implemented.
RULE 6: pmpaddr0 is only accessible to M-mode.
RULE 7: pmpaddr0 exists only if at least one PMP entry is implemented.
RULE 8: If the PMP entry 0 configuration field A is set to TOR, the lower bound is zero and the entry matches any address y that is less than pmpaddr0.
RULE 9: If pmpaddr0 is zero and the PMP entry 0 configuration field A is TOR, then PMP entry 0 matches no addresses.
RULE 10: In NAPOT mode, the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 encode the size of the matched range according to the pattern of trailing zeros and ones defined in Table 24.
RULE 11: When the PMP granularity G is at least 2 and the configuration field pmpcfg0.A[1] is set (indicating NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr0[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 12: When the PMP granularity G is at least 1 and the configuration field pmpcfg0.A[1] is clear (indicating OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr0[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 13: The bits pmpaddr0[G-1:0] do not affect the address-matching logic when the entry operates in TOR mode.
RULE 14: Changing the configuration field pmpcfg0.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr0 but does not change the underlying stored value, and consequently pmpaddr0[G-1] retains its original value when the entry is switched from NAPOT to TOR/OFF and back to NAPOT.
RULE 15: Software may determine the PMP granularity by writing zero to pmp0cfg, writing all ones to pmpaddr0, reading back pmpaddr0, and interpreting the index G of the least-significant set bit such that the granularity equals 2^G + 2 bytes.
RULE 16: If PMP entry 0 is locked, any write to pmpaddr0 is ignored.
RULE 17: The lock on PMP entry 0 causes the associated address register pmpaddr0 to be ignored.
RULE 18: If PMP entry 1 is locked and pmp1 cfg.A is set to TOR, any write to pmpaddr0 is ignored.
RULE 19: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 0 locks the entry even when its A field is OFF, and consequently any write to pmpaddr0 is ignored.
RULE 20: For the PMP entry containing pmpaddr0 to be valid, the A field of the associated pmpcfg0 register MUST NOT be OFF.
RULE 21: If the address-matching mode A of pmpcfg1 is TOR, then pmpaddr0 MUST be less than pmpaddr1.
RULE 22: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr0 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3b0; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 23: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr0 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3b0; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 24: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr0 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3b0; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 25: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr0.ADDR (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3b0, a0; csrr a1, 0x3b0; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 26: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr0 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3b0; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr1
NUMBER: 0x3b1
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr1[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of that bit returns 0.
RULE 2: If a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction targets any bit of pmpaddr1 other than the G-1 bit, the operation will read the G-1 bit as 0 and then write that 0 back, causing the underlying G-1 bit value to become 0.
RULE 3: If pmpaddr1 is not set to grant machine‑mode read‑write permission, then a machine‑mode load from or store to an address within the pmpaddr1 range raises a load or store access‑fault exception (mcause = 12 for a load, 13 for a store).
RULE 4: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr1 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 5: pmpaddr1 is a WARL register because not all physical address bits may be implemented.
RULE 6: Some PMP settings additionally use the address register of the preceding PMP entry, and when such a setting applies to PMP entry 2, the value stored in pmpaddr1 directly determines the address used for that PMP entry.
RULE 7: If pmpcfg1.A = NA4, then a value of the form yyyy…yyyy in pmpaddr1 encodes a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 8: If pmpcfg1.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr1 has the form yyyy…yyy0, then it encodes an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 9: If pmpcfg1.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr1 has the form yyyy…yy01, then it encodes a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg1.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr1 has the form yyyy…y011, then it encodes a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: If pmpcfg1.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr1 has the form yy01…1111, then it encodes a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg1.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr1 has the form y011…1111, then it encodes a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If pmpcfg1.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr1 has the form 0111…1111, then it encodes a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If pmpcfg1.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr1 has the form 1111…1111, then it encodes a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: If pmpcfg1.A = TOR, then pmpaddr1 forms the top of the address range and the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr0 ≤ y < pmpaddr1 irrespective of the value of pmpcfg0.A.
RULE 16: If pmpcfg1.A = TOR and pmpaddr0 ≥ pmpaddr1, then PMP entry 1 matches no addresses.
RULE 17: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg1.A[1] is set, then bits pmpaddr1[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 18: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg1.A[1] is clear, then bits pmpaddr1[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 19: Bits pmpaddr1[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 20: Changing pmpcfg1.A[1] affects the value read from pmpaddr1 but does not affect the underlying stored value in pmpaddr1; in particular pmpaddr1[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg1.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF then back to NAPOT.
RULE 21: When G ≥ 1, the NA4 mode is not selectable; therefore pmpaddr1 cannot be used in NA4 mode when G ≥ 1.
RULE 22: If PMP entry 1 is locked, writes to pmpaddr1 are ignored.
RULE 23: When the L bit in pmp1cfg is set, PMP entry 1 is considered locked, causing writes to pmpaddr1 to be ignored.
RULE 24: If pmpcfg1.A is TOR, then pmpaddr1 MUST be greater than pmpaddr0.
RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr1 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3b1; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 26: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr1 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3b1; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 27: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr1 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3b1; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 28: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr1.ADDR (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3b1, a0; csrr a1, 0x3b1; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr1 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3b1; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr1 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3b1; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr2
NUMBER: 0x3b2
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: The most-significant bit of pmpaddr2 (pmpaddr2[G-1]) may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of pmpaddr2 returns 0 for that bit.
RULE 2: Executing CSRRC or CSRRS on pmpaddr2 to modify a bit other than pmpaddr2[G-1] will cause a read of 0 from pmpaddr2[G-1].
RULE 3: Executing CSRRC or CSRRS on pmpaddr2 to modify a bit other than pmpaddr2[G-1] will write back that 0, updating the underlying value of pmpaddr2[G-1] to 0.
RULE 4: pmpaddr2 is accessible with machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 5: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr2 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 6: The value of pmpaddr2 is a WARL field because implementations may not implement all physical address bits.
RULE 7: Access to the pmpaddr2 CSR is permitted only in M-mode.
RULE 8: If PMP entry 2's A field is set to TOR, then pmpaddr2 forms the top of the address range and pmpaddr1 forms the bottom of the address range.
RULE 9: When the A field of entry 2 is TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr1 ≤ y < pmpaddr2, independent of the value of pmpcfg1.
RULE 10: If pmpaddr1 ≥ pmpaddr2 and pmpcfg2.A = TOR, then PMP entry 2 matches no addresses.
RULE 11: If pmpaddr2 bits are all y (yyyy…yyyy) and pmpcfg2.A = NA4, then the entry defines a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If pmpaddr2 bits match the pattern yyyy…yyy0 and pmpcfg2.A = NAPOT, then the entry defines an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If pmpaddr2 bits match the pattern yyyy…yy01 and pmpcfg2.A = NAPOT, then the entry defines a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If pmpaddr2 bits match the pattern yyyy…y011 and pmpcfg2.A = NAPOT, then the entry defines a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: If pmpaddr2 bits match the pattern yy01…1111 and pmpcfg2.A = NAPOT, then the entry defines a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 16: If pmpaddr2 bits match the pattern y011…1111 and pmpcfg2.A = NAPOT, then the entry defines a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 17: If pmpaddr2 bits match the pattern 0111…1111 and pmpcfg2.A = NAPOT, then the entry defines a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 18: If pmpaddr2 bits match the pattern 1111…1111 and pmpcfg2.A = NAPOT, then the entry defines a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 19: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg2.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr2[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 20: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg2.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr2[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 21: Bits pmpaddr2[G-1:0] do not affect TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 22: Changing pmpcfg2.A[1] alters the value read from pmpaddr2 but does not modify the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr2[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg2.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 23: The PMP granularity is 2^G + 2 bytes and must be identical for all PMP regions, therefore the same G applies to pmpaddr2.
RULE 24: If PMP entry 2 is locked, writes to pmpaddr2 are ignored.
RULE 25: When the L bit of PMP entry 2 is set, writes to pmpaddr2 are ignored.
RULE 26: Locked PMP entry 2 remains locked until the hart is reset, therefore writes to pmpaddr2 remain ignored until a hart reset occurs.
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr2 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3b2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 28: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr2 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3b2; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 29: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr2 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3b2; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 30: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr2.ADDR (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3b2, a0; csrr a1, 0x3b2; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr2 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3b2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr3
NUMBER: 0x3b3
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: M, Smepmp
RULE 1: The G-1 bit of the pmpaddr3 CSR may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of pmpaddr3 returns 0 for that bit.
RULE 2: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction that modifies a bit of pmpaddr3 other than the G-1 bit causes the hardware to read the G-1 bit of pmpaddr3 as 0 and then write back 0, updating the underlying value of pmpaddr3[G-1] to 0.
RULE 3: Because not all physical address bits are required to be implemented, the pmpaddr registers are WARL, and the value read from or written to pmpaddr3 may be altered by the implementation to reflect only the implemented bits.
RULE 4: When pmpcfg3.A is set to NAPOT, the low-order bits of pmpaddr3 encode the size of the range according to the NAPOT encoding.
RULE 5: A pmpaddr3 value ending in "…0" selects an 8-byte NAPOT range, and a value ending in "…01" selects a 16-byte NAPOT range, with larger patterns selecting proportionally larger powers-of-two sizes.
RULE 6: When pmpcfg3.A is TOR, pmpaddr3 defines the top of the address range for PMP entry 3, while pmpaddr2 defines the bottom of the range.
RULE 7: When pmpcfg3.A is TOR, PMP entry 3 matches any address y such that pmpaddr2 ≤ y < pmpaddr3, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg2.A.
RULE 8: When pmpcfg3.A is TOR and pmpaddr2 is greater than or equal to pmpaddr3, PMP entry 3 matches no addresses.
RULE 9: If the PMP granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg3.A[1] is 1 (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr3[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 10: If the PMP granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg3.A[1] is 0 (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr3[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 11: In TOR mode, bits pmpaddr3[G-1:0] do not affect the address-matching logic.
RULE 12: Changing pmpcfg3.A[1] alters the value read from pmpaddr3 but does not modify the underlying stored value of pmpaddr3.
RULE 13: The bit pmpaddr3[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg3.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 14: If PMP entry 3 is locked, writes to pmpaddr3 are ignored.
RULE 15: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr3 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3b3; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 16: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3b3; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 17: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr3 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3b3; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 18: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr3.ADDR (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3b3, a0; csrr a1, 0x3b3; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 19: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr3 register while M extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: M; csrr a0, 0x3b3; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 20: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr3 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3b3; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr4
NUMBER: 0x3b4
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr4[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 but be read as 0.
RULE 2: Executing a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that modifies a bit other than G-1 of pmpaddr4 will cause a read of 0 from pmpaddr4[G-1] and will write back 0, updating the underlying value of pmpaddr4[G-1] to 0.
RULE 3: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its source register rs1 is x0, the instruction shall not write to pmpaddr4 and shall not cause any side effects that would occur on a CSR write, nor shall it raise an illegal-instruction exception on a read-only pmpaddr4.
RULE 4: A CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that targets pmpaddr4 shall always read pmpaddr4 and shall cause any read side effects regardless of the values of rs1 and rd.
RULE 5: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction accesses pmpaddr4 with rs1 specifying a register other than x0 that contains the value zero, the instruction will not action any per-field side effects but will action any side effects caused by writing the entire pmpaddr4.
RULE 6: A CSRRW instruction that accesses pmpaddr4 with rs1 equal to x0 will attempt to write zero to pmpaddr4.
RULE 7: When a CSRRW instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its destination register rd is not x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 8: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its source register rs1 is x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall not write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 9: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its source register rs1 is not x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 10: When a CSRRWI instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its destination register rd is x0, the instruction shall not read pmpaddr4 but shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 11: When a CSRRWI instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its destination register rd is not x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 12: When a CSRRSI or CSRRCI instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its immediate rs1 (uimm) is zero, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall not write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 13: When a CSRRSI or CSRRCI instruction targets pmpaddr4 and its immediate rs1 (uimm) is non-zero, the instruction shall read pmpaddr4 and shall write to pmpaddr4.
RULE 14: If pmpaddr4 is written by a CSRRW or CSRRWI instruction, then the PMP address matching for region 4 is updated to the written value, causing any subsequent memory access that is disallowed by the new PMP configuration to raise an access‑fault exception.
RULE 15: When pmpaddr4 is written by a CSRRS, CSRRC, CSRRSI, or CSRRCI instruction, side effects shall be enacted only for those fields of pmpaddr4 whose corresponding bits are set in the rs1 register or uimm argument.
RULE 16: pmpaddr4 can be accessed only while the hart is in M-mode.
RULE 17: When pmpcfg4.A = NAPOT, bits pmpaddr4 encode the NAPOT range size as follows: pattern …yyy0 selects an 8-byte range, …yy01 selects a 16-byte range, …y011 selects a 32-byte range, …yy01…1111 selects a 2 XLEN-byte range, …y011…1111 selects a 2 XLEN+1-byte range, 0111…1111 selects a 2 XLEN+2-byte range, and 1111…1111 selects a 2 XLEN+3-byte range.
RULE 18: When pmpcfg4.A = NA4, the value of pmpaddr4 is ignored and the entry defines a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 19: When pmpcfg4.A = TOR, pmpaddr4 defines the top address of the TOR range and the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr3 ≤ y < pmpaddr4, irrespective of pmpcfg3.
RULE 20: If pmpaddr3 ≥ pmpaddr4 and pmpcfg4.A = TOR, then PMP entry 4 matches no addresses.
RULE 21: When the granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg4.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr4[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 22: When the granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg4.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr4[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 23: Bits pmpaddr4[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 24: Changing pmpcfg4.A[1] alters the read-value of pmpaddr4 but does not change the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr4[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg4.A changes from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 25: When the granularity G is at least 1, the NA4 mode is not selectable, so pmpaddr4 cannot be used with pmpcfg4.A = 2 (NA4) in such implementations.
RULE 26: If PMP entry 4 is locked, any write to the address register pmpaddr4 has no effect and is ignored.
RULE 27: If PMP entry 4 is locked and its configuration register pmp4 cfg specifies address-matching mode TOR, any write to the preceding address register pmpaddr4-1 is ignored.
RULE 28: Setting the L bit in pmp4 cfg locks PMP entry 4 regardless of the value of pmp4 cfg.A (including OFF), causing subsequent writes to pmpaddr4 to be ignored.
RULE 29: When the L bit in pmp4 cfg is set, the R, W, and X permission checks associated with entry 4 are enforced for M-mode accesses that match pmpaddr4 as well as for S- and U-mode accesses.
RULE 30: When the L bit in pmp4 cfg is clear, M-mode accesses that match entry 4 as defined by pmpaddr4 succeed irrespective of the R, W, and X permission bits, while S- and U-mode accesses that match pmpaddr4 are still subject to those permission checks.
RULE 31: pmpaddr3 MUST be less than pmpaddr4 when the address-matching mode field A of pmpcfg4 is TOR.
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr4 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3b4; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 33: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3b4; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 34: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3b4; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 35: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr4.ADDR (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3b4, a0; csrr a1, 0x3b4; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr4 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3b4; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 37: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr4 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3b4; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr5
NUMBER: 0x3b5
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: M, Smepmp
RULE 1: The most-significant bit (bit G-1) of pmpaddr5 may have an underlying value of 1 but read as 0.
RULE 2: If pmpaddr5 CSR is accessed when the current privilege level is not Machine, then an illegal‑instruction exception is raised (mcause = 2).
RULE 3: If a privilege mode other than Machine attempts to read or write the CSR pmpaddr5, then the core raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = 2); when accessed in Machine mode, reads return the current register value and writes update pmpaddr5.
RULE 4: pmpaddr5 can be read or written only while executing in M-mode.
RULE 5: pmpaddr5 is a Write-Any-Values-Read-Legal (WARL) register; any value written to pmpaddr5 is permitted, while a read of pmpaddr5 may return a value that reflects only the subset of address bits implemented.
RULE 6: When the low-order bits of pmpaddr5 are all ones (pattern yyyy…yyyy) and pmpcfg5.A encodes NA4, the entry defines a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 7: When the low-order bits of pmpaddr5 end with a single zero (pattern yyyy…yyy0) and pmpcfg5.A encodes NAPOT, the entry defines an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 8: When the low-order bits of pmpaddr5 end with the pattern 01 (pattern yyyy…yy01) and pmpcfg5.A encodes NAPOT, the entry defines a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 9: When the low-order bits of pmpaddr5 end with the pattern 011 (pattern yyyy…y011) and pmpcfg5.A encodes NAPOT, the entry defines a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 10: When the low-order bits of pmpaddr5 match the pattern yy01…1111 and pmpcfg5.A encodes NAPOT, the entry defines a 2·XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: When the low-order bits of pmpaddr5 match the pattern y011…1111 and pmpcfg5.A encodes NAPOT, the entry defines a (2·XLEN+1)-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: When the low-order bits of pmpaddr5 match the pattern 0111…1111 and pmpcfg5.A encodes NAPOT, the entry defines a (2·XLEN+2)-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: When the low-order bits of pmpaddr5 match the pattern 1111…1111 and pmpcfg5.A encodes NAPOT, the entry defines a (2·XLEN+3)-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If pmpcfg5.A is set to TOR, the PMP entry 5 matches any address y such that pmpaddr4 ≤ y < pmpaddr5, irrespective of pmpcfg4.
RULE 15: If pmpaddr4 ≥ pmpaddr5 and pmpcfg5.A is TOR, then PMP entry 5 matches no addresses.
RULE 16: If the granularity index G is ≥ 1 and software writes the A field of pmpcfg5 to the NA4 encoding (0b10), then a subsequent read of pmpcfg5 returns A = 0b00 (OFF), indicating the NA4 selection was ignored and the PMP entry performs no address checks.
RULE 17: When G ≥ 2 and the second bit of pmpcfg5.A (pmpcfg5.A[1]) is set, bits pmpaddr5[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 18: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg5.A[1] is clear, bits pmpaddr5[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 19: Bits pmpaddr5[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 20: Changing pmpcfg5.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr5 but does not modify the stored value; specifically, pmpaddr5[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg5.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 21: If PMP entry 5 is locked, writes to pmpaddr5 are ignored.
RULE 22: The L bit of PMP entry 5 indicates that the entry is locked, and writes to pmpaddr5 are ignored.
RULE 23: Setting the L bit for PMP entry 5 locks the PMP entry (including pmpaddr5) even when the A field is set to OFF.
RULE 24: When the L bit for PMP entry 5 is set, the entry is locked; consequently, writes to pmpaddr5 are ignored.
RULE 25: If pmpcfg5.A = TOR and pmpaddr4 ≥ pmpaddr5, then the PMP entry is treated as disabled, so a memory access to an address that would lie in the intended region does not raise a PMP‑access‑fault exception.
RULE 26: If a PMP reset is performed, then a read of the pmpaddr5 CSR returns its safe default reset value.
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr5 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3b5; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 28: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr5 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3b5; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 29: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr5 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3b5; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 30: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr5.ADDR (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3b5, a0; csrr a1, 0x3b5; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr5 register while M extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: M; csrr a0, 0x3b5; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr5 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3b5; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr6
NUMBER: 0x3b6
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: The pmpaddr6 register contains a field named pmpaddr6[G-1] that may have an underlying value of 1 while being read as 0.
RULE 2: When a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction modifies any bit other than pmpaddr6[G-1], the instruction reads a value of 0 from pmpaddr6[G-1].
RULE 3: When a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction modifies any bit other than pmpaddr6[G-1], the instruction writes the read value 0 back to pmpaddr6[G-1], causing the underlying value of pmpaddr6[G-1] to become 0.
RULE 4: pmpaddr6 has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 5: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr6 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 6: If a write to pmpaddr6 sets any bit beyond the implemented physical‑address width, then a subsequent read of pmpaddr6 returns a value with those out‑of‑range bits cleared, so the readback is a legal address value.
RULE 7: If a program writes any value to the pmpaddr6 CSR and then reads it, the readback value may be zero.
RULE 8: When pmpcfg6.A = NA4 or NAPOT, the low-order bits of pmpaddr6 encode the size of the range according to Table 24 (e.g., "yyyy…yyy0" for an 8-byte NAPOT range, "yyyy…yy01" for a 16-byte NAPOT range, …, "1111…1111" for a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range).
RULE 9: When pmpcfg6.A = TOR, pmpaddr6 defines the top of the address range and the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr5 ≤ y < pmpaddr6, irrespective of pmpcfg5.A.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg6.A = TOR and pmpaddr5 ≥ pmpaddr6, then PMP entry 6 matches no addresses.
RULE 11: When the granularity G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg6.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr6[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 12: When the granularity G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg6.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr6[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 13: If pmpcfg6.A = TOR, bits pmpaddr6[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 14: When pmpcfg6.A[1] is changed, the underlying stored value of pmpaddr6[G-1] retains its original value, while the value read from pmpaddr6 may change according to the read-value rules.
RULE 15: If the L bit of PMP entry 6 is set, writes to pmpaddr6 MUST be ignored.
RULE 16: A locked PMP entry 6 MUST remain locked until a hart reset, causing writes to pmpaddr6 to continue to be ignored until that reset.
RULE 17: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 6 MUST lock the entry, which controls pmpaddr6 behavior, regardless of the A field value.
RULE 18: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr6 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3b6; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 19: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr6 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3b6; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 20: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr6 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3b6; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 21: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr6.ADDR (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3b6, a0; csrr a1, 0x3b6; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 22: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr6 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3b6; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 23: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr6 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3b6; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr7
NUMBER: 0x3b7
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr7 may have an underlying value of 1 in its most-significant bit (bit G-1) while reads of that bit return 0.
RULE 2: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction that modifies any bit of pmpaddr7 other than the most-significant bit will cause the most-significant bit to be read as 0 and then written back, updating its underlying value to 0.
RULE 3: pmpaddr7 can be read or written only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 4: In an RV64 implementation, pmpaddr7 holds bits 55-2 of the physical address used by PMP entry 7.
RULE 5: Writes to pmpaddr7 may be ignored or masked according to the implemented address bits.
RULE 6: Reads from pmpaddr7 may return any value that is a legal encoding of the implemented address bits, including possibly all zeros.
RULE 7: The fields of pmpaddr7 are WARL and may read back as zero if the implementation does not support the written bits.
RULE 8: When a PMP setting for entry 8 uses the preceding address register, pmpaddr7 directly influences the behavior of entry 8.
RULE 9: If the A field of pmpcfg7 is NA4, then pmpaddr7 must contain a value of the form yyyy…yyyy and matches a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 10: If the A field of pmpcfg7 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr7 have the pattern yyyy…yyy0, then pmpaddr7 matches an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: If the A field of pmpcfg7 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr7 have the pattern yyyy…yy01, then pmpaddr7 matches a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If the A field of pmpcfg7 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr7 have the pattern yyyy…y011, then pmpaddr7 matches a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If the A field of pmpcfg7 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr7 follow the pattern yy01…1111, then pmpaddr7 matches a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If the A field of pmpcfg7 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr7 follow the pattern y011…1111, then pmpaddr7 matches a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: If the A field of pmpcfg7 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr7 follow the pattern 0111…1111, then pmpaddr7 matches a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 16: If the A field of pmpcfg7 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr7 follow the pattern 1111…1111, then pmpaddr7 matches a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 17: If pmpcfg7.A is TOR, then pmpaddr7 defines the top of the address range while pmpaddr6 defines the bottom of the address range.
RULE 18: If pmpcfg7.A is TOR and pmpaddr6 ≤ y < pmpaddr7, then PMP entry 7 matches address y irrespective of the value of pmpcfg6.
RULE 19: If pmpaddr6 ≥ pmpaddr7 and pmpcfg7.A is TOR, then PMP entry 7 matches no addresses.
RULE 20: If the platform granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg7.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), then the bits pmpaddr7[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 21: If the platform granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg7.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), then the bits pmpaddr7[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 22: Bits pmpaddr7[G-1:0] do not influence the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 23: Changing pmpcfg7.A[1] does not modify the stored value of pmpaddr7, and pmpaddr7[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg7.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 24: The PMP grain equals 2^G + 2 bytes, is identical for all PMP regions, and the granularity G determines which bits of pmpaddr7 are subject to the read-mask rules.
RULE 25: If the L bit of PMP entry 7 is set, the entry is locked and writes to pmpaddr7 are ignored.
RULE 26: If the L bit of PMP entry 7 is set, writes to the associated configuration register pmp7cfg are ignored, and the entry remains locked such that writes to pmpaddr7 are also ignored.
RULE 27: If the L bit of PMP entry 7 is set, the PMP entry is locked even when its A field is OFF, and writes to pmpaddr7 remain ignored regardless of the A field value.
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr7 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3b7; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr7 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3b7; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 30: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr7 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3b7; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 31: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr7.ADDR (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3b7, a0; csrr a1, 0x3b7; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr7 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3b7; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr8
NUMBER: 0x3b8
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P
RULE 1: The pmpaddr8 register is a WARL field because not all physical address bits may be implemented.
RULE 2: The pmpaddr8 register is accessible only in M-mode because PMP CSRs are only accessible to M-mode.
RULE 3: When pmpcfg8.A = NA4, pmpaddr8 bits all equal y encode a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 4: When pmpcfg8.A = NAPOT and the low-order bit of pmpaddr8 is 0 (pattern yyyy…yyy0), pmpaddr8 encodes an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 5: When pmpcfg8.A = NAPOT and the two low-order bits of pmpaddr8 are 01 (pattern yyyy…yy01), pmpaddr8 encodes a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 6: When pmpcfg8.A = NAPOT and the three low-order bits of pmpaddr8 are 011 (pattern yyyy…y011), pmpaddr8 encodes a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 7: When pmpcfg8.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr8 matches the pattern yy01…1111, pmpaddr8 encodes a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN bytes.
RULE 8: If pmpcfg8.A is set to NAPOT and pmpaddr8 matches the bit pattern 0111…1111, then PMP entry 8 defines a NAPOT region whose size is 2 × XLEN + 2 bytes; this is observable because a memory access to any address within that range succeeds, while an access to the first address just outside the range (base + 2 × XLEN + 2) raises a PMP access‑fault exception.
RULE 9: When pmpcfg8.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr8 matches the pattern 1111…1111, pmpaddr8 encodes a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN + 3 bytes.
RULE 10: When pmpcfg8.A = TOR, pmpaddr8 participates in address matching such that any address y satisfying pmpaddr7 ≤ y < pmpaddr8 is matched, irrespective of pmpcfg7.
RULE 11: If pmpaddr7 ≥ pmpaddr8 and pmpcfg8.A = TOR, then pmpaddr8 matches no addresses.
RULE 12: When the granularity index G is greater than or equal to 1, the NA4 mode is not selectable for pmpaddr8.
RULE 13: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg8.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr8[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 14: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg8.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr8[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 15: Bits pmpaddr8[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 16: Changing pmpcfg8.A[1] may change the value read from pmpaddr8 but does not alter the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr8[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg8.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 17: If the L bit of PMP entry 8 is set, writes to pmpaddr8 are ignored.
RULE 18: If PMP entry 8 is locked, writes to pmpaddr8 are ignored.
RULE 19: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr8 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3b8; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 20: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr8 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3b8; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 21: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr8 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3b8; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 22: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr8.ADDR (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3b8, a0; csrr a1, 0x3b8; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 23: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr8 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3b8; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targets the pmpaddr9 CSR, then after execution the pmpaddr9 register may contain bits that differ from its original read value even when the corresponding bits in rs1 are zero, and rd receives the original pmpaddr9 value.

RULE 11: When the L bit for PMP entry 9 is clear, any M-mode access that matches the address range defined by pmpaddr9 will succeed, and the R, W, and X permissions of pmpaddr9 apply only to S and U modes.

REGISTER: pmpaddr10
NUMBER: 0x3ba
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: The pmpaddr10 register contains a field pmpaddr10[G-1] that may have an underlying value of 1 while reads of that field return 0.
RULE 2: CSRRS and CSRRC instructions executed on pmpaddr10 may modify bits whose read value differs from their underlying value, even if the corresponding bit in rs1 is not set, and this behavior applies to the pmpaddr10[G-1] field.
RULE 3: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction on pmpaddr10 to modify a bit other than pmpaddr10[G-1] will cause a read of 0 from pmpaddr10[G-1] and will write back that 0, updating the underlying value of pmpaddr10[G-1] to 0.
RULE 4: pmpaddr10 has Machine-level Read/Write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 5: If a program writes a value to pmpaddr10 that has any bit set beyond the implemented physical‑address width, then reading back pmpaddr10 returns those upper bits cleared (to zero or the implementation‑defined WARL value) and the write does not raise any exception.
RULE 6: For pmpaddr10, when it is used for a NAPOT entry, the low-order bits of pmpaddr10 encode the size of the NAPOT range.
RULE 7: If pmpaddr10 matches the pattern yyyy…yyyy and pmpcfg10.A indicates NA4, then the NAPOT range size is 4 bytes.
RULE 8: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr10 match the pattern yyyy…yyy0 and pmpcfg10.A indicates NAPOT, then the NAPOT range size is 8 bytes.
RULE 9: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr10 match the pattern yyyy…yy01 and pmpcfg10.A indicates NAPOT, then the NAPOT range size is 16 bytes.
RULE 10: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr10 match the pattern yyyy…y011 and pmpcfg10.A indicates NAPOT, then the NAPOT range size is 32 bytes.
RULE 11: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr10 match the pattern yy01…1111 and pmpcfg10.A indicates NAPOT, then the NAPOT range size is 2 XLEN bytes.
RULE 12: If the low-order bits of pmpaddr10 match the pattern y011…1111 and pmpcfg10.A indicates NAPOT, then the NAPOT range size is 2 XLEN+1 bytes.
RULE 13: When pmpcfg10.A is TOR, pmpaddr10 defines the top address of the TOR range and pmpaddr9 defines the bottom address of that range.
RULE 14: When pmpcfg10.A is TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr9 ≤ y < pmpaddr10, regardless of the value of pmpcfg9.
RULE 15: If pmpaddr9 ≥ pmpaddr10 and pmpcfg10.A is TOR, then entry 10 matches no addresses.
RULE 16: When the granularity G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg10.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr10[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 17: When the granularity G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg10.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr10[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 18: Bits pmpaddr10[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 19: Changing pmpcfg10.A[1] alters the value read from pmpaddr10 but does not change the underlying stored value of pmpaddr10; specifically, pmpaddr10[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg10.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 20: If the L bit of PMP entry 10 is set, writes to pmpaddr10 are ignored.
RULE 21: The lock on PMP entry 10, which causes writes to pmpaddr10 to be ignored, remains in effect until the hart is reset.
RULE 22: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 10 locks the PMP entry, causing writes to pmpaddr10 to be ignored, even when the A field of that entry is set to OFF.
RULE 23: A PMP rule that includes pmpaddr10 must have pmpcfg10.A not equal to OFF.
RULE 24: If pmpcfg10.A is TOR, then pmpaddr9 must be less than pmpaddr10.
RULE 25: If, after a PMP reset, pmpaddr10 does not contain the safe default value, then reading the pmpaddr10 CSR returns a value different from that safe default.

REGISTER: pmpaddr13
NUMBER: 0x3bd
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr13 is a machine-level CSR that can be read and written by machine mode (privilege field MRW).
RULE 2: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr13 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 3: The register pmpaddr13 is a WARL (write-any-value-read-legal) register.
RULE 4: Reads of pmpaddr13 must occur in M-mode; reads from lower privilege modes are not permitted.
RULE 5: Writes to pmpaddr13 must occur in M-mode; writes from lower privilege modes are not permitted.
RULE 6: For pmpaddr13, a bit pattern of all ones (yyyy…yyyy) together with pmpcfg13.A = NA4 encodes a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 7: For pmpaddr13, a bit pattern ending with a single zero (yyyy…yyy0) together with pmpcfg13.A = NAPOT encodes an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 8: For pmpaddr13, a bit pattern ending with "01" (yyyy…yy01) together with pmpcfg13.A = NAPOT encodes a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 9: For pmpaddr13, a bit pattern ending with "011" (yyyy…y011) together with pmpcfg13.A = NAPOT encodes a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 10: For pmpaddr13, a bit pattern of the form "yy01…1111" together with pmpcfg13.A = NAPOT encodes a 2·XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: For pmpaddr13, a bit pattern of the form "y011…1111" together with pmpcfg13.A = NAPOT encodes a (2·XLEN+1)-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: For pmpaddr13, a bit pattern of the form "0111…1111" together with pmpcfg13.A = NAPOT encodes a (2·XLEN+2)-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: For pmpaddr13, a bit pattern of the form "1111…1111" together with pmpcfg13.A = NAPOT encodes a (2·XLEN+3)-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If pmpcfg13.A = TOR then pmpaddr13 specifies the top bound of the address range for PMP entry 13.
RULE 15: When pmpcfg13.A = TOR, the address range matched by PMP entry 13 includes all addresses y such that pmpaddr12 ≤ y < pmpaddr13.
RULE 16: If pmpaddr12 ≥ pmpaddr13 and pmpcfg13.A = TOR then PMP entry 13 matches no addresses.
RULE 17: When the PMP granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg13.A[1] is set, the bits pmpaddr13[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 18: When the PMP granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg13.A[1] is clear, the bits pmpaddr13[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 19: Bits pmpaddr13[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 20: Changing pmpcfg13.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr13 but does not change the underlying stored value of pmpaddr13.
RULE 21: Specifically, the bit pmpaddr13[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg13.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 22: If PMP entry 13 is locked, writes to pmpaddr13 are ignored.
RULE 23: If PMP entry 13 is locked and pmp13 cfg.A is TOR, writes to the preceding address register pmpaddr13-1 are ignored.
RULE 24: When PMP entry 13 is locked, the lock on pmpaddr13 persists until the hart is reset.
RULE 25: The L bit of PMP entry 13 indicates that pmpaddr13 is locked, causing writes to pmpaddr13 to be ignored.
RULE 26: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 13 locks pmpaddr13 even when the A field of pmp13 cfg is OFF.
RULE 27: When the L bit of PMP entry 13 is clear, any M-mode access that matches pmpaddr13 succeeds, while the R/W/X permissions for pmpaddr13 apply only to S and U modes.
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr13 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3bd; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr13 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3bd; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

RULE 15: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr17 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3c1; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 16: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr17 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3c1; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 17: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr17 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3c1; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 18: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr17.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3c1, a0; csrr a1, 0x3c1; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].

RULE 20: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr17 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3c1; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr18

MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: The privilege level for pmpaddr18 is MRW (Machine Read/Write).
RULE 2: If a software writes a 1 to any physical‑address bit of pmpaddr18 that is not implemented, then a subsequent read of pmpaddr18 returns the written value with those unsupported bits cleared.
RULE 3: pmpaddr18 may be read or written only when the hart is in M-mode.
RULE 4: If the L bit of PMP entry 18 is set, writes to pmpaddr18 are ignored.
RULE 5: Locked PMP entries remain locked until the hart is reset, therefore pmpaddr18 remains locked until the hart is reset.

REGISTER: pmpaddr19
NUMBER: 0x3c3
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction accesses pmpaddr19 and the rs1 mask does not set the bit position corresponding to pmpaddr19[G-1], the instruction reads 0 from pmpaddr19[G-1] and writes that 0 back, updating the underlying value of pmpaddr19[G-1] to 0.
RULE 2: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction accesses pmpaddr19 and the underlying value of pmpaddr19[G-1] is 1 while a read of that bit returns 0, the instruction reads 0 and any write caused by the instruction writes back that 0, causing the underlying value of pmpaddr19[G-1] to become 0.
RULE 3: If a CSRRW instruction targeting pmpaddr19 has rd = x0, the instruction shall not read pmpaddr19 and shall write the value in rs1 to pmpaddr19.
RULE 4: If a CSRRW instruction targeting pmpaddr19 has rd ≠ x0, the instruction shall read the old value of pmpaddr19, zero-extend it to XLEN bits, write it to rd, and shall write the value in rs1 to pmpaddr19.
RULE 5: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targeting pmpaddr19 has rs1 = x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr19, shall not write to it, and shall not cause any side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write.
RULE 6: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targeting pmpaddr19 has rs1 ≠ x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr19, shall write to it, and shall action side effects only for fields for which rs1 has at least one bit set corresponding to that field.
RULE 7: If a CSRRWI instruction targeting pmpaddr19 has rd = x0, the instruction shall not read pmpaddr19 and shall write zero to pmpaddr19.
RULE 8: If a CSRRWI instruction targeting pmpaddr19 has rd ≠ x0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr19, shall write the zero-extended immediate to pmpaddr19, and shall action side effects for all fields of the written CSR.
RULE 9: If a CSRRSI or CSRRCI instruction targeting pmpaddr19 has uimm = 0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr19, shall not write to it, and shall not cause any side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write.
RULE 10: If a CSRRSI or CSRRCI instruction targeting pmpaddr19 has uimm ≠ 0, the instruction shall read pmpaddr19, shall write to it, and shall action side effects only for fields for which the immediate has at least one bit set corresponding to that field.
RULE 11: CSRRW and CSRRWI instructions that write pmpaddr19 shall action side effects for all fields within pmpaddr19.
RULE 12: CSRRS, CSRRC, CSRRSI, and CSRRCI instructions that write pmpaddr19 shall action side effects only for fields of pmpaddr19 where the rs1 register or immediate argument has at least one bit set corresponding to that field.
RULE 13: The privilege of pmpaddr19 is MRW, meaning it is readable and writable in Machine mode.
RULE 14: The pmpaddr19 CSR may be read or written only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 15: On an RV64 hart, the value held in pmpaddr19 specifies bits 55-2 of the 56-bit physical address used for PMP matching.
RULE 16: If a PMP configuration selects the preceding‑entry address rule, then the address field of pmpaddr19 must be used as the address for the PMP entry that follows it; otherwise an access that falls within the intended range will raise an access‑fault exception (mcause set to the appropriate load/store/instruction access‑fault).
RULE 17: When pmpcfg19.A is NA4 and the bits of pmpaddr19 all have the same value (pattern yyyy…yyyy), the entry defines a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 18: When pmpcfg19.A is NAPOT and pmpaddr19 matches the pattern yyyy…yyy0, the entry defines an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 19: When pmpcfg19.A is NAPOT and pmpaddr19 matches the pattern yyyy…yy01, the entry defines a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 20: When pmpcfg19.A is NAPOT and pmpaddr19 matches the pattern yyyy…y011, the entry defines a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 21: When pmpcfg19.A is NAPOT and pmpaddr19 matches the pattern y011…1111, the entry defines a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 22: When pmpcfg19.A is TOR, pmpaddr19 serves as the upper bound of the TOR range whose lower bound is pmpaddr18, and the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr18 ≤ y < pmpaddr19.
RULE 23: When pmpcfg19.A is TOR and pmpaddr18 ≥ pmpaddr19, the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 24: If the system granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg19.A indicates NAPOT, reads of bits pmpaddr19[G-2:0] return all ones.
RULE 25: If G is at least 1 and pmpcfg19.A indicates OFF or TOR, reads of bits pmpaddr19[G-1:0] return all zeros.
RULE 26: The low G bits of pmpaddr19 are ignored by the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 27: The stored bit pmpaddr19[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg19.A changes among NAPOT, TOR, and OFF and then returns to NAPOT.
RULE 28: If granularity G is at least 1, the NA4 mode cannot be selected for pmpaddr19.
RULE 29: Setting the L bit for PMP entry 19 locks the entry even when the entry's A field is set to OFF, and consequently writes to the pmpaddr19 register are ignored.
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr19 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3c3; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr19 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3c3; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 32: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr19 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3c3; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 33: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr19.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3c3, a0; csrr a1, 0x3c3; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 34: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr19 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3c3; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 35: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr19 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3c3; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

RULE 1: The bit pmpaddr21[G-1] may have an underlying stored value of 1 but be read as 0.

RULE 20: A PMP rule that includes pmpaddr21 is considered valid only when the address-matching field A of the associated pmpcfg21 register is not OFF.

REGISTER: pmpaddr23
NUMBER: 0x3c7
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: The most-significant address bit of pmpaddr23 (pmpaddr23[G-1]) may have an underlying stored value of 1 while a read of the CSR returns 0.
RULE 2: When a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction modifies any bit of pmpaddr23 other than pmpaddr23[G-1], the hardware will read pmpaddr23[G-1] as 0 and write that 0 back, thereby changing the underlying stored value of pmpaddr23[G-1] to 0.
RULE 3: If rs1 = x0 in a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that addresses pmpaddr23, the instruction shall not write to pmpaddr23, shall not cause any write-side effects, and shall not raise illegal-instruction exceptions on read-only accesses.
RULE 4: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction specifies pmpaddr23 as the CSR, then the destination register (when rd ≠ x0) contains the current value of pmpaddr23 and any read‑side effects of pmpaddr23 are observed, regardless of the values in rs1 or rd.
RULE 5: When rs1 = x0 in a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that addresses pmpaddr23, the instruction reads pmpaddr23 and does not write to it.
RULE 6: When rs1 ≠ x0 in a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that addresses pmpaddr23, the instruction reads pmpaddr23 and writes to it.
RULE 7: If an instruction executing at a privilege level other than Machine attempts to read or write pmpaddr23, then a privileged‑instruction (illegal‑instruction) exception is raised; otherwise, when executed in Machine mode, reads of pmpaddr23 return the value most recently written to it.
RULE 8: For RV64 implementations, pmpaddr23 encodes bits 55 down to 2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 9: pmpaddr23 is a WARL register.
RULE 10: pmpaddr23 is accessible only in M-mode.
RULE 11: When pmpcfg23.A selects NA4, pmpaddr23 encodes a 4-byte NAPOT range.

RULE 13: When pmpcfg23.A selects NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr23 are 01, pmpaddr23 encodes a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: When pmpcfg23.A selects NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr23 are 011, pmpaddr23 encodes a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: When pmpcfg23.A selects NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr23 match the pattern yy01 followed by all ones, pmpaddr23 encodes a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.

RULE 17: When pmpcfg23.A selects NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr23 match the pattern 0111 followed by all ones, pmpaddr23 encodes a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 18: If pmpcfg23.A selects NAPOT and every low‑order bit of pmpaddr23 is 1, then the PMP entry encodes a NAPOT region of size 2^{XLEN+3} bytes, so the PMP match signal is asserted for any memory address.
RULE 19: When pmpcfg23.A selects TOR, pmpaddr23 provides the top address of the range while pmpaddr22 provides the bottom address of the range.

RULE 23: When the granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg23.A[1] is clear (indicating OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr23[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 24: Bits pmpaddr23[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.

RULE 26: If the L bit in pmp23cfg is set, implementations MUST ignore all writes to pmpaddr23.
RULE 27: When the L bit in pmp23cfg is set, the PMP entry 23 is locked even if pmp23cfg.A is OFF, and implementations MUST ignore writes to pmpaddr23 regardless of the value of pmp23cfg.A.
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr23 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3c7; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
