FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr24 belongs to the Machine Memory Protection CSR group and has machine-mode read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: In RV64, pmpaddr24 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address for PMP entry 24.
RULE 3: Reads and writes of pmpaddr24 must occur while the hart is in M-mode, and accesses from lower privilege modes are not permitted.
RULE 4: If the PMP configuration register pmpcfg24 selects the TOR address-matching mode, then PMP entry 24 matches any address y such that pmpaddr23 ≤ y < pmpaddr24, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg23.
RULE 5: If pmpaddr23 ≥ pmpaddr24 and pmpcfg24 selects the TOR address-matching mode, then PMP entry 24 matches no addresses.
RULE 6: When the implementation defines G ≥ 2 and the A field bit A[1] of pmpcfg24 is set (indicating NAPOT mode), then the bits pmpaddr24[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 7: When the implementation defines G ≥ 1 and the A field bit A[1] of pmpcfg24 is clear (indicating OFF or TOR mode), then the bits pmpaddr24[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 8: The bits pmpaddr24[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for PMP entry 24.
RULE 9: Changing the A field bit A[1] of pmpcfg24 changes the value read from pmpaddr24.
RULE 10: Changing pmpcfg24 does not alter the underlying stored value of pmpaddr24, and the bit pmpaddr24[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg24 is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 11: If PMP entry 24 is locked, writes to pmpaddr24 are ignored.
RULE 12: Setting the L bit in pmp24cfg locks PMP entry 24, and consequently pmpaddr24 becomes write-ignored even when the A field is set to OFF.
RULE 13: A lock on PMP entry 24 remains in effect for pmpaddr24 until the hart is reset.
RULE 14: When the L bit is set, writes to pmpaddr24 are ignored.
RULE 15: When the L bit is set, the lock on pmpaddr24 persists across privilege modes until a hart reset.
RULE 16: A PMP entry consisting of pmpaddr24 and pmpcfg24 encodes a valid protected physical memory region only if pmpcfg24.A is not OFF.
RULE 17: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr24 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3c8; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 18: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr24 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3c8; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 19: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr24 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3c8; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 20: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr24.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3c8, a0; csrr a1, 0x3c8; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 21: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr24 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3c8; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr25
NUMBER: 0x3c9
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: If the implementation does not support the address bits mapped to pmpaddr25, then any write to pmpaddr25 has no effect and a read of the pmpaddr25 CSR always returns 0.
RULE 2: pmpaddr25 can be accessed only in M-mode.
RULE 3: When pmpcfg25.A = TOR, pmpaddr25 serves as the top address of the range.
RULE 4: If pmpaddr24 ≥ pmpaddr25 and pmpcfg25.A = TOR, then PMP entry 25 matches no addresses.
RULE 5: If G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg25.A[1] = 1, then bits pmpaddr25[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 6: If G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg25.A[1] = 0, then bits pmpaddr25[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 7: When TOR matching is used, bits pmpaddr25[G-1:0] are ignored by the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 8: pmpaddr25[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg25.A is changed between NAPOT and TOR or OFF.
RULE 9: If PMP entry 25 is locked, writes to pmpaddr25 are ignored.
RULE 10: If PMP entry 25 is locked and its cfg.A field is set to TOR, writes to pmpaddr24 are ignored.
RULE 11: Setting the L bit for PMP entry 25 locks the PMP entry even when the A field is set to OFF.
RULE 12: Locked PMP entries, including entry 25, remain locked until the hart is reset.
RULE 13: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr25 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3c9; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 14: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr25 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3c9; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 15: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr25 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3c9; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 16: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr25.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3c9, a0; csrr a1, 0x3c9; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 17: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr25 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3c9; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr26
NUMBER: 0x3ca
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr26[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of the register returns 0.
RULE 2: Executing CSRRC or CSRRS to modify a different bit causes a read of pmpaddr26[G-1] to return 0 and subsequently writes back 0, updating the underlying value of pmpaddr26[G-1] to 0.
RULE 3: For RV64, pmpaddr26 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 4: If a value containing bits that are not implemented in the physical address space is written to pmpaddr26, then a subsequent read of pmpaddr26 returns a value in which all unimplemented bits are cleared (read as zero) while the implemented bits reflect the written value.
RULE 5: On RV64, pmpaddr26 is limited to bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address because the RV64 PMP address registers impose the same limit as the Sv39 and Sv48 virtual-memory schemes.
RULE 6: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 is 0, then the PMP entry is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 7: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NA4, then pmpaddr26 encodes a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 8: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the least-significant bit of pmpaddr26 is 0, then the entry matches an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 9: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the two least-significant bits of pmpaddr26 are 01, then the entry matches a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 10: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the three least-significant bits of pmpaddr26 are 011, then the entry matches a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr26 have the pattern yy01 followed by all ones, then the entry matches a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr26 have the pattern y011 followed by all ones, then the entry matches a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr26 have the pattern 0111 followed by all ones, then the entry matches a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 selects NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr26 are all ones, then the entry matches a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: If the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 is TOR, then the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr25 ≤ y < pmpaddr26, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg25.
RULE 16: If pmpaddr25 ≥ pmpaddr26 and the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 is TOR, then the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 17: When G ≥ 2 and the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 has its high bit set (mode NAPOT), then bits pmpaddr26[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 18: When G ≥ 1 and the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 has its high bit clear (mode OFF or TOR), then bits pmpaddr26[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 19: The low-order G bits of pmpaddr26 do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 20: Changing the A field of the configuration register associated with pmpaddr26 from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT does not alter the stored value of bit pmpaddr26[G-1]; the stored bit remains unchanged.
RULE 21: When the L bit of PMP entry 26 is set, any write to the pmpaddr26 register is ignored.
RULE 22: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr26 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3ca; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 23: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr26 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3ca; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 24: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr26 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3ca; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 25: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr26.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3ca, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ca; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 26: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr26 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3ca; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr27
NUMBER: 0x3cb
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies a bit in pmpaddr27 that is different from the G-1 bit, and the underlying hardware value of pmpaddr27[G-1] is 1 while the read value of pmpaddr27[G-1] is 0, then the instruction reads 0 from pmpaddr27[G-1] and writes 0 back, updating the underlying hardware value of pmpaddr27[G-1] to 0.
RULE 2: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies any bit of pmpaddr27 other than the G-1 bit, a mismatch between the underlying hardware value and the read value of pmpaddr27[G-1] can cause the read value (0) to be written back, thereby updating the underlying hardware value of pmpaddr27[G-1] to match the read value.
RULE 3: pmpaddr27 is a Machine-level CSR with read/write privilege (MRW).
RULE 4: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr27 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 5: PMP CSRs are only accessible to M-mode, therefore pmpaddr27 is only accessible to M-mode.
RULE 6: When pmpcfg27.A = NAPOT, the pattern of the low-order bits of pmpaddr27 encodes the size of the matched NAPOT region exactly as specified in the NAPOT range encoding table.
RULE 7: When pmpcfg27.A = TOR, pmpaddr27 provides the top address of the range while pmpaddr26 provides the bottom address.
RULE 8: When pmpcfg27.A = TOR, the PMP entry 27 matches any address y such that pmpaddr26 ≤ y < pmpaddr27, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg26.
RULE 9: If pmpcfg27.A = TOR and pmpaddr26 ≥ pmpaddr27, then PMP entry 27 matches no addresses.
RULE 10: When the implementation granularity G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg27.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), reads of pmpaddr27 return all ones in bits G-2 down to 0.
RULE 11: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg27.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), reads of pmpaddr27 return all zeros in bits G-1 down to 0.
RULE 12: The low bits of pmpaddr27 masked by granularity (bits G-1 down to 0) are ignored by the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 13: The physical bit pmpaddr27[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg27.A is changed between NAPOT and OFF/TOR modes, even though the read value of pmpaddr27 may change.
RULE 14: If PMP entry 27 is locked, writes to pmpaddr27 are ignored.
RULE 15: Setting the L bit for entry 27 locks the PMP entry even when the A field is set to OFF, and consequently writes to pmpaddr27 are ignored.
RULE 16: For the PMP rule that uses pmpaddr27 to be a valid protected physical memory region, the field pmpcfg27.A must not be OFF.
RULE 17: If pmpcfg27.A is TOR, then the value in pmpaddr26 must be strictly less than the value in pmpaddr27.
RULE 18: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr27 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3cb; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 19: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr27 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3cb; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 20: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr27 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3cb; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 21: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr27.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3cb, a0; csrr a1, 0x3cb; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 22: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr27 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3cb; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 23: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr27 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3cb; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr28
NUMBER: 0x3cc
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: A CSRRW instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rs1 = x0 will attempt to write zero to pmpaddr28.
RULE 2: A CSRRS instruction that targets pmpaddr28 reads the value of pmpaddr28, zero-extends it to XLEN bits, writes it to integer register rd, and treats the initial value in rs1 as a bit mask that sets corresponding writable bits in pmpaddr28.
RULE 3: A CSRRC instruction that targets pmpaddr28 reads the value of pmpaddr28, zero-extends it to XLEN bits, writes it to integer register rd, and treats the initial value in rs1 as a bit mask that clears corresponding writable bits in pmpaddr28.
RULE 4: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targets pmpaddr28 and rs1 has a zero for a bit position, but the value read from that bit differs from the underlying stored bit, then after execution the CSR’s stored value for that bit may be altered (the CSR readback value can differ from the original underlying value).
RULE 5: If pmpaddr28[G-1] has an underlying value of 1 but reads as 0, executing CSRRC or CSRRS on pmpaddr28 to modify a different bit will cause 0 to be read from pmpaddr28[G-1] and then written back, updating the underlying value to 0.
RULE 6: For CSRRS and CSRRC instructions targeting pmpaddr28, if rs1 = x0, the instruction will not write to pmpaddr28 at all, shall not cause any of the side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write, and shall not raise illegal-instruction exceptions on accesses to read-only pmpaddr28.
RULE 7: CSRRS and CSRRC instructions targeting pmpaddr28 always read pmpaddr28 and cause any read side effects regardless of the values of rs1 and rd.
RULE 8: The CSRRWI, CSRRSI, and CSRRCI immediate-form instructions targeting pmpaddr28 behave as their register-operand counterparts, using a zero-extended 5-bit immediate instead of rs1.
RULE 9: If a CSRRSI or CSRRCI instruction targeting pmpaddr28 has an immediate field uimm[4:0] equal to zero, the instruction will not write to pmpaddr28, shall not cause any of the side effects that might otherwise occur on a CSR write, and shall not raise illegal-instruction exceptions on accesses to read-only pmpaddr28.
RULE 10: For a CSRRW instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rd != x0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 11: For CSRRS or CSRRC instructions targeting pmpaddr28 with rs1 = x0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and does not write to pmpaddr28.
RULE 12: For CSRRS or CSRRC instructions targeting pmpaddr28 with rs1 != x0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 13: For a CSRRWI instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rd = x0, the instruction does not read pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 14: For a CSRRWI instruction targeting pmpaddr28 with rd != x0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 15: For CSRRSI or CSRRCI instructions targeting pmpaddr28 with uimm = 0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and does not write to pmpaddr28.
RULE 16: For CSRRSI or CSRRCI instructions targeting pmpaddr28 with uimm != 0, the instruction reads pmpaddr28 and writes to pmpaddr28.
RULE 17: pmpaddr28 is not among the CSRs that are automatically modified as side effects of instruction execution, so no automatic update side effect applies to pmpaddr28.
RULE 18: Software may write any value to pmpaddr28.
RULE 19: pmpaddr28 is accessible only in machine mode.
RULE 20: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is 0, the entry is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 21: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is 1, the entry uses TOR mode with pmpaddr28 serving as the top of the address range.
RULE 22: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is 2, the entry uses NA4 mode and pmpaddr28 encodes a 4-byte range.
RULE 23: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is 3, the entry uses NAPOT mode and pmpaddr28 encodes a naturally aligned power-of-two range.
RULE 24: If the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is set to TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr27 ≤ y < pmpaddr28, irrespective of the value of the preceding configuration register.
RULE 25: If pmpaddr27 ≥ pmpaddr28 and the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is TOR, then the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 26: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NA4, the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 encode a 4-byte range as defined by the NA4 encoding.
RULE 27: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern yyyy…yyy0, the entry matches an 8-byte range.
RULE 28: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern yyyy…yy01, the entry matches a 16-byte range.
RULE 29: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern yyyy…y011, the entry matches a 32-byte range.
RULE 30: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern yy01…1111, the entry matches a range of size 2 × XLEN bytes.
RULE 31: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern y011…1111, the entry matches a range of size 2 × XLEN + 1 bytes.
RULE 32: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern 0111…1111, the entry matches a range of size 2 × XLEN + 2 bytes.
RULE 33: When the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr28 match the pattern 1111…1111, the entry matches a range of size 2 × XLEN + 3 bytes.
RULE 34: If the PMP granularity G is ≥ 1 and NA4 mode is selected for the entry whose address register is pmpaddr28, then the CSR write that sets this NA4 mode raises an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 35: When G ≥ 2 and the high bit of the A field (A[1]) for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is set, bits pmpaddr28[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 36: When G ≥ 1 and the high bit of the A field (A[1]) for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 is clear, bits pmpaddr28[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 37: Bits pmpaddr28[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for the entry that contains pmpaddr28.
RULE 38: Changing the high bit of the A field for the entry that contains pmpaddr28 changes the value read from pmpaddr28 but does not alter the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr28[G-1] retains its original value when the configuration is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 39: Writes to pmpaddr28 are ignored when PMP entry 28 is locked.
RULE 40: The L bit of PMP entry 28 indicates that the entry is locked, causing writes to the configuration register and associated address registers, including pmpaddr28, to be ignored.
RULE 41: When pmpaddr28 is locked, it remains locked until the hart is reset.
RULE 42: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr28 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3cc; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 43: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr28 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3cc; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 44: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr28 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3cc; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 45: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr28.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3cc, a0; csrr a1, 0x3cc; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 46: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr28 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3cc; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr29
NUMBER: 0x3cd
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction on pmpaddr29 with a mask that modifies a bit other than G-1 will cause the read of pmpaddr29[G-1] to return 0.
RULE 2: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction on pmpaddr29 with a mask that modifies a bit other than G-1 will cause the read value 0 to be written back to pmpaddr29[G-1], updating the underlying stored value of pmpaddr29[G-1] to 0.
RULE 3: For RV64, pmpaddr29 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 4: pmpaddr29 is a WARL field because not all physical address bits may be implemented.
RULE 5: Reads or writes of pmpaddr29 are only permitted when the processor is executing in M-mode.
RULE 6: If the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 has its A field set to NA4, then the value stored in pmpaddr29 is of the form yyyy…yyyy and pmpaddr29 matches a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 7: If the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is set to NAPOT and the value stored in pmpaddr29 ends with a single zero (…0), then pmpaddr29 matches an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 8: If the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is set to NAPOT and the value stored in pmpaddr29 ends with the bit pattern …01, then pmpaddr29 matches a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 9: If the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is set to NAPOT and the value stored in pmpaddr29 ends with the bit pattern …011, then pmpaddr29 matches a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 10: If the PMP configuration register for pmpaddr29 has its A field set to NAPOT and the stored pmpaddr29 value consists entirely of ones, then the PMP entry matches a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN + 3 bytes (so any address check against this entry reports a match) and the entry’s encoding follows the intermediate‑size pattern defined in Table 24.
RULE 11: If the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 29 is set to TOR, then pmpaddr29 defines the top of the address range and the preceding address register pmpaddr28 defines the bottom of the address range.
RULE 12: If the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 29 is set to TOR, then entry 29 matches any address y such that pmpaddr28 ≤ y < pmpaddr29, irrespective of the value of the configuration register for entry 28.
RULE 13: If pmpaddr28 ≥ pmpaddr29 and the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 29 is TOR, then entry 29 matches no addresses.
RULE 14: When the PMP granularity G satisfies G ≥ 2 and bit 1 of the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is set (indicating NAPOT mode), then bits pmpaddr29[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 15: When the PMP granularity G satisfies G ≥ 1 and bit 1 of the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 is clear (indicating OFF or TOR mode), then bits pmpaddr29[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 16: Bits pmpaddr29[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for entry 29.
RULE 17: Although changing bit 1 of the A field of the PMP configuration register associated with pmpaddr29 alters the value read from pmpaddr29, it does not modify the underlying stored bits, and specifically bit pmpaddr29[G-1] retains its original stored value when the A field is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 18: Software may determine the PMP granularity by writing zero to pmp0cfg, writing all ones to pmpaddr29, and then reading back pmpaddr29; the index G of the least-significant set bit in the read value indicates that the granularity is 2^G + 2 bytes.
RULE 19: If the L bit of PMP entry 29 is set, writes to pmpaddr29 are ignored.
RULE 20: Once the L bit of PMP entry 29 has been set, the lock on pmpaddr29 persists until a hart reset occurs.
RULE 21: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 29 locks the entry and causes writes to pmpaddr29 to be ignored regardless of the value of the A field in pmp29 cfg.
RULE 22: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr29 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3cd; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr30
NUMBER: 0x3ce
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr30[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of pmpaddr30 returns 0 for that bit.
RULE 2: If a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction accesses pmpaddr30 and modifies a bit other than the G-1 bit, the read of pmpaddr30[G-1] will return 0.
RULE 3: If a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction accesses pmpaddr30 and modifies a bit other than the G-1 bit, the subsequent writeback will update the underlying value of pmpaddr30[G-1] to 0.
RULE 4: The CSR pmpaddr30 has Machine-level read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 5: The CSR pmpaddr30 may be read and written only when executing at Machine privilege level.
RULE 6: Because not all physical address bits may be implemented, the pmpaddr30 register is WARL.
RULE 7: When the A field in PMP entry 30's configuration register is set to TOR, pmpaddr30 defines the top of the address range for that entry, with pmpaddr29 defining the bottom.
RULE 8: When pmpcfg30.A = TOR, an address y matches PMP entry 30 if and only if pmpaddr29 ≤ y < pmpaddr30, regardless of the value of pmpcfg29.
RULE 9: If pmpaddr29 is greater than or equal to pmpaddr30 while pmpcfg30.A = TOR, then PMP entry 30 matches no addresses.
RULE 10: When the granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg30.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr30[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 11: When the granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg30.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr30[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 12: Bits pmpaddr30[G-1:0] are ignored by the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 13: Changing pmpcfg30.A[1] modifies the value read from pmpaddr30 but does not modify the underlying stored value of pmpaddr30.
RULE 14: The bit pmpaddr30[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg30.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 15: When pmpaddr30 bits are all ones (yyyy…yyyy) and pmpcfg30.A = NA4, the entry defines a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 16: When pmpaddr30 bits end with 01 (yyyy…yy01) and pmpcfg30.A = NAPOT, the entry defines a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 17: When pmpaddr30 bits end with 011 (yyyy…y011) and pmpcfg30.A = NAPOT, the entry defines a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 18: When pmpaddr30 bits start with yy01 followed by all ones (yy01…1111) and pmpcfg30.A = NAPOT, the entry defines a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 19: When pmpaddr30 bits start with y011 followed by all ones (y011…1111) and pmpcfg30.A = NAPOT, the entry defines a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 20: When pmpaddr30 bits are 0 followed by all ones (0111…1111) and pmpcfg30.A = NAPOT, the entry defines a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 21: When pmpaddr30 bits are all ones (1111…1111) and pmpcfg30.A = NAPOT, the entry defines a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 22: If PMP entry 30 is locked, any write to pmpaddr30 is ignored.
RULE 23: When the L bit of PMP entry 30 is set, the entry is locked and writes to pmpaddr30 are ignored.
RULE 24: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr30 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3ce; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 25: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr30 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3ce; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr31[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 but be read as 0.

RULE 8: For CSRRS or CSRRC with rs1 = x0, the instruction reads pmpaddr31 and does not write it.

RULE 24: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 31 locks the PMP entry, thereby causing writes to pmpaddr31 to be ignored even when the entry's A field is set to OFF.
RULE 25: When the L bit of PMP entry 31 is clear, the R/W/X permissions of pmpaddr31 apply only to S and U modes.
RULE 26: If pmpcfg[31].A equals TOR, then the value in pmpaddr30 is less than the value in pmpaddr31.

REGISTER: pmpaddr33
NUMBER: 0x3d1
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P
RULE 1: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction accesses the pmpaddr33 CSR, then any bit whose read value differs from the hidden underlying value may be changed to the underlying value even when the corresponding rs1 bit is zero; consequently, after execution the readback of pmpaddr33 may differ from its pre‑instruction value in those bits.
RULE 2: A CSRRC or CSRRS instruction that modifies a different bit of pmpaddr33 will cause the G-1 bit of pmpaddr33 to be read as 0.
RULE 3: The 0 read from the G-1 bit of pmpaddr33 by such a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction is then written back, updating its underlying value to 0.
RULE 4: If pmpaddr33 is accessed without machine‑mode read/write privilege, then the access raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = 2).
RULE 5: pmpaddr33 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address for RV64.
RULE 6: pmpaddr33 is WARL.
RULE 7: If a program writes a value to pmpaddr33 that has any non‑implementable bit set, then reading pmpaddr33 returns zero in those bits (the write of those bits is ignored).
RULE 8: pmpaddr33 can be accessed only when the hart is in M-mode.

RULE 24: If PMP entry 33 is locked, writes to pmpaddr33 are ignored.

REGISTER: pmpaddr34
NUMBER: 0x3d2
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies a bit other than the top-most G-1 bit of pmpaddr34, the hardware may read pmpaddr34[G-1] as 0 (even if its underlying value is 1) and subsequently write back 0, thereby possibly clearing the underlying value of pmpaddr34[G-1].
RULE 2: CSRRS and CSRRC always read the addressed CSR pmpaddr34 and cause any read side effects, regardless of the values in rs1 and rd.
RULE 3: When rs1 equals x0, a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction with csr = pmpaddr34 does not write pmpaddr34 and does not trigger any write-side effects.
RULE 4: When rs1 is not x0, a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction with csr = pmpaddr34 writes pmpaddr34 after performing the read-modify-write operation, and any write-side effects associated with writing pmpaddr34 occur.
RULE 5: If rs1 is not x0 and contains 0, then executing a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targeting pmpaddr34 does not trigger any per‑field side effects on pmpaddr34; the CSR’s value after the instruction remains unchanged except for any whole‑CSR write effects, and the destination register receives the original CSR value.
RULE 6: If an individual field of pmpaddr34 is written, then only the pmpaddr34 CSR is updated (the written field reflects the new value) and no other architectural state changes—no exception is raised, mcause remains unchanged, and no other CSR values are altered.
RULE 7: The read-modify-write semantics of CSRRS and CSRRC can indirectly clear the underlying pmpaddr34[G-1] bit even when the instruction does not explicitly modify that bit.
RULE 8: For RV64, pmpaddr34 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 9: pmpaddr34 can be accessed only when the hart is in M-mode.
RULE 10: The implementation may alter the value read from or written to pmpaddr34 to reflect only the implemented bits.
RULE 11: When pmpcfg34.A = 0 (OFF), pmpaddr34 is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 12: When pmpcfg34.A = 1 (TOR), the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr33 <= y < pmpaddr34, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg33.
RULE 13: If pmpaddr33 >= pmpaddr34 and pmpcfg34.A = 1 (TOR), then pmpaddr34 matches no addresses.
RULE 14: When pmpcfg34.A = 2 (NA4), the low-order bits of pmpaddr34 encode a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: When pmpcfg34.A = 3 (NAPOT), a low-order bit pattern ending in "0" (...yyy0) in pmpaddr34 encodes an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 16: When pmpcfg34.A = 3 (NAPOT), a low-order bit pattern ending in "01" (...yy01) in pmpaddr34 encodes a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 17: When pmpcfg34.A = 3 (NAPOT), low-order bit patterns of pmpaddr34 can encode NAPOT ranges up to the maximum 2^XLEN-byte range as defined by the encoding table.
RULE 18: When G >= 2 and pmpcfg34.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr34[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 19: When G >= 1 and pmpcfg34.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr34[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 20: Bits pmpaddr34[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 21: Changing pmpcfg34.A[1] affects the value read from pmpaddr34 but does not affect the underlying stored value in pmpaddr34.
RULE 22: The bit pmpaddr34[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg34.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 23: If the L bit of PMP entry 34 is set, writes to pmpaddr34 are ignored.
RULE 24: A PMP entry 34 that is locked, as indicated by its L bit, remains locked until the hart is reset, affecting the behavior of pmpaddr34.
RULE 25: When the L bit of PMP entry 34 is set, the R/W/X permissions linked to pmpaddr34 are enforced for all privilege modes.
RULE 26: When the L bit of PMP entry 34 is clear, any M-mode access that matches the PMP entry defined by pmpaddr34 will succeed.
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr34 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3d2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 28: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr34 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3d2; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 29: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr34 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3d2; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr34 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3d2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr35
NUMBER: 0x3d3
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: On an RV64 hart, pmpaddr35 encodes bits 55-2 of the 56-bit physical address used for PMP entry 35.
RULE 2: If a value containing unimplemented bits is written to the pmpaddr35 CSR, then a subsequent read of pmpaddr35 returns a value in which all unimplemented bits are cleared (i.e., the readback value contains only the implemented bits).
RULE 3: When a PMP entry's configuration (A field) selects the preceding-address mode, pmpaddr35 can be used as the address register for PMP entry 36, directly affecting the region defined for that entry.
RULE 4: If the A field of pmpcfg35 is 0, then pmpaddr35 operates in OFF mode; if the A field is 1, then pmpaddr35 operates in TOR mode; if the A field is 2, then pmpaddr35 operates in NA4 mode; and if the A field is 3, then pmpaddr35 operates in NAPOT mode.
RULE 5: When pmpcfg35.A equals TOR, pmpaddr35 supplies the upper bound of the address range so that any address y satisfying pmpaddr34 ≤ y < pmpaddr35 is matched (the value of pmpcfg34 is irrelevant).
RULE 6: When pmpcfg35.A equals TOR and pmpaddr34 is greater than or equal to pmpaddr35, the pmpaddr35 entry matches no addresses.
RULE 7: When pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT, the low-order bits of pmpaddr35 encode the size of the range according to the pattern definitions in Table 24.
RULE 8: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `yyyy…yyyy`, the entry defines a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 9: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `yyyy…yyy0`, the entry defines an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `yyyy…yy01`, the entry defines a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `yyyy…y011`, the entry defines a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `yy01…1111`, the entry defines a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `y011…1111`, the entry defines a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `0111…1111`, the entry defines a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: If pmpcfg35.A equals NAPOT and pmpaddr35 matches the pattern `1111…1111`, the entry defines a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 16: When the PMP granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg35.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), reads of bits pmpaddr35[G-2:0] return all ones.
RULE 17: When the PMP granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg35.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), reads of bits pmpaddr35[G-1:0] return all zeros.
RULE 18: Bits pmpaddr35[G-1:0] are ignored by the TOR address-matching logic.

RULE 20: The stored bit pmpaddr35[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg35.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 21: If the PMP granularity G is at least 1, the NA4 mode is not selectable for entry 35, so pmpaddr35 cannot be used with a pmpcfg35.A encoding of NA4.

REGISTER: pmpaddr37
NUMBER: 0x3d5
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies a bit other than the top-most PMP address bit of pmpaddr37, the hardware must read the current read value of pmpaddr37[G-1] (which may be 0 even if the underlying value is 1), must write that read value back, and must update the underlying value of that bit to match the read value.
RULE 2: CSRRS and CSRRC always read pmpaddr37 and cause any read side effects defined for pmpaddr37 regardless of the rs1 and rd fields.
RULE 3: CSRRS or CSRRC with rs1 = x0 must not write to pmpaddr37 and shall not cause any write side effects on pmpaddr37.
RULE 4: For any CSRRS or CSRRC targeting pmpaddr37, the CSR is always read and it is written only when rs1 ≠ x0.
RULE 5: CSRRSI or CSRRCI with uimm[4:0] = 0 shall not write to pmpaddr37 and shall not cause any write side effects on pmpaddr37.
RULE 6: CSRRSI or CSRRCI with uimm[4:0] ≠ 0 must read and write pmpaddr37 and must follow the same per-field side-effect rules as CSRRS or CSRRC.
RULE 7: A CSRRW targeting pmpaddr37 with rs1 = x0 must write the value 0 into pmpaddr37.
RULE 8: The architectural privilege level for pmpaddr37 is MRW (Machine-Read/Write).
RULE 9: Reads or writes to the register pmpaddr37 MUST be performed only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 10: When executing on an RV64 hart, the value written to the register pmpaddr37 supplies bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address for PMP entry 37.
RULE 11: If a write to pmpaddr37 sets any bits that correspond to physical‑address bits not implemented in the processor, then the implementation may silently mask those bits or cause the register to read back a different legal value, and no exception is raised.
RULE 12: With pmpcfg37.A = 2 (NA4), the low-order bits of pmpaddr37 are all ones and represent a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: With pmpcfg37.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr37 ending in 0, the encoded region size is 8 bytes.
RULE 14: With pmpcfg37.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr37 ending in 01, the encoded region size is 16 bytes.
RULE 15: When pmpcfg37.A = TOR, pmpaddr37 serves as the top bound of the address range and the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr36 ≤ y < pmpaddr37, regardless of the value of pmpcfg36.
RULE 16: If G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg37.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), then bits pmpaddr37[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 17: If G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg37.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), then bits pmpaddr37[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 18: Bits pmpaddr37[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 19: Changing pmpcfg37.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr37 but does not alter the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr37[G-1] retains its original value when the mode is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and back to NAPOT.
RULE 20: If the L bit in pmpcfg37 is set, writes to pmpaddr37 are ignored.
RULE 21: The lock of PMP entry 37, which governs pmpaddr37, remains in effect until the hart is reset.
RULE 22: The architectural rule that a locked PMP entry causes writes to its pmpaddr register to be ignored applies to entry 37, so the L bit in pmpcfg37 directly causes the write-ignore behavior for pmpaddr37.
RULE 23: A PMP rule that includes pmpaddr37 is valid only when pmpcfg37.A is not OFF.
RULE 24: If pmpcfg37.A TOR, then a PMP rule that includes pmpaddr37 is valid only when pmpaddr36 is less than pmpaddr37.
RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr37 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3d5; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 26: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr37 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3d5; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: pmpaddr38
NUMBER: 0x3d6
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: The register pmpaddr38 may have an underlying bit value that differs from the value read, such that pmpaddr38[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 but be read as 0.
RULE 2: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies a different bit of pmpaddr38, the instruction will read the mismatched bit value and then write that same read value back, updating the underlying value to match the read value.
RULE 3: If the mismatched bit of pmpaddr38 reads as 0, executing CSRRS or CSRRC to modify a different bit will cause 0 to be read and then written back, updating the underlying value to 0.

RULE 14: If pmpcfg38.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr38 match the pattern `1111…1111` then the entry defines a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.

RULE 11: When pmpcfg42.A = TOR, the PMP entry 42 matches any address y such that pmpaddr41 ≤ y < pmpaddr42, irrespective of the configuration of entry 41.
RULE 12: If pmpaddr41 ≥ pmpaddr42 and pmpcfg42.A = TOR, then PMP entry 42 matches no addresses.
RULE 13: When the PMP granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg42.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr42[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 14: When the PMP granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg42.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr42[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 15: The low-order G bits of pmpaddr42 are ignored by the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 16: Changing pmpcfg42.A[1] alters the read value of pmpaddr42 but does not modify the stored bit pmpaddr42[G-1], which retains its original value across mode changes between NAPOT, TOR, and OFF.
RULE 17: If PMP entry 42 is locked, any write to the pmpaddr42 CSR is ignored.
RULE 18: If PMP entry 42 is locked and the address-matching field A of its configuration register is set to TOR, any write to the pmpaddr41 CSR is ignored.
RULE 19: The L bit in the configuration register for PMP entry 42 indicates that the entry is locked, causing writes to the configuration register and all associated address registers, including pmpaddr42, to be ignored.
RULE 20: If pmpcfg42.A equals TOR, then pmpaddr41 is less than pmpaddr42.
RULE 21: During a PMP reset, pmpaddr42 is re-initialized to its reset default value.
RULE 22: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr42 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3da; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 23: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr42 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3da; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 24: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr42 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3da; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 25: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr42.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3da, a0; csrr a1, 0x3da; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 26: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr42 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3da; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr43
NUMBER: 0x3db
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: The pmpaddr43[G-1] field may have an underlying value of 1 but be read as 0.
RULE 2: Executing CSRRC or CSRRS to modify a different bit will cause 0 to be read from pmpaddr43[G-1] and then written back, updating the underlying value to 0.
RULE 3: If a CSR instruction accesses address 0x3B (pmpaddr43) while the processor is not in Machine mode, the instruction raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = 2).
RULE 4: pmpaddr43 is machine-read/write (MRW).
RULE 5: When executing on an RV64 hart, pmpaddr43 encodes bits 55-2 of the 56-bit physical address for PMP entry 43.
RULE 6: Accesses to pmpaddr43 MUST occur only while the hart is in M-mode.
RULE 7: If pmpcfg43.A is set to NA4 but pmpaddr43 does not have the required low‑order bits all set to 1 (the pattern that encodes a 4‑byte NAPOT range), then an access to the 4‑byte aligned address that would be covered by a correct encoding raises a load/store access‑fault exception.
RULE 8: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] ends with a single 0 (...0), then the PMP entry matches an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 9: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] ends with the bits 01 (...01), then the PMP entry matches a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] ends with the bits 011 (...011), then the PMP entry matches a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] has the form yy01...1111, then the PMP entry matches a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] has the form y011...1111, then the PMP entry matches a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] has the form 0111...1111, then the PMP entry matches a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If pmpcfg43.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr43[XLEN-2:0] has the form 1111...1111, then the PMP entry matches a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: If pmpcfg43.A = TOR, then pmpaddr43 defines the upper bound of the address range so that the PMP entry matches any address y satisfying pmpaddr42 ≤ y < pmpaddr43, independent of pmpcfg42.
RULE 16: If pmpcfg43.A = TOR and pmpaddr42 ≥ pmpaddr43, then the PMP entry 43 matches no addresses.
RULE 17: When the PMP granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg43.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), then the bits pmpaddr43[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 18: When the PMP granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg43.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), then the bits pmpaddr43[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 19: The bits pmpaddr43[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 20: Changing pmpcfg43.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr43 but does not modify the underlying stored value, and the bit pmpaddr43[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg43.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 21: If PMP entry 43 is locked, any write to pmpaddr43 is ignored.
RULE 22: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 43 locks the entry, causing writes to pmpaddr43 to be ignored.
RULE 23: A locked PMP entry 43 remains locked until a hart reset, so the ignore-write behavior for pmpaddr43 persists until a hart reset.
RULE 24: Setting the L bit locks PMP entry 43 even when its A field is OFF, and consequently writes to pmpaddr43 are ignored when A=OFF.
RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr43 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3db; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 26: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr43 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3db; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 27: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr43 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3db; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 28: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr43.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3db, a0; csrr a1, 0x3db; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr43 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3db; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr44
NUMBER: 0x3dc
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: When the hart implements RV64, pmpaddr44 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 2: Because not all physical-address bits may be implemented, pmpaddr44 is WARL.
RULE 3: When the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 44 is NA4, the low-order bits of pmpaddr44 are interpreted as "yyyy…yyyy" and the entry matches a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 4: If the PMP configuration register entry 44 has its A field set to NAPOT and the low‑order bits of pmpaddr44 end with the pattern “…1110” (all ones except the least‑significant bit), then the PMP entry defines an exact 8‑byte NAPOT range: a memory access to any address within that 8‑byte range causes the PMP match flag for entry 44 to be set, whereas an access to any address outside that range leaves the match flag cleared.
RULE 5: When the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 44 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr44 end with the pattern "yyyy…yy01", the entry matches a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 6: When the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 44 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr44 end with the pattern "yyyy…y011", the entry matches a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 7: If the A field of PMP configuration register entry 44 is NAPOT but the low‑order bits of pmpaddr44 are not a contiguous run of 1s (i.e., they do not follow the required pattern where each added leading 1 doubles the range size up to the maximum encoding), then the hardware treats the entry as the minimum NAPOT range (8 bytes) and a memory access to an address that should be covered by a larger range raises a load/store access‑fault exception.
RULE 8: When the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 44 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr44 match the pattern "y011…1111", the entry matches a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 9: When the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 44 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr44 match the pattern "0111…1111", the entry matches a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 10: When the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 44 is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr44 match the pattern "1111…1111", the entry matches a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: When the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 44 is TOR, pmpaddr44 forms the top of the address range, pmpaddr43 forms the bottom, and the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr43 ≤ y < pmpaddr44, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg43.A.
RULE 12: If pmpaddr43 ≥ pmpaddr44 and the A field of the PMP configuration register for entry 44 is TOR, then entry 44 matches no addresses.
RULE 13: When the PMP granularity G is at least 2 and the A[1] bit of pmpcfg44 is set (indicating NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr44[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 14: When the PMP granularity G is at least 1 and the A[1] bit of pmpcfg44 is clear (indicating OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr44[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 15: Bits pmpaddr44[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for entry 44.
RULE 16: Changing the A[1] bit of pmpcfg44 changes the value read from pmpaddr44 but does not modify the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr44[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg44.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 17: Setting the L bit for PMP entry 44 locks the entry and causes writes to pmpaddr44 to be ignored.
RULE 18: A locked PMP entry 44 remains locked until the hart is reset.
RULE 19: When the L bit of PMP entry 44 is set, writes to pmpaddr44 are ignored regardless of the value of the A field.
RULE 20: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr44 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3dc; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 21: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr44 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3dc; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 22: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr44 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3dc; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 23: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr44.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3dc, a0; csrr a1, 0x3dc; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 24: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr44 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3dc; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr44 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3dc; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr45
NUMBER: 0x3dd
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr45 [G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 while the value read from pmpaddr45 [G-1] is 0.
RULE 2: When a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction modifies a different bit while pmpaddr45 [G-1] reads as 0, the instruction reads 0 from pmpaddr45 [G-1] and writes back 0, updating the underlying value of pmpaddr45 [G-1] to 0.
RULE 3: pmpaddr45 is accessible only in M-mode.
RULE 4: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr45 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 5: If a value with any unimplemented physical‑address bits set is written to pmpaddr45, then reading pmpaddr45 must return the written value with all unimplemented physical‑address bits cleared (the CSR readback value has zeros in every unimplemented physical‑address bit).
RULE 6: If pmpcfg45.A = 0 then pmpaddr45 operates in OFF mode, defining a null region that is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 7: If pmpcfg45.A = 1 then pmpaddr45 operates in TOR mode, acting as the top of an address range whose bottom is defined by pmpaddr44.
RULE 8: If pmpcfg45.A = 2 then pmpaddr45 operates in NA4 mode, defining a naturally aligned four-byte region.
RULE 9: If pmpcfg45.A = 3 then pmpaddr45 operates in NAPOT mode, defining a naturally aligned power-of-two region of size at least eight bytes.
RULE 10: When pmpcfg45.A = 2 (NA4) the low-order bits of pmpaddr45 encode a 4-byte NAPOT range, with the most-significant bits (the "y" bits) unchanged.
RULE 11: When pmpcfg45.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr45 end in 0 (pattern …yyy0) the register encodes an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: When pmpcfg45.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr45 end in 01 (pattern …yy01) the register encodes a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: When pmpcfg45.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr45 end in 011 (pattern …y011) the register encodes a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: When pmpcfg45.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr45 match the pattern …yy01…1111 the register encodes a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN bytes.
RULE 15: When pmpcfg45.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr45 match the pattern …y011…1111 the register encodes a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN + 1 bytes.
RULE 16: When pmpcfg45.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr45 match the pattern …1111…1111 the register encodes a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN + 3 bytes.
RULE 17: If pmpcfg45.A = TOR then an address y matches the PMP entry 45 precisely when pmpaddr44 ≤ y < pmpaddr45, regardless of the value of pmpcfg44.A.
RULE 18: If pmpcfg45.A = TOR and pmpaddr44 ≥ pmpaddr45 then PMP entry 45 matches no addresses.
RULE 19: When the granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg45.A[1] is set (indicating NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr45[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 20: When the granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg45.A[1] is clear (indicating OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr45[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 21: Bits pmpaddr45[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for PMP entry 45.
RULE 22: Changing pmpcfg45.A[1] does not alter the stored value of pmpaddr45, and the bit pmpaddr45[G-1] retains its original value when the mode is changed away from and later restored to NAPOT.
RULE 23: If PMP entry 45 is locked, writes to pmpaddr45 are ignored.
RULE 24: If the L bit of PMP entry 45 is set, the PMP entry 45, which governs pmpaddr45, is locked even when its A field is OFF.
RULE 25: If pmpcfg45.A is not OFF but the combination of pmpcfg45 and pmpaddr45 does not encode a valid protected physical memory region, then the PMP entry is treated as disabled (as if A were OFF), so accesses that would be denied by a valid entry are allowed and no access‑fault exception is raised.
RULE 26: When pmpcfg45.A is TOR, pmpaddr44 must be less than pmpaddr45.
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr45 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3dd; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 28: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr45 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3dd; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 29: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr45 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3dd; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 30: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr45.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3dd, a0; csrr a1, 0x3dd; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr45 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3dd; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr45 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3dd; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr46
NUMBER: 0x3de
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: The privilege level for pmpaddr46 is MRW (machine-read/write).
RULE 2: pmpaddr46 is a PMP address register CSR and is only accessible to M-mode.
RULE 3: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr46 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 4: If a write to pmpaddr46 sets any bits beyond the implementation’s supported physical‑address width, then a subsequent read of pmpaddr46 returns the value masked to the supported width, with all higher bits cleared.
RULE 5: If the A field in pmpcfg46 is 0 (OFF), then the PMP address register pmpaddr46 is ignored and no access can be trapped by this entry; if the A field is 1 (TOR), then pmpaddr46 supplies the top bound of the address range and an access whose address is ≥ the lower bound (from pmpaddr45) and < pmpaddr46 triggers the entry’s permission check; if the A field is 2 (NA4), then pmpaddr46 defines a single 4‑byte region and any access whose address equals pmpaddr46[31:2]·4 triggers the entry’s permission check; if the A field is 3 (NAPOT), then pmpaddr46 encodes a naturally aligned power‑of‑two region and any access whose address falls within that region triggers the entry’s permission check. Any mismatch between the A field value and the way pmpaddr46 is interpreted results in the PMP check using the mode indicated by the A field; no exception is raised solely for an incorrectly formatted pmpaddr46 value.
RULE 6: When pmpcfg46.A is TOR, the PMP entry 46 matches any address y such that pmpaddr45 <= y < pmpaddr46.
RULE 7: If pmpaddr45 is greater than or equal to pmpaddr46 while pmpcfg46.A is TOR, then PMP entry 46 matches no addresses.
RULE 8: When pmpcfg46.A is NAPOT, the low-order bits of pmpaddr46 encode the size of the NAPOT range according to the patterns defined in Table 24.
RULE 9: If the platform granularity G is at least 2 and pmpcfg46.A[1] equals 1, reading pmpaddr46 returns all ones in bits [G-2:0].
RULE 10: If the platform granularity G is at least 1 and pmpcfg46.A[1] equals 0, reading pmpaddr46 returns all zeros in bits [G-1:0].
RULE 11: Bits pmpaddr46[G-1:0] are ignored by the TOR address-matching logic and do not affect whether an address falls within the TOR range.
RULE 12: Changing pmpcfg46.A[1] does not modify the stored value of pmpaddr46, and specifically bit [G-1] of pmpaddr46 retains its original value when pmpcfg46.A is changed between NAPOT and TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 13: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr46 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3de; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 14: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr46 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3de; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: pmpaddr49
NUMBER: 0x3e1
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: The pmpaddr49[G-1] bit may have an underlying value of 1 while reads of that bit return 0.
RULE 2: When a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction modifies any bit of pmpaddr49 other than G-1, the read of pmpaddr49[G-1] returns 0.
RULE 3: When a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction modifies any bit of pmpaddr49 other than G-1, the value 0 read from pmpaddr49[G-1] is written back, causing the underlying value of pmpaddr49[G-1] to become 0.
RULE 4: Access to pmpaddr49 is permitted only in machine mode (M-mode).
RULE 5: pmpaddr49 is a WARL (write-any-values-that-are-read-logical) register.
RULE 6: When the PMP entry's A field is set to TOR, the address register pmpaddr49 defines the top of the protected address range.
RULE 7: When the PMP entry's A field is set to TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr48 ≤ y < pmpaddr49, regardless of the value of pmpcfg48.
RULE 8: If pmpaddr48 ≥ pmpaddr49 and pmpcfg49.A = TOR, then PMP entry 49 matches no addresses.
RULE 9: In NAPOT address-matching mode, the low-order bits of pmpaddr49 encode the size of the address range according to the patterns defined in Table 24.
RULE 10: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg49.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr49[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 11: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg49.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr49[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 12: The bits pmpaddr49[G-1:0] do not influence the TOR address-matching computation.
RULE 13: Changing pmpcfg49.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr49 but does not modify the underlying stored bits, so pmpaddr49[G-1] retains its original value when the mode is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF and back to NAPOT.
RULE 14: When PMP entry 49 is locked, writes to pmpaddr49 are ignored.
RULE 15: Setting the L bit locks the PMP entry that maps to pmpaddr49 even when its A field is set to OFF.
RULE 16: Because the lock applies regardless of the A field value, writes to pmpaddr49 are ignored regardless of the A field setting.
RULE 17: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr49 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3e1; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 18: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr49 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3e1; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 19: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr49 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3e1; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 20: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr49.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3e1, a0; csrr a1, 0x3e1; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 21: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr49 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3e1; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr50
NUMBER: 0x3e2
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: Executing a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that modifies a bit other than the most-significant bit causes a read of 0 from the most-significant bit of pmpaddr50.
RULE 2: After such a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction reads 0 from the most-significant bit of pmpaddr50, the instruction writes that 0 back, updating the underlying value of the most-significant bit of pmpaddr50 to 0.
RULE 3: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targeting pmpaddr50 has rs1 = x0, the instruction does not write to pmpaddr50; otherwise it writes to pmpaddr50.
RULE 4: A CSRRS or CSRRC instruction always reads pmpaddr50, regardless of the values of rs1 and rd, and therefore always triggers any read side effects of pmpaddr50.
RULE 5: pmpaddr50 can be read or written only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 6: In an RV64 implementation, pmpaddr50 holds bits 55-2 of the 56-bit physical address used by PMP entry 50.
RULE 7: pmpaddr50 is a WARL register, meaning any value written may be read back, but the write may be restricted to the subset of address bits that are physically implemented.
RULE 8: The value of pmpcfg50.A determines how pmpaddr50 is interpreted.
RULE 9: When pmpcfg50.A is NAPOT, the low-order bits of pmpaddr50 select the NAPOT range size.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg50.A is NAPOT and pmpaddr50 matches the pattern yyyy…yyy0, the entry defines an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: If pmpcfg50.A is NAPOT and pmpaddr50 matches the pattern yyyy…yy01, the entry defines a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg50.A is NAPOT and pmpaddr50 matches the pattern yyyy…y011, the entry defines a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If pmpcfg50.A is NAPOT and pmpaddr50 matches the pattern yy01…1111, the entry defines a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If pmpcfg50.A is NAPOT and pmpaddr50 matches the pattern y011…1111, the entry defines a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: If pmpcfg50.A is NAPOT and pmpaddr50 matches the pattern 1111…1111, the entry defines a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 16: When pmpcfg50.A is TOR, pmpaddr50 provides the top (exclusive upper bound) of the address range for PMP entry 50.
RULE 17: When pmpcfg50.A is TOR, any address y satisfying pmpaddr49 ≤ y < pmpaddr50 matches entry 50 irrespective of pmpcfg49.
RULE 18: If pmpcfg50.A is TOR and pmpaddr49 ≥ pmpaddr50, then entry 50 matches no addresses.
RULE 19: With granularity G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg50.A set to NAPOT, the bits pmpaddr50[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 20: With granularity G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg50.A set to OFF or TOR, the bits pmpaddr50[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 21: The bits pmpaddr50[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for entry 50.
RULE 22: Changing pmpcfg50.A between NAPOT and TOR or OFF does not modify the stored value of pmpaddr50[G-1]; the bit remains unchanged.
RULE 23: If PMP entry 50 is locked, writes to pmpaddr50 are ignored.
RULE 24: If PMP entry 50 is locked, writes to pmpcfg50 are ignored, and the lock also causes writes to pmpaddr50 to be ignored.
RULE 25: If PMP entry 50 is locked and pmpcfg50.A is set to TOR, writes to pmpaddr49 are ignored, and the lock likewise prevents writes to pmpaddr50.
RULE 26: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 50 locks the entry even when the A field is OFF, causing the lock behavior that applies to pmpaddr50.
RULE 27: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr50 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3e2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 28: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr50 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3e2; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 29: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr50 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3e2; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 30: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr50.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3e2, a0; csrr a1, 0x3e2; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 31: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr50 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3e2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr50 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3e2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr51
NUMBER: 0x3e3
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P
RULE 1: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction accesses pmpaddr51 and a bit’s current read value differs from its underlying stored value, then that bit can be altered by the instruction even when the corresponding rs1 bit is zero, causing the CSR read‑back value after execution to differ from the original value for that bit.

RULE 6: pmpaddr51 is a WARL register because not all physical address bits may be implemented.
RULE 7: pmpaddr51 is accessible only in M-mode.
RULE 8: The A field of pmpcfg51 encodes the address-matching mode of pmpaddr51, where OFF = 0, TOR = 1, NA4 = 2, and NAPOT = 3.
RULE 9: When pmpcfg51.A is NA4 or NAPOT, the low-order bits of pmpaddr51 encode the size of the address range according to the pattern defined in Table 24.

RULE 11: When pmpcfg51.A is TOR, the PMP entry matches any address y satisfying pmpaddr50 ≤ y < pmpaddr51, independent of pmpcfg50.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg51.A is TOR and pmpaddr50 is greater than or equal to pmpaddr51, then the PMP entry matches no addresses.

RULE 20: Setting the L bit for PMP entry 51 locks the entry and causes writes to pmpaddr51 to be ignored even when the A field is set to OFF.

RULE 22: For the PMP entry that uses pmpaddr51, the associated pmpcfg[51].A field MUST NOT be OFF for the entry to encode a valid protected physical memory region.
RULE 23: If the associated pmpcfg[51].A field is TOR then pmpaddr50 MUST be less than pmpaddr51.

REGISTER: pmpaddr53
NUMBER: 0x3e5
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpaddr53[G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 while a read of that bit returns 0.
RULE 2: Executing a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction on pmpaddr53 to modify a bit other than G-1 will cause a read of pmpaddr53[G-1] that returns 0 and will subsequently write back 0, updating its underlying value to 0.
RULE 3: Any CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that targets pmpaddr53 always reads pmpaddr53 and triggers any read-side effects regardless of the values of rs1 and rd.
RULE 4: For a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targeting pmpaddr53, if rs1 equals x0 the instruction reads pmpaddr53 but does not write it.
RULE 5: For a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction targeting pmpaddr53, if rs1 is not x0 the instruction reads pmpaddr53 and writes it, subject to the per-field side-effect rules.
RULE 6: The privilege of pmpaddr53 is MRW, allowing read and write access only in machine mode.
RULE 7: If a software writes any value to pmpaddr53, then no exception is raised and a subsequent read of pmpaddr53 returns the written value with all illegal bits cleared (i.e., the readback value is the written value masked to the register’s legal field).
RULE 8: pmpaddr53 can be read only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 9: pmpaddr53 can be written only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 10: When a PMP setting that additionally uses the preceding address register applies to PMP entry 53, the behavior of pmpaddr53 can be directly affected by the value in pmpaddr52.
RULE 11: If the A field of PMP entry 53 is 0 (OFF), the entry is disabled and matches no addresses, and the value stored in pmpaddr53 is irrelevant for matching.
RULE 12: In TOR mode, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr52 <= y < pmpaddr53, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg52.
RULE 13: If pmpaddr52 >= pmpaddr53 and pmpcfg53.A = TOR, then PMP entry 53 matches no addresses.
RULE 14: If the A field of PMP entry 53 is NA4, the entire contents of pmpaddr53 are used as a 4-byte NAPOT range aligned to a four-byte boundary, and the low-order bits are not interpreted for size.
RULE 15: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 are all 1, the NAPOT region size is 4 bytes.
RULE 16: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 end with 01, the NAPOT region size is 16 bytes.
RULE 17: If the least-significant bits of pmpaddr53 end with 011, the NAPOT region size is 32 bytes.
RULE 18: If the least‑significant bits of pmpaddr53 match the pattern …yy01…1111, then the PMP entry defines a NAPOT region whose size is exactly 2 × XLEN bytes (an access to the base address plus 2 × XLEN − 1 bytes succeeds, while an access to base + 2 × XLEN bytes triggers a PMP access‑fault exception).
RULE 19: If the least‑significant bits of pmpaddr53 match the pattern …y011…1111, then the PMP entry is interpreted as a NAPOT region of size 2 × XLEN + 1 bytes; accesses to addresses within that range are granted according to the entry’s permissions, and accesses to any address outside that range raise a PMP access‑fault exception.
RULE 20: If the least‑significant bits of PMP address register pmpaddr53 match the pattern …0111…1111, then the decoded NAPOT region size for that entry is 2 * XLEN + 2 bytes.
RULE 21: If the least‑significant bits of pmpaddr53 are all 1, then the NAPOT region defined by that PMP entry has a size of 2*XLEN+3 bytes, so an access to any address within that range succeeds and an access to the first address beyond the range triggers a PMP access‑fault exception.
RULE 22: If G >= 2 and pmpcfg53.A[1] is set (entry 53 is in NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr53[G-2:0] read as all ones regardless of their stored values.
RULE 23: If G >= 1 and pmpcfg53.A[1] is clear (entry 53 is OFF or TOR), bits pmpaddr53[G-1:0] read as all zeros and these bits do not affect TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 24: Changing pmpcfg53.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr53 but does not change the underlying value stored in the register.
RULE 25: Bit pmpaddr53[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg53.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 26: If PMP entry 53 is locked, any write to the address register pmpaddr53 is ignored.
RULE 27: When the L bit of PMP entry 53 is set, writes to the address register pmpaddr53 are ignored.
RULE 28: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 53 locks the entry and causes writes to pmpaddr53 to be ignored even if the A field of pmpcfg53 is OFF.
RULE 29: A locked PMP entry 53, and therefore its address register pmpaddr53, remains locked and write-ignored until the hart is reset.
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr53 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3e5; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr53 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3e5; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: pmpaddr54

MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR

RULE 1: If a privilege level lower than Machine attempts to read or write the CSR pmpaddr54, then an illegal‑instruction exception is raised (mcause = 2).
