REGISTER: pmpaddr55
NUMBER: 0x3e7
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: The G-1 bit of pmpaddr55 (pmpaddr55[G-1]) may have an underlying stored value of 1 while being read as 0.
RULE 2: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction that modifies any bit of pmpaddr55 other than G-1 MUST cause the value read from pmpaddr55[G-1] (which may be 0) to be written back to the register, thereby updating the underlying stored value of pmpaddr55[G-1] to the value that was read.
RULE 3: If a non‑Machine privilege level attempts to read or write pmpaddr55, then an illegal‑instruction exception is raised (mcause = 2); otherwise, a Machine‑mode read of pmpaddr55 returns the value most recently written to it.
RULE 4: In RV64 implementations, pmpaddr55 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 5: pmpaddr55 can be read only while the hart is in machine mode.
RULE 6: pmpaddr55 can be written only while the hart is in machine mode.
RULE 7: When the configuration register field A for PMP entry 55 is 1 (TOR), pmpaddr55 provides the top bound of the address range while the preceding address register provides the bottom bound.
RULE 8: When entry 55 has A = TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr54 ≤ y < pmpaddr55, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg54.
RULE 9: When entry 55 has A = TOR and pmpaddr54 is greater than or equal to pmpaddr55, the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 10: When entry 55 has A = 2 (NA4), the low-order bits of pmpaddr55 follow the pattern …yyyy…yyyy to define a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: When entry 55 has A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr55 match the pattern …yyyy…yyy0, the entry defines an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: When entry 55 has A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr55 match the pattern …yyyy…yy01, the entry defines a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: When entry 55 has A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr55 match the pattern …yyyy…y011, the entry defines a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: When entry 55 has A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr55 match the pattern …yy01…1111, the entry defines a 2·XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: When entry 55 has A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr55 match the pattern …y011…1111, the entry defines a 2·XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 16: When entry 55 has A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr55 match the pattern …0111…1111, the entry defines a 2·XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 17: When entry 55 has A = 3 (NAPOT) and the low-order bits of pmpaddr55 match the pattern …1111…1111, the entry defines a 2·XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 18: When the granularity G is at least 2 and the high bit A[1] of the configuration register for entry 55 is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr55[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 19: When the granularity G is at least 1 and the high bit A[1] of the configuration register for entry 55 is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr55[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 20: Bits pmpaddr55[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for entry 55.
RULE 21: The stored bit pmpaddr55[G-1] retains its original value when the A field of entry 55 is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT, even though the value read from pmpaddr55 may change.
RULE 22: If PMP entry 55 is locked, writes to the pmpaddr55 register are ignored.
RULE 23: Setting the L bit of PMP entry 55 locks the entry even when the A field is OFF, causing writes to pmpaddr55 to be ignored.
RULE 24: When the L bit of PMP entry 55 is set, the R, W, and X permission bits associated with pmpaddr55 are enforced for all privilege modes.
RULE 25: When the L bit of PMP entry 55 is clear, any machine-mode access that matches the address range defined by pmpaddr55 succeeds regardless of the R, W, and X permission bits.
RULE 26: When the L bit of PMP entry 55 is clear, the R, W, and X permission bits associated with pmpaddr55 apply only to supervisor and user mode accesses.
RULE 27: The contents of pmpaddr55 together with pmpcfg55 encode a valid protected physical memory region only when pmpcfg55.A is not OFF.
RULE 28: When pmpcfg55.A equals TOR, the address stored in pmpaddr54 must be less than the address stored in pmpaddr55.
RULE 29: If the L bit in pmpcfg55 is 1, the PMP entry that includes pmpaddr55 is Locked.
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr55 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3e7; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr55 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3e7; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: pmpaddr56
NUMBER: 0x3e8
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies any bit of pmpaddr56 other than bit G-1 while the stored value of pmpaddr56[G-1] is 1 and a read of pmpaddr56 returns 0, the instruction will cause 0 to be read from pmpaddr56[G-1] and then written back, updating the stored value of pmpaddr56[G-1] to 0.

RULE 3: If a non‑Machine privilege level attempts to read or write the pmpaddr56 CSR, then the core raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = 2); otherwise, a Machine‑mode read returns the current address value and a Machine‑mode write updates the register.
RULE 4: On RV64 harts, pmpaddr56 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 5: A write to pmpaddr56 may be masked to the subset of physical address bits that are implemented.
RULE 6: When PMP entry 56 is configured in TOR address-matching mode, pmpaddr56 may serve as the upper bound address while pmpaddr55 supplies the lower bound.
RULE 7: If pmpcfg56.A = 0, pmpaddr56 defines a null region (disabled).
RULE 8: If pmpcfg56.A = 1, pmpaddr56 defines the top of a TOR address range.
RULE 9: If pmpcfg56.A = 2, pmpaddr56 defines a naturally aligned four-byte (NA4) region.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg56.A = 3, pmpaddr56 defines a naturally aligned power-of-two region of size at least eight bytes (NAPOT).
RULE 11: If pmpcfg56.A = TOR, the address range matched by pmpaddr56 includes all addresses y such that pmpaddr55 ≤ y < pmpaddr56, irrespective of pmpcfg55.A.
RULE 12: If pmpcfg56.A = TOR and pmpaddr55 ≥ pmpaddr56, the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 13: If pmpcfg56.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr56 ends with …0 (pattern yyyy…yyy0), the matched region is an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: If pmpcfg56.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr56 ends with …011 (pattern yyyy…y011), the matched region is a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: If pmpcfg56.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr56 matches the pattern yy01…1111, the matched region size is 2 XLEN-byte.
RULE 16: If pmpcfg56.A is set to NAPOT and pmpaddr56 holds the bit pattern 0 followed by all 1s, then PMP entry 56 matches a region whose size is 2^(XLEN+2) bytes (2 XLEN+2‑byte), so an access to the address at the base plus 2^(XLEN+2)‑1 is treated as inside the region and an access to the base plus 2^(XLEN+2) is treated as outside the region.
RULE 17: If pmpcfg56.A = NAPOT and pmpaddr56 matches the pattern 1111…1111, the matched region size is 2 XLEN+3-byte.

RULE 19: If G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg56.A[1] is clear, bits pmpaddr56[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 20: Bits pmpaddr56[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 21: Changing pmpcfg56.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr56 but does not change the underlying stored value; specifically, pmpaddr56[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg56.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.

RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr56 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3e8; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

RULE 3: When the A field of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is 0, the entry is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 4: When the A field of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is 1 (TOR), pmpaddr60 provides the top of the address range.
RULE 5: When the A field of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is 2 (NA4), the entry matches a naturally aligned four-byte region.
RULE 6: When the A field of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is 3 (NAPOT), the entry matches a naturally aligned power-of-two region of size at least eight bytes.
RULE 7: If the A field of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is set to TOR, the entry matches any address y such that the value in the preceding PMP address register is ≤ y < pmpaddr60.
RULE 8: If the value in the preceding PMP address register is greater than or equal to pmpaddr60 and the A field of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is TOR, then the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 9: If pmpaddr60 contains all y bits and its associated A field is NA4, then a memory access to the address (pmpaddr60 << 2) with the two least‑significant bits zero causes the PMP match condition to be true for a four‑byte NAPOT range, and accesses to any other address cause the PMP match condition to be false.
RULE 10: If pmpaddr60 ends with a single 0 bit (pattern yyyy…yyy0) and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches an eight-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 11: If pmpaddr60 ends with the bit pattern 01 (pattern yyyy…yy01) and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches a sixteen-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 12: If pmpaddr60 ends with the bit pattern 011 (pattern yyyy…y011) and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches a thirty-two-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: If pmpaddr60 matches the pattern yy01…1111 and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN bytes.
RULE 14: If pmpaddr60 matches the pattern y011…1111 and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN + 1 bytes.
RULE 15: If pmpaddr60 matches the pattern 0111…1111 and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN + 2 bytes.
RULE 16: If pmpaddr60 matches the pattern 1111…1111 and the associated A field is NAPOT, the entry matches a NAPOT range of size 2 × XLEN + 3 bytes.
RULE 17: When the granularity G is at least 2 and the A[1] bit of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr60[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 18: When the granularity G is at least 1 and the A[1] bit of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr60[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 19: Bits pmpaddr60[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 20: Changing the A[1] bit of the PMP entry associated with pmpaddr60 alters the value read from pmpaddr60 but does not modify the underlying stored value, and the bit pmpaddr60[G-1] retains its original value when the A field is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 21: Once PMP entry 60 is locked, it remains locked until the hart is reset, so pmpaddr60 stays locked.
RULE 22: Setting the L bit locks PMP entry 60 (and thus pmpaddr60) even when the A field is set to OFF.
RULE 23: When the L bit of PMP entry 60 is set, the R/W/X permissions associated with pmpaddr60 are enforced for all privilege modes.
RULE 24: When the L bit of PMP entry 60 is clear, any M-mode access matching pmpaddr60 will succeed and the R/W/X permissions apply only to S and U modes.
RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr60 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3ec; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 26: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr60 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3ec; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 27: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr60 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3ec; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 28: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr60.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3ec, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ec; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr60 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3ec; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr61
NUMBER: 0x3ed
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: The pmpaddr61 register [G-1] may have an underlying value of 1 while a read returns 0.
RULE 2: Executing a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction that modifies a different bit will cause 0 to be read from pmpaddr61 [G-1] and then written back, updating the underlying value to 0.
RULE 3: When pmpcfg61.A is set to TOR, pmpaddr61 defines the top address of the TOR-matched range, with pmpaddr60 defining the bottom address.
RULE 4: When pmpcfg61.A is set to TOR, entry 61 matches any address y such that pmpaddr60 ≤ y < pmpaddr61, irrespective of pmpcfg60.
RULE 5: If pmpaddr60 ≥ pmpaddr61 while pmpcfg61.A is set to TOR, entry 61 matches no addresses.
RULE 6: When pmpcfg61.A is set to NAPOT, the low-order bits of pmpaddr61 encode the size of the NAPOT range.
RULE 7: For a 4-byte NAPOT range, the low-order bits of pmpaddr61 are all zero.
RULE 8: For an 8-byte NAPOT range, the least significant bit of pmpaddr61 is zero and the next least significant bit is one.
RULE 9: For a 16-byte NAPOT range, the two least significant bits of pmpaddr61 are "01".
RULE 10: The NAPOT encoding pattern continues such that the maximum 2^(XLEN+3)-byte range is represented by pmpaddr61 having all bits set to one.
RULE 11: If G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg61.A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr61[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 12: If G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg61.A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr61[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 13: Bits pmpaddr61[G-1:0] are ignored by the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 14: Changing pmpcfg61.A[1] alters the value read from pmpaddr61 but does not modify the underlying stored value of pmpaddr61.
RULE 15: The bit pmpaddr61[G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg61.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 16: If PMP entry 61 is locked, any write to pmpaddr61 is ignored.
RULE 17: Setting the L bit for PMP entry 61 locks the entry even when the A field is OFF, causing writes to pmpaddr61 to be ignored.
RULE 18: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr61 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3ed; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 19: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr61 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3ed; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 20: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr61 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3ed; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 21: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr61.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3ed, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ed; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 22: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr61 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3ed; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 23: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr61 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3ed; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr62
NUMBER: 0x3ee
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: If a CSRRC or CSRRS instruction is executed on pmpaddr62 and the rs1 operand attempts to modify any bit other than the intended PMP address bit, then the value read back into rd is a mismatched value that does not reflect the actual contents of pmpaddr62.
RULE 2: If a mismatched read of pmpaddr62 is followed by writing that read value back to pmpaddr62, then a subsequent read of pmpaddr62 returns the written value.
RULE 3: In RV64, pmpaddr62 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 4: pmpaddr62 may be read or written only while the hart is in M-mode.
RULE 5: pmpaddr62 exists only in implementations that provide 64 PMP entries and is absent in implementations that provide 0 or 16 PMP entries.
RULE 6: If the preceding‑address configuration bit for PMP entry 63 is set, then the effective address for entry 63 is taken from pmpaddr62; consequently, a memory access to the address contained in pmpaddr62 is evaluated against entry 63’s permission bits (e.g., a disallowed load to that address raises a load‑access fault, while an allowed load succeeds).
RULE 7: If PMP entry 62 is locked, writes to pmpaddr62 MUST be ignored.
RULE 8: Once PMP entry 62 becomes locked, it remains locked until a hart reset, so pmpaddr62 stays locked until that reset.
RULE 9: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr62 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3ee; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 10: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr62 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3ee; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 11: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr62 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3ee; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 12: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr62.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3ee, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ee; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 13: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr62 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3ee; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 14: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr62 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3ee; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpaddr63
NUMBER: 0x3ef
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=ADDR
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: If a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction modifies any bit of pmpaddr63 other than bit G‑1, then the implementation must read pmpaddr63, and if the read value of bit G‑1 differs from its previously stored value, it must write that read value back, so that after the instruction the stored value of bit G‑1 equals the value read from the CSR.
RULE 2: Bit G-1 of pmpaddr63 may be stored as 1 but read as 0.
RULE 3: Any CSRRS or CSRRC instruction that targets pmpaddr63 shall read pmpaddr63 and shall cause any read side effects associated with pmpaddr63 regardless of the values in rs1 or rd.
RULE 4: When a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction with rs1 = x0 targets pmpaddr63, the instruction shall not write to pmpaddr63, shall not cause any write-side effects on pmpaddr63, and shall not raise an illegal-instruction exception for a read-only access to pmpaddr63.
RULE 5: For pmpaddr63, a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction with rs1 not equal to x0 shall both read pmpaddr63 and write pmpaddr63.
RULE 6: For pmpaddr63, a CSRRS or CSRRC instruction with rs1 = x0 shall read pmpaddr63 and shall not write pmpaddr63.
RULE 7: The pmpaddr63 CSR has privilege MRW (machine-read/write).
RULE 8: In RV64 systems, pmpaddr63 encodes bits 55-2 of a 56-bit physical address.
RULE 9: pmpaddr63 may be accessed (read or written) only while executing in M-mode.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg63.A = OFF, pmpaddr63 defines a null (disabled) region.
RULE 11: If pmpcfg63.A = TOR, pmpaddr63 forms the top address of the range, with pmpaddr62 as the bottom address.
RULE 12: When pmpcfg63.A = TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr62 ≤ y < pmpaddr63, irrespective of pmpcfg62.
RULE 13: If pmpcfg63.A = TOR and the entry is the first PMP entry, then zero is used as the lower bound and the entry matches any address y < pmpaddr63.
RULE 14: If pmpaddr62 ≥ pmpaddr63 and pmpcfg63.A = TOR, then the entry using pmpaddr63 matches no addresses.
RULE 15: pmpaddr63 MUST NOT be used to represent the address 2^XLEN+2 as the top of a TOR range, and therefore a TOR entry using pmpaddr63 cannot grant access to the uppermost word of memory.
RULE 16: If pmpcfg63.A = NA4, pmpaddr63 specifies a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 17: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 end with 0, then pmpaddr63 encodes an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 18: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 end with 01, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 19: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 end with 011, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 20: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 match the pattern yy01…1111, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 2 XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 21: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 match the pattern y011…1111, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 2 XLEN+1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 22: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 match the pattern 0111…1111, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 2 XLEN+2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 23: If pmpcfg63.A = NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr63 match the pattern 1111…1111, then pmpaddr63 encodes a 2 XLEN+3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 24: If G ≥ 1 and pmpaddr63 is configured in NA4 mode, then an illegal‑instruction exception is raised (mcause = 2) and the PMP entry is not applied.
RULE 25: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg63.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr63[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 26: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg63.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr63[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 27: Bits pmpaddr63[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 28: Changing pmpcfg63.A[1] does not modify the stored value of bit pmpaddr63[G-1]; the original bit value is retained across mode changes.
RULE 29: If the L bit of PMP entry 63 is set, any write to pmpaddr63 is ignored.
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr63 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3ef; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In S-mode, accessing pmpaddr63 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3ef; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 32: In U-mode, accessing pmpaddr63 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3ef; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 33: In M-mode, setting pmpaddr63.ADDR (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3ef, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ef; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 34: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr63 register while P extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: P; csrr a0, 0x3ef; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 35: In M-mode, accessing pmpaddr63 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3ef; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpcfg0
NUMBER: 0x3a0
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp0cfg, 15..8=pmp1cfg, 23..16=pmp2cfg, 31..24=pmp3cfg, 39..32=pmp4cfg, 47..40=pmp5cfg, 55..48=pmp6cfg, 63..56=pmp7cfg
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp, Smmpm, Zicfilp, Zkr
RULE 1: The pmpcfg0 CSR has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and pmpcfg0.L is 1 in any rule or entry, including disabled entries, mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further modifications to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 3: When mseccfg.MML is set, a pmpcfg0.L bit set marks the rule as M-mode-only and a pmpcfg0.L bit clear marks the rule as S/U-mode-only.
RULE 4: When mseccfg.MML is set, the encoding pmpcfg0.RW=01 is no longer reserved but encodes a Shared-Region.
RULE 5: If mseccfg.MML = 1 and a PMP configuration register’s LRWX bits are 1111, then that PMP entry is treated as a Shared‑Region, so memory accesses to addresses covered by that entry follow the Shared‑Region permission semantics for both M‑mode and S‑mode.
RULE 6: A Shared-Region rule is enforced on all modes and, if pmpcfg0.L is clear, the rule is not executable, M-mode has read/write access, and S/U-mode has read access when pmpcfg0.X is clear or read/write access when pmpcfg0.X is set.
RULE 7: A Shared-Region rule is enforced on all modes and, if pmpcfg0.L is set, the rule is not writable, both M-mode and S/U-mode have execute access, and M-mode also has read access when pmpcfg0.X is set.
RULE 8: If a PMP entry is locked with R=1, W=1, X=1 (pmpcfg0.LRWX = 1111) and a memory address falls within that entry, then a load executed in M‑mode or S/U‑mode completes without raising a PMP exception and the destination register receives the memory value.
RULE 9: An M-mode-only rule, identified by pmpcfg0.L set when mseccfg.MML is set, is enforced on Machine mode, denied in Supervisor and User modes, and remains locked so that any further modifications to its configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 10: A locked Shared-Region rule, identified by pmpcfg0.L set, also remains locked so that further modifications to its configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 11: When mseccfg.MML is set, attempts to write pmpcfg0 with executable privileges that would create an M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule are ignored, leaving pmpcfg0 unchanged.
RULE 12: When mseccfg.MML is set, the restriction on writing executable pmpcfg0 entries can be temporarily lifted by setting mseccfg.RLB.
RULE 13: Executing code with Machine mode privileges is permitted only from memory regions covered by a matching M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule with executable privileges as encoded in pmpcfg0; execution from a region without such a rule or covered only by a matching S/U-mode-only rule is denied.
RULE 14: In RV64 implementations, any odd-numbered PMP configuration CSR other than pmpcfg0 (e.g., pmpcfg1, pmpcfg3, …, pmpcfg15) is illegal.
RULE 15: Any read or write of pmpcfg0 MUST be performed in M-mode; accesses from lower privilege modes are NOT permitted.
RULE 16: In pmpcfg0, the R, W, and X bits, when set, indicate that the PMP entry permits read, write, and instruction execution, respectively.
RULE 17: In pmpcfg0, when any of the R, W, or X bits is clear, the corresponding access type is denied.
RULE 18: In pmpcfg0, the R, W, and X bits together form a collective WARL field for which the combination R = 0 and W = 1 is reserved.
RULE 19: If the X bit in pmpcfg0 for a PMP entry is clear, attempting to fetch an instruction from the corresponding region raises an instruction access-fault exception.
RULE 20: If the R bit in pmpcfg0 for a PMP entry is clear, attempting to execute a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction that accesses a physical address within the region raises a load access-fault exception.
RULE 21: If the W bit in pmpcfg0 for a PMP entry is clear, attempting to execute a store, store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero instruction that accesses a physical address within the region raises a store access-fault exception.
RULE 22: In pmpcfg0, an A field value of 0 (OFF) encodes a null region that is disabled.
RULE 23: If the A field of a PMP entry in pmpcfg0 equals 1, then that entry matches addresses using TOR mode, so an address is treated as inside the PMP region only when it is ≥ pmpaddr[i‑1] and < pmpaddr[i] (observable by the resulting access permission).
RULE 24: In pmpcfg0, an A field value of 2 (NA4) encodes the naturally aligned four-byte region mode.
RULE 25: In pmpcfg0, an A field value of 3 (NAPOT) encodes the naturally aligned power-of-two region mode of size at least eight bytes.
RULE 26: If the A field of pmpcfg0 is set to TOR, the lower bound of the range is zero and the entry matches any address y such that y < pmpaddr0.
RULE 27: When the A field of pmpcfg0 is set to TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr(i-1) ≤ y < pmpaddr0, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg(i-1).
RULE 28: If pmpaddr(i-1) ≥ pmpaddr0 and the A field of pmpcfg0 is TOR, then the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 29: When the PMP granularity G is greater than or equal to 1, the NA4 mode (A = 2) is not selectable in pmpcfg0.
RULE 30: When G ≥ 2 and bit 1 of the A field in pmpcfg0 is set (indicating NAPOT mode), the bits pmpaddr0[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 31: When G ≥ 1 and bit 1 of the A field in pmpcfg0 is clear (indicating OFF or TOR mode), the bits pmpaddr0[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 32: Bits pmpaddr0[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic of pmpcfg0.
RULE 33: Changing bit 1 of the A field in pmpcfg0 changes the value read from pmpaddr0 but does not change the underlying stored bits of pmpaddr0; specifically, pmpaddr0[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg0.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 34: Software can discover the PMP granularity by writing zero to pmpcfg0, writing all ones to pmpaddr0, reading back pmpaddr0, and interpreting the index of the least-significant set bit G as a granularity of 2 G + 2 bytes.
RULE 35: If pmpcfg0.A is NA4 and the pattern of pmpaddr0 is all ones, the matched region is a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 36: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 end with 0 (pattern yyyy…yyy0), the matched region is an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 37: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 end with 01 (pattern yyyy…yy01), the matched region is a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 38: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 end with 011 (pattern yyyy…y011), the matched region is a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 39: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 follow the pattern yy01…1111, the matched region size is 2 × XLEN bytes.
RULE 40: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 follow the pattern y011…1111, the matched region size is 2 × XLEN + 1 bytes.
RULE 41: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 follow the pattern 0111…1111, the matched region size is 2 × XLEN + 2 bytes.
RULE 42: If pmpcfg0.A is NAPOT and the low-order bits of pmpaddr0 follow the pattern 1111…1111, the matched region size is 2 × XLEN + 3 bytes.
RULE 43: If pmpcfg0.A is OFF, then the PMP entry defined by that pmpcfg0 never matches any address, so its permissions are not applied to any memory access.
RULE 44: If pmpcfg0.A is TOR, then pmpaddr[i-1] must be less than pmpaddr0.
RULE 45: When pmpcfg0.L equals 1, the PMP entry defined by pmpcfg0 and pmpaddr0 is locked.
RULE 46: When a PMP rule defined by pmpcfg0 matches an address range, the permissions encoded in pmpcfg0 are ignored and all accesses to that range are allowed.
RULE 47: When a PMP rule defined by pmpcfg0 matches an address range, only the access types specified by pmpcfg0 are allowed and any disallowed access causes an access-fault exception.
RULE 48: When a PMP rule defined by pmpcfg0 matches an address range and is denied, all accesses to that range are prohibited and any attempted access causes an access-fault exception.
RULE 49: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception indicating an inaccessible region.
RULE 50: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception indicating an inaccessible region.
RULE 51: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 52: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are treated as an Execute-only region.
RULE 53: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses constitute a shared data region with read/write permission, while S/U-Mode accesses are read-only.
RULE 54: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are read-only in the shared data region described for pmpcfg0.
RULE 55: If pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, then any load or store to an address that matches PMP entry 0 completes without raising an exception in M‑mode, S‑mode, or U‑mode, and the memory location contains the stored value (loads return that value).
RULE 56: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are a shared data region with read/write permission for both M-Mode and S/U-Mode.
RULE 57: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 58: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are treated as a read-only region.
RULE 59: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 60: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are a read/execute region.
RULE 61: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 62: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are a read/write region.
RULE 63: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 64: When pmpcfg0.L = 0, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are a read/write/execute region.
RULE 65: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception for a locked inaccessible region*.
RULE 66: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception for a locked inaccessible region*.
RULE 67: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses are a locked execute-only region*.
RULE 68: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 69: If pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, then an instruction fetch from the PMP region completes without raising an illegal‑instruction exception in M‑mode, S‑mode, or U‑mode; a load from that region raises a load‑access‑fault exception in any mode; a store to that region raises a store‑access‑fault exception in S‑mode or U‑mode but succeeds in M‑mode.
RULE 70: If pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, then an instruction fetch from an address covered by PMP entry 0 while executing in M‑mode raises an illegal‑instruction exception, while the same fetch in S‑mode or U‑mode succeeds; a load from that address in M‑mode succeeds, but a store to that address in M‑mode raises an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 71: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 0, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are a locked shared code region that executes only on S/U-Mode and provides read/execute permission on M-Mode*.
RULE 72: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses are a locked read-only region*.
RULE 73: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 74: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses are a locked read/execute region*.
RULE 75: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 0, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 76: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses are a locked read/write region*.
RULE 77: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 0, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses generate an Access Exception.
RULE 78: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, M-Mode accesses are a locked shared data region that is read-only for both M-Mode and S/U-Mode*.
RULE 79: When pmpcfg0.L = 1, pmpcfg0.R = 1, pmpcfg0.W = 1, pmpcfg0.X = 1, and mseccfg.MML = 1, S/U-Mode accesses are a locked shared data region that is read-only for both M-Mode and S/U-Mode*.

REGISTER: pmpcfg2
NUMBER: 0x3a2
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp8cfg, 15..8=pmp9cfg, 23..16=pmp10cfg, 31..24=pmp11cfg, 39..32=pmp12cfg, 47..40=pmp13cfg, 55..48=pmp14cfg, 63..56=pmp15cfg
EXTENSIONS: H, Smepmp, Smmpm, Zicfilp, Zkr
RULE 1: The pmpcfg2 CSR is accessible in machine mode with read/write privileges (MRW).
RULE 2: When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and a pmpcfg2 entry has its L bit set, then mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further writes to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 3: When mseccfg.MML is set, the L bit in each pmpcfg2 entry indicates an M-mode-only rule if the bit is 1 and a S/U-mode-only rule if the bit is 0.
RULE 4: If mseccfg.MML is set and a pmpcfg2 entry’s RW field equals 01 or its LRWX field equals 1111, then that PMP entry is interpreted as a Shared‑Region rule, causing memory accesses that match the entry to be granted to all privilege levels according to shared‑region semantics (e.g., a load that would fault under normal PMP succeeds).
RULE 5: When mseccfg.MML is set and a pmpcfg2 entry is an M-mode-only rule (L=1), the rule is enforced in Machine mode, denied in Supervisor and User modes, and remains locked against further configuration or address-register modifications until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 6: When mseccfg.MML is set and a pmpcfg2 entry is a S/U-mode-only rule (L=0), the rule is enforced in Supervisor and User modes and denied in Machine mode.
RULE 7: When mseccfg.MML is set and a pmpcfg2 entry encodes a Shared-Region with L=1, the rule provides execute access to both Machine and S/U modes, is not writable, grants M-mode read access if the X bit is set, and remains locked against further configuration or address-register modifications until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 8: When mseccfg.MML is set and a pmpcfg2 entry encodes a Shared-Region with LRWX=1111, the rule provides read-only access to both Machine and S/U modes and remains locked against further configuration or address-register modifications until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 9: When a pmpcfg2 write attempts to create a rule that grants executable privileges to an M-mode-only rule or to a locked Shared-Region, the write is ignored and the pmpcfg2 entry remains unchanged unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 10: Execution of Machine-mode code from a memory region is permitted only if the corresponding pmpcfg2 entry is an M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule that includes executable privileges; otherwise execution is denied.
RULE 11: In RV64, the CSR pmpcfg2 is legal while the odd-numbered configuration registers such as pmpcfg1 are illegal.
RULE 12: RV64 harts use the CSR pmpcfg2, instead of pmpcfg1, to hold the configurations for PMP entries 8 through 15.
RULE 13: The CSR pmpcfg2 is accessible only in M-mode.
RULE 14: In each 8-bit field of pmpcfg2, setting the R bit indicates that the corresponding PMP entry permits read accesses, setting the W bit indicates write permission, and setting the X bit indicates instruction execution permission.
RULE 15: If any of the R, W, or X bits in a given 8-bit field of pmpcfg2 is clear, the corresponding access type (read, write, or execute) is denied for that PMP entry.
RULE 16: If a program writes an 8‑bit subfield of pmpcfg2 with the R and W bits set to 0 and 1 respectively, then a subsequent read of that subfield must not return the illegal R=0 ,W=1 pattern (the hardware will modify the stored value to a legal combination, e.g., clearing W).
RULE 17: If the X bit in the relevant pmpcfg2 field denies execute permission for a PMP region, an instruction fetch from that region raises an instruction access-fault exception.
RULE 18: If the R bit in the relevant pmpcfg2 field denies read permission for a PMP region, executing a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction that accesses a physical address in that region raises a load access-fault exception.
RULE 19: If the W bit in the relevant pmpcfg2 field denies write permission for a PMP region, executing a store, store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero instruction that accesses a physical address in that region raises a store access-fault exception.
RULE 20: In pmpcfg2, A = 0 selects the OFF mode, which disables the entry and matches no addresses.
RULE 21: In pmpcfg2, A = 1 selects the TOR mode, which defines a top-of-range address region.
RULE 22: In pmpcfg2, A = 2 selects the NA4 mode, which defines a naturally aligned four-byte region.
RULE 23: In pmpcfg2, A = 3 selects the NAPOT mode, which defines a naturally aligned power-of-two region of at least eight bytes.
RULE 24: When pmpcfg2 entry i is in TOR mode, the associated address register forms the top of the address range and the preceding PMP address register forms the bottom of the address range.
RULE 25: If pmpcfg2 entry i has A = TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr(i-1) ≤ y < pmpaddr(i), irrespective of the value of pmpcfg(i-1).
RULE 26: If pmpcfg2 entry 0 has A = TOR, the lower bound is zero, so the entry matches any address y < pmpaddr0.
RULE 27: If pmpaddr(i-1) ≥ pmpaddr(i) and pmpcfg2 entry i has A = TOR, then entry i matches no addresses.
RULE 28: In NAPOT mode (A = 3) of pmpcfg2, the low-order bits of the associated address register encode the region size.
RULE 29: In NA4 mode (A = 2) of pmpcfg2, the associated address register defines a naturally aligned four-byte region.
RULE 30: When the PMP granularity G is greater than or equal to 1, the NA4 mode is not selectable in pmpcfg2.
RULE 31: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg2's A[1] bit is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr[i][G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 32: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg2's A[1] bit is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr[i][G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 33: Bits pmpaddr[i][G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for entries configured via pmpcfg2.
RULE 34: Changing pmpcfg2's A[1] bit alters the value read from the corresponding pmpaddr register but does not alter the underlying stored value of that register.
RULE 35: The bit pmpaddr[i][G-1] retains its original stored value when pmpcfg2's A field is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg2 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3a2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 37: In S-mode, accessing pmpcfg2 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3a2; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 38: In U-mode, accessing pmpcfg2 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3a2; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 39: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg2.pmp8cfg (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3a2, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a2; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 40: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg2.pmp9cfg (bit 8) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x100) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100; csrs 0x3a2, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a2; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x100].
RULE 41: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg2.pmp10cfg (bit 16) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x10000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10000; csrs 0x3a2, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a2; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x10000].
RULE 42: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg2.pmp11cfg (bit 24) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000; csrs 0x3a2, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a2; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1000000].
RULE 43: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg2.pmp12cfg (bit 32) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x100000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100000000; csrs 0x3a2, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a2; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x100000000].
RULE 44: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg2.pmp13cfg (bit 40) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x10000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10000000000; csrs 0x3a2, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a2; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x10000000000].
RULE 45: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg2.pmp14cfg (bit 48) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000000000; csrs 0x3a2, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a2; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000].
RULE 46: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg2.pmp15cfg (bit 56) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x100000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100000000000000; csrs 0x3a2, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a2; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x100000000000000].
RULE 47: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg2 register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x3a2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 48: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg2 register while Smepmp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smepmp; csrr a0, 0x3a2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 49: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg2 register while Smmpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Smmpm; csrr a0, 0x3a2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 50: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg2 register while Zicfilp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfilp; csrr a0, 0x3a2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 51: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg2 register while Zkr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zkr; csrr a0, 0x3a2; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpcfg4
NUMBER: 0x3a4
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp16cfg, 15..8=pmp17cfg, 23..16=pmp18cfg, 31..24=pmp19cfg, 39..32=pmp20cfg, 47..40=pmp21cfg, 55..48=pmp22cfg, 63..56=pmp23cfg
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and pmpcfg4.L is 1, mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further modifications to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 2: When mseccfg.MML is set, pmpcfg4.L marks a rule as M-mode-only when set and as S/U-mode-only when unset.
RULE 3: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg4.RW = 01 and pmpcfg4.LRWX = 1111, then the corresponding PMP entry is interpreted as a Shared‑Region, so a load or store to an address covered by that entry executes without raising a PMP‑violation (access‑fault) exception regardless of the current privilege mode.
RULE 4: If a memory access in Supervisor or User mode would violate an M‑mode‑only PMP rule defined in pmpcfg4, then the rule is ignored and the access does not raise a PMP access‑fault exception.
RULE 5: An M-mode-only rule defined by pmpcfg4 remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 6: An S/U-mode-only rule defined by pmpcfg4 is enforced in Supervisor and User modes and denied in Machine mode.
RULE 7: A Shared-Region rule defined by pmpcfg4 where pmpcfg4.L is not set is not executable, grants Machine mode read/write access, and grants Supervisor/User mode read access if pmpcfg4.X is not set or read/write access if pmpcfg4.X is set.
RULE 8: A Shared-Region rule defined by pmpcfg4 where pmpcfg4.L is set is not writable, grants execute access to both Machine and Supervisor/User modes, and grants Machine mode read access if pmpcfg4.X is set; the rule remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 9: A Shared-Region rule defined by pmpcfg4 with encoding pmpcfg4.LRWX=1111 provides read-only access to both Machine and Supervisor/User modes and remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 10: Writes to pmpcfg4 that would create a rule with executable privileges and that is either M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region are ignored, leaving pmpcfg4 unchanged; this restriction can be temporarily lifted by setting mseccfg.RLB.
RULE 11: Execution of code with Machine mode privileges is permitted only from regions for which pmpcfg4 defines a matching M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule with executable privileges, and is denied from regions without such a matching rule or with a matching S/U-mode-only rule.
RULE 12: Reads and writes to pmpcfg4 are permitted only when the hart is executing in M-mode.
RULE 13: Each 8-bit configuration entry stored in pmpcfg4 contains an R bit that, when set, indicates the PMP entry permits read accesses.
RULE 14: Each 8-bit configuration entry stored in pmpcfg4 contains a W bit that, when set, indicates the PMP entry permits write accesses.
RULE 15: Each 8-bit configuration entry stored in pmpcfg4 contains an X bit that, when set, indicates the PMP entry permits instruction-execute accesses.
RULE 16: If software writes any pattern to the R, W, and X bits of a PMP entry in pmpcfg4, then the implementation may replace those bits with a legal combination, and a subsequent read of that pmpcfg4 entry returns the R, W, X bits in that legal (potentially different) state without raising an exception.
RULE 17: If a write to any PMP entry in pmpcfg4 sets R=0 and W=1, then reading back that entry returns a value where the W bit is cleared (the R‑W combination is not 0‑1).
RULE 18: If pmpcfg4.A = 0, then entry 4 matches no addresses.
RULE 19: If pmpcfg4.A = TOR, then entry 4 matches any address y such that pmpaddr3 ≤ y < pmpaddr4, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg3.
RULE 20: If the PMP granularity G ≥ 1, then pmpcfg4 cannot select the NA4 mode (A = 2).
RULE 21: If G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg4.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), then bits pmpaddr4[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 22: If G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg4.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), then bits pmpaddr4[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 23: When pmpcfg4.A = TOR, bits pmpaddr4[G-1:0] do not influence the TOR address-matching logic for entry 4.
RULE 24: Modifying pmpcfg4.A[1] may change the value read from pmpaddr4, but the physical bit pmpaddr4[G-1] remains unchanged when pmpcfg4.A is toggled between NAPOT and TOR/OFF and later restored to NAPOT.
RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg4 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3a4; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 26: In S-mode, accessing pmpcfg4 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3a4; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: pmpcfg6
NUMBER: 0x3a6
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp24cfg, 15..8=pmp25cfg, 23..16=pmp26cfg, 31..24=pmp27cfg, 39..32=pmp28cfg, 47..40=pmp29cfg, 55..48=pmp30cfg, 63..56=pmp31cfg
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpcfg6 can be accessed only when the processor is executing in M-mode.
RULE 2: When the R bit in pmpcfg6 is set, the corresponding PMP entry permits read accesses; when the R bit is clear, read accesses are denied.
RULE 3: When the W bit in pmpcfg6 is set, the corresponding PMP entry permits write accesses; when the W bit is clear, write accesses are denied.
RULE 4: When the X bit in pmpcfg6 is set, the corresponding PMP entry permits instruction fetches; when the X bit is clear, instruction fetches are denied.
RULE 5: If a write to pmpcfg6 sets R = 0 and W = 1 (regardless of X), then the write raises an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 6: When pmpcfg6.A = 0, this PMP entry is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 7: If pmpcfg6.A = 1, the associated address register forms the top of the address range and the preceding PMP address register forms the bottom of the address range.
RULE 8: If pmpcfg6.A = 1 for entry i, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr(i-1) ≤ y < pmpaddr(i), irrespective of the value of pmpcfg(i-1).
RULE 9: If pmpcfg6.A = 1 for entry 0, zero is used for the lower bound and the entry matches any address y < pmpaddr0.
RULE 10: If pmpcfg6.A = 1 and pmpaddr(i-1) ≥ pmpaddr(i), then entry i matches no addresses.
RULE 11: If the G bit for entry 6 is 1 (G ≥ 1) and software writes pmpcfg6.A = 2 (NA4 mode), then the write is ignored: reading back pmpcfg6.A does not return 2 (it retains its prior value) and no exception is raised.
RULE 12: When pmpcfg6.A = 2 (NA4) and the pmpaddr pattern is all ones, the entry matches a 4-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 13: When pmpcfg6.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the pmpaddr pattern ends with a single 0 (…0), the entry matches an 8-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 14: When pmpcfg6.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the pmpaddr pattern ends with …01, the entry matches a 16-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 15: When pmpcfg6.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the pmpaddr pattern ends with …011, the entry matches a 32-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 16: When pmpcfg6.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the pmpaddr pattern matches yy01…1111, the entry matches a 2 × XLEN-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 17: When pmpcfg6.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the pmpaddr pattern matches y011…1111, the entry matches a 2 × XLEN + 1-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 18: When pmpcfg6.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the pmpaddr pattern matches 0111…1111, the entry matches a 2 × XLEN + 2-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 19: When pmpcfg6.A = 3 (NAPOT) and the pmpaddr pattern matches 1111…1111, the entry matches a 2 × XLEN + 3-byte NAPOT range.
RULE 20: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg6.A[1] is set (mode NAPOT), bits pmpaddr6[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 21: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg6.A[1] is clear (mode OFF or TOR), bits pmpaddr6[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 22: Bits pmpaddr6[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic when pmpcfg6.A = 1.
RULE 23: Changing pmpcfg6.A[1] affects the value read from pmpaddr6 but does not affect the underlying stored value; specifically, pmpaddr6[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg6.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF then back to NAPOT.
RULE 24: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg6 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3a6; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 25: In S-mode, accessing pmpcfg6 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3a6; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: pmpcfg8
NUMBER: 0x3a8
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp32cfg, 15..8=pmp33cfg, 23..16=pmp34cfg, 31..24=pmp35cfg, 39..32=pmp36cfg, 47..40=pmp37cfg, 55..48=pmp38cfg, 63..56=pmp39cfg
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: If mseccfg.RLB is 0 and pmpcfg8.L is 1 in any rule or entry (including disabled entries), then mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further writes to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 2: If mseccfg.MML is 1, then the encoding pmpcfg8.RW = 01 is interpreted as a Shared-Region.
RULE 3: If the MSECCFG.MML bit is 1 and the PMP entry 8 configuration bits LRWX are set to 1111, then accesses to the address range defined by PMP entry 8 from S‑mode or U‑mode are permitted under shared‑region semantics (no access‑fault exception is raised).
RULE 4: If mseccfg.MML = 1 and pmpcfg8.L = 1, then a memory access that matches the PMP entry raises a load‑access‑fault exception (mcause = 12) or store‑access‑fault exception (mcause = 13) when executed in Supervisor or User mode, while the same access in Machine mode completes normally and the destination register receives the loaded value (or the store succeeds).
RULE 5: If mseccfg.MML is 1 and pmpcfg8.L is 1, then the rule remains locked so that further modifications to its configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is 1.
RULE 6: If mseccfg.MML = 1 and pmpcfg8.L = 0, then a load or store that violates the active PMP entry causes a PMP‑violation exception (mcause set to the PMP‑violation code) when executed in Supervisor or User mode, but the same access executed in Machine mode completes without raising an exception.
RULE 7: If mseccfg.MML = 1 and pmpcfg8.L = 0 and a PMP entry is configured as a Shared‑Region, then any instruction fetch whose address matches that PMP entry raises an instruction‑access‑fault exception (mcause set to the instruction‑page‑fault code).
RULE 8: If mseccfg.MML is 1, pmpcfg8.L is 0, and the rule is a Shared-Region, then Machine mode has read/write access to the region.
RULE 9: If mseccfg.MML is 1, pmpcfg8.L is 0, and the rule is a Shared-Region, then Supervisor and User modes have read access if pmpcfg8.X is 0, or read/write access if pmpcfg8.X is 1.
RULE 10: If mseccfg.MML is 1, pmpcfg8.L is 1, and the rule is a Shared-Region, then the rule is not writable.
RULE 11: If mseccfg.MML is 1, pmpcfg8.L is 1, and the rule is a Shared-Region, then both Machine mode and Supervisor/User modes have execute access to the region.
RULE 12: If mseccfg.MML is 1, pmpcfg8.L is 1, and the rule is a Shared-Region, then the rule remains locked so that further modifications to its configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is 1.
RULE 13: If mseccfg.MML is 1 and pmpcfg8.LRWX = 1111, then both Machine mode and Supervisor/User modes have read-only access to the region.
RULE 14: If mseccfg.MML is 1 and pmpcfg8.LRWX = 1111, then the rule remains locked so that further modifications to its configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is 1.
RULE 15: If a write to pmpcfg8 attempts to set executable privileges for a rule that would be M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region while mseccfg.RLB is 0, then the write is ignored and pmpcfg8 remains unchanged.
RULE 16: Execution in Machine mode is permitted only from a region that matches a pmpcfg8 rule that is M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region with executable privileges.
RULE 17: Execution in Machine mode is denied if the region does not match any pmpcfg8 rule or matches a pmpcfg8 rule that is S/U-mode-only.
RULE 18: pmpcfg8 must be accessed only in M-mode.
RULE 19: All fields within pmpcfg8 are WARL and may be read-only zero.
RULE 20: Within pmpcfg8, an R bit set permits reads and a cleared R bit denies reads.
RULE 21: Within pmpcfg8, a W bit set permits writes and a cleared W bit denies writes.
RULE 22: Within pmpcfg8, an X bit set permits instruction execution and a cleared X bit denies execution.
RULE 23: If a subfield of pmpcfg8 is written with R = 0 and W = 1, then the write raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = 2).
RULE 24: If the X bit supplied by pmpcfg8 for a PMP entry is clear, an attempt to fetch an instruction from that region raises an instruction access-fault exception.
RULE 25: If the R bit supplied by pmpcfg8 for a PMP entry is clear, an attempt to execute a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction that accesses that region raises a load access-fault exception.
RULE 26: If the W bit supplied by pmpcfg8 for a PMP entry is clear, an attempt to execute a store, store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero instruction that accesses that region raises a store access-fault exception.
RULE 27: In pmpcfg8, the A field value 0 selects the OFF mode, which disables the PMP entry and matches no addresses.
RULE 28: In pmpcfg8, the A field value 1 selects the TOR mode, where pmpaddr8 forms the top of the address range and pmpaddr7 forms the bottom.
RULE 29: In pmpcfg8 TOR mode, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr7 ≤ y < pmpaddr8 irrespective of the value of pmpcfg7.
RULE 30: In pmpcfg8 TOR mode, if pmpaddr7 ≥ pmpaddr8 then the PMP entry matches no addresses.
RULE 31: In pmpcfg8, the A field value 2 selects the NA4 mode, which matches a naturally aligned four-byte region.
RULE 32: In pmpcfg8, the A field value 3 selects the NAPOT mode, where the size of the matched region is encoded in the low-order bits of pmpaddr8.
RULE 33: In pmpcfg8 NAPOT mode, the low-order bits of pmpaddr8 encode the region size according to Table 24, ranging from an 8-byte region up to a 2 XLEN+3-byte power-of-two region.
RULE 34: When PMP granularity G ≥ 1, the NA4 mode is not selectable and therefore pmpcfg8 A cannot be set to 2.
RULE 35: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg8 A[1] is set (NAPOT mode), bits pmpaddr8[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 36: When G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg8 A[1] is clear (OFF or TOR mode), bits pmpaddr8[G-1:0] read as all zeros, and these bits do not affect TOR address-matching logic.
RULE 37: Changing pmpcfg8 A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr8 but does not modify the underlying stored value, and pmpaddr8[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg8 A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF and back to NAPOT.
RULE 38: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg8 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3a8; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 39: In S-mode, accessing pmpcfg8 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3a8; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 40: In U-mode, accessing pmpcfg8 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3a8; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 41: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg8.pmp32cfg (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3a8, a0; csrr a1, 0x3a8; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpcfg10
NUMBER: 0x3aa
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp40cfg, 15..8=pmp41cfg, 23..16=pmp42cfg, 31..24=pmp43cfg, 39..32=pmp44cfg, 47..40=pmp45cfg, 55..48=pmp46cfg, 63..56=pmp47cfg
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: If mseccfg.RLB=0 and pmpcfg10.L=1, then mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further modifications to mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 2: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.L=1 (M-mode-only rule), then the rule is enforced in Machine mode and denied in Supervisor and User modes.
RULE 3: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.L=1 (M-mode-only rule), then the rule remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 4: If mseccfg.MML = 1 and pmpcfg10.L = 0, then a memory access in Supervisor or User mode is checked against the PMP entry (raising a load/store/execute access exception on violation), while the same access in Machine mode raises an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 5: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=0, then the region is not executable.
RULE 6: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=0, then Machine mode has read/write access to the region.
RULE 7: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=0 and pmpcfg10.X=0, then Supervisor and User modes have read-only access to the region.
RULE 8: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=0 and pmpcfg10.X=1, then Supervisor and User modes have read/write access to the region.
RULE 9: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=1, then the region is not writable.
RULE 10: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=1, then both Machine mode and Supervisor/User modes have execute access to the region.
RULE 11: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=1 and pmpcfg10.X=1, then Machine mode also has read access to the region.
RULE 12: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.RW=01 defines a Shared-Region and pmpcfg10.L=1, then the rule remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 13: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.LRWX=1111, then both Machine mode and Supervisor/User modes have read-only access to the region.
RULE 14: If mseccfg.MML is set and pmpcfg10.LRWX=1111, then the rule remains locked so that any further modifications to its associated configuration or address registers are ignored until a PMP reset unless mseccfg.RLB is set.
RULE 15: If a pmpcfg10 write attempts to add a rule with executable privileges that would be M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region, then the write is ignored and pmpcfg10 remains unchanged.
RULE 16: Execution of code with Machine mode privileges is permitted only from regions that have an M-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule with executable privileges as encoded in pmpcfg10; execution from regions without such a matching rule or with a matching S/U-mode-only rule is denied.
RULE 17: Only M-mode may read or write pmpcfg10; attempts from U, S, or HS modes are not permitted.
RULE 18: In pmpcfg10 the R bit, when set, permits read accesses to the PMP entries it configures, and when clear, read accesses are denied.
RULE 19: In pmpcfg10 the W bit, when set, permits write accesses to the PMP entries it configures, and when clear, write accesses are denied.
RULE 20: In pmpcfg10 the X bit, when set, permits instruction-fetch (execute) accesses to the PMP entries it configures, and when clear, execute accesses are denied.
RULE 21: The R, W, and X fields of pmpcfg10 together form a WARL field for which the combination R=0 and W=1 is reserved and must not be used.
RULE 22: If the X bit in pmpcfg10 does not permit execute permission for a PMP region, an instruction fetch from that region raises an instruction access-fault exception.
RULE 23: If the R bit in pmpcfg10 does not permit read permission for a PMP region, a load that accesses an address in that region raises a load access-fault exception.
RULE 24: If pmpcfg10.A = 0, then the PMP entry is disabled and matches no addresses.
RULE 25: If pmpcfg10.A = 1 (TOR), then the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr9 ≤ y < pmpaddr10, irrespective of the value of pmpcfg9.
RULE 26: If pmpcfg10.A = 1 and pmpaddr9 ≥ pmpaddr10, then the entry matches no addresses.
RULE 27: If G ≥ 1, then the NA4 encoding (value 2) is not selectable for pmpcfg10.A.
RULE 28: If G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg10.A[1] = 1 (indicating NAPOT mode), then bits pmpaddr10[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 29: If G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg10.A[1] = 0 (indicating OFF or TOR mode), then bits pmpaddr10[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 30: The bits pmpaddr10[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic for pmpcfg10.
RULE 31: Changing pmpcfg10.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr10 but does not modify the underlying stored bits of pmpaddr10, and the stored bit pmpaddr10[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg10.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT.
RULE 32: If the L bit in pmpcfg10 is set, then the PMP Entry formed with pmpaddr10 is a Locked entry.
RULE 33: If the address‑matching field pmpcfg10.A is set to OFF, then the PMP entry is invalid and the processor treats the entry as disabled, so any memory access that would otherwise be matched by this entry proceeds without PMP protection (the access succeeds as if the entry were not present).
RULE 34: If pmpcfg10.A is TOR and pmpaddr9 ≥ pmpaddr10, then PMP entry 10 is disabled, so memory accesses that would lie in the intended TOR range do not trigger any PMP‑related protection (no access fault occurs).
RULE 35: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg10 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3aa; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 36: In S-mode, accessing pmpcfg10 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3aa; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

RULE 38: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg10.pmp40cfg (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3aa, a0; csrr a1, 0x3aa; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].

REGISTER: pmpcfg12
NUMBER: 0x3ac
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp48cfg, 15..8=pmp49cfg, 23..16=pmp50cfg, 31..24=pmp51cfg, 39..32=pmp52cfg, 47..40=pmp53cfg, 55..48=pmp54cfg, 63..56=pmp55cfg
EXTENSIONS: Smepmp
RULE 1: If the MSECCFG.MML bit is set, then a pmpcfg12 entry whose L bit is 1 causes the corresponding PMP rule to be interpreted as Machine-mode-only.
RULE 2: If the MSECCFG.MML bit is set, then a pmpcfg12 entry whose L bit is 0 causes the corresponding PMP rule to be interpreted as Supervisor/User-mode-only.
RULE 3: If MSECCFG.MML is set and a PMP entry is programmed with a pmpcfg12 encoding where RW = 01 and LRWX = 1111, then a read of that entry’s pmpcfg CSR returns RW = 01 and LRWX = 1111 and the entry is interpreted as a Shared‑Region rule.
RULE 4: When the MSECCFG.MML bit is set, a write to pmpcfg12 that would create a rule with executable privileges and that is either Machine-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region must be ignored, leaving the entire pmpcfg register, including pmpcfg12, unchanged.
RULE 5: If the MSECCFG.MML bit is set and the MSECCFG.RLB bit is set, then writes to pmpcfg12 that would create a rule with executable privileges and that is either Machine-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region are permitted and are not ignored.
RULE 6: When the MSECCFG.MML bit is set, Machine-mode execution is permitted only from memory regions whose pmpcfg12 entries define a matching Machine-mode-only rule or a locked Shared-Region rule with executable privileges; execution from regions without such a matching rule or with a matching Supervisor/User-mode-only rule is denied.
RULE 7: If MSECCFG.RLB is 0 and any pmpcfg12 entry has its L bit set to 1, then MSECCFG.RLB remains 0 and any further writes to MSECCFG.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 8: pmpcfg12 can be read or written only when the processor is executing in M-mode.
RULE 9: In pmpcfg12, the R, W, and X bits, when set, indicate that the PMP entry permits read, write, and instruction execution, respectively.
RULE 10: In pmpcfg12, a clear R, W, or X bit denies the corresponding read, write, or execute access type.
RULE 11: If a write to pmpcfg12 sets R = 0 and W = 1 in any entry, then a subsequent read of that entry will never return R = 0 and W = 1 (the hardware coerces the value to a legal combination, e.g., setting R = 1 or clearing W).
RULE 12: If an entry in pmpcfg12 has X = 0, an instruction fetch from the corresponding region must raise an instruction access-fault exception.
RULE 13: If an entry in pmpcfg12 has R = 0, a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction accessing that region must raise a load access-fault exception.
RULE 14: If an entry in pmpcfg12 has W = 0, a store, store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero instruction accessing that region must raise a store access-fault exception.
RULE 15: pmpcfg12.A = 0 selects the OFF null region (disabled).
RULE 16: pmpcfg12.A = 2 selects the NA4 naturally aligned four-byte region mode.
RULE 17: pmpcfg12.A = 3 selects the NAPOT naturally aligned power-of-two region mode of size at least eight bytes.
RULE 18: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 ends with a zero (yyyy…yyy0), the region size is 8 bytes.
RULE 19: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 ends with the bits 01 (yyyy…yy01), the region size is 16 bytes.
RULE 20: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 ends with the bits 011 (yyyy…y011), the region size is 32 bytes.
RULE 21: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 matches the pattern yy01…1111, the region size is 2 × XLEN bytes.
RULE 22: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 matches the pattern y011…1111, the region size is 2 × XLEN + 1 bytes.
RULE 23: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 matches the pattern 0111…1111, the region size is 2 × XLEN + 2 bytes.
RULE 24: When pmpcfg12.A encodes NAPOT and pmpaddr12 matches the pattern 1111…1111, the region size is 2 × XLEN + 3 bytes.
RULE 25: If a CSR write sets pmpcfg12.A to 2 while the PMP granularity G is ≥ 1, then an illegal‑instruction exception is raised (mcause = 2) and the pmpcfg12 register value does not change.
RULE 26: If G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg12.A[1] = 1 (NAPOT mode), then reads of pmpaddr12 return ones in bits [G-2:0].
RULE 27: If G ≥ 1 and pmpcfg12.A[1] = 0 (OFF or TOR mode), then reads of pmpaddr12 return zeros in bits [G-1:0].
RULE 28: The bits pmpaddr12[G-1:0] do not affect address matching when pmpcfg12.A selects TOR.
RULE 29: Writing pmpcfg12.A[1] to change between NAPOT and OFF/TOR does not modify the stored value of pmpaddr12[G-1]; only the masked read value changes.
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg12 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3ac; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In S-mode, accessing pmpcfg12 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3ac; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 32: In U-mode, accessing pmpcfg12 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3ac; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 33: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg12.pmp48cfg (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3ac, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ac; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 34: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg12.pmp49cfg (bit 8) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100; csrs 0x3ac, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ac; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 35: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg12.pmp50cfg (bit 16) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10000; csrs 0x3ac, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ac; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 36: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg12.pmp51cfg (bit 24) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000; csrs 0x3ac, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ac; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
