REGISTER: pmpcfg14
NUMBER: 0x3ae
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 7..0=pmp56cfg, 15..8=pmp57cfg, 23..16=pmp58cfg, 31..24=pmp59cfg, 39..32=pmp60cfg, 47..40=pmp61cfg, 55..48=pmp62cfg, 63..56=pmp63cfg
EXTENSIONS: P, Smepmp
RULE 1: pmpcfg14 has machine-read/write (MRW) privilege.
RULE 2: When mseccfg.MML is set, the pmpcfg14.L field marks a rule as M-mode-only if the bit is 1 and as S/U-mode-only if the bit is 0.
RULE 3: If mseccfg.MML is set and a PMP entry’s pmpcfg14.RW field equals 01, then that entry is interpreted as a Shared‑Region rule, allowing accesses that match the entry in both M‑mode and S‑mode without raising a PMP violation.
RULE 4: A write to pmpcfg14 that attempts to add a rule with executable privileges which is either M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region is ignored and leaves pmpcfg14 unchanged.
RULE 5: Executing code with Machine-mode privileges is permitted only from memory regions that have a matching pmpcfg14 entry that is M-mode-only or a locked Shared-Region with executable privileges.
RULE 6: Executing code with Machine-mode privileges from a memory region that lacks a matching pmpcfg14 entry or that matches a pmpcfg14 entry that is S/U-mode-only is denied.
RULE 7: When mseccfg.RLB is 0 and any pmpcfg14.L bit is 1 (including in disabled entries), mseccfg.RLB remains 0 and any further attempts to modify mseccfg.RLB are ignored until a PMP reset.
RULE 8: pmpcfg14 is accessible only in M-mode.
RULE 9: Each 8-bit configuration field in pmpcfg14 contains an R bit that, when set, indicates the PMP entry permits read accesses and, when clear, denies read accesses.
RULE 10: Each 8-bit configuration field in pmpcfg14 contains a W bit that, when set, indicates the PMP entry permits write accesses and, when clear, denies write accesses.
RULE 11: Each 8-bit configuration field in pmpcfg14 contains an X bit that, when set, indicates the PMP entry permits instruction execution and, when clear, denies execution.
RULE 12: If an instruction fetch accesses a physical address within a PMP region whose configuration in pmpcfg14 has the X bit clear, an instruction access-fault exception is raised.
RULE 13: If a load, load-reserved, or cache-block management instruction accesses a physical address within a PMP region whose configuration in pmpcfg14 has the R bit clear, a load access-fault exception is raised.
RULE 14: If a store, store-conditional, AMO, or cache-block zero instruction accesses a physical address within a PMP region whose configuration in pmpcfg14 has the W bit clear, a store access-fault exception is raised.
RULE 15: In pmpcfg14, A=0 selects the OFF mode which disables the entry and causes it to match no addresses.
RULE 16: In pmpcfg14, A=1 selects the TOR mode, causing pmpaddr14 to serve as the top of the address range and pmpaddr13 to serve as the bottom of the address range.
RULE 17: When pmpcfg14.A = TOR, the entry matches any address y that satisfies pmpaddr13 ≤ y < pmpaddr14 regardless of the value of pmpcfg13.
RULE 18: If pmpaddr13 ≥ pmpaddr14 and pmpcfg14.A = TOR, then entry 14 matches no addresses.
RULE 19: In pmpcfg14, A=2 selects the NA4 mode, causing the entry to match a naturally aligned four-byte region.
RULE 20: In pmpcfg14, A=3 selects the NAPOT mode, and the low-order bits of pmpaddr14 encode the size of the matched region according to the NAPOT pattern table.
RULE 21: When the granularity G is greater than or equal to 1, pmpcfg14.A must not be 2, so the NA4 mode is not selectable.
RULE 22: When G ≥ 2 and the high bit of pmpcfg14.A (pmpcfg14.A[1]) is set, bits pmpaddr14[G-2:0] read as all ones.
RULE 23: When G ≥ 1 and the high bit of pmpcfg14.A (pmpcfg14.A[1]) is clear, bits pmpaddr14[G-1:0] read as all zeros.
RULE 24: Bits pmpaddr14[G-1:0] do not affect the TOR address-matching logic of pmpcfg14.
RULE 25: Changing pmpcfg14.A[1] changes the value read from pmpaddr14 but does not modify the underlying stored value of pmpaddr14.
RULE 26: When pmpcfg14.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR or OFF and then back to NAPOT, the bit pmpaddr14[G-1] retains its original stored value.
RULE 27: If zero is written to pmp0cfg, all‑ones are written to pmpaddr0, and the value read back from pmpaddr0 defines granularity G, then any later write to pmpcfg14 that specifies a region size not aligned to G is ignored, so reading back pmpcfg14 yields the previous value.
RULE 28: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=0, W=0, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, the region is inaccessible and causes an Access Exception in both MMode and S/U Mode.
RULE 29: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=0, W=0, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode generates an Access Exception while S/U Mode treats the region as execute-only.
RULE 30: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=0, W=1, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, both MMode and S/U Mode see a shared data region with read/write permission for both modes.
RULE 31: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=1, W=0, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode generates an Access Exception while S/U Mode sees a read-only region.
RULE 32: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=1, W=0, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode generates an Access Exception while S/U Mode sees a read/execute region.
RULE 33: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=1, W=1, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode generates an Access Exception while S/U Mode sees a read/write region.
RULE 34: When pmpcfg14.L=0, R=1, W=1, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode generates an Access Exception while S/U Mode sees a read/write/execute region.
RULE 35: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=0, W=0, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, both MMode and S/U Mode treat the region as a locked inaccessible region* and cause an Access Exception.
RULE 36: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=0, W=0, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode sees a locked execute-only region* while S/U Mode generates an Access Exception.
RULE 37: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=0, W=1, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, both MMode and S/U Mode see a locked shared code region that is execute-only for both modes*.
RULE 38: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=0, W=1, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode sees a locked shared code region that is read/execute*, while S/U Mode sees the same region as execute-only*.
RULE 39: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=1, W=0, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode sees a locked read-only region* while S/U Mode generates an Access Exception.
RULE 40: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=1, W=0, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode sees a locked read/execute region* while S/U Mode generates an Access Exception.
RULE 41: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=1, W=1, X=0 and mseccfg.MML=1, MMode sees a locked read/write region* while S/U Mode generates an Access Exception.
RULE 42: When pmpcfg14.L=1, R=1, W=1, X=1 and mseccfg.MML=1, both MMode and S/U Mode see a locked shared data region that is read-only for both modes*.
RULE 43: In M-mode, accessing pmpcfg14 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x3ae; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 44: In S-mode, accessing pmpcfg14 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x3ae; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 45: In U-mode, accessing pmpcfg14 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x3ae; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 46: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg14.pmp56cfg (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x3ae, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ae; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 47: In M-mode, setting pmpcfg14.pmp57cfg (bit 8) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100; csrs 0x3ae, a0; csrr a1, 0x3ae; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].

REGISTER: satp
NUMBER: 0x180
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 63..60=MODE, 59..44=ASID, 43..0=PPN
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The satp CSR is accessible with supervisor read/write (SRW) privileges.
RULE 2: When TVM=1, any attempt to read or write the satp CSR while executing in S-mode MUST raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 3: When TVM=0, reads and writes of the satp CSR are permitted while executing in S-mode.
RULE 4: If Svpbmt is not implemented, PBMTE is read-only zero irrespective of any satp configuration.
RULE 5: After changing menvcfg.PBMTE, executing an SFENCE.VMA with rs1=x0 and rs2=x0 suffices to synchronize address-translation caches for translations that use the page tables identified by satp.
RULE 6: When ADUE=1, hardware updating of PTE A/D bits is enabled during S-mode address translation that uses the page table whose physical address is held in satp, and the implementation behaves as though Svade were not implemented for S-mode address translation.
RULE 7: If Svadu is not implemented, ADUE is read-only zero regardless of any satp setting.
RULE 8: If satp.MODE is read-only zero (always Bare), the implementation may make the FIOM bit in the senvcfg CSR read-only zero.
RULE 9: When MODE=Bare, supervisor virtual addresses are equal to supervisor physical addresses and there is no additional memory protection beyond the physical memory protection scheme described in Section 3.7.
RULE 10: Implementations are not required to support all satp MODE settings and if satp is written with an unsupported MODE the entire write has no effect; no fields in satp are modified.
RULE 11: The number of implemented ASID bits, termed ASIDLEN, may be determined by writing one to every bit position in the ASID field of satp and then reading back satp to see which bit positions hold a one.
RULE 12: The least-significant bits of the satp ASID field are implemented first, so if ASIDLEN > 0 then ASID[ASIDLEN-1:0] of satp is writable.
RULE 13: If a program writes an ASID value to the satp register that requires more than 9 bits when the current translation mode is Sv32, or more than 16 bits when the mode is Sv39, Sv48, or Sv57, then the write raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = illegal‑instruction).
RULE 14: For SXLEN=64, satp MODE encoding value 0 denotes Bare, values 1-7 are reserved for standard use, value 8 denotes Sv39, value 9 denotes Sv48, value 10 denotes Sv57, value 11 denotes Sv64 (reserved for page-based 64-bit virtual addressing), values 12-13 are reserved for standard use, and values 14-15 are designated for custom use.
RULE 15: Changing satp.MODE from Bare to other modes and vice versa takes effect immediately without requiring execution of an SFENCE.VMA instruction.
RULE 16: Changes to satp.ASID take effect immediately.
RULE 17: The immediate effect of changing satp.MODE or satp.ASID applies even when the virtual-address width for that translation differs from the width currently specified by satp.MODE.
RULE 18: Implementations that make satp.MODE read-only zero (always Bare) might raise an illegal-instruction exception when an SFENCE.VMA instruction is executed.
RULE 19: The physical page number of the root page table is stored in the satp register.
RULE 20: A write to satp with an unsupported MODE value is ignored.
RULE 21: When V=0, a write to satp containing a MODE field value that is not supported is ignored.
RULE 22: The condition that the ignore transformation replaces the upper PMLEN bits with 0 applies both when executing in M-mode and when executing in any other privilege mode with the active satp register's MODE field set to Bare.

REGISTER: scause
NUMBER: 0x142
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 63..63=INT, 62..0=CODE
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Ssdbltrp, Sstc
RULE 1: The privilege level for accessing scause is supervisor mode.
RULE 2: The access type for scause is supervisor read/write (SRW).
RULE 3: When a trap is delegated to S-mode, the scause register is written with the trap cause.
RULE 4: The interrupt cause number i reported in the scause register corresponds to bit i in both the sip and sie registers.
RULE 5: scause is an SXLEN-bit read-write CSR.
RULE 6: When a trap is taken into S-mode, the implementation writes scause with a code indicating the event that caused the trap.
RULE 7: When a trap is not taken into S-mode, the implementation never writes scause, although software may write it explicitly.
RULE 8: The Interrupt bit of scause is set to 1 if the trap was caused by an interrupt.
RULE 9: The Exception Code field of scause contains a code that identifies the last exception or interrupt.
RULE 10: The Exception Code field of scause is required to implement bits 4-0, thereby supporting values 0 through 31.
RULE 11: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is 1, the scause value indicates a supervisor software interrupt.
RULE 12: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is 5, the scause value indicates a supervisor timer interrupt.
RULE 13: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is 9, the scause value indicates a supervisor external interrupt.
RULE 14: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 1 and the Exception Code field of scause is 13, the scause value indicates a counter-overflow interrupt.
RULE 15: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 0, the scause value indicates an instruction address misaligned exception.
RULE 16: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 1, the scause value indicates an instruction access fault.
RULE 17: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 2, the scause value indicates an illegal instruction.
RULE 18: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 3, the scause value indicates a breakpoint.
RULE 19: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 4, the scause value indicates a load address misaligned exception.
RULE 20: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 5, the scause value indicates a load access fault.
RULE 21: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 6, the scause value indicates a store/AMO address misaligned exception.
RULE 22: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 7, the scause value indicates a store/AMO access fault.
RULE 23: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 8, the scause value indicates an environment call from U-mode.
RULE 24: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 9, the scause value indicates an environment call from S-mode.
RULE 25: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 12, the scause value indicates an instruction page fault.
RULE 26: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 13, the scause value indicates a load page fault.
RULE 27: If the interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the exception code field equals 14, then the scause register contains a reserved value.
RULE 28: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 15, the scause value indicates a store/AMO page fault.
RULE 29: If the Interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the Exception Code field of scause is 18, the scause value indicates a software check.
RULE 30: If the interrupt bit of scause is 0 and the exception‑code field of scause contains a value in the range 20‑23, then the scause value is architecturally reserved, and any subsequent use of that scause value must raise an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 31: If the scause CSR is accessed (read or write) while the current privilege level is not Supervisor, then an illegal‑instruction exception is taken and mcause is set to 2.
RULE 32: The most-significant bit of scause (bit VSXLEN-1) is the Interrupt flag.
RULE 33: When the most-significant interrupt bit of scause is 1, the exception-code field values 0-15 and ≥16 are defined as: 0 reserved, 1 supervisor software interrupt, 2 virtual supervisor software interrupt, 3 machine software interrupt, 4 reserved, 5 supervisor timer interrupt, 6 virtual supervisor timer interrupt, 7 machine timer interrupt, 8 reserved, 9 supervisor external interrupt, 10 virtual supervisor external interrupt, 11 machine external interrupt, 12 supervisor guest external interrupt, 13 counter-overflow interrupt, 14-15 reserved, and codes ≥16 are designated for platform use.
RULE 34: If an instruction can raise multiple synchronous exceptions, the exception with the highest priority according to Table 51 is the one whose code is placed in scause.
RULE 35: In M-mode, accessing scause register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x142; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 36: In S-mode, accessing scause register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x142; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 37: In U-mode, accessing scause register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x142; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 38: In M-mode, setting scause.INT (bit 63) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8000000000000000; csrs 0x142, a0; csrr a1, 0x142; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8000000000000000].
RULE 39: In M-mode, setting scause.CODE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x142, a0; csrr a1, 0x142; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].

REGISTER: seed
NUMBER: 0x015
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: XLEN
FIELDS: 31..30=OPST, 29..24=WPRI, 23..16=custom, 15..0=entropy, UNKNOWN..UNKNOWN=UNKNOWN
EXTENSIONS: Zkr
RULE 1: Attempted access to seed using a read-only CSR-access instruction (CSRRS or CSRRC with rs1=x0, or CSRRSI or CSRRCI with uimm=0) raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 2: If the seed instruction receives a write value in rs1 or uimm, then the seed CSR (or architectural seed register) must retain its prior value; observing the seed CSR change to the supplied operand indicates the implementation failed to ignore the write value.
RULE 3: Seed is also access-controlled by execution mode, and attempted read or write of seed outside M mode raises an illegal-instruction exception unless access is explicitly granted.
RULE 4: If the OPST field of the seed is not ES16, then reading the seed shows the entropy field equal to 0.
RULE 5: If a BIST alarm bit in the seed CSR is set and the seed CSR has not been read at least once thereafter, then the alarm bit remains set; reading the seed CSR clears the alarm bit.
RULE 6: If the ES16 status register is written with 0x8000ABCD, then a subsequent read of that CSR returns 0x8000ABCD and the entropy‑bits field of the register equals 0xABCD.
RULE 7: If the seed field is encoded as 0xFFFFFFFF, then executing the instruction raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = 2).
RULE 8: Implementations may implement mseccfg such that the [s,u]seed fields are read-only constant values of 0.
RULE 9: Software may discover whether access to the seed CSR can be enabled in U and S modes by writing a 1 to the [s,u]seed fields and reading back the result.
RULE 10: If the OPST bits of the seed CSR are 0b11, then the entropy source is reported as unavailable (the availability flag is cleared and reads of the entropy data CSR return zero).
RULE 11: When the OPST bits of the seed CSR are 00 (BIST), they indicate that feature discovery has failed and the entropy source is not available.
RULE 12: A read of the seed CSR returns a 16-bit value.
RULE 13: When the mnoise register's NOISE_TEST bit (mnoise[31]) is set to 1, the seed CSR must not return any data via the ES16 interface.
RULE 14: The seed CSR has URW access, meaning it is unprivileged and both readable and writable.
RULE 15: When USEED = 0, any access to the seed CSR in U-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 16: When USEED = 1, read-write access to the seed CSR from U-mode is allowed.
RULE 17: When USEED = 1, all non-read-write accesses to the seed CSR from U-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 18: When SSEED = 0, any access to the seed CSR from S-mode or HS-mode raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 19: When SSEED = 1, read-write access to the seed CSR from S-mode or HS-mode is allowed.
RULE 20: When SSEED = 1, all non-read-write accesses to the seed CSR from S-mode or HS-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 21: When the H extension is implemented, all other types of access to the seed CSR raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 22: The seed CSR is always available in machine mode as a normal read-write CSR.
RULE 23: An attempted read of the seed CSR without a preceding write raises an illegal-instruction exception regardless of privilege mode and access-control bits.
RULE 24: When operating in U-mode and USEED = 0, any access to the seed CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 25: When operating in U-mode and USEED = 1, the seed CSR is accessible as normal and no exception is raised for read-write accesses.
RULE 26: When operating in S-mode or HS-mode and SSEED = 0, any access to the seed CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 27: When operating in S-mode or HS-mode and SSEED = 1, the seed CSR is accessible as normal and no exception is raised for read-write accesses.
RULE 28: In M-mode, reading seed register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x015; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 29: In S-mode, reading seed register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x015; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 30: In U-mode, reading seed register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x015; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: senvcfg
NUMBER: 0x10a
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 7..7=CBZE, 6..6=CBCFE, 5..4=CBIE, 8..8=UKTE, 3..3=SSE, 0..0=FIOM
EXTENSIONS: Ssnpm, Zicbom, Zicboz, Zicfilp, Zicfiss
RULE 1: If priv_mode == U and senvcfg.CBIE == 00, a CBO.INVAL instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 2: If priv_mode == U and senvcfg.CBCFE is false, a CBO.CLEAN or CBO.FLUSH instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 3: If priv_mode == U and senvcfg.CBZE is false, a CBO.ZERO instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 4: If (priv_mode == U and senvcfg.CBZE is true) or (priv_mode == VU and henvcfg.CBZE and senvcfg.CBZE are both true), a CBO.ZERO instruction executes and performs the zero operation.
RULE 5: The CBIE, CBCFE, and CBZE fields in each xenvcfg register, including those in senvcfg, do not affect the read and write behavior of the same fields in the other xenvcfg registers.
RULE 6: If privilege_mode is U and senvcfg.SSE is 0, an illegal-instruction exception is raised for the SSAMOSWAP.W/D instruction.
RULE 7: senvcfg has SRW privilege, allowing Supervisor-mode reads and writes.
RULE 8: When menvcfg.SSE is 0, the senvcfg.SSE field is read-only and always returns zero.
RULE 9: The value of the ENVCFG bit in the mstateen0 CSR determines whether software can access the senvcfg CSR.
RULE 10: The value of the ENVCFG bit in the hstateen0 CSR determines whether software can access the senvcfg CSR.
RULE 11: If an instruction writes a value to the senvcfg CSR, then a subsequent CSR read of senvcfg returns that same SXLEN‑bit value (with any undefined bits masked out), reflecting the updated U‑mode execution environment.
RULE 12: Execution of CBO.ZERO in U-mode is enabled only if execution of the instruction is enabled for use in S-mode and CBZE is set to 1 in senvcfg; otherwise an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 13: Execution of CBO.CLEAN and CBO.FLUSH instructions in U-mode is enabled only if execution of these instructions is enabled for use in S-mode and CBCFE is set to 1 in senvcfg; otherwise an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 14: Execution of CBO.INVAL in U-mode is enabled only if execution of the instruction is enabled for use in S-mode and CBIE is 01b or 11b in senvcfg; otherwise an illegal-instruction exception is raised.
RULE 15: If the Ssnpm extension is not implemented, PMM is read-only zero in senvcfg.
RULE 16: If PMM is 00 in senvcfg, pointer masking is disabled (PMLEN = 0).
RULE 17: If PMM is 10 in senvcfg, pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN = XLEN-57 (PMLEN = 7 on RV64).
RULE 18: If PMM is 11 in senvcfg, pointer masking is enabled with PMLEN = XLEN-48 (PMLEN = 16 on RV64).
RULE 19: When the LPE field is 0 in senvcfg, the Zicfilp extension is not enabled in VU/U-mode.
RULE 20: When the SSE field is set to 1 in senvcfg, the Zicfiss extension is activated in VU/U-mode.
RULE 21: When the SSE field is 0 in senvcfg, the Zicfiss extension remains inactive in VU/U-mode.
RULE 22: If SSE is 0 in senvcfg, 16-bit Zicfiss instructions revert to their behavior as defined by Zcmop.
RULE 23: If senvcfg.SSE is 0 and V=1, then 16-bit Zicfiss instructions revert to the behavior defined by Zcmop.
RULE 24: If senvcfg.SSE is 0, then reads of senvcfg.SSE return zero and the field is read-only.
RULE 25: When the processor is in U-mode and senvcfg.SSE is 0, an illegal-instruction exception is raised on any access to the ssp CSR.
RULE 26: For privilege mode U or VU with S-mode implemented, the xSSE value is equal to the value of senvcfg.SSE.
RULE 27: If the xSSE bit derived from senvcfg.SSE is cleared for the current U or VU privilege mode, then backward‑edge control‑flow integrity using shadow stacks is not enabled, and a mismatched return address does not raise a trap (no mcause change).
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing senvcfg register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x10a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In S-mode, accessing senvcfg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x10a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 30: In U-mode, accessing senvcfg register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x10a; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 31: In M-mode, setting senvcfg.CBZE (bit 7) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x80) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x80; csrs 0x10a, a0; csrr a1, 0x10a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x80].
RULE 32: In M-mode, setting senvcfg.CBCFE (bit 6) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x40) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x40; csrs 0x10a, a0; csrr a1, 0x10a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x40].
RULE 33: In M-mode, setting senvcfg.CBIE (bit 4) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x10) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x10; csrs 0x10a, a0; csrr a1, 0x10a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x10].
RULE 34: In M-mode, setting senvcfg.UKTE (bit 8) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x100) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x100; csrs 0x10a, a0; csrr a1, 0x10a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x100].
RULE 35: In M-mode, setting senvcfg.SSE (bit 3) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8; csrs 0x10a, a0; csrr a1, 0x10a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8].
RULE 36: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the senvcfg register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x10a, a0; csrr a1, 0x10a; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 37: In M-mode, accessing senvcfg register while Ssnpm extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssnpm; csrr a0, 0x10a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: sepc
NUMBER: 0x141
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=PC
EXTENSIONS: H, S, Ssdbltrp
RULE 1: The sepc CSR has Supervisor Read/Write (SRW) privilege.
RULE 2: When a trap is delegated to S-mode, the sepc register is written with the virtual address of the instruction that took the trap.
RULE 3: Setting a bit in medeleg or mideleg delegates the corresponding trap that occurs in S-mode or U-mode to the S-mode trap handler, and as a result the sepc register is written with the virtual address of the instruction that took the trap.
RULE 4: When a double-trap exception is delivered to M-mode because the S-mode-disable-trap (SDT) bit is already 1, the hart writes the sepc register with the same information that the unexpected trap would have written if it had been taken into M-mode.
RULE 5: sepc is an SXLEN-bit read/write CSR.
RULE 6: The low bit sepc[0] is always zero.
RULE 7: In implementations that support only IALIGN = 32, both low bits sepc[1:0] are always zero.
RULE 8: Whenever IALIGN = 32, reads of sepc mask bit sepc[1] so that it appears to be zero.
RULE 9: The implicit read of sepc performed by the SRET instruction also masks bit sepc[1] when IALIGN = 32.
RULE 10: Even when IALIGN = 32 masks sepc[1] on reads, software may still write to bit sepc[1].
RULE 11: sepc is a WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual addresses.
RULE 12: When a trap is taken into S-mode, the implementation writes sepc with the virtual address of the interrupted or faulting instruction.
RULE 13: Apart from trap handling, the implementation never writes sepc; it may only be written explicitly by software.
RULE 14: If stval is written with a nonzero value during an instruction access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception on a hart that supports variable-length instructions, then sepc points to the beginning of the faulting instruction.
RULE 15: When an illegal-instruction exception occurs and the stval register is used to return the faulting instruction bits, then sepc points to the faulting instruction in memory.
RULE 16: The architectural effect of taking a trap into HS-mode is that the value of the sepc register is updated as part of the trap entry sequence.
RULE 17: When the SRET instruction is executed in M-mode or HS-mode with V=0, the processor sets the program counter to the value contained in sepc after the new privilege mode has been determined.
RULE 18: In M-mode, accessing sepc register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x141; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 19: In S-mode, accessing sepc register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x141; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 20: In U-mode, accessing sepc register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x141; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 21: In M-mode, setting sepc.PC (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x141, a0; csrr a1, 0x141; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 22: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the sepc register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x141, a0; csrr a1, 0x141; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 23: In M-mode, accessing sepc register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x141; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 24: In M-mode, accessing sepc register while S extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: S; csrr a0, 0x141; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 25: In M-mode, accessing sepc register while Ssdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x141; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: sie
NUMBER: 0x104
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 1..1=SSIE, 5..5=STIE, 9..9=SEIE, 13..13=LCOFIE
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Sstc
RULE 1: If code executing in a non‑supervisor mode (e.g., user mode) attempts to read or write the sie CSR, then a privileged‑instruction/illegal‑instruction exception is raised (mcause = 2).
RULE 2: The sie register is readable and writable in supervisor mode (SRW).
RULE 3: If an interrupt is delegated to S-mode by setting the corresponding bit in the mideleg register, then that interrupt can be masked using the sie register.
RULE 4: If the corresponding bit in the mideleg register is not set, then the corresponding bits in the sie register are read-only zero.
RULE 5: The supervisor can disable individual interrupt sources using the sie CSR.
RULE 6: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, SPIE is set to the value of SIE.
RULE 7: When an SRET instruction is executed, SIE is set to the value of SPIE.
RULE 8: When an SRET instruction is executed, SPIE is set to 1.
RULE 9: Reading SIE in sstatus mirrors reading SIE in mstatus.
RULE 10: Writing SIE in sstatus mirrors writing SIE in mstatus.
RULE 11: If a program writes a value to the sie CSR, then a subsequent read of sie must return that same SXLEN‑bit value, and any interrupt‑enable bit that is set enables the corresponding interrupt (observable by the interrupt being taken and mcause indicating its cause), while a cleared bit disables that interrupt.
RULE 12: Interrupt cause number i corresponds with bit i in both sip and sie.
RULE 13: An interrupt i will trap to S-mode only if the corresponding sie bit i is set.
RULE 14: A write to sie causes the interrupt-trap conditions to be evaluated immediately.
RULE 15: A bit in sie must be writable if the corresponding interrupt can ever become pending.
RULE 16: Bits of sie that are not writable are read-only zero.
RULE 17: If a standard interrupt type (SEI, STI, SSI, or LCOFI) is not implemented, the corresponding sie bit is a read-only zero.
RULE 18: If a program writes any bit pattern to the sie CSR, then a subsequent read of sie returns a value whose each bit is a defined legal value for that field (e.g., illegal bits are cleared to 0) and no exception is raised.
RULE 19: Implemented sie bits can be discovered by writing one to every bit location in sie and reading back to identify bits that retain a one.
RULE 20: Reading a sie bit reads the corresponding mie bit, and writing a writable sie bit writes the corresponding mie bit.
RULE 21: Bit 13 of the sie register is assigned to the count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 22: In the sie register, the LCOFIE bit is the interrupt-enable bit for the count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 23: The interrupt-enable bits for the count-overflow interrupt include the sie LCOFIE bit.
RULE 24: Whether the count-overflow interrupt is enabled by the sie LCOFIE bit depends on the delegation setting in the mideleg register.
RULE 25: For each writable bit in sie, the corresponding bit in both hip and hie shall be read-only zero.
RULE 26: The nonzero bits in sie and hie are always mutually exclusive, and the nonzero bits in sip and hip are always mutually exclusive.
RULE 27: An interrupt i traps to HS-mode if (1) the current operating mode is HS-mode and the SIE bit in the sstatus register is set, or the current operating mode has less privilege than HS-mode; (2) bit i is set in both sip and sie, or in both hip and hie; and (3) bit i is not set in hideleg.
RULE 28: When hideleg[13] is one, vsie.LCOFIE is an alias of sie.LCOFIE.
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing sie register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x104; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In S-mode, accessing sie register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x104; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 31: In U-mode, accessing sie register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x104; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 32: In M-mode, setting sie.SSIE (bit 1) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x104, a0; csrr a1, 0x104; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2].
RULE 33: In M-mode, setting sie.STIE (bit 5) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x20) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x20; csrs 0x104, a0; csrr a1, 0x104; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x20].
RULE 34: In M-mode, setting sie.SEIE (bit 9) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x200) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x200; csrs 0x104, a0; csrr a1, 0x104; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x200].
RULE 35: In M-mode, setting sie.LCOFIE (bit 13) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2000; csrs 0x104, a0; csrr a1, 0x104; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2000].
RULE 36: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the sie register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x104, a0; csrr a1, 0x104; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 37: In M-mode, accessing sie register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0x104; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 38: In M-mode, accessing sie register while Sstc extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sstc; csrr a0, 0x104; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: sip
NUMBER: 0x144
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 1..1=SSIP, 5..5=STIP, 9..9=SEIP, 13..13=LCOFIP
EXTENSIONS: Sscofpmf, Sstc
RULE 1: The sip register is accessible with Supervisor-read/write privilege (SRW).
RULE 2: The sip register provides a restricted view of the mip register for supervisor level.
RULE 3: If an interrupt is delegated to S-mode by setting a bit in the mideleg register, then that bit becomes visible in the sip register.
RULE 4: If the corresponding bit is not set in the mideleg register, then the corresponding bits in the sip register and the sie register are read-only zero.
RULE 5: When the Sstc extension is implemented and the STCE bit in menvcfg is zero, the STIP field in the sip CSR reverts to its defined behavior as if the Sstc extension were not implemented.
RULE 6: The sip register can be interrogated to determine the presence of any interrupt in supervisor mode.
RULE 7: An interrupt i traps to S-mode if the current privilege mode is S and the SIE bit in sstatus is set, or if the current privilege mode has less privilege than S-mode, and bit i is set in both sip and sie.
RULE 8: Each individual bit in sip may be writable or read-only; when a bit i in sip is writable, a pending interrupt i can be cleared by writing 0 to that bit; if bit i in sip is read-only while interrupt i can become pending, the implementation must provide some other mechanism for clearing the pending interrupt.
RULE 9: If software writes the SEIP bit in the sip CSR, then the SEIP bit retains its previous value (the write is ignored) and no exception is raised.
RULE 10: If implemented, the SSIP bit in sip is writable and may also be set to 1 by a platform-specific interrupt controller.
RULE 11: If the Sscofpmf extension is implemented, the LCOFIP bit in sip is read-write and reflects the occurrence of a local-counter-overflow interrupt request resulting from any mhpmevent n.OF bit being set; if the Sscofpmf extension is not implemented, sip.LCOFIP is a read-only zero.
RULE 12: Reading any implemented field of sip or writing any writable field of sip causes a read or write of the homonymous field of mip.
RULE 13: In the sip register, the new count overflow interrupt will be treated as a standard local interrupt.
RULE 14: The new count overflow interrupt is assigned to bit 13 in the sip register.
RULE 15: The count-overflow-interrupt-request signal is treated as a standard local interrupt that corresponds to bit 13 of the sip register.
RULE 16: Bit 13 of the sip register, named LCOFIP, functions as the interrupt-pending bit for the count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 17: The LCOFIP bit in the sip register is cleared by software before servicing the count-overflow interrupt.
RULE 18: hip and hie are HSXLEN-bit read/write registers that supplement HS-level's sip.
RULE 19: Nonzero bits in sip and hip are always mutually exclusive.
RULE 20: An interrupt i traps to HS-mode when bit i is set in both sip and sie, provided that either the current mode is HS-mode with the SIE bit in sstatus set or the current mode has less privilege than HS-mode, and bit i is not set in hideleg.
RULE 21: In M-mode, accessing sip register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x144; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 22: In S-mode, accessing sip register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x144; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 23: In U-mode, accessing sip register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x144; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 24: In M-mode, setting sip.SSIP (bit 1) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x144, a0; csrr a1, 0x144; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2].
RULE 25: In M-mode, setting sip.STIP (bit 5) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x20; csrs 0x144, a0; csrr a1, 0x144; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 26: In M-mode, setting sip.SEIP (bit 9) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x200; csrs 0x144, a0; csrr a1, 0x144; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].
RULE 27: In M-mode, setting sip.LCOFIP (bit 13) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2000; csrs 0x144, a0; csrr a1, 0x144; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2000].
RULE 28: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the sip register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x144, a0; csrr a1, 0x144; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 29: In M-mode, accessing sip register while Sscofpmf extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sscofpmf; csrr a0, 0x144; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In M-mode, accessing sip register while Sstc extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sstc; csrr a0, 0x144; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: siselect
NUMBER: 0x150
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: H, Smcntrpmf, Smctr, Smstateen, Ssaia, Sscofpmf, Sscsrind, Ssctr, Ssstateen
RULE 1: The siselect CSR has supervisor-read/write (SRW) privilege, meaning it is accessible only in supervisor mode for both reads and writes.
RULE 2: The CSRIND bit in hstateen0 controls access to the siselect CSR provided by the Sscsrind extensions.
RULE 3: If a value greater than 0xFFF is written to the siselect CSR, then the implementation may raise an illegal‑instruction exception (the result is not architecturally defined).
RULE 4: The siselect CSR is always XLEN bits wide (the current XLEN) and is not VSXLEN.
RULE 5: If mstateen0[60] = 0 and an attempt to access siselect is made from a privilege mode less privileged than M-mode, the attempt results in an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: If the hypervisor extension is implemented, bit 60 of the hypervisor CSR hstateen0 controls access to siselect and any CSR accessed indirectly through siselect.
RULE 7: If the Smstateen extension is implemented and mstateen0[60]=0, any access to siselect from a privilege mode less privileged than M-mode must be prohibited.
RULE 8: When siselect equals 0x41, the accessed register is the memory-mapped mtime register, which is not a performance-monitoring counter and therefore any access must raise an illegal-instruction exception.

REGISTER: sscratch
NUMBER: 0x140
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=SCRATCH
EXTENSIONS: S
RULE 1: The sscratch CSR is a supervisor-level CSR that permits both read and write operations.
RULE 2: The sscratch CSR is an SXLEN-bit read/write register that is dedicated for use by the supervisor.
RULE 3: When V=1, the contents of sscratch are not written.
RULE 4: In M-mode, accessing sscratch register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x140; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 5: In S-mode, accessing sscratch register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x140; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: ssp
NUMBER: 0x011
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: XLEN
FIELDS: 63..3=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: Zaamo, Zcmop, Zicfiss, Zicsr, Zimop
RULE 1: Reading the ssp register yields its current contents.
RULE 2: The ssp CSR is an unprivileged read-write (URW) CSR.
RULE 3: The ssp CSR reads and writes the XLEN low-order bits of the shadow stack pointer ssp.
RULE 4: Bits 1:0 of ssp are read-only zero.
RULE 5: If the UXLEN or SXLEN may never be 32, then bit 2 of ssp is read-only zero.
RULE 6: A shadow-stack push operation is defined as a decrement of the ssp register by XLEN/8 followed by a store of the link-register value to memory at the new top of the shadow stack.
RULE 7: The base address for the store performed by SSPUSH and C.SSPUSH is implicitly the current value of the ssp register.
RULE 8: The access width of the store performed by SSPUSH and C.SSPUSH is implicitly XLEN bits.
RULE 9: SSPUSH and C.SSPUSH decrement the ssp register by XLEN/8 only when the condition xSSE == 1 holds.
RULE 10: The ssp register is decremented by SSPUSH and C.SSPUSH only if the store to the shadow stack completes successfully.
RULE 11: The SSPOPCHK and C.SSPOPCHK instructions perform a load identical to existing load instructions except that the base address is implicitly ssp and the access width is implicitly XLEN.
RULE 12: The pseudo-code for SSPOPCHK/C.SSPOPCHK specifies that, after a successful operation, ssp is updated as ssp = ssp + (XLEN/8).
RULE 13: Only the architectural registers x1 and x5 may be used as the source register for SSPOPCHK/C.SSPOPCHK; using any other source register raises a software-check exception and ssp is not incremented.
RULE 14: If the value loaded from the address referenced by ssp does not equal the value in rs1, a software-check exception with cause = 18 is raised and xtval is set to "shadow stack fault (code=3)", and ssp is not incremented.
RULE 15: ssp is incremented by SSPOPCHK and C.SSPOPCHK only when the load from the shadow stack completes without error and no software-check exception is raised.
RULE 16: The increment applied to ssp by SSPOPCHK and C.SSPOPCHK is exactly XLEN divided by 8 bytes.
RULE 17: The SSRDP instruction moves the contents of ssp to a destination register, subject to the xSSE condition.
RULE 18: If xSSE == 1, SSRDP writes the current value of ssp to the destination register.
RULE 19: If xSSE != 1, SSRDP does not read ssp and instead writes 0 to the destination register.
RULE 20: The csrw ssp instruction writes the supplied value to the ssp register.
RULE 21: When the instruction csrrw ra, ssp, ra is executed, the CSR ssp is written with the original value of register ra.
RULE 22: The ssp register is accessible with URW privilege, meaning it can be read and written by unprivileged software.
RULE 23: If the current privilege mode is less than M and menvcfg.SSE is 0, accessing the ssp CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 24: If the current privilege mode is U-mode and senvcfg.SSE is 0, accessing the ssp CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 25: If any of the preceding conditions that restrict access to the ssp CSR are true, then an attempt to read or write the ssp CSR raises an illegal‑instruction exception; otherwise the access succeeds and the CSR value is read or written as specified.
RULE 26: If the virtual address in ssp is not XLEN-aligned, then the C.SSPUSH instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 27: If the virtual address in ssp is not XLEN-aligned, then the SSPOPCHK instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 28: If the virtual address in ssp is not XLEN-aligned, then the C.SSPOPCHK instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 29: If the memory referenced by ssp is not idempotent, then the SSPUSH instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 30: If the memory referenced by ssp is not idempotent, then the C.SSPOPCHK instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 31: If the memory referenced by ssp is not idempotent, then the SSAMOSWAP.W/D instruction causes a store/AMO access-fault exception.
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing ssp register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 33: In S-mode, accessing ssp register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 34: In U-mode, accessing ssp register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 35: In M-mode, setting ssp.VALUE (bit 3) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x8) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x8; csrs 0x011, a0; csrr a1, 0x011; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x8].
RULE 36: In M-mode, accessing ssp register while Zaamo extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zaamo; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 37: In M-mode, accessing ssp register while Zcmop extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zcmop; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 38: In M-mode, accessing ssp register while Zicfiss extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfiss; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 39: In M-mode, accessing ssp register while Zicsr extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicsr; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 40: In M-mode, accessing ssp register while Zimop extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zimop; csrr a0, 0x011; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: sstateen0

REGISTER: sstateen1
NUMBER: 0x10d
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=DATA
EXTENSIONS: Smctr, Smstateen, Ssctr, Ssstateen
RULE 1: sstateen1 has privilege (access type) SRW, indicating Supervisor Read/Write access.
RULE 2: The upper 32 bits of the CSR sstateen1 are always zeros.
RULE 3: The CSR sstateen1 controls access to state at all less-privileged levels but does not control access at the supervisor level itself.
RULE 4: Any bit of sstateen1 that controls state not implemented by a hart is read-only zero for that hart.
RULE 5: Any reserved bit of sstateen1 that has not been given a defined meaning is read-only zero.
RULE 6: For every bit that is zero in mstateen1, the same bit appears as read-only zero in sstateen1.
RULE 7: No bit of sstateen1 may be read-only one unless the same bit is read-only one in the matching mstateen1 CSR and, if present, in the matching hstateen1 CSR.
RULE 8: On reset, all writable bits of mstateen1 are initialized by hardware to zeros, and machine-level software that changes those bits must also initialize the corresponding writable bits of sstateen1 to zeros.
RULE 9: Bit 63 of mstateen1 controls access to the CSR sstateen1 (and to hstateen1).
RULE 10: Bit 63 of hstateen1 controls access to the CSR sstateen1.
RULE 11: In M-mode, accessing sstateen1 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x10d; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 12: In S-mode, accessing sstateen1 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x10d; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 13: In U-mode, accessing sstateen1 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x10d; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 14: In M-mode, setting sstateen1.DATA (bit 0) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x10d, a0; csrr a1, 0x10d; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].

RULE 1: sstateen2 is SRW (supervisor read/write) accessible.

REGISTER: sstateen3
NUMBER: 0x10f
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=DATA
EXTENSIONS: Smstateen, Ssstateen
RULE 1: sstateen3 has privilege SRW, indicating it is readable and writable in supervisor mode.

REGISTER: sstatus
NUMBER: 0x100
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: SXLEN
FIELDS: 63..63=SD, 33..32=UXL, 23..23=SPELP, 19..19=MXR, 18..18=SUM, 16..15=XS, 14..13=FS, 10..9=VS, 8..8=SPP, 6..6=UBE, 5..5=SPIE, 1..1=SIE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: If a CMO instruction accesses a cache block while the effective privilege mode is not granted access by the combination of SUM and MXR bits in sstatus together with the MPRV, MPV, and MPP bits in mstatus and the SUM and MXR bits in mstatus and vsstatus, then the instruction raises an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 2: If a CMO instruction’s effective address maps to a cache block that is not permitted by the current sstatus settings (i.e., the required combination of the SUM and MXR bits is not set), then the instruction raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = 2).
RULE 3: The sstatus register bits 10-9 are defined as a vector context status field named VS that is a shadow of the corresponding bits 10-9 in the mstatus register.
RULE 4: sstatus is readable and writable at supervisor privilege level.
RULE 5: When an MRET or SRET instruction is executed while the hart is in M-mode, the sstatus.MDT bit is set to 0.
RULE 6: If the new privilege mode after an MRET or SRET return is U, VS, or VU, the sstatus.SDT field is set to 0.
RULE 7: If the Ssdbltrp extension is not implemented, the sstatus.SDT bit is read-only zero (and the vsstatus.SDT and henvcfg.DTE bits are also read-only zero).
RULE 8: The FS field in the sstatus register blocks access to the floating-point f registers.
RULE 9: The sstatus register is an SXLEN-bit read/write register.
RULE 10: When a trap is taken, the SPP bit in sstatus is set to 0 if the trap originated from user mode, or set to 1 otherwise.
RULE 11: When an SRET instruction is executed, the privilege level is set to user mode if the SPP bit in sstatus is 0, or set to supervisor mode if the SPP bit in sstatus is 1.
RULE 12: When an SRET instruction is executed, the SPP bit in sstatus is set to 0.
RULE 13: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, the SPIE bit in sstatus is set to the previous value of the SIE bit in sstatus.
RULE 14: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, the SIE bit in sstatus is set to 0.
RULE 15: When an SRET instruction is executed, the SIE bit in sstatus is set to the previous value of the SPIE bit in sstatus.
RULE 16: When an SRET instruction is executed, the SPIE bit in sstatus is set to 1.
RULE 17: In a straightforward implementation, reading any field in sstatus yields the same value as reading the homonymous field in mstatus.
RULE 18: In a straightforward implementation, writing any field in sstatus updates the homonymous field in mstatus with the same value.
RULE 19: When the sstatus register indicates that SXLEN=64, the UXL field is a WARL field that encodes the current value of UXLEN.
RULE 20: When the sstatus register indicates that UXLEN < SXLEN, user-mode instruction-fetch addresses and load and store effective addresses are taken modulo 2^UXLEN.
RULE 21: When the MXR bit in sstatus is 0, only loads from pages marked readable (R=1) will succeed.
RULE 22: When the MXR bit in sstatus is 1, loads from pages marked either readable or executable (R=1 or X=1) will succeed.
RULE 23: The MXR bit in sstatus has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.
RULE 24: If the SUM bit in sstatus is 0 and a supervisor‑mode load or store accesses a user‑mode address, then the operation raises a load/store page‑fault exception (mcause set to the appropriate load or store page‑fault code); if the SUM bit is 1, the same access completes normally and the destination register contains the loaded value (or the store writes the data to memory).
RULE 25: The SUM bit in sstatus has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.
RULE 26: The SUM bit in sstatus has no effect when executing in U-mode.
RULE 27: The SUM bit in sstatus is read-only 0 if satp.MODE is read-only 0.
RULE 28: The SUM bit in sstatus does not grant S-mode software permission to execute instructions in user code pages.
RULE 29: The UBE bit in the sstatus register is a WARL (write-any-value-read-legal) field.
RULE 30: When the UBE bit in the sstatus register is 0, explicit load and store memory accesses made from U-mode are performed in little-endian order, and when the UBE bit is 1 they are performed in big-endian order.
RULE 31: The UBE bit in the sstatus register has no effect on instruction fetches, which are implicit memory accesses that are always little-endian.
RULE 32: For implicit accesses to supervisor-level memory-management data structures such as page tables, the endianness defined by S-mode applies and the UBE bit in the sstatus register is ignored.
RULE 33: When the V bit is 0, any access to the SPELP field in sstatus accesses the homonymous SPELP field in mstatus.
RULE 34: The clearing of the SIE bit occurs regardless of any value written to the SIE bit by the same CSR write.
RULE 35: The SIE bit in sstatus may be set to 1 by an explicit CSR write only if the same write sets the SDT bit to 0 or the SDT bit is already 0.
RULE 36: When a trap is to be taken into S-mode and the SDT bit in sstatus is 0, the SDT bit is set to 1 before the trap is delivered.
RULE 37: An SRET instruction sets the SDT bit in sstatus to 0.
RULE 38: An interrupt i will trap to S-mode when the current privilege mode is S, the SIE bit in the sstatus register is set, and bit i is set in both sip and sie.
RULE 39: The evaluation of interrupt trap conditions must occur immediately after an explicit write to the sstatus register.
RULE 40: Changes to the sstatus SUM field take effect immediately and do not require execution of an SFENCE.VMA instruction.
RULE 41: Changes to the sstatus MXR field take effect immediately and do not require execution of an SFENCE.VMA instruction.
RULE 42: If the SUM bit in sstatus is clear, supervisor code will fault on accesses to pages whose PTE U bit = 1.
RULE 43: Irrespective of the SUM bit in sstatus, the supervisor may not execute code on pages whose PTE U bit = 1.
RULE 44: When any trap is taken, the implementation sets the SPP bit in sstatus to the nominal privilege mode that was in effect at the time of the trap.
RULE 45: Executing an SRET instruction that transfers control to U-mode always clears the SPP bit in sstatus to 0.
RULE 46: An interrupt i will trap to HS-mode only if, when the current operating mode is HS-mode, the SIE bit in the sstatus register is set.
RULE 47: During execution of hypervisor virtual-machine load and store instructions, the HS-level sstatus.SUM field is ignored.
RULE 48: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the sstatus.SPP field is set to 0 if the previous privilege mode was U-mode.
RULE 49: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the sstatus.SPP field is set to 1 if the previous privilege mode was HS-mode.
RULE 50: When the SRET instruction is executed in M-mode or HS-mode with V = 0, the architectural value of sstatus.SPP together with hstatus.SPV determines the new privilege mode as defined by the specification.
RULE 51: After SRET has determined the new privilege mode while executing in M-mode or HS-mode with V = 0, the instruction sets sstatus.SPP to 0.
RULE 52: After SRET has determined the new privilege mode while executing in M-mode or HS-mode with V = 0, the instruction sets sstatus.SIE to the current value of sstatus.SPIE.
RULE 53: After SRET has determined the new privilege mode while executing in M-mode or HS-mode with V = 0, the instruction sets sstatus.SPIE to 1.
RULE 54: sstatus includes the SPELP bit and any read or write of that bit accesses the same architectural field as mstatus.SPELP.
RULE 55: In M-mode, accessing sstatus register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x100; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 56: In S-mode, accessing sstatus register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x100; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: stval
NUMBER: 0x143
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: H, Ssdbltrp, Zicfilp, Zicfiss
RULE 1: The stval register is accessible with supervisor read/write privilege (SRW).
RULE 2: When a trap is delegated to S-mode (i.e., the trap occurs in S-mode or U-mode and the corresponding bit in medeleg or mideleg is set), the stval register is written with an exception-specific datum.
RULE 3: The stval CSR is an SXLEN-bit read-write register.
RULE 4: When a trap is taken into S-mode, the implementation writes stval with exception-specific information to assist software in handling the trap.
RULE 5: Otherwise, the implementation never writes stval, though it may be explicitly written by software.
RULE 6: If stval is written with a nonzero value when a breakpoint, address-misaligned, access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on an instruction fetch, load, or store, then stval will contain the faulting virtual address.
RULE 7: On a breakpoint exception raised by an EBREAK or C.EBREAK instruction, stval is written with either zero or the virtual address of the instruction.
RULE 8: If stval is written with a nonzero value when a misaligned load or store causes an access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception, then stval will contain the virtual address of the portion of the access that caused the fault.
RULE 9: If stval is written with a nonzero value when an instruction access-fault, page-fault, or hardware-error exception occurs on a hart with variable-length instructions, then stval will contain the virtual address of the portion of the instruction that caused the fault, while sepc will point to the beginning of the instruction.
RULE 10: If stval is written with a nonzero value when an illegal-instruction exception occurs, then stval will contain the shortest of the actual faulting instruction, the first ILEN bits of the faulting instruction, or the first SXLEN bits of the faulting instruction.
RULE 11: The value loaded into stval on an illegal-instruction exception is right-justified and all unused upper bits are cleared to zero.
RULE 12: On a trap caused by a software-check exception, stval holds the cause for the exception.
RULE 13: When the cause of a software-check exception is 0, stval is 0 to indicate no information provided.
RULE 14: When the cause of a software-check exception is 2, stval is 2 to indicate a Landing Pad Fault as defined by the Zicfilp extension.
RULE 15: When the cause of a software-check exception is 3, stval is 3 to indicate a Shadow Stack Fault as defined by the Zicfiss extension.
RULE 16: For other traps, stval is set to zero, but a future standard may redefine stval's setting for other traps.
RULE 17: stval is a WARL register that must be able to hold all valid virtual addresses and the value 0.
RULE 18: If the feature to return the faulting instruction bits is implemented, stval must also be able to hold all values less than 2^N, where N is the smaller of SXLEN and ILEN.
RULE 19: When any other trap into HS-mode writes to stval, the GVA field in stval is set to 0.
RULE 20: For breakpoint and memory-access traps that write a nonzero value to stval, the GVA field in stval is set to the same value as the SPV field.
RULE 21: If the explicit memory access of an HLV, HLVX, or HSV instruction causes a fault, SPV is set to 0 and GVA is set to 1 in stval.
RULE 22: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, hardware writes the stval register with exception-specific information.
RULE 23: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the implementation writes the CSR stval.
RULE 24: The write of the CSR stval is performed as part of the trap entry actions for a trap taken into HS-mode.
RULE 25: The positive difference between the faulting virtual address written to stval and the original virtual address can be nonzero only for a misaligned memory access.
RULE 26: When the hardware writes an address to the stval CSR during exception handling, pointer masking is applied to that write if pointer masking is applicable to that address.
RULE 27: During exception delivery, the hardware applies pointer masking to any address written into stval if pointer masking is applicable to that address.
RULE 28: In M-mode, accessing stval register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 29: In S-mode, accessing stval register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 30: In U-mode, accessing stval register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 31: In M-mode, setting stval.VALUE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x143, a0; csrr a1, 0x143; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 32: In M-mode, accessing stval register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 33: In M-mode, accessing stval register while Ssdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 34: In M-mode, accessing stval register while Zicfilp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfilp; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 35: In M-mode, accessing stval register while Zicfiss extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfiss; csrr a0, 0x143; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: stvec
NUMBER: 0x105
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..2=BASE, 1..0=MODE
EXTENSIONS: H, Ssdbltrp
RULE 1: stvec is a Supervisor-mode CSR.
RULE 2: stvec is readable and writable.
RULE 3: stvec is an SXLEN-bit read/write register that holds trap vector configuration consisting of a vector base address (BASE) and a vector mode (MODE).
RULE 4: In the CSR layout, bits SXLEN-1 down to 2 of stvec hold the BASE field and are WARL, and bits 1-0 of stvec hold the MODE field and are WARL.
RULE 5: The BASE field of stvec must contain a 4-byte-aligned virtual or physical address.
RULE 6: The stvec CSR stores only bits XLEN-1 through 2 of the BASE address, and the lower two bits are implicitly zeroed to form an XLEN-bit address that is always 4-byte aligned.
RULE 7: When the MODE field of stvec is set to Direct, all traps into supervisor mode cause the program counter to be set to the address contained in the BASE field of stvec.
RULE 8: When the MODE field of stvec is set to Vectored, all synchronous exceptions into supervisor mode cause the program counter to be set to the address contained in the BASE field of stvec.
RULE 9: A supervisor-mode timer interrupt causes the program counter to be set to stvec.BASE plus 0x14.
RULE 10: Pointer masking is not applied when software writes to stvec.
RULE 11: During trap delivery, the address taken from stvec for the trap handler is used without pointer masking.
RULE 12: In M-mode, accessing stvec register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x105; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 13: In S-mode, accessing stvec register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x105; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 14: In U-mode, accessing stvec register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x105; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 15: In M-mode, setting stvec.BASE (bit 2) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4; csrs 0x105, a0; csrr a1, 0x105; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4].
RULE 16: In M-mode, setting stvec.MODE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x105, a0; csrr a1, 0x105; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 17: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the stvec register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x105, a0; csrr a1, 0x105; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 18: In M-mode, accessing stvec register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x105; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 19: In M-mode, accessing stvec register while Ssdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x105; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: tdata1
NUMBER: 0x7a1
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: XLEN
FIELDS: 63..60=TYPE, 59..59=DMODE, 58..0=DATA
EXTENSIONS: Zicbom, Zicbop, Zicboz
RULE 1: If a trigger is programmed with tdata1.type = 6 and mcontrol6.select = 0, then when the processor fetches an instruction whose address matches the trigger’s address fields, the trigger must fire and cause entry into debug mode (the processor must take the configured debug exception); if debug mode is not entered, the implementation violates the rule.
RULE 2: If a CSR write sets tdata1.type to 2, then an illegal‑instruction exception is raised and the tdata1 CSR value does not change.
RULE 3: When the Zicboz extension is implemented, implementing address-match triggers that satisfy tdata1.type = 6 and mcontrol6.select = 0 should be mandatory.
RULE 4: If the Zicbom extension is implemented and a trigger is programmed with tdata1.type = 6 and mcontrol6.select = 1, then writing that trigger raises an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 5: If the Zicboz extension is implemented and software writes a trigger with tdata1.type = 6 and mcontrol6.select = 1, then the write must not raise an illegal‑instruction exception and a subsequent memory access that matches the trigger must fire the trigger (e.g., raise a breakpoint exception and set mcause to the trigger‑exception code).
RULE 6: If the Zicbop extension is implemented and a trigger is programmed with tdata1.type = 6 and mcontrol6.select = 1, then the CSR write that configures the trigger raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = 2).
RULE 7: If a CSR instruction in M‑mode reads or writes tdata1, then the operation completes without exception and the CSR readback value reflects the written value; if the instruction is executed in any mode other than M‑mode, then it raises an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 8: In M-mode, accessing tdata1 register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x7a1; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 9: In S-mode, accessing tdata1 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x7a1; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 10: In U-mode, accessing tdata1 register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x7a1; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 11: In M-mode, setting tdata1.TYPE (bit 60) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000000) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1000000000000000; csrs 0x7a1, a0; csrr a1, 0x7a1; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1000000000000000].
RULE 12: In M-mode, setting tdata1.DMODE (bit 59) should not be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x800000000000000; csrs 0x7a1, a0; csrr a1, 0x7a1; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x0].

REGISTER: time
NUMBER: 0xc01
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=COUNT
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The TIME CSR must be read-only and may be accessed using the csrrs canonical form or any of the read-only CSR instruction forms based on CSRRC, CSRRSI, or CSRRCI.
RULE 2: On implementations with XLEN ≥ 64, the RDTIME pseudoinstruction reads the full 64-bit TIME counter.
RULE 3: If a real‑time clock tick occurs, then the 64‑bit TIME CSR value increments by one.
RULE 4: The real-time clocks of all harts must be synchronized to within one tick of the TIME clock.
RULE 5: Implementations must make it appear to software that the TIME values observed on different harts differ by no more than one tick.
RULE 6: Software must observe TIME values across harts to be monotonically nondecreasing.
RULE 7: The CSR at address 0xC01 named time is an unprivileged read-only register that provides the timer value for the RDTIME instruction.
RULE 8: The time CSR has URO privilege, meaning it is readable by unprivileged code and cannot be written by any privilege level.
RULE 9: The htimedelta CSR provides the lower 32 bits of the virtual supervisor time delta, is readable and writable in hypervisor mode, and is located at CSR address 0x605 (with the upper 32 bits at address 0x615 for RV64).
RULE 10: Accesses to the timeh CSR read or modify bits 63:32 of the corresponding 64-bit time CSR.
RULE 11: When XLEN = 64, an attempt to access the timeh CSR typically raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 12: When the TM bit in the mcounteren register is clear, attempts to read the time CSR while executing in S-mode or U-mode cause an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 13: When the TM bit in the mcounteren register is set, reading the time CSR in the next implemented lower-privilege mode (S-mode if implemented, otherwise U-mode) succeeds.
RULE 14: In harts that implement U-mode, the mcounteren register must be implemented, its fields are WARL and may be read-only zero, and a zero TM field causes a read of the time CSR in S-mode or U-mode to raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 15: Changing the accessibility settings of the time CSR does not affect the underlying time counter, which continues to increment even when the time CSR is not accessible.
RULE 16: Because the mtime counter can be shared between multiple cores, it cannot be inhibited with the mcountinhibit mechanism.
RULE 17: When the Sstc extension is implemented and the time-related STCE bit in menvcfg is zero, the STIP time-interrupt pending bits in mip and sip revert to their defined behavior as if the extension is not implemented.
RULE 18: The machine timer interrupt remains pending until mtimecmp becomes greater than the time register mtime.
RULE 19: If the result of the comparison between the time register mtime and mtimecmp changes, the change is guaranteed to be reflected in MTIP eventually, but not necessarily immediately.
RULE 20: The time CSR is a read-only shadow of the memory-mapped time register mtime.
RULE 21: If the mtime register is updated, then reads of the time or timeh CSR may initially return the old value, but after a finite number of cycles the CSR readback must equal the updated mtime value.
RULE 22: When the TM bit in the scounteren register is clear, a read of the time CSR in U-mode causes an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 23: When the TM bit in the scounteren register is set, a read of the time CSR in U-mode is permitted.
RULE 24: If the TM bit in the scounteren register is read-only zero, a read of the time CSR in U-mode causes an exception.
RULE 25: U-mode may only access the time CSR when both the TM bit in scounteren and the TM bit in mcounteren are set.
RULE 26: When the Interrupt bit in scause is 1 and the Exception Code field equals 5, the scause register indicates a supervisor timer interrupt.
RULE 27: When the Interrupt bit in scause is 1 and the Exception Code field equals 13, the scause register indicates a counter-overflow interrupt, which is a time-related event.
RULE 28: If adding htimedelta to the time CSR produces a value larger than the XLEN‑wide register can hold, then the overflow is ignored and the time CSR is written with the low XLEN bits of the sum (wrap‑around), and no exception is raised.
RULE 29: When XLEN=64, the htimedeltah CSR does not exist, so the time CSR delta is accessed only via htimedelta.
RULE 30: A supervisor timer interrupt, which is a time interrupt, is indicated by interrupt code 5.
RULE 31: A machine timer interrupt, which is a time interrupt, is indicated by interrupt code 7.
RULE 32: When XLEN>32, any attempt to access the high-half time CSR always raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 33: In M-mode, accessing time register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc01; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 34: In S-mode, accessing time register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc01; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 35: In U-mode, accessing time register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc01; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 36: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the time register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0xc01, a0; csrr a1, 0xc01; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: tselect
NUMBER: 0x7a0
MODE: M-mode
WIDTH: XLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=INDEX
EXTENSIONS: Sdtrig
RULE 1: In M-mode, accessing tselect register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x7a0; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
