RULE 3: In U-mode, accessing tselect register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x7a0; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 4: In M-mode, setting tselect.INDEX (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x7a0, a0; csrr a1, 0x7a0; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 5: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the tselect register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x7a0, a0; csrr a1, 0x7a0; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 6: In M-mode, accessing tselect register while Sdtrig extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Sdtrig; csrr a0, 0x7a0; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vcsr
NUMBER: 0x00f
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 2..1=VXRM, 0..0=VXSAT
EXTENSIONS: V
RULE 1: The vcsr register's least-significant bit (vcsr[0]) mirrors the vxsat bit, indicating whether a fixed-point instruction has saturated an output value to fit the destination format.
RULE 2: Bits 2 and 1 of vcsr implement the fixed-point rounding mode.
RULE 3: Bit 0 of vcsr implements the fixed-point accrued saturation flag.
RULE 4: The vcsr register has URW privilege, allowing user-mode read and write access.
RULE 5: When VS = Off, any attempt to read vcsr raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: When VS = Off, any attempt to write vcsr raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 7: When VS is Initial, Clean, or Dirty, executing a read of vcsr succeeds and leaves the VS field unchanged.
RULE 8: In M-mode, accessing vcsr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x00f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 9: In S-mode, accessing vcsr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x00f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 10: In U-mode, accessing vcsr register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x00f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 11: In M-mode, setting vcsr.VXRM (bit 1) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x2; csrs 0x00f, a0; csrr a1, 0x00f; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x2].
RULE 12: In M-mode, setting vcsr.VXSAT (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x00f, a0; csrr a1, 0x00f; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 13: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the vcsr register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x00f, a0; csrr a1, 0x00f; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 14: In M-mode, accessing vcsr register while V extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: V; csrr a0, 0x00f; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vl
NUMBER: 0xc20
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The vl CSR has URO privilege, meaning it is unprivileged and read-only.
RULE 2: The vl CSR is an XLEN-bit-wide, read-only register.
RULE 3: vl can only be updated by the vset{i}vl{i} instructions and by the fault-only-first vector load instruction variants.
RULE 4: The vset{i}vl{i} instructions set both the vtype CSR and the vl CSR according to their arguments and also write the resulting vl value into the destination register rd.
RULE 5: If the vtype value is not supported by the implementation, then the vl register is set to zero.
RULE 6: If rd is not a destination register and rs1 is not x0, the instruction performs normal strip mining and sets vl based on the AVL value in the rs1 register.
RULE 7: If rd is a destination register and rs1 is x0, the instruction sets vl to VLMAX.
RULE 8: If both rd and rs1 are x0, the instruction leaves vl unchanged (while vtype may change).
RULE 9: When rs1 is not x0, the instruction writes the newly computed vl value to the integer register specified by rd.
RULE 10: When rs1 is x0 and rd is not x0, the instruction writes VLMAX to vl and also writes VLMAX to the integer register specified by rd.
RULE 11: When both rs1 and rd are x0, the instruction uses the current vl as the AVL, computes a new vl value, writes it to vl, and does not write to any integer register.
RULE 12: If AVL ≥ 2 * VLMAX then vl = VLMAX.
RULE 13: For identical input AVL and VLMAX values, the resulting vl is deterministic on any given implementation.
RULE 14: If a value read from vl is later used as the AVL argument to vsetvl and the resultant VLMAX equals the VLMAX at the time vl was read, then the new vl equals the previously read vl value.
RULE 15: If AVL = 0 then vl = 0.
RULE 16: vl is never greater than AVL.
RULE 17: The integer register supplied as the second operand to vsetvli (a0) provides the total element count that the hardware uses to compute vl for the iteration.
RULE 18: If an element with an index greater than zero raises an exception, the corresponding trap is not taken and vl must be reduced to the index of that element.
RULE 19: For fault-only-first segment loads, when an exception is detected partway through accessing a subsequent segment, vl is reduced to the index of that segment.
RULE 20: If vl = 0, the instruction performs no operation and does not update the destination register.
RULE 21: The vfredosum instruction must sum the floating-point values in element order, starting with the scalar in vs1[0] and then adding the elements vs2[0] through vs2[vl-1], where vl is the current vector length.
RULE 22: If vl equals zero, no additions are performed and the scalar in vs1[0] is simply copied to the destination register without canonicalizing NaN values and without setting any exception flags.
RULE 23: When vl = 0, the vcpop.m instruction writes the value 0 to the integer register x[rd].
RULE 24: The instruction `csrr t1, vl` copies the current value of the register vl into integer register t1.
RULE 25: vmv.x.s performs its operation even if vstart ≥ vl or vl = 0.
RULE 26: vmv.s.x performs no operation and does not update the destination register when vstart ≥ vl.
RULE 27: vmv.s.x updates no elements in the destination vector register group when vl = 0, regardless of vstart.
RULE 28: vfmv.f.s performs its operation even when vstart ≥ vl.
RULE 29: vfmv.f.s performs its operation even when vl = 0.
RULE 30: vfmv.s.f performs no operation and does not update the destination register when vstart ≥ vl.
RULE 31: If vstart is greater than or equal to vl, the instruction performs no operation and leaves the destination vector register unchanged.
RULE 32: If OFFSET is less than vl, destination elements whose indices range from OFFSET through vl-1 are written provided they are unmasked.
RULE 33: For any element index i satisfying max(vstart, OFFSET) ≤ i < vl, the destination element is written as vd[i] = vs2[i-OFFSET] when the corresponding v0.mask[i] bit is enabled.
RULE 34: If an element index i satisfies vl ≤ i < VLMAX, then after the vector instruction the i‑th element of the destination vector register is produced according to the architecturally defined tail‑handling policy (e.g., unchanged, zeroed, or otherwise specified by the policy).
RULE 35: If an element index i satisfies vl ≤ i < VLMAX, then after the vector instruction the destination vector register element i must reflect the current tail policy (e.g., remain unchanged for an undisturbed policy or be zeroed for an agnostic policy); otherwise the destination register element i contains an unexpected value.
RULE 36: If vstart < vl and 0 ≤ i + OFFSET < VLMAX, then src[i] is set to vs2[i + OFFSET].
RULE 37: If vstart < vl and VLMAX ≤ i + OFFSET, then src[i] is set to zero.
RULE 38: If vstart ≤ i < vl and the mask bit v0.mask[i] is enabled, then vd[i] is written with src[i].
RULE 39: If a destination element index i satisfies vl ≤ i < VLMAX and the element after execution does not match the value prescribed by the current tail policy (e.g., retains its original value for an undisturbed policy or is zero for an agnostic policy), then reading that register element yields an unexpected value, indicating a violation of the tail‑policy rule.
RULE 40: For the vslide1up instruction, when vl > 0 and the element index i is less than vstart, the destination element remains unchanged.
RULE 41: For the vslide1up instruction, when vl > 0 and the element index i equals vstart, the destination element vd[i] is set to x[rs1] if the corresponding v0.mask[i] bit is enabled.
RULE 42: For the vslide1up instruction, when vl > 0 and max(vstart, 1) ≤ i < vl, the destination element vd[i] is set to vs2[i-1] if the corresponding v0.mask[i] bit is enabled.
RULE 43: For the vslide1up instruction, the active vl − 1 elements are copied from index i in the source vector register group to index i + 1 in the destination vector register group.
RULE 44: The vl register specifies the maximum number of destination vector register elements that the vslide1down instruction may write with source values, with any elements beyond vl handled by the current tail policy.
RULE 45: The vslide1down instruction copies the first vl-1 active elements from index i+1 of the source vector register group to index i of the destination vector register group.
RULE 46: The vslide1down instruction writes the scalar x register argument to the destination vector element at index vl-1 when that element is active.
RULE 47: For every index i satisfying vstart ≤ i < vl-1, the vslide1down operation performs vd[i] = vs2[i+1] if the corresponding v0.mask[i] is enabled.
RULE 48: For the index i equal to vl-1 and satisfying vstart ≤ i, the vslide1down operation performs vd[vl-1] = x[rs1] if the corresponding v0.mask[i] is enabled.
RULE 49: If vstart ≥ vl when one of these instructions is executed, then the destination vector register is still written (its elements are updated), observable as a change in the register’s contents.
RULE 50: If vstart < evl when one of these instructions is executed, then the instruction makes no architectural changes (e.g., destination registers, memory, and CSRs retain their previous values).
RULE 51: When element group instructions are present and the AVL value is greater than VLMAX, the vl value MUST be set to either VLMAX or a positive integer multiple of EGSMAX, where EGSMAX is the largest element group size supported by the implementation.
RULE 52: The number of element groups operated upon by a vector instruction equals vl divided by the element group size (EGS).
RULE 53: When LMUL multiplied by VLEN is less than the Element Group Width (EGW) for an element-group instruction, the processor raises an illegal-instruction exception even if vl equals zero.
RULE 54: When EGS = 4 for SEW = 32, vl MUST be a multiple of 4.
RULE 55: If the implementation processes a number of element groups different from the integer division of vl by EGS, then after the instruction completes the destination vector register will contain unchanged (or incorrect) element values for the groups beyond the expected count, observable by reading the register.
RULE 56: If vl is not a multiple of EGS‑4, then executing the vector instruction raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause is set to the illegal‑instruction code).
RULE 57: If VAESZ.vs processes a number of element groups that differs from the eg_len value computed from the current VL, then the destination vector register will contain untransformed elements beyond eg_len, causing the result to mismatch the expected transformed pattern.
RULE 58: In the execution of VWSLL.VV, the vl register is read to set the loop's upper bound so that element indices i iterate from vstart up to but not including vl.
RULE 59: In the execution of VWSLL.VX, the vl register is read to set the loop's upper bound so that element indices i iterate from vstart up to but not including vl.
RULE 60: In the execution of VWSLL.VI, the vl register is read to set the loop's upper bound so that element indices i iterate from vstart up to but not including vl.
RULE 61: For VWSLL.VV, VWSLL.VX, and VWSLL.VI, elements with indices i >= vl are not processed.
RULE 62: The SD bit is read-only and is set when VS is Dirty; consequently, if vl makes VS Dirty, the SD bit will be 1.
RULE 63: In M-mode, accessing vl register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc20; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 64: In S-mode, accessing vl register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc20; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 65: In U-mode, accessing vl register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc20; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vsepc
NUMBER: 0x241
MODE: VS-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..0=PC
EXTENSIONS: H
RULE 1: The vsepc CSR is readable and writable only in hypervisor mode (HRW privilege/access).
RULE 2: The low bit vsepc[0] is always zero.
RULE 3: In implementations that support only IALIGN = 32, both low bits vsepc[1:0] are always zero.
RULE 4: Whenever IALIGN = 32, reads of vsepc mask bit vsepc[1] so that it appears to be zero.
RULE 5: The implicit read of vsepc performed by the SRET instruction also masks bit vsepc[1] when IALIGN = 32.
RULE 6: Even when IALIGN = 32 masks vsepc[1] on reads, software may still write to bit vsepc[1].
RULE 7: In M-mode, accessing vsepc register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x241; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 8: In U-mode, accessing vsepc register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x241; # Result: mcause = 0x2].

REGISTER: vsie
NUMBER: 0x204
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..16=WPRI, 15..14=RES10-11, 13..13=VSIE.LCOFIE, 12..12=RES9, 11..10=RES7-8, 9..9=VSIE.SEIE, 8..8=RES6, 7..6=RES4-5, 5..5=VSIE.STIE, 4..4=RES3, 3..2=RES1-2, 1..1=VSIE.SSIE, 0..0=RES0
EXTENSIONS: H, Shlcofideleg, Smaia, Smcdeleg, Ssaia, Sscofpmf
RULE 1: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, SPIE is set to the value of SIE.
RULE 2: If a program writes an SXLEN‑wide value to the vsie CSR, then a subsequent read of vsie returns exactly that SXLEN‑wide value (with any bits above SXLEN masked off).
RULE 3: If a standard interrupt type (SEI, STI, SSI, or LCOFI) is not implemented, the corresponding vsie bit is a read-only zero.
RULE 4: An interrupt i traps to HS-mode if (1) the current operating mode is HS-mode and the SIE bit in the sstatus register is set, or the current operating mode has less privilege than HS-mode; (2) bit i is set in both sip and vsie, or in both hip and hie; and (3) bit i is not set in hideleg.
RULE 5: In M-mode, accessing vsie register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x204; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vstart
NUMBER: 0x008
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: If a CSR read or write uses address 0x008, then the operation accesses the vstart register, so the read returns the current vstart value and a write updates vstart to the written value.
RULE 2: Hardware normally writes vstart on a trap on a vector instruction, storing the element on which the trap was taken and indicating where execution should resume after a resumable trap is handled.
RULE 3: At the start of every vector instruction, including vsetvl, the implementation resets the vstart CSR to zero.
RULE 4: Vector instructions that raise illegal-instruction exceptions do not modify the vstart CSR.
RULE 5: Certain vector instructions cannot be executed with a non-zero vstart value and will raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 6: If a vector load instruction raises an exception during execution, then the vstart CSR contains a non‑zero value indicating the element index where the fault occurred.
RULE 7: If the vstart CSR holds a non‑zero value when a vector load instruction executes, then the load starts at element index vstart, the destination vector register’s element 0 receives the memory value at base address + vstart·SEW/8 (with subsequent elements loaded sequentially), and no exception is raised.
RULE 8: Vector store instructions may accept a non-zero vstart value.
RULE 9: If a fault‑only‑first instruction traps because an interrupt is taken, then the vstart CSR is written and its readback value is defined (e.g., contains the index of the first element).
RULE 10: A vector reduction operation must raise an illegal-instruction exception if vstart is non-zero.
RULE 11: During execution of a vector mask-logical instruction, elements whose indices are less than the current value of vstart are left unchanged.
RULE 12: When a trap is taken on the vmsbf.m instruction, the architectural value of the vstart register must be zero.
RULE 13: The vmsbf instruction must raise an illegal-instruction exception whenever the vstart register is non-zero.
RULE 14: When a trap is taken on the vmsif.m instruction, the architectural value of vstart reported to software MUST be 0.
RULE 15: The vmsif instruction MUST raise an illegal-instruction exception whenever the architectural value of vstart is non-zero.
RULE 16: The vmsof instruction will raise an illegal-instruction exception if vstart is non-zero.
RULE 17: After handling a trap on a viota.m instruction, execution shall be restarted from the beginning, which requires the architectural vstart register to be zero.
RULE 18: An illegal-instruction exception shall be raised whenever the architectural vstart register holds a nonzero value.
RULE 19: The vmv.x.s instruction performs its operation even when vstart is greater than or equal to vl or when vl is zero.
RULE 20: The vmv.s.x instruction performs no operation and does not update the destination register when vstart is greater than or equal to vl.
RULE 21: For each vslideup, vslidedown, v[f]slide1up, and v[f]slide1down instruction, if the vstart register holds a value greater than or equal to the current vl, the instruction performs no operation and leaves the destination vector register unchanged.
RULE 22: When the current vl is zero, no elements of the destination vector register group are updated by any of the listed slide instructions, regardless of the value in the vstart register.
RULE 23: If an element index i is ≥ min(vl, max(vstart, OFFSET)) or the mask bit for element i is zero, then the destination element must retain its original value (no write occurs).
RULE 24: When v0.mask[i] is enabled and i satisfies 0 ≤ i < min(vl, max(vstart, OFFSET)), the destination element vd[i] is assigned the value of vs2[i-OFFSET].
RULE 25: Satisfying the non-overlap constraint between the destination and source vector register groups enables restart of the instruction with a non-zero vstart.
RULE 26: When vstart is less than vl, for each element index i in the slide such that 0 ≤ i + OFFSET < VLMAX, the source element src[i] is defined as vs2[i + OFFSET].
RULE 27: When vstart is less than vl, for each element index i in the slide such that VLMAX ≤ i + OFFSET, the source element src[i] is defined as zero.
RULE 28: When vstart is less than vl, for each element index i with 0 ≤ i < vstart, the destination element vd[i] remains unchanged.
RULE 29: When vstart is less than vl, for each element index i with vstart ≤ i < vl, the destination element vd[i] is set to src[i] if the corresponding mask bit v0.mask[i] is enabled.
RULE 30: When vstart is less than vl, for each element index i with vl ≤ i < VLMAX, the handling of vd[i] follows the current tail policy.
RULE 31: When vl > 0 and an element index i is less than vstart, the destination element vd[i] remains unchanged.
RULE 32: When i equals vstart (which is also the case i = 0 as specified in the source), the destination element vd[i] is set to the scalar x[rs1] if the mask bit v0.mask[i] is enabled.
RULE 33: When an element index i satisfies max(vstart,1) <= i < vl, the destination element vd[i] is set to the vector element vs2[i-1] if the mask bit v0.mask[i] is enabled.
RULE 34: The mask bit v0.mask[i] directly governs whether the update specified for a given vstart condition is performed.
RULE 35: If an element index i is less than the current vstart value, the corresponding destination element vd[i] is unchanged.
RULE 36: If an element index i satisfies vstart ≤ i < vl-1 and the mask bit v0.mask[i] is enabled, then the destination element vd[i] is written with the source element vs2[i+1].
RULE 37: If the element index i equals vl-1, vstart ≤ i, and the mask bit v0.mask[i] is enabled, then the destination element vd[vl-1] is written with the scalar register x[rs1].
RULE 38: If the element index i equals vl-1, vstart ≤ i, and the mask bit v0.mask[i] is not enabled, then the destination element vd[vl-1] remains unchanged according to the mask-agnostic/undisturbed policy.
RULE 39: When a trap occurs during execution of a vector instruction, the vstart CSR contains the index of the vector element on which the trap was taken.
RULE 40: If after a precise vector trap the architectural state (registers or memory) shows a modification for any vector element whose index is ≥ vstart, then that modification must be identical to the modification that would result from restarting the trapped vector instruction at vstart and completing it; otherwise the implementation violates precise‑trap semantics.
RULE 41: If vstart is not an integer multiple of the element group size when executing a vector‑crypto instruction that uses element groups, the instruction raises an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 42: If vstart is not a multiple of 4 when executing a vsha2* vector‑crypto instruction, then the instruction raises an illegal‑instruction exception.
RULE 43: If a vsm3* instruction executes with vstart % 8 ≠ 0, then it raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause set to 2).
RULE 44: For Vector Crypto instructions matching the pattern vsm4*, the required EGS for vstart is 4.
RULE 45: vstart must be a multiple of 4, which is the element group size (EGS) for Zvkned vector AES instructions.
RULE 46: If the expression ((vstart % EGS) <> 0) | (LMUL*VLEN < EGW) evaluates to true, the implementation must raise an illegal-instruction exception by executing handle_illegal() and the instruction must retire with RETIRE_FAIL.
RULE 47: If vstart is set to a value less than the current vector length vl1, then after executing vclmulh the destination vector register contains the high‑half of the carry‑less product for each element index i where vstart ≤ i < vl1 and retains its original value for each index i < vstart; if vstart ≥ vl1, then the destination register is unchanged.
RULE 48: If a vclmulh instruction is executed, then the vstart CSR retains its prior value and no exception (e.g., no illegal‑instruction exception and mcause unchanged) is raised.
RULE 49: The vclz.v operation processes elements whose indices are greater than or equal to the current value of vstart and less than or equal to vl1.
RULE 50: The vcpop.v instruction reads the architectural register vstart to obtain the starting element index for its element-wise loop.
RULE 51: If the first element‑group index i used by a vector instruction is not equal to the integer result of vstart ÷ EGS, then the instruction starts processing the wrong element‑group and the destination vector register after execution contains data shifted by one or more element‑groups relative to the correct result.
RULE 52: For the VROR.VV, VROR.VX, and VROR.VI instructions, the element index i begins at the value contained in the vstart register.
RULE 53: The range of vector elements processed by VROR.VV, VROR.VX, and VROR.VI is defined by the vstart register as the starting index and by vl-1 as the ending index.
RULE 54: In the VSHA2c instruction, the start element-group index eg_start is computed as the architectural value of vstart divided by the element-group size EGS.
RULE 55: If VSHA2c starts its element‑group iteration at an index other than the one derived from vstart (eg_start) or does not proceed sequentially through all groups up to eg_len‑1, then the destination vector register’s final contents differ from the architecturally defined result.
RULE 56: The vstart CSR has URW privilege.
RULE 57: A read or write of the vstart CSR causes an illegal-instruction exception when the VS field is set to Off.
RULE 58: In M-mode, accessing vstart register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x008; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 59: In S-mode, accessing vstart register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x008; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 60: In U-mode, accessing vstart register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x008; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 61: In M-mode, setting vstart.VALUE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x008, a0; csrr a1, 0x008; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 62: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the vstart register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x008, a0; csrr a1, 0x008; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: vstval
NUMBER: 0x243
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: VSXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: H, Ssdbltrp, Zicfilp
RULE 1: When a trap is taken into HS-mode, the implementation writes the CSR vstval.
RULE 2: In M-mode, accessing vstval register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x243; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 3: In S-mode, accessing vstval register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x243; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 4: In U-mode, accessing vstval register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x243; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 5: In M-mode, setting vstval.VALUE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x243, a0; csrr a1, 0x243; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 6: In M-mode, accessing vstval register while H extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: H; csrr a0, 0x243; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 7: In M-mode, accessing vstval register while Ssdbltrp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Ssdbltrp; csrr a0, 0x243; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 8: In M-mode, accessing vstval register while Zicfilp extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: Zicfilp; csrr a0, 0x243; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vstvec
NUMBER: 0x205
MODE: S-mode
WIDTH: 64
FIELDS: 63..2=BASE, 1..0=MODE
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: The vstvec CSR is accessible in hypervisor mode with read-write permission.
RULE 2: vstvec is readable and writable.
RULE 3: In the CSR layout, bits SXLEN-1 down to 2 of vstvec hold the BASE field and are WARL, and bits 1-0 of vstvec hold the MODE field and are WARL.
RULE 4: The BASE field of vstvec must contain a 4-byte-aligned virtual or physical address.
RULE 5: When the MODE field of vstvec is set to Vectored, all synchronous exceptions into supervisor mode cause the program counter to be set to the address contained in the BASE field of vstvec.
RULE 6: In M-mode, accessing vstvec register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x205; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 7: In S-mode, accessing vstvec register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x205; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 8: In U-mode, accessing vstvec register should result in illegal-instruction exception (# Result: mcause = 0x2) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x205; # Result: mcause = 0x2].
RULE 9: In M-mode, setting vstvec.BASE (bit 2) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x4) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x4; csrs 0x205, a0; csrr a1, 0x205; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x4].
RULE 10: In M-mode, setting vstvec.MODE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x205, a0; csrr a1, 0x205; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 11: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the vstvec register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x205, a0; csrr a1, 0x205; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].

REGISTER: vtype
NUMBER: 0xc21
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..63=VILL, 7..7=VMA, 6..6=VTA, 5..3=VSEW, 2..0=VLMUL
EXTENSIONS: -
RULE 1: vtype can only be updated by vset{i}vl{i} instructions.
RULE 2: Non-zero values in bits vtype[XLEN-2:8] are reserved.
RULE 3: Bit XLEN-1 of vtype, named vill, is illegal if set.
RULE 4: When vsew[2:0] in vtype is 000, the selected element width (SEW) is 8.
RULE 5: When vsew[2:0] in vtype is 001, the selected element width (SEW) is 16.
RULE 6: When vsew[2:0] in vtype is 010, the selected element width (SEW) is 32.
RULE 7: When vsew[2:0] in vtype is 011, the selected element width (SEW) is 64.
RULE 8: When vsew[2:0] in vtype matches the pattern 1xx, the encoding is reserved.
RULE 9: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 1 0 0, the resulting LMUL encoding is reserved, the number of groups is undefined, VLMAX is undefined, and the register grouping is reserved.
RULE 10: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 1 0 1, LMUL is 1/8, the vector register file is divided into 32 groups, VLMAX equals VLEN/SEW/8, and each group consists of a single register v n.
RULE 11: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 1 1 0, LMUL is 1/4, the vector register file is divided into 32 groups, VLMAX equals VLEN/SEW/4, and each group consists of a single register v n.
RULE 12: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 1 1 1, LMUL is 1/2, the vector register file is divided into 32 groups, VLMAX equals VLEN/SEW/2, and each group consists of a single register v n.
RULE 13: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 0 0 0, LMUL is 1, the vector register file is divided into 32 groups, VLMAX equals VLEN/SEW, and each group consists of a single register v n.
RULE 14: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 0 0 1, LMUL is 2, the vector register file is divided into 16 groups, VLMAX equals 2 × VLEN/SEW, and each group contains registers v n and v n + 1.
RULE 15: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 0 1 0, LMUL is 4, the vector register file is divided into 8 groups, VLMAX equals 4 × VLEN/SEW, and each group contains registers v n through v n + 3.
RULE 16: When the vlmul[2:0] bits in vtype are 0 1 1, LMUL is 8, the vector register file is divided into 4 groups, VLMAX equals 8 × VLEN/SEW, and each group contains registers v n through v n + 7.
RULE 17: When LMUL derived from vtype equals 2, the vector register group contains registers v n and v n + 1, providing twice the vector length in bits.
RULE 18: When vtype encodes LMUL = 2, instructions that specify a vector register group with an odd-numbered base register are reserved.
RULE 19: When LMUL derived from vtype equals 4, the vector register group contains four consecutive registers.
RULE 20: When LMUL derived from vtype equals 8, the vector register group contains eight consecutive registers.
RULE 21: When vtype encodes LMUL = 8, instructions that specify a vector register group using a base register number that is not a multiple of eight are reserved.
RULE 22: Mask destination tail elements are always treated as tail-agnostic irrespective of the vta bit value in vtype.
RULE 23: If a set of destination elements is marked undisturbed by the vtype bits, those elements retain the value previously held in the vector register group.
RULE 24: If the vill bit in vtype is set, any attempt to execute a vector instruction that depends on vtype shall raise an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 25: When the vill bit in vtype is set, all other XLEN-1 bits of vtype shall be zero.
RULE 26: If a vector instruction’s source and destination registers overlap but have different EEW, then the instruction is tail‑agnostic: the values of elements beyond VL are unspecified (may be unchanged or undefined) regardless of the vta and vma bits in vtype.
RULE 27: If a masked vector instruction writes a destination register, then the elements beyond the effective vector length (tail elements) of that destination retain their original values, regardless of the vta bit setting in vtype.
RULE 28: When vtype.vta = 0, tail elements do not raise exceptions and do not update any destination vector register group.
RULE 29: All vset{i}vl{i} instructions update the vtype CSR with a value derived from their operands.
RULE 30: The vsetivli instruction uses its third operand vtypei as the new vtype setting that is written to the vtype CSR.
RULE 31: When a vset{i}vl{i} instruction updates the vtype CSR, it also updates the vl CSR based on the same arguments.
RULE 32: In the vtype register, bit XLEN-1 is named vill and indicates an illegal value if set; for XLEN values other than 32, vill resides at bit XLEN-1.
RULE 33: Bits 5 down to 3 of the vtype register form the vsew[2:0] field that encodes the selected element width (SEW) setting.
RULE 34: Bits 2 down to 0 of the vtype register form the vlmul[2:0] field that encodes the vector register group multiplier (LMUL) setting.
RULE 35: Assembler name e8 encodes SEW = 8 bits in the vsew[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 36: Assembler name e16 encodes SEW = 16 bits in the vsew[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 37: Assembler name e32 encodes SEW = 32 bits in the vsew[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 38: Assembler name e64 encodes SEW = 64 bits in the vsew[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 39: Assembler name mf8 encodes LMUL = 1/8 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 40: Assembler name mf4 encodes LMUL = 1/4 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 41: Assembler name mf2 encodes LMUL = 1/2 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 42: Assembler name m1 encodes LMUL = 1 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 43: Assembler name m2 encodes LMUL = 2 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 44: Assembler name m4 encodes LMUL = 4 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 45: Assembler name m8 encodes LMUL = 8 in the vlmul[2:0] field of the vtype register.
RULE 46: Executing vsetvli with arguments e8, m1, ta, ma sets the vsew[2:0] field of vtype to encode SEW = 8 bits, sets the vlmul[2:0] field to encode LMUL = 1, and sets both the vta and vma bits of vtype to 1.
RULE 47: Executing vsetvli with arguments e8, m2, ta, ma sets the vsew[2:0] field of vtype to encode SEW = 8 bits, sets the vlmul[2:0] field to encode LMUL = 2, and sets both the vta and vma bits of vtype to 1.
RULE 48: Executing vsetvli with arguments e32, mf2, ta, ma sets the vsew[2:0] field of vtype to encode SEW = 32 bits, sets the vlmul[2:0] field to encode LMUL = 1/2, and sets both the vta and vma bits of vtype to 1.
RULE 49: If a vtype value is not supported by the implementation, the vl register is set to zero.
RULE 50: When both rd and rs1 are x0 in a vsetvli or vsetvl instruction, the existing vl must be kept while the vtype register may be changed.
RULE 51: When the instruction vsetvli a3, a0, e16, m4, ta, ma is executed, the vtype register is set to 16-bit integer vectors.
RULE 52: Masked vector loads do not update inactive elements in the destination vector-register group unless masked-agnostic operation is specified by setting vtype.vma to 1.
RULE 53: When vtype.vma is set to 1, masked vector loads update inactive elements, indicating that masked-agnostic behavior is in effect.
RULE 54: The SEW field encoded in vtype specifies the selected element width for the data values of vector indexed load and store instructions.
RULE 55: If the vill bit in vtype is set when executing vsm.v, then the instruction raises an illegal‑instruction exception (mcause = 2).
RULE 56: If the VTYPE setting yields a VLMAX that is smaller than the VL operand supplied to a vlm.v instruction, then the hardware truncates the effective VL to VLMAX, so after execution the vl CSR equals VLMAX and only VLMAX mask elements are loaded into the destination mask register.
RULE 57: Whole-register load and store instructions compute their effective vector length as evl = NFIELDS * VLEN / EEW and do not consider the current vtype setting.
RULE 58: The value of the vlmul field in vtype does not affect which vector register is used by vector mask-register logical instructions.
RULE 59: Vector mask-register logical instructions do not change the vlmul field of vtype.
RULE 60: In the masked viota.m example the vtype register's vma field is 0 (vtype.vma = 0).
RULE 61: The usual reservation rule that an instruction is reserved when vstart exceeds the largest element index defined by vtype does not apply to vmv<nr>r.v instructions.
RULE 62: vmv<nr>r.v instructions are reserved only when vstart is greater than or equal to evl, irrespective of the vtype-defined largest element index.
RULE 63: If the opcode statically encodes the EEW of all operands for a single-size operation, the vtype SEW field value is ignored.
RULE 64: The vtype CSR has unprivileged read-only (URO) privilege.
RULE 65: If VS is Off, a read of the vtype CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 66: If VS is Off, a write to the vtype CSR raises an illegal-instruction exception.
RULE 67: If S-mode is implemented but the vector registers are not, VS may be read-only zero and the vtype CSR is not present.
RULE 68: In M-mode, accessing vtype register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0xc21; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 69: In S-mode, accessing vtype register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0xc21; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 70: In U-mode, accessing vtype register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0xc21; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vxrm
NUMBER: 0x00a
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: V
RULE 1: The vxrm CSR is defined with URW privilege, meaning it can be read and written by unprivileged software.
RULE 2: The vxrm register holds a two-bit read-write rounding-mode field in the least-significant bits vxrm[1:0].
RULE 3: The rounding-mode value in vxrm is also reflected as a field in the vcsr register.
RULE 4: When vxrm[1:0] = 0b00, the rounding mode is round-to-nearest-up (add +0.5 LSB) and the rounding increment r used in (v >> d) + r is v[d-1].
RULE 5: When vxrm[1:0] = 0b01, the rounding mode is round-to-nearest-even and the rounding increment r used in (v >> d) + r is v[d-1] & (v[d-2:0] ≠ 0 | v[d]).
RULE 6: When vxrm[1:0] = 0b10, the rounding mode is round-down and the rounding increment r used in (v >> d) + r is 0.
RULE 7: When vxrm[1:0] = 0b11, the rounding mode is round-to-odd (OR bits into LSB, aka "jam") and the rounding increment r used in (v >> d) + r is !v[d] & v[d-1:0] ≠ 0.
RULE 8: In the vcsr CSR, bits 2 down to 1 constitute the vxrm[1:0] field.
RULE 9: The bits 2:1 of vcsr are named vxrm[1:0].
RULE 10: The vxrm[1:0] field in vcsr specifies the fixed-point rounding mode.
RULE 11: The rounding operation that follows the infinite-precision computation and truncation uses the rounding mode selected by vxrm.
RULE 12: The vector single-width logical right-shift scaling instruction vssrl rounds the shifted-out bits according to the current setting of the vxrm register.
RULE 13: Rounding that uses the mode specified in vxrm is performed around the least-significant bit of the destination.
RULE 14: Rounding that uses the mode specified in vxrm is performed before saturation.
RULE 15: The vxrm CSR has privilege URW, meaning it can be read and written in user mode.
RULE 16: In M-mode, accessing vxrm register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x00a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 17: In S-mode, accessing vxrm register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x00a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 18: In U-mode, accessing vxrm register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x00a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 19: In M-mode, setting vxrm.VALUE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x00a, a0; csrr a1, 0x00a; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 20: In M-mode, accessing vxrm register while V extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: V; csrr a0, 0x00a; # Result: mcause = 0x0].

REGISTER: vxsat
NUMBER: 0x009
MODE: U-mode
WIDTH: MXLEN
FIELDS: 63..0=VALUE
EXTENSIONS: V
RULE 1: The vxsat CSR contains a single read-write least-significant bit named vxsat[0].
RULE 2: The vxsat[0] bit indicates whether a fixed-point instruction has saturated an output value to fit into the destination format.
RULE 3: The vxsat bit is mirrored in the vcsr register.
RULE 4: The vxsat CSR can also be accessed as a field within the XLEN-bit-wide vector control and status CSR named vcsr.
RULE 5: If a value with any non‑zero bits beyond bit 0 is written to the vxsat CSR, then reading the CSR returns a value where only bit 0 reflects the written value and all higher bits read back as zero.
RULE 6: For the vnclip instruction, the shifted-rounded source value is treated as a signed integer and the operation saturates if the result would overflow the destination viewed as a signed integer, and such an overflow sets the vxsat bit.
RULE 7: vxsat has URW privilege, meaning it is readable and writable in user mode.
RULE 8: When the vector registers are implemented, the VS field shall not be read-only zero, therefore the vxsat CSR shall not be read-only zero.
RULE 9: Changing the VS field has no effect on the value of the vxsat CSR.
RULE 10: In M-mode, accessing vxsat register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; csrr a0, 0x009; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 11: In S-mode, accessing vxsat register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_supervisor; csrr a0, 0x009; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 12: In U-mode, accessing vxsat register should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; call machine_to_user; csrr a0, 0x009; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
RULE 13: In M-mode, setting vxsat.VALUE (bit 0) should be reflected on the readback (# Result: a2 = 0x1) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0x1; csrs 0x009, a0; csrr a1, 0x009; and a2, a0, a1; # Result: a2 = 0x1].
RULE 14: In M-mode, writing 0xffffffffffffffff to the vxsat register should not set it to 0xffffffff or 0xffffffffffffffff (# Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff) [# Extension Must Be Active: NONE; li a0, 0xffffffffffffffff; csrw 0x009, a0; csrr a1, 0x009; # Result: a1 != 0xffffffff & a1 != 0xffffffffffffffff].
RULE 15: In M-mode, accessing vxsat register while V extension is active should result in no exception (# Result: mcause = 0x0) [# Extension Must Be Active: V; csrr a0, 0x009; # Result: mcause = 0x0].
